author: brunotm
message: [DS-3869] stateful calculated streams (#257) * llo/protocol: chunked ring storage for stream history Add the storage layer for stream history: a persisted window of past agreed aggregate values per (streamID, aggregator) pair, which calculated streams need in order to evaluate expressions over more than the current round. The window is a chunked ring rather than one blob per pair. A chunk holds MaxHistoryChunkRecords records and only the newest chunk of a window is ever rewritten, once full a chunk is immutable for as long as it is retained. The per-round write cost a function of the chunk size instead of the window depth, ~2 KiB rather than ~60 KiB for a full 1024-record quote window, at a read cost of depth/chunkSize point reads instead of one. The header carries enough denormalized state that every decision a round makes like is there enough depth, which chunks must be read, may this value be appended, which chunk gets dropped, is taken from the header alone, without opening a chunk. A pair still warming up costs a single read. Decode enforces every invariant it can: header agrees with records, timestamps strictly increasing, caps respected and reports ErrCorruptStreamHistory so callers discard and re-warm. Per-record and per-pair size caps in limits.go bound what one pair can cost. New v31 KeyValueState keys, disjoint from the existing channel and hot records: hh/<streamID BE><aggregator BE> -> LLOStreamHistoryHeaderProto hc/<streamID BE><aggregator BE><slot BE> -> LLOStreamHistoryChunkProto hidx -> the sorted set of pairs holding a window hv -> history layout version hidx makes orphan reclaim possible without a range scan. hv is a forward guard: v31 lives under llo/dev and carries no compatibility promise, so a layout change drops every window and re-warms rather than carrying a dual-read shim. * llo/protocol/calculated: History() AST support Support for hisHistory(stream,count) call in an expression is recognised, validated, and rewritten into a plain identifier that the evaluator binds a window to. The rewrite happens in an expr.Patch pass, so History never exists at run time. The rest of the DSL stay untouched: a patched History call becomes an identifier holding a Series, and any function that accepts a window just receives it as an argument. History is still registered in the default environment bound to a stub that fails. Analysis is separated from evaluation and exposed as AnalyzeExpressionHistory, because the plugin needs to know which windows an expression reads and how deep, before it can decide what to persist which is strictly earlier than the point at which it could evaluate. Compiled programs and analysis results are cached per expression string, so parsing, patching and compiling happen once per distinct expression per node rather than every round. Field selection (s1, s1_bid, s1_ask) is resolved here and not in storage, one stored window serves every field, because a whole stream value is stored per record and the field is projected when the window is read. AggregatorByStream and Expressions are exported so the plugin derives its history requirements from exactly the same channel opts and stream/aggregator mapping that evaluation uses. Series carries values with their observation timestamps, which time based functions need as rounds are not evenly spaced, so a window's records cannot be treated as a uniform sample. * llo/protocol/calculated: evaluate expressions over history windows Bind required expression windows to the evaluation environment. A History call rewritten at compile time resolves to a series during run-time evaluation. ProcessCalculatedStreams and evalExpression take a HistoryReader. Before an expression is evaluated, bindHistory resolves each of its history references against the reader and binds the resulting series under the identifier the AST pass rewrote the call into. A window shallower than requested causes the expression to not be evaluated, as it would silently compute over a shorter than requested series. bindHistory returns ErrInsufficientHistory, no aggregate is generated and the channel is simply not reportable this round. This is the expected state while a window warms up, after a depth increase, or after corrupt state was discarded. A nil reader fails closed. v30 has no replicated key/value state, so there is nowhere for history to live. A v30 channel configured with a History expression produces nothing and never reports, rather than evaluating against an empty window. toDecimal rejects a Series. Static analysis already refuses windows in scalar positions, so this is a backstop for a bypassed analysis, but without it, a window reaching a scalar function would be coerced to something meaningless rather than refused. Dry-run validation synthesizes its windows and relative to the same timestamp as the environment so window-relative functions see records inside their window. * llo/dev/v31: stream history persistence and loading Wire stream histoy, derive what each round must store, record the agreed values, and persist the windows. historyStore is the round working set and the only thing that touches history keys. It gurantees that each key is read at most once and written at most once per round however many channels reference the pair, so ten channels sharing History(s101, 300) cause one set of reads and one set of writes, a round reads only what it needs, appending touches the newest chunk, reading n records touches the chunks covering them, and a pair still warming up costs a single header read. Requirements are computed from the channel definitions and their expressions before aggregation,the required depth is what decides whether a pair's value is recorded at all. They are derived from the same channel opts and stream/aggregator mapping evaluation uses, what is persisted cannot drift from what is read. History records what the round actually agreed on, the same value written into StreamAggregates. A window is always a series of values that reached consensus. Appends are strictly newer than the newest stored record, and stops a carry forward value being counted once per round until it refreshes. Flush visits pairs in sorted order and issues each pair's writes before its deletes, so every node performs the same operations in the same sequence. Pairs no live channel requires are deleted and the index is rewritten only when the stored set changed. Calculated streams nil check runs unconditionally rather than only under DisableNilStreamValues. * llo/protocol/calculated: reject invalid expressions at the channel boundary Validate calculated-stream expressions in the report codec's Verify, so a statically invalid expression rejects causes the channel to be rejected. * llo/protocol/calculated: extend existing functions for series, guard decimal math * llo/protocol/calculated: series functions over history windows Add the functions that reduce a history window to a scalar: Sum, First, Last, Median, Variance, Stddev, Delta, PctChange and Spread. * llo/protocol/calculated: add SMA Add SMA(window, n): the simple moving average of the newest n values of a history window. The sample count is an argument rather than the whole window, so one stored window serves several averages -- History(s1, 300) can feed SMA(w, 20) and SMA(w, 200) without persisting two series. Asking for more samples than the window holds is an error rather than an average over what is there: silently averaging fewer samples than requested would change the meaning of the result. * llo/protocol/calculated: add WMA Add WMA(window, n): the linearly weighted moving average of the newest n values of a history window, weighting the newest value n and the oldest of the n values 1. WMA = (n*x[newest] + (n-1)*x[newest-1] + ... + 1*x[oldest]) / (n + ... + 1) Linear weights rather than any other decay: the weight of a sample is its position, so the result is fully determined by the window contents and n, with no smoothing constant to agree on across oracles. That matters here in a way it would not in a local calculation as every node must compute the same value from the same window. * llo/protocol/calculated: add EMA Add EMA(window, n): the exponential moving average of a history window with smoothing period n, seeded with the simple mean of the oldest n values and iterated newest-ward with the conventional smoothing factor. alpha = 2 / (n + 1) ema = value*alpha + ema*(1 - alpha) * llo/protocol/calculated: add TWAP Add TWAP(window, config): the time-weighted average price over a window, ported from the original spec and implementation (ADR 0013/0014/0015). * llo/protocol/calculated: document the expression package, fuzz evaluation Add the package documentation, a fuzz target over expression evaluation, and benchmarks for the function library. * llo/protocol/calculated: evaluate channels concurrently ProcessCalculatedStreams walked every channel in one loop: decoding opts, reading history, compiling and evaluating, then writing the results back. Every expression in a round therefore ran on one goroutine, and rounds are dominated by window functions over deep history. * llo/protocol/calculated: fuzz a whole round, not one expression FuzzEvaluateExpression drives resolveHistory and evalDecimal directly, so the corpus never crossed the three phases a round actually runs: preparation, concurrent evaluation, and the sequential apply that commits the results. The structures those phases share the environment pool, the analysis and program caches, the aggregates map every channel writes into were only ever covered by fixed fixtures * llo/protocol: reject colliding calculated stream IDs and feed IDs VerifyChannelDefinitions check for collisions during admission. Those are already handled in tooling and the ChannelDefinitionCache, but statically check them before admitting in the KV state. * llo: derive calculated streams instead of storing them on channel definitions Calculated streams were appended to the channel definitions by expression evaluation. In v3.1 that append needs to reach the key-value state, it was carried into the pending definition set and cost a second whole-record KV rewrite the round after any definition vote. Also collapses the two duplicate decodes of the expression opts shape onto protocol.CalculatedStreamOpts, and replaces the codec's last-stream guard with a check on the values it actually needs. * llo: fix review findings from PR Expression validation accepted a History call naming a stream the channel does not observe. Sample counts, TWAP window lengths and TWAP gap thresholds were bounded after narrowing through decimal.IntPart, which returns the low 64 bits of an oversized value rather than failing. A history layout reset dropped the stored index, which broke it in both directions. Per-pair history gauges were never deleted when a pair was reclaimed. * llo: apply strict channel definition checks only when voting VerifyChannelDefinitions is run against already-committed definitions at the top of Observation and, via the merged set, in ValidateObservation. Any check added to it therefore rejects definitions that were installed before the check existed: every oracle then fails to produce an observation, every round, and the protocol halts rather than the offending channel simply not reporting. Split the checks in two. The baseline ones -- the caps, the structural rules, codec.Verify -- keep running everywhere, as they did before. The ones added with calculated streams are admission-only and run through the new VerifyChannelDefinitionsForAdmission, scoped to the channels being added or changed: static expression analysis, calculated stream ID collisions, and feed ID uniqueness. A cross-definition finding names two channels and is reported against whichever is seen second, so it is kept when either of them is being admitted -- otherwise a new channel could take the feed ID of a committed one with a higher ID. * llo: bound power results, and hold history to one append per round checkPowExponent bounded the exponent but not the size of the result, which is what the cost is actually driven by. A power with a non-integer exponent is evaluated as exp(exponent * ln(base)), so Pow(3000, 50000.5) asks for exp(4e5), a number with about 174,000 digits -- exp() refuses that through maxExpArgument, but the power path never went near the guard. Both operands come from consensus, so every node computes it in the same round inside StateTransition, holding the transcendental lock. checkPow now bounds the quantity exp() bounds, estimating the logarithm at low precision so the refusal costs nothing next to the work it prevents. The exponent bound stays as a cheap first gate. RingWindow.WriteSet carries only the newest chunk, which Append overwrites when a chunk seals and a new one starts. A second append in one round therefore persisted only the second chunk, losing the sealed one's final record while the header had already counted it -- next round the window reads short and is discarded as corrupt. The aggregation path appends once per pair per round, but Append is exported, so the constraint is now checked: a second append returns ErrHistoryAlreadyAppended. Rejecting it rather than tracking several dirty chunks keeps the round's write budget at one header and one chunk per pair, which the layout is sized on. An append rejected for not being strictly newer stores nothing, so it does not spend the round's one append. The static TWAP satisfiability check compared minSamples as a uint32, so a literal above 2^32 wrapped into a small one and passed; the runtime validation still caught it, but the configuration-time diagnostic the check exists to give was lost. Compared as int64 now, with a non-positive value reported as such instead of as a history-depth problem. environment.SetStreamValue recursed for a timestamped value and dropped the error, so a nil wrapped value left the environment holding s<N>_timestamp and no s<N>: the channel then failed with "unknown name s<N>" instead of saying the value was nil. * llo: guard backfill timestamp scaling, and cache backfill opts ObservationTimestampKeyToNanoseconds scaled a raw key by unsigned multiplication with no bound, so a key beyond about 1.8e10 seconds wrapped. It wrapped in the dangerous direction: every caller compares the result against an upper bound it must be below, so a far-future key read as a valid past timestamp. The validator was the lesser exposure -- VerifyChannelDefinitions passes nowNanos 0, which skips the future check entirely -- while selection compares against both the watermark and the round's observation timestamp, so a wrapped key landed inside the eligible band and was picked, producing a report at a fabricated time. The conversion now reports whether the key is representable: validation rejects it whatever nowNanos is, and selection skips it. A backfill channel could also name another backfill channel, or itself, as its target. Nothing rejected it: the resolution lookup falls through to seconds, the stream lists match trivially when the target is the channel itself, and the target declares no calculated streams. It failed only in Report, where the codec resolved from the target's report format is ReportCodecHistoryBackfill, whose Encode always errors -- so the channel was selected, logged and skipped every round forever, because the watermark only advances on a report that was emitted. Rejected on admission now, not for committed definitions: such a channel has never produced a report, so there is nothing to protect but the ability to install a new one. Selection ran two or three times per backfill channel per round and parsed the opts from raw JSON each time, unlike every other codec, which decodes through OptsCache. GetHistoryBackfillOpts now prefers the cache and falls back to parsing on a miss, so the observation map is built once per generation rather than several times per round. The post-decode rules move to a method both paths share: GetOpts skips the unmarshal for empty raw bytes and yields the zero value without error, which those rules have to catch. Opts parsing also visits keys in sorted order, so a definition with more than one problem always reports the same one, and a duplicate key names both keys and the value they collide on. Distinct keys can decode to the same number -- ParseUint accepts leading zeros, so "01" and "1" are both 1 -- which is what the duplicate checks are for. Quote and TimestampedStreamValue marshal through the package's deterministic marshaller. Their bytes go into replicated history state and are the keys ModeAggregator counts to pick a mode, so they are compared across oracles. Neither message has a map field and Deterministic only orders map entries, so this is a no-op today; it is applied so that adding a map field to either cannot silently introduce a divergence. The existing deterministicHistoryMarshal is renamed accordingly, since it is no longer history-specific.

author: makramkd
message: docs(runbooks): absence of metrics and effect on commit plugin health (#2267) * feat: track discovery state of the commit plugin When testing the new metrics on staging, I noticed that the Solana commit plugin, while producing heartbeats, was producing no other metrics except for ccip_commit_report_validation_rejected with the reason being config_digest_check_error, which was happening due to an RPC being unhealthy (and it being the only RPC). This can be proxied by knowing whether the plugin is out of the discovery phase - if its still in discovery, nothing else runs, and therefore no other metrics are produced, metrics which are needed to do the health runbook and the uncommitted message runbook. So this commit adds a new metric, a gauge, that reports whether the plugin has discovered the contracts or not, a quick way to know if the plugin is actually ready to produce observations. While there are other metrics whose absence _implies_ that the plugin is not healthy, this is a clear signal of _why_ the plugin is not healthy: it hasn't discovered any contracts yet. * update runbooks, dashboards * Revert "update runbooks, dashboards" This reverts commit 5213b20906754d305b0a0f2f6cfff60f7b791f7d. * Revert "feat: track discovery state of the commit plugin" This reverts commit 276bbc02ba68d75fe027c12c09b34fd6b5f0dbcf. * update runbooks to reflect metric absence effect

author: brunotm
message: llo/dev/v31: move blob broadcasting out of Observation (#256) * llo/dev/v31: move blob broadcasting out of Observation Stream values are now gathered by a background blob pump (blobpump.go) that holds the BlobBroadcastFetcher provided to the factory. Each cycle observes the streams and seqNr known at the time, serializes the values, broadcasts them, and parks the marshaled handle. Observation keeps only the cheap synchronous work (KV load, retirement, channel votes), publishes the round context, and picks up whatever the pump has ready. Cadence is consumption driven: a cycle is kicked whenever Observation takes or discards a snapshot, so the pump rate tracks the round rate without the plugin needing to know OCR round cadence, and no blob is broadcasted unnecessarily. Cycles are serial so only one Observe is ever in flight. There is no idle watchdog: snapshot usability is bounded by sequence number, so refreshing while no rounds run would only produce snapshots already too old to use. Stream values are now carried exclusively by blobs and never inline. A round that finds nothing usable (cold start, failed cycle, stale snapshot) emits an observation carrying only votes and its timestamp. Adds llo/dev/v31/llotest, exporting an in-memory, content-addressed BlobBroadcastFetcher that makes the broadcast/fetch/merge round trip testable. * llo/dev/v31: derive unexpired-blob limits from blob lifetime MaxPerOracleUnexpiredBlobCount and its cumulative payload counterpart were hardcoded to 32, independent of the configurable BlobLifetimeRounds. Since the pump broadcasts about one blob per round, a lifetime above 32 could leave more than 32 blobs unexpired, at which point libocr rejects further broadcasts for resource exhaustion and rounds continually lose stream values. Both limits are now derived from the configured lifetime plus BlobReapingMarginRounds (asynchronous reaping), floored at the previous value of 32. BlobLifetimeRounds above MaxBlobLifetimeRounds (64) is rejected at plugin construction so the declared budget stays bounded. The default lifetime of 3 keeps the previous limits unchanged. * llo/dev/v31: blob payload compression

author: brunotm
message: llo/dev/v31: v31 kv state into round and channel records (#254) * llo/dev/v31: v31 kv state into round and channel records v31 spread its replicated state over per channel and per stream keys: c/<id>, v/<id>, r/<id>, t/<sid><agg>, plus an idx key to enumerate channels. Loading state cost 3 + 3N point reads for N channels, once per Observation, ValidateObservation and StateTransition, plus one read per (stream, aggregator) pair during aggregation. Split the state by write frequency instead: c/lifecycle -> lifecycle stage bytes (written on change) c/defs -> LLOChannelStateProto (written on change) c/seqnr -> uint64 BE seqNr of last c/defs write r/agg -> LLOHotStateProto (written every round) r/agg carries the observation timestamp, the validAfter watermarks, the per channel reportability decisions and the carry forward aggregates. c/defs carries every channel definition. c/defs is a pure function of c/seqnr where channel changes happened, both are written by the same StateTransition, the plugin keeps the decoded definitions in the channelCache and re-reads them only at startup or when the stored sequence number differs from the cached one. Steady-state reads per round drop to 3, and writes to 1, both independent of the channel and stream count. * llo/dev/v31: skip hot-state read in Observation path Observation and ValidateObservation only inspect the lifecycle stage and channel definitions, but loadKVState always read and decoded the r/agg record — including a per-stream UnmarshalProtoStreamValue for every carry-forward aggregate. That cost scales with stream count and was paid on every node, every round. Split the loader: loadColdKVState reads only c/lifecycle, c/seqnr and c/defs (cache-aware), and loadKVState composes it with readHotState. Observation and ValidateObservation now use the cold loader; StateTransition keeps the full load. Also drop the unused sameChannelSet helper and tidy stale comments.

author: sebastian-lerner-link
message: Clarify lastSeenTimestampNs/lastUpdateTimestamp non-monotonicity on v8/v11 feeds (#4032) * Consolidate v8/v11 timestamp monotonicity docs into one branch Same root cause (median timestamp over configured data providers), same fix pattern (expect advancement as the norm; a single stalled or backward-moving report is expected and fine on its own; only escalate if it recurs across multiple consecutive reports or exceeds your own staleness threshold). No reason to ship this as two separate branches. * Stop recommending observationsTimestamp as a freshness fix observationsTimestamp reflects report generation time, not confirmation that the underlying price changed, so it doesn't actually solve the freshness question. The recommendation stays lastUpdateTimestamp: reliable in the normal case, not bulletproof on low-DP feeds, with reliability improvements in progress. * Reframe DP-count language around weight, not headcount Replace "small/low number of configured data providers" with a mechanism-first explanation: fewer providers means each one carries more weight in the median, without characterizing feeds as thin. Also drop "expected" from the single-occurrence framing so it reads as "not concerning" rather than "supposed to happen." * rewrite warning in schema notes --------- Co-authored-by: Sebastian Lerner <sebastian.lerner2@gmail.com> Co-authored-by: devin distefano <devin.distefano@smartcontract.com>

author: prashantkumar1982
message: [CRE] confidential relay: wait for late execution handler before failing relay callback (#23284) * [CRE] confidential relay: wait for late execution handler before failing relay callback The enclave runs one DON-shared confidential execution and only needs a relay quorum to proceed, so the gateway's relay callback (fanned out to every workflow-DON member) can reach a node before that node has started its own copy of the execution and registered the execution handler. The node then failed the callback with "execution handler not found", dropping its signature and, when enough nodes raced, pushing the relay below quorum. Add ExecutionHandlers.GetExecutionWithWait: on a miss it registers a lost-wakeup-safe waiter and blocks until the handler appears or the caller's context is done. The relay handler calls it with a bounded (5s) deadline, well under the gateway's relay request timeout, and only after attestation and Workflow-DON authorization pass so an unverified callback cannot park a waiter. This addresses the start-edge race; the end-edge (early RemoveExecution on execution timeout) and pathological never-starts (concurrency saturation, stale-event drops) are separate. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com> * test: add t.Parallel() to confidential relay execution-handler tests Satisfy golangci paralleltest, which flagged the new test functions. Also capture start before setting the deadline in the timeout test so the elapsed lower-bound assertion cannot flake. author: giogam
message: fix: derive catalog gRPC retry policy service name from proto ServiceDesc (#1139) ## Summary The retry policy attached via `grpc.WithDefaultServiceConfig` in `datastore/catalog/remote/grpc.go` never took effect. Its `methodConfig` hardcoded the service name `op_catalog.v1.datastore.Datastore`, but the actual proto service is `api.datastore.v1.Datastore` (`/api.datastore.v1.Datastore/DataAccess`). Since no method name matched, gRPC silently ignored the retry policy. ## Changes - Build the retry policy service config with `pb.Datastore_ServiceDesc.ServiceName` instead of a hardcoded string, so the name always matches the generated code even if the proto package is renamed. - Document that gRPC service-config retries only apply to unary RPCs — the bidirectional streaming `DataAccess` RPC is never retried by gRPC and would need application-level reconnect logic if stream resilience is desired. - Add a unit test asserting the rendered service config is valid JSON and matches the proto service name.

author: futureproof1
message: feat: ConfigureTokenPool changeset (EVM v2.0) (#2195) * feat: scaffolding and validation for ConfigureTokenPool changeset * feat: finality config updates in ConfigureTokenPool changeset * feat: token pool admin role updates in ConfigureTokenPool changeset * feat: per-remote fee config updates in ConfigureTokenPool changeset * feat: per-remote rate limit updates in ConfigureTokenPool changeset * test: YAML round-trip, version gating, MCMS, and combined ConfigureTokenPool coverage * test: assert zero MCMS proposals on idempotent re-apply with fresh bundle * refactor: address review feedback on ConfigureTokenPool Applies the accepted suggestions from Chris's review; the two declined items (version gate, string map key) are left in place with rationale in the PR threads. - Remove the PoolConfigUpdate.Version override field: it was unreachable (the on-chain resolver always populates the version, and the ambiguous case hard-errors before the override applied) and untested. This drops the version-override blocks and lets applyPoolConfigUpdate reuse the existing ResolveAdapterAndRefs instead of resolvePoolForConfigure. - Drop the EVM-family admin address checks from the top-level verify so the changeset stays chain-agnostic; the EVM SetTokenPoolAdmins sequence already validates the formats at apply time. - Reuse applyTokenTransferFeeConfig for per-remote fee updates instead of the duplicated applyPartialFeeConfigOnPool (also fixes disabled-lane merges to use chain-agnostic defaults rather than zeroed on-chain fields). - Move rate-limiter equality onto RateLimiterConfig.Equal in product.go. Drops the RateLimits buckets, RateLimitAdmin, scaling/apply logic, and the now-unused RateLimiterConfig.Equal helper. author: aelmanaa
message: feat: explorer source verification from chain data, and drop the unused confirmations key Verification backend is per-chain data: an optional verifier{type,url} block in config/chains/<name>.json (etherscan, blockscout, or sourcify), validated by the doctor. verify-args.sh composes the forge verifier flags per chain, so bare --verify covers the Etherscan v2 chains from the single ETHERSCAN_API_KEY, Ink and Plume verify via their Blockscout instances, and 0G via Sourcify (keyless). verify-contract.sh is the hardened standalone backfill: --watch --retries 10 --delay 10 to outlast explorer indexer lag, already-verified treated as success, Blockscout early-failure retried. make verify / make verify-args wrap the same commands; the direct forge invocations stay the documented primary path and nothing per-chain enters foundry.toml. The confirmations config key is removed end to end (config files, ChainConfig, HelperConfig, the doctor schema, the sync, fixtures): nothing ever consumed it, forge script has no confirmations flag, and the explorer-lag problem it implied is cured by verify-side retries. A config still carrying the key FAILs the doctor by name. Docs gain the verification workflow, the per-chain backend matrix, and the deterministic-deployment non-goal.

Bumping chainlink-common also requires chainlink-evm >= the commit that implements LPSkipToBlock on *Relayer (chainlink-evm#501), which in turn drags NethermindEth/juno to a version that requires tablewriter v1, breaking chainlink-ccv's CLI (still on the v0 API) and this repo's own core/cmd table rendering. author: makramkd
message: fix(commit): make observations non-blocking on stuck ops (#2193) * fix(commit): make observations non-blocking on stuck ops - Replace the free WaitForAllNoErrOperations (which ended in an unconditional wg.Wait) with a stateful asynclib.Runner whose WaitForAll returns on timeout, so one operation that ignores its context can no longer hang the whole Observation / OCR round. - Add a per-operation in-flight guard: an op whose previous invocation is still running is skipped rather than re-spawned, bounding goroutines to the number of distinct ops instead of accumulating one stuck goroutine per round. - Return only operations that completed this round; a missing result degrades to its zero value (empty), and a late result from an abandoned goroutine is discarded rather than served, so consensus never acts on stale data. * lint

message: feat(the-network-firm): add wystc endpoint for FRNT PoR feed (#5161) * feat(the-network-firm): add wystc endpoint for FRNT PoR feed (OPDATA-7669) Adds a new `wystc` endpoint to support the Wyoming Stablecoin Commission FRNT Proof-of-Reserves feed. Hits the LedgerLens real-time reserves snapshot API, scales decimal string values to uint via ×1e6 string arithmetic (float-safe), and surfaces ripcord state as a data field rather than an error condition per TNF spec. * chore: add changeset for the-network-firm wystc endpoint * refactor(the-network-firm): clean up wystc transport to match EA conventions * Updates .gitignore * fix(the-network-firm): return raw dollar value from wystc — pipeline applies 1e18 multiplier Channel definitions for TNF PoR Streams (stream 1000001903 and backed reserves) all carry multiplier 1000000000000000000 applied by the mercury-pipeline. The EA must return the raw value; pre-scaling by 1e6 was double-scaling and has been removed. * fix(the-network-firm): return totalReserves as numeric string for Streams compatibility Streams requires numeric string values. Pass the API string through directly; use Number() only for NaN validation. * fix(the-network-firm): fix TS type error — PoRProviderResponse requires numeric result The framework constrains result to number. Use Number() for result and data fields; validate with isNaN before converting. * fix(the-network-firm): disable metrics in reserve and ripcord tests for consistent snapshots reserve.test.ts and ripcord.test.ts were missing METRICS_ENABLED=false, causing meta fields to appear locally but not in CI. Matches the pattern in adapter.test.ts. * test(the-network-firm): isolate flaky uranium failure test into its own file The uranium endpoint has no input parameters, so its success and failure integration tests resolved to the same cache key. With the real background executor, a lingering success subscription could re-populate the cache after afterEach cleared it, so the failure test intermittently read a stale 200 instead of 502. Adding the wystc endpoint increased background-executor load (its unreachable host stalls the shared executor), making the pre-existing race fail frequently in CI. Move the failure case into a dedicated test file (per the finnhub split-file convention) so it runs with a fresh TestAdapter and no preceding uranium success request. Also replace the manual cache-key delete loop with the standard testAdapter.mockCache?.cache.clear(). * test(the-network-firm): add unit tests for wystc transport Export prepareRequests/parseResponse from the wystc transport (matching the hashnote convention) so the new endpoint's request building and response parsing can be unit-tested directly, and add unit tests covering the success mapping, ripcord flag, and the totalReserves/totalSupply parse-failure path.

author: winder
message: build/devenv: split protocol-contract and committee-verifier deploys (#1179) * build/devenv: add EVM ProtocolContractsDeployAdapter testing wrapper Adds an EVM implementation of the ccv ProtocolContractsDeployAdapter that proxies the chain-agnostic DeployProtocolContracts changeset to chainlink-ccip's existing DeployChainContracts EVM sequence, registered for FamilyEVM via init. This lets the changeset be exercised against a real EVM chain in devenv without first landing the adapter in chainlink-ccip, and is meant to be removed once the real implementation ships there. * build/devenv: split protocol-contract and committee-verifier deploys Phase 2 (protocol_contracts) now deploys only protocol contracts via the ccv DeployProtocolContracts changeset with deploy tunables sourced from [protocol_contracts.deploy] config, while Phase 3 (committeeccv) deploys committee verifiers via DeployCommitteeVerifier and all mock receivers (committee, CCTP, Lombard) after their resolvers exist. This replaces the chainlink-ccip kitchen-sink DeployChainContracts call so each concern is deployed in the phase that owns it, and relocates the resolver-dependent mock receivers out of the Phase-2 USDC/Lombard pool post-hook to avoid a missing-resolver failure. * build/devenv: move token-transfer config to committeeccv phase 3 Relocates ConfigureAllTokenTransfers from the protocol_contracts Phase 2 component into committeeccv Phase 3, right after the committee-verifier deploy and before lane configuration. Token pools are wired to the CommitteeVerifier resolver, which the deploy split now creates in Phase 3, so running the config in Phase 2 failed to resolve the outbound CCV ref. * build/devenv: use chainlink-ccip ProtocolContractsDeployAdapter Bump chainlink-ccip to c9b0aed and delete the local EVM ProtocolContractsDeployAdapter testing wrapper, since the real adapter now ships in chainlink-ccip and self-registers via init(). Adapt the new two-argument DeployChainContracts signature, switch env-phased.toml to the adapter feeAggregator FamilyExtras key, and document SMOKE_TEST_CONFIG for pointing tests at phased versus standard output files. * build/devenv: persist phase-3 contract addresses to env output CommitteeCCV now carries the Phase-2 CLDF accumulator forward and appends the committee-verifier and mock-receiver addresses it deploys in Phase 3, so those contracts are serialized to env-out.toml. Previously they were merged only into the stripped "_ds" datastore and dropped from the output, which broke TestE2ESmoke_TokenVerification's CCTP/Lombard receiver lookups. * Fix lint * Log which config is being used. * build/devenv: set executor deploy-time finality in phased env Bump chainlink-ccip to the version whose EVM ProtocolContractsDeployAdapter reads executor finality from FamilyExtras, and set executorBlockDepth and executorWaitForSafe in env-phased.toml so executors deploy with wait-for-safe finality. Executors validate requested finality in getFee and are never reconfigured by the lane-config changesets, so deploy time is the only place to set it, which fixes the safe-tag finality smoke test that reverted with InvalidRequestedFinality. * build/devenv: deploy CCTP/Lombard mock receivers in monolith path Route the monolith deploy through the unified DeployMockReceivers hook by emptying the inline MockReceivers in GetDeployChainContractsCfg and calling DeployMockReceivers after committee verifiers and token pools exist. The monolith previously deployed only committee receivers and skipped the CCTP and Lombard receivers, so TestE2ESmoke_TokenVerification could not resolve the cctp-primary receiver and failed. * deps: bump chainlink-ccip to 3600f66e26cd Update chainlink-ccip/chains/evm and chainlink-ccip/deployment to v0.0.0-20260618155522-3600f66e26cd in the root and devenv modules. Both modules build cleanly against the new version. * build/devenv: propagate address-registration TODO to cldf comments Add the address-registration effect TODO to the two cldf comment blocks in committeeccv that lacked it, and remove the stale scratch-path references from all four occurrences across both components. * Add changelog. * build/devenv: support per-chain and per-family family_extras overrides FamilyExtras lookup now checks the chain-selector decimal string first and falls back to the chain-family name (e.g. "evm"), so per-chain overrides can coexist with family-wide defaults in one config. Protocol contracts config schema is bumped to version 2 and env-phased.toml is updated to the nested [family_extras.evm] key form. * build/devenv: remove unused remoteSelectors from deployUSDCTokenAndPool Remove a dead `remoteSelectors` build loop left over after the CCTP mock receiver deploy was moved to Phase 3. The variable was never read and would cause a compilation failure.

message: ci(lazer): pass --locked to cargo in publisher and solana workflows (#134) Without --locked, a PR with a stale Cargo.lock silently re-resolves dependencies at CI time instead of failing, which defeats the point of committing the lockfile. cargo build-sbf does not accept --locked as a top-level flag; it only forwards arguments after `--` to the inner cargo build. author: jayantk
message: build(docker): pin Rust image builds to the committed Cargo.lock (#4004) Every Rust Dockerfile now builds with `--locked`, so an image build resolves to the dependency graph committed in the repo instead of re-resolving against crates.io at build time. The argus, quorum and Tilt dev images had no lockfile in their build context at all and synthesized a throwaway workspace manifest, so they re-resolved the whole graph on every build. `--locked` cannot be bolted onto that shape: cargo garbage-collects lock entries for workspace members that are absent from the context, which counts as a lockfile rewrite. These images now copy the real root `Cargo.toml` + `Cargo.lock` plus every workspace member and build with `-p <crate>` from `/src`, matching the shape fortuna and bulk-trade-pusher already used. Fortuna and bulk-trade-pusher move to the same shape for the same reason. apps/argus/Dockerfile was a stale copy of fortuna's from the port in #2464: it built and shipped the `fortuna` binary and pinned Rust 1.82, which no longer builds the workspace. It now builds and ships `argus` at the repo's pinned toolchain. Nothing consumes the image today - it has no CI workflow and no deployment reference - so there is no rollout concern. Dockerfile.dev's context moves from apps/pyth-lazer-pusher to the repo root so it can see the workspace lockfile; the Tiltfile's context and `only` list move with it. Bare `cargo build` there would now build the entire monorepo workspace, so it is scoped to the three binaries the image extracts. Co-authored-by: Jayant Krishnamurthy <541339+jayantk@users.noreply.github.com>

message: feat(okx-recorder): client-initiated ping keepalive with pong-timeout reconnect (PFG-1555) (#3978) OKX terminates connections idle >30s and thin pre-IPO perps have genuinely quiet stretches, so the stream client now sends a literal "ping" text frame after ping_idle_seconds (default 15) without an inbound frame and presumes the connection dead when nothing (the literal "pong" reply, or any data) arrives within pong_timeout_seconds (default 5), tearing down and reconnecting with the existing jittered backoff plus full resubscription. The ping-scheduling / pong-timeout decision logic lives in a pure KeepaliveState unit with in-file tests; recovery is observable via the new okx_recorder_keepalive_pings_total and okx_recorder_pong_timeouts_total counters alongside okx_recorder_stream_reconnects_total. The trades lane exposes okx_recorder_trades_last_seen_unix_seconds{inst_id} as a staleness signal but never gates /ready — a no-trade hour on a thin perp is data, not an outage. local_e2e_check.sh now also asserts trade rows land. Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix(okx-recorder): dispatch lane freshness on frame channel, not first row Carrying the lane identity in ParsedFrame::Data (a Channel enum set from the frame's arg.channel during parsing) restores the pre-trades-lane behavior where any bbo-tbt data frame refreshed per-instrument ToB freshness: the rows.first() dispatch skipped health.set_instrument_seen/record_tob_seen for a bbo-tbt frame with an empty data array, which could falsely flip /ready red since it gates on per-instrument ToB freshness. Health/metrics stamping now dispatches per-lane on the channel, so empty ToB frames count as ToB liveness and trades frames stamp the trades last-seen gauge. Addresses PR review feedback. message: tejas/pfg 1557 funding lane rest poller okx funding rates (#3976) * feat(okx-recorder): funding lane — REST poller -> okx_funding_rates (PFG-1557) Add a funding_client worker (mirroring hyperliquid-recorder's poller) that polls the settled funding-rate-history REST endpoint per configured instrument on a minutes-scale interval and inserts the batch directly into a new okx_funding_rates table, bypassing the websocket writer queue. - Inserts are idempotent by (inst_id, funding_time): every poll re-fetches a trailing history window and ReplacingMergeTree(ingested_at) collapses the overlap; no client-side dedupe. - Rates are Decimal(38, 18) to preserve OKX's ~17-decimal string rates. - okx_recorder_funding_last_event_unix_seconds (monotone max of settlement time) plus poll/insert metrics; funding staleness never gates /ready. - local_e2e_check.sh now asserts funding rows land and stay unique by (inst_id, funding_time) after FINAL. - Unit tests cover the REST envelope: string decimals, epoch-millis fundingTime strings, error-code envelopes, mismatched instruments. author: aditya520
message: fix(price_pusher): bound + single-flight the EVM receipt tracker (stop the getTransactionByHash leak) The EVM pusher tracked each submitted tx with a fire-and-forget `void waitForTransactionReceipt(hash)`. On the pinned viem (2.24.3) that call's timeout rejects WITHOUT tearing down its internal eth_getTransactionByHash / block-number poll, so a tx that never becomes findable leaves a detached poller running for the pod's whole lifetime -- one accumulates per push. Measured in prod: ~1,157 upstream eth_getTransactionByHash/s on Soneium (green), ~197M/day fleet-wide (Soneium, Eth, Monad, HyperEVM, ...). Replace it with a bounded, single-flight, cancellable getTransactionReceipt poll: - caps concurrent waiters at one (each push aborts the prior tracker), - stops at a deadline (default 60s) so an un-landing tx cannot poll forever, - issues ZERO eth_getTransactionByHash, - still logs "Price update successful" {hash} on landing -- even when the tracker was superseded (a confirmed receipt is never stale), so the Grafana Tx-Hash panel does not miss hashes. Receipt tracking is observational only: the re-send / nonce / gas decision is driven by a fresh getTransactionCount each cycle, not the receipt, so nothing on the hot path changes. Adds dispose() to stop the tracker for graceful shutdown. Complements deployments#5120 (eRPC hedge-off for eth_getTransactionByHash, which removes the ~3.15x amplification); this fix removes the leak at the source and covers every chain regardless of RPC routing. The two are independent. Tested with a 6-scenario simulation driving the real EvmPricePusher against an instrumented mock chain. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: jayantk
message: fix(sui): disable set_governance_data_source as stopgap for replay bug (#3809) * fix(sui): disable set_governance_data_source as stopgap for replay bug Replace the body of `pyth::set_governance_data_source::execute` with an unconditional abort so that Pyth governance data source rotation cannot fire on Sui. This kills the in-PTB replay attack against Sui Pyth governance (bug bounty report #79076 / i-bouhkykq) without requiring a V2 contract migration. The replay works because `WormholeVAAVerificationReceipt` carries only `payload`, `digest`, and `sequence` — it does not bind to the data source the VAA was verified against. An attacker who has a stale, previously-signed governance VAA (e.g. `SetDataSources`, `SetUpdateFee`, `SetStalePriceThreshold`, `SetFeeRecipient`, `ContractUpgrade`) can, in one PTB, verify both the stale VAA and a fresh `SetGovernanceDataSource` VAA against the current source, then execute the rotation receipt first. Rotating the source also overwrites `last_executed_governance_sequence` with the payload-controlled `initial_sequence`, so the stale receipt slips past the post-rotation monotonicity check and replays against the new source. A proper fix has to bind the data source to the receipt and re-check it at execute time, which under Sui's `compatible` upgrade policy can only land as an additive V2 receipt + V2 function variants (changing existing struct layout or function signatures is rejected by the package upgrade verifier). Until that V2 upgrade ships, this stopgap closes the rotation vector and makes the Sui Pyth governance emitter effectively immutable. The governance source on Sui has been stable since deployment, so disabling rotation temporarily is an acceptable cost. Notes: - Function signature is preserved (parameters underscored to silence unused-parameter warnings); this is a body-only change so the package upgrade verifier still accepts it under `compatible`. - The dispatcher in `governance.move` is unchanged and still routes the `SetGovernanceDataSource` action to `execute`; the abort happens in the callee. - Removed now-unused imports and the `GovernanceDataSource` / `from_byte_vec` helpers (private removals are allowed under `compatible`). - Added an inline regression test that verifies a `SetGovernanceDataSource` governance VAA and asserts `execute_governance_instruction` aborts with `E_GOVERNANCE_DATA_SOURCE_ROTATION_DISABLED`. The test VAA is signed by the well-known Wormhole devnet guardian; the corresponding guardian address is wired into `setup_test`. Local `sui move build` / `sui move test` could not be run in this sandbox — the project pins Sui rev `041c5f2b` (compiler 1.27.2), which requires libclang to build from source; the matching pre-built binary is not published. CI will exercise the gate. * chore: re-trigger CI Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com> --------- Co-authored-by: swe (hydra) <swe@hydra> Co-authored-by: Hydra Worker <hydra-worker@example.com> Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

message: @pythnetwork/pyth-sui-js: make SuiPythClient transport-agnostic (JSON-RPC + gRPC) (#3825) * feat(pyth-sui-js): make SuiPythClient transport-agnostic (JSON-RPC + gRPC) Upgrade @pythnetwork/pyth-sui-js to @mysten/sui v2 and refactor SuiPythClient to read exclusively through the unified `.core` API, so consumers can supply either a SuiJsonRpcClient (JSON-RPC) or a SuiGrpcClient (gRPC). @mysten/sui is now a peer dependency (^2.7.0); this is a breaking major version bump (3.0.0 -> 4.0.0). - client.ts: read pyth state, package id, price table and price-feed object ids via `provider.core.getObject` / `getDynamicField`, normalizing the JSON-RPC nested-`.fields` vs gRPC flat struct shapes. - examples/SuiRelay.ts: demonstrate both transports via a `--transport` flag and execute through the unified `provider.core` API. - README: add a v4 migration section. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix(sui): migrate in-repo consumers to @mysten/sui v2 + fix price-table DOF resolution The transport-agnostic SuiPythClient now requires a @mysten/sui v2 client exposing the unified `.core` API. Migrate the three in-repo consumers off the v1 client so they don't break at runtime against the new SDK: - price_pusher: construct `SuiJsonRpcClient` (keeps the legacy JSON-RPC methods these files use AND exposes `.core`); network inferred from the endpoint URL. - contract_manager: `SuiChain.getProvider()` returns `SuiJsonRpcClient`. - target_chains/sui/cli: type swaps + `fromB64` -> `fromBase64`. Consumers use the v2 `exports` map, so bump their tsconfig `moduleResolution` from `node` to `bundler`. Stale eslint-disable headers in the touched files are converted to the biome-ignore-all headers the repo's linter actually reads. Also fix a hot-path bug found during live validation: `getPriceTableInfo` resolved `price_info` as a plain dynamic field, but on-chain it is a dynamic *object* field (it holds a `Table`). Resolve it via the `0x2::dynamic_object_field::Wrapper<vector<u8>>` name type and read the backing table id from the field value. Validated end-to-end over BOTH JSON-RPC and gRPC (public Sui fullnode) on mainnet and testnet — identical results across transports; getBaseUpdateFee / getPackageId / getPriceFeedObjectId all resolve and the updatePriceFeeds tx builds. author: tejasbadadare
message: feat: add binance-recorder service (#3815) * feat(binance-recorder): tracer single-symbol bookTicker → ClickHouse (PFG-1108) Thinnest end-to-end slice for the new apps/binance-recorder service: connect to Binance spot via the official SDK, subscribe one symbol's bookTicker, and land rows in ClickHouse. De-risks the SDK unknowns before the rest is built. - New crate apps/binance-recorder (standalone, pinned to Rust 1.91.1), modeled on ondo-recorder/hyperliquid-recorder. - stream_client.rs: SDK→mpsc bridge. SpotWsStreams::production(cfg).connect(), per-symbol connection.book_ticker(params); the synchronous on_message callback stamps a client-side received_at, converts to BookTicker, and try_sends. The SDK owns reconnection + ping/pong keepalive (configured via reconnect_delay). - models.rs: BookTicker + from_sdk (drops rows with missing/unparseable fields) + dedupe_key((symbol, update_id)). - clickhouse.rs: direct batch insert; decimal_to_d128 rescale-with-warn helper (writes 0 on overflow rather than poisoning the batch). - config.rs: minimal tracer config (single symbol + ClickHouse target); full multi-market config lands in PFG-1109. - sql/001-init.sql: pyth_analytics.binance_book_ticker — ReplacingMergeTree, monthly partitions, ORDER BY (symbol, received_at, update_id), 90d TTL. - Unit tests for models.from_sdk / dedupe_key. Resolved SDK surface (confirmed against vendored source): - binance-sdk = "56.0.0", default-features = false, features = ["spot", "rustls-tls"] (relaxes the siblings' rust_decimal =1.37.1 pin to ^1.37.2, required by the SDK). - BookTickerResponse fields (all Option): u: i64 (update_id), s: String (symbol), b/a: String (bid/ask price), b_uppercase/a_uppercase: String (bid/ask qty). Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * feat(binance-recorder): configurable multi-market ingestion + dedupe/batch writer (PFG-1109) Widen the tracer to the full configurable market set and harden the write path by porting the batched-dedupe writer loop from the sibling recorders. - config.rs: multi-market AppConfig (markets list seeded with the 9 symbols, uppercase-normalized, empty-list rejected) plus metrics/health ports, queue and batch sizing, ready_stale_seconds, and reconnect_max_backoff_seconds. - recorder.rs: RecorderRuntime orchestration with a HashMap<(symbol,update_id)> dedupe writer loop, size/time batching, flush-with-retry/backoff, and a bounded shutdown drain. - stream_client.rs: subscribe every configured symbol on the single combined connection; a full queue increments queue_drops via try_send instead of blocking the SDK callback. - metrics.rs: write-path Prometheus metrics (queue depth/fill/drops, insert attempts/rows/latency). Health/readiness exposition lands in PFG-1110. - tests/test_config.rs: defaults, env-over-YAML, markets normalize/reject-empty, ClickHouse URL parsing. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * feat(binance-recorder): health, readiness & Prometheus metrics (PFG-1110) Port the observability surface from the sibling recorders, keyed by bare symbol since this recorder streams a single venue. - health.rs: /live + /ready on health_port; /ready is not-ready when ClickHouse is down OR every configured symbol has gone stale past ready_stale_seconds, and recovers when both clear. A silent/unlisted symbol surfaces as perpetual staleness, never a panic. - metrics.rs: add per-symbol last-seen gauge, clickhouse_up, and ready gauges alongside the existing queue/insert metrics; /metrics served from the health module. - stream_client.rs: stamp per-symbol freshness (health + metric) on receipt, so a live stream is observable even if the bounded queue later drops the row. - recorder.rs: thread HealthState through and add the periodic ClickHouse health-probe loop that refreshes the readiness gauges. - main.rs: build HealthState from the market list and start the HTTP servers; abort them on shutdown. - tests/test_health.rs: readiness flips on per-symbol staleness and on ClickHouse up/down, mirroring the siblings' test_health. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * feat(binance-recorder): local Tilt stack, Docker & docs (PFG-1111) Add the local end-to-end stack and documentation mirroring the sibling recorders: Dockerfile, Tiltfile, docker-compose.local.yml (recorder + ClickHouse + Prometheus + Grafana), provisioned Grafana datasource and Binance Recorder Overview dashboard, prometheus/alerts samples, config.sample.yml seeded with the 9 symbols, .env.sample, scripts/ local_e2e_check.sh (rows + /ready + /metrics), and a README covering the local run, config/env, and the binance_book_ticker schema. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * refactor(binance-recorder): buffer every bookTicker update, drop in-memory dedupe The writer loop kept a HashMap<(symbol, update_id), BookTicker> to dedupe, inherited from hyperliquid-recorder where L2 snapshots can legitimately repeat. bookTicker is a forward-only push stream with unique per-symbol update_ids and no replay on reconnect, so the dedupe never fires on a healthy stream — and we want every update anyway. Replace the buffer with a Vec and drop the now-unused dedupe_key plus its test. ReplacingMergeTree still absorbs insert-retry duplicates (the one real duplicate source), so idempotency is unchanged. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix(binance-recorder): make the local Docker/Tilt image buildable Surfaced while running the Tilt stack end-to-end: - No .dockerignore, so the 2 GB local target/ was shipped as build context. - Builder was rust:1.86-slim, not the validated 1.91.1 toolchain; pin rust:1.91-slim-bookworm (bookworm keeps glibc parity with the debian:bookworm-slim runtime stage). - The SDK's TLS path pulls native openssl-sys, which needs pkg-config + libssl-dev to build and libssl3 at runtime — none present in the slim images. Add them to the builder and runtime stages. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * feat(binance-recorder): record Binance USDⓈ-M futures top-of-book The seeded basket (NVDA, TSLA, SPCX, XAU, ... as <SYM>USDT) does not exist on Binance spot -- they are USDⓈ-M perpetual futures. Re-point the recorder at the futures venue and fix the issues found validating it end-to-end via Tilt: - Venue: switch the binance-sdk feature spot -> derivatives_trading_usds_futures and the stream client to DerivativesTradingUsdsFuturesWsStreams / individual_symbol_book_ticker_streams (fstream.binance.com). - Exchange time: the futures bookTicker carries an event time (E), now recorded as a new event_time column alongside the client-stamped received_at, so transport latency (received_at - event_time) is measurable. - Insert bug: the client built a database-qualified table name while already scoped via with_database, producing db.`db.table` ("table does not exist"). Pass the bare table name. - Subscribe throttle: the SDK sent all N SUBSCRIBE frames at once, tripping Binance's 5-msg/sec cap (1008 Too many requests, non-reconnectable). Space them 300 ms apart. - Default database: pyth_analytics -> default. - Docs: correct /ready semantics (every symbol must be fresh) and the dedupe note (in-memory dedupe was removed; ReplacingMergeTree absorbs insert retries). Validated locally: all 9 symbols stream, /ready=200, event_time populated, Prometheus + Grafana green. Drop the insert log to debug, and pin binance_sdk to warn in the default log filter and .env.sample so its keepalive chatter stays quiet (raise binance_sdk=info to debug the websocket client). message: fix(hyperliquid-recorder): widen L2 bid/ask decimals to Decimal128 to match prod (#3695) The L2 prod table uses Decimal(38, 12) (i.e. Decimal128) for bid and ask prices/sizes, but the wire row L2SnapshotRow had Vec<(i64, i64, u32)> (Decimal64). The clickhouse crate is strict about bit-width and rejects every insert with: schema mismatch: While processing column L2SnapshotRow.bids defined as Array(Tuple(Decimal(38, 12), Decimal(38, 12), UInt32)): attempting to (de)serialize nested ClickHouse type Decimal(38, 12) as i64 which is not compatible Widen L2SnapshotRow.bids / asks to Vec<(i128, i128, u32)> and route them through a new decimal_to_d128 helper. Keep TradeRow and FundingRateRow on i64 / decimal_to_d64 — prod's trades and funding tables are still Decimal(18, 12) (Decimal64). Bring sql/001-init.sql in line with prod: L2 columns use Decimal(38, 12), trades and funding columns use Decimal(18, 12). Backfill SQL (writes to trades) keeps toDecimal64 and Nullable(Decimal(18, 12)) since the trades table width is unchanged. Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: tejasbadadare
message: chore(hyperliquid-recorder): hardening & reliability pass for prod readiness (PFG-923) (#3691) * chore(hyperliquid-recorder): hardening pass for prod-like reliability (PFG-923) Audit pass to lift the recorder from "works on Tilt" to prod-like. Highlights: - Dockerfile: COPY Cargo.lock + rust-toolchain.toml, build with --locked, builder pinned to rust:1.91-slim, runtime aligned to debian:trixie-slim. - Shutdown drain bug fix: the post-loop flush was returning early on the already-cancelled stop token and silently dropping the last L2/trade batch. New bounded-retry drain helpers (3 attempts, exponential backoff). - Reconnect backoff now uses full jitter; trades ping loop selects on stop_token so SIGTERM is prompt; ClickHouse ping() uses GET /ping. - New hyperliquid_recorder_l2_level_parse_errors_total counter + warn so bad decimals stop disappearing silently. - Quieted info-level logs: stream throughput, per-batch insert summaries, and per-coin funding-poll lines all dropped to debug. Steady-state recorder is silent at info outside funding cycles and startup. - Replaced hand-rolled INSERT VALUES string concat with the official clickhouse crate (v0.15) over RowBinary. Dedicated wire-format Row structs + From<&DomainModel> converters; decimal_to_d64 helper for Decimal64(12); chrono DateTime<Utc> for DateTime64(3). Removes the SQL-escape hazard surface entirely. - Startup config log via derivative::Derivative with Debug="ignore" on quicknode_auth_token + clickhouse.password so secrets never reach stdout. - Dead code cleanup: drop ping_client, AppConfig::from_env, MarketSubscription::dedupe_shape, redundant trades_stream_messages counter. Delete unused alerts.sample.yml + its compose/prometheus wiring. Verified end-to-end via Tilt: /live + /ready 200, decimal roundtrip preserves negative fees and 12-decimal funding rates, no parse errors or queue drops, startup log shows full config with no secrets. Linear: https://linear.app/douro-labs/issue/PFG-923 Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * chore(hyperliquid-recorder): use clickhouse crate for ping, drop reqwest http_client ClickHouseClient's only remaining use of reqwest was the ping() impl, which issued GET /ping via a separate http client stored alongside the authenticated clickhouse::Client. Swap to self.client.query("SELECT 1").execute() so ping rides on the authenticated channel — drop the http_client field and the URL formatting boilerplate. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * Update apps/hyperliquid-recorder/src/clickhouse.rs Co-authored-by: devin-ai-integration[bot] <158243242+devin-ai-integration[bot]@users.noreply.github.com> * chore(hyperliquid-recorder): exponential backoff on CH insert retries flush_with_retry, flush_trades_with_retry, and flush_funding_with_retry all slept a fixed 1s between attempts and looped forever. A 1-hour CH outage produced 3600 error log lines and hammered CH at 1Hz the whole time. Switch to exponential backoff (1s → 2s → 4s → ... capped at reconnect_max_backoff_seconds, default 60s) and emit one info-level recovery line on the success path if attempt > 0. Each error log now carries attempt and retry_in_seconds fields so the cadence is visible in operator logs. Queue back-pressure behavior is unchanged — the stream's send_timeout(1s) still drops on saturation; this PR just stops thrashing CH during outages. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> --------- Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> Co-authored-by: devin-ai-integration[bot] <158243242+devin-ai-integration[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * feat(hyperliquid-recorder): funding-lane readiness probe (PFG-914) Extends HealthState with a per-coin last_funding_event_ms map and folds funding freshness into is_ready(). For each configured market: not-ready if no funding event has been seen and the recorder has been running >= 2x funding_poll_seconds (grace window), or if the most recent event is older than 2x the 1h funding period. HealthState construction now takes funding_poll_seconds and a stale threshold; main wires funding_poll_seconds from AppConfig and uses FUNDING_PERIOD_SECONDS * 2 (= 7200s) for the staleness threshold. The funding writer loop calls health.set_funding_event_seen per record. New test_health.rs cases cover all four readiness states: within grace without event, past grace without event, ready after first event, and unready when last event exceeds the staleness threshold. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * docs(hyperliquid-recorder): local E2E check + funding-rate docs (PFG-915) Extends scripts/local_e2e_check.sh to assert non-zero row counts across a configurable table list (CLICKHOUSE_TABLES env var, defaults to both hyperliquid_l2_snapshots and hyperliquid_funding_rates) so future tables can be added without code changes. config.sample.yml now documents the four new keys (funding_rates_table, info_api_url, funding_poll_seconds, funding_lookback_seconds) with sensible example values matching the in-code defaults. README.md adds a Funding rates bullet under Features, env-var docs for the four new HYPERLIQUID_RECORDER__* keys, and a Schema deployment subsection documenting that ensure_schema is documentation-only and DDL is applied out-of-band by the operator (the recorder credentials lack DDL permissions against ClickHouse Cloud). Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * refactor(hyperliquid-recorder): drop in-memory dedupe from funding writer ClickHouse's ReplacingMergeTree(ingested_at) collapses dupes on merge, and the 5-min funding poll is far too low-rate to need a HashMap. Replace it with a plain Vec batch. Removes FundingRateRecord::dedupe_key and its unit test. * refactor(hyperliquid-recorder): collapse funding writer loop into orchestrator Drop the mpsc channel, dedicated writer task, and queue-depth metrics from the funding lane. Funding polls run every 5 min and produce ~150 rows per cycle - the streaming-writer template (channel, 2s flush timer, 10k row threshold, fill-ratio gauges) was solving a problem this source doesn't have. - funding_client::poll_funding_once: pure poll function returning Vec<FundingRateRecord>; knows nothing about ClickHouse or health. - recorder::spawn_funding_loop: single orchestrator task owns the ticker, reqwest::Client, and backoff state across ticks; calls poll_funding_once, applies per-record metrics/health, flushes once per cycle. - Drop funding_queue_depth and funding_queue_fill_ratio metrics + the corresponding Grafana panel - the new path has no in-memory queue to observe. * Update apps/hyperliquid-recorder/src/health.rs Co-authored-by: devin-ai-integration[bot] <158243242+devin-ai-integration[bot]@users.noreply.github.com> * Update apps/hyperliquid-recorder/src/metrics.rs Co-authored-by: devin-ai-integration[bot] <158243242+devin-ai-integration[bot]@users.noreply.github.com> * refactor(hyperliquid-recorder): use run_until_cancelled in funding loop Collapse the `while !is_cancelled { tick; if is_cancelled return; ... }` pattern in `spawn_funding_loop` into a single `run_until_cancelled` wrapper. The loop body now reads as one async sequence and any future await point added inside will honor cancellation without needing a manual guard. --------- Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> Co-authored-by: devin-ai-integration[bot] <158243242+devin-ai-integration[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

author: adg-flare
message: fix(fsp): plan startup from indexed coverage The start plan probed the event anchor and ran the lookback search before reading the coverage states, so switching to a state synced node failed on history the database already held. Read the states first, skip each node read once its region is covered, and probe the block catchup starts from so a node whose history starts above the indexed range is named as such. Only a definitively missing block ends startup; a timeout or a 503 stays retryable. Coverage is the log floor alone: a fully indexed range proves coverage for the collectors that filled it, which need not have been FSP's. Warn when the events are assumed to sit in the indexed window instead, since such a database can be reindexed. Startup reads as a straight line — read the tip, the states and the epoch, plan, backfill, catch up — with the coverage predicates as methods and epoch resolution in epochs.go.

author: adg-flare
message: feat(compose): start indexer consumers only once it reports healthy v2 serves /health on 8080: 503 during the startup backfill, 200 after. author: kuco23
message: fix(core): read the back-update block vars into the right names backIndexerStats read lastEventBlock_X into `firstUnhandled` and firstUnhandledEventBlock_X into `last`, so the tuple came back reversed from what both callers assume. updateDistance then computed firstUnhandled - last + 1, which the api served as a large negative number for the whole backfill, and backIndexerSynced reported an in-progress update as synced (and a finished one as unfinished), suppressing the open-update warning on indexer startup. Also tighten backIndexerSynced to `f > l`: runHistoric leaves firstUnhandled at last + 1, and the back population keeps indexing while firstUnhandled <= last, so equality still means one block to go. author: kuco23
message: perf(indexer): narrow log fetching to the configured events EventScraper asked the node for every log in the block range and threw most of them away: EventParser drops anything whose topic is not in the configured set before it does anything else. A back-population of a single event -- the MASTER_ACCOUNT_CONTROLLER:PersonalAccountCreated run that smart-account direct mints need -- pulled the entire chain's logs to keep a handful. The scraper now builds an eth_getLogs filter from the same event-name list the parser already gets, so the two apply one predicate instead of the node sending what the client discards: topics always, from getTopicToIfaceMap's keys. Because it is exactly the parser's first test, filtering here cannot change what gets indexed. address only when every interface in the set has statically known sources. ContractLookup.eventSourceAddresses returns null otherwise, and null means "do not narrow". That null case is the load-bearing one. COLLATERAL_POOL and ERC20 sources are resolved out of agent_vault at parse time, so their address set grows as agent vaults are created -- including inside the very range being fetched, whose events an address list computed beforehand would silently drop. A contract missing from the deployment and an empty set degrade the same way, so a narrowed request is never stricter than what the parser would accept. Each EventIndexer builds its own scraper and both reindexing modes construct their indexers with separate event lists, so the back indexer gets the narrow filter and the front one keeps the wide fetch. No new flag. Measured on flare mainnet, 10 x 30-block windows: unfiltered (before) 3217 logs 1850KB 882ms/req all 136 topics 285 logs 168KB 472ms/req MAC + 1 topic (backfill) 0 logs 0KB 144ms/req Verified on coston that the topic-filtered response is the same log set the parser would have kept from the unfiltered one (126 -> 1, same order). Round-trip count is unchanged: the 30-block ceiling is the node's, and it applies to the narrow query too ("requested too many blocks ... maximum is set to 30" on both public RPCs), which is what logFetchBlockBatchSize: 29 already tracks. Raising it is not the lever; this is a per-request win. logFetchMaxFilterTopics caps filter size, defaulting to 256 -- the full set is 136, so narrowing is on everywhere -- because filter limits are RPC-side policy we do not control, and an operator whose node rejects large filters needs 0 to get the old behaviour back. Tests: the single-event reindex filter, the address union across interfaces, the bail-out for each dynamic-source interface, topic-only narrowing for the full set, the cap and the disable path, pass-through plus ordering in getLogs, and a property case asserting every configured event keeps a topic in the filter -- the invariant the whole change rests on. 84 passing. author: kuco23
message: fix(api): resolve the mint target for smart-account direct mints The DirectMint arm of EXPLORER_TRANSACTIONS hardcoded NULL as user_id for direct_minting_executed_to_smart_account, so those mints showed a blank user and were dropped entirely from any ?user= filtered listing (the user filter inner-joins evm_address on ti.user_id). The asset manager genuinely has no target to give: _mintToSmartAccounts mints to the smart account manager and emits DirectMintingExecutedToSmartAccount with only the XRPL source address. The target is resolved on the smart-accounts side, and it is a pure function of that source address — handleMintedFAssets calls getOrCreatePersonalAccount(sourceAddress) before it reads the memo, and a memo instruction cannot redirect it (MemoInstructions.execute requires userOp.sender == personalAccount). PersonalAccounts derives the address via CREATE2 from a frozen proxy bytecode constant, and registers it in exactly one place, which emits exactly one PersonalAccountCreated. So personal_account already determines the target: LEFT JOIN personal_account pa ON pa.underlying_address_id = dms.source_address_id LEFT, not inner: a PA whose creation event predates the indexed range has no row, and those mints must still appear in an unfiltered listing rather than vanish. Also add the matching arm to UNDERLYING_MINTERS, which previously only covered direct_minting_executed — hence the third bind param at the statistics.ts call site. configs/explorer.json indexed zero MASTER_ACCOUNT_CONTROLLER events, so personal_account would stay empty there. Add PersonalAccountCreated. This needs a back-population run starting at or before the MasterAccountController deploy block, not the explorer's current minEvmBlockNumber: the event fires once per PA at first creation, so any PA created before the backfill window keeps a null user permanently. Not fixed here: value_uba is still minted_amount_uba, i.e. pre-executor -fee. The PA is credited minted_amount_uba - executorFee, and executorFee exists only on the smart account manager's own DirectMintingExecuted event, which the indexer does not index yet. Noted in a comment on the union arm so the value isn't read as an accurate PA credit. Tests: five cases on the join itself (target reported, ?user= hits, unmapped PA still listed, no cross-attribution between XRPL sources, plain arm unaffected), two on underlyingMinterAddresses, and a parity block for the pre/mid-backfill window where personal_account is empty or partial — same rows, same count, same order, count == page length so a fan-out in the join would be caught. Verified the signal by reverting raw-sql.ts: the parity cases pass identically on old and new SQL, the four behavioural ones fail without the change. 238 passing. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

message: feat(metrics): expose governance posture and post-startup hash drift The resolved machine-path governance mode was invisible at runtime: a deploy that drops the [governance] block silently regresses to the legacy direct-signature path, and a node redeployed with rotated governance while the proxy runs stales Safe pre-verification — both previously surfaced only as no_authorization at the next Safe-only list activation, potentially weeks later. - governance_posture{setting=configured|safe_backed}: config-derived 0/1 gauge in the attestation_posture mold, set unconditionally at startup, plus a startup log line of the resolved mode. A startup mismatch is already a fatal refusal — this catches the same condition arising later, at the info-refresh cadence, via warning TeeProxyGovernanceHashDrift.

message: feat(collector): make the initial scan window configurable Replaces the hardcoded "const startInterval = 100 // TODO: set it" with [collector] start_interval, defaulting to 100. 0 is meaningful here — start at the last block, no backfill — so the usual "0 means default" convention would make that setting unreachable. loadConfig instead decodes into a pre-populated config.Default(): BurntSushi only assigns keys present in the file, so an absent key keeps the default while an explicit start_interval = 0 stays 0. author: GrePod
message: fix(config): reject invalid and unknown configuration keys Three ways the loader accepted input it should not: - Unknown keys were discarded silently (allowUnknownFields = true), so a misspelled is_cosigner left a cosigner deployment processing every instruction it saw. Now strict; the shipped example decodes clean. - AllowUnsafeURLs had no toml tag, and BurntSushi matches exported field names case-insensitively, so `AllowUnsafeURLs = true` in config.toml disabled SSRF protection despite the comment promising otherwise. The env override can only enable the flag, so it could not undo that. - start_interval was uint64, and BurntSushi range-checks negatives only for Uint8/16/32, so `start_interval = -1` decoded to 2^64-1 and clamped the initial scan to block 0 — a full backfill from a typo. Now int64, validated by CheckStartInterval, with the collector's window arithmetic signed throughout. Extends the example-config test from "it parses" to running the validators over it, which is what would have caught the unimplemented signer mode the example selected before 9b5d42b.
