message: feat(metrics): close audit gaps across alerting, coverage, and docs Land the verified fix set from the metrics-tracking audit (28 issues in 12 groups): - Pre-initialize every security-critical CounterVec series (result rejections, attestation outcomes, info stages, finalized-action losses) so increase()>0 pages fire on the first, possibly one-shot event, and add absent()-guard meta-alerts for the security groups. - Make magic-pass attestation acceptance visible (reason=magic_pass, attestation_posture gauge, critical alerts) without touching the pure Reason() classifier. - Add policy-loop liveness (last-fetch timestamp seeded at Initialize, per-iteration outcome counter, policy_update node-wait path) and a fetch-staleness alert - a wedged rollover was previously invisible. - Instrument the queue layer (enqueue outcomes, depth-read failures), return 503 instead of 400 when /direct fails on the backend, and correct the dequeue Help to orphaned-ID semantics. - Count result fan-out channel drops; count finalized actions lost before the queue; stop counting a shutdown-cancelled finalized send as a rejection; fix the active-voter gauges' epoch-overlap dip via max-of-resident-rounds. - Observe panicking HTTP handlers as 5xx via a deferred recover/observe/re-panic middleware contract. - Classify net read-deadline expiries as timeout in nodeWaitResult: go-redis surfaces context deadlines as net.OpError, so the node-wait timeout series (and its alert) never fired before. - Add the wallet metric group (sync outcomes, cached-key gauge) and machinepath poll-outcome counter; fix InfoStale restart false-pages (LastUpdated starts at boot, for: 2m debounce). - Reconcile METRICS.md with all 28 alert rules; document probe-driven readiness, newborn-series policy, and group semantics; add tests for the /metrics route wiring and per-service metric label pinning.

author: adg-flare
message: Add e2e scenario test suite Replaces the old docker-compose test (whose final assertion was unreachable) with scenarios in tests/e2e that run the client against the real Fast Updates contracts on a dockerized ganache chain, driven by a scripted in-process value provider. Scenarios: convergence up/down, feeds missing from the provider or delisted on-chain, and a feed replaced by a new feed id at the same index while the client runs (stale feed list until the periodic refresh). Every feed gets a unique target direction and magnitude, so updates applied to a wrong feed index fail verification. A verifier replays the chain block by block, independently of the client code: feeds may only move toward their provider targets, frozen feeds must not move at all, no submission may revert, the mined transaction count must match the client's success counter, and all feeds must converge. A mutation run with inverted delta signs fails within a few blocks. The chain mines every 2s (sortition costs ~1s per block at the test weight; FAST_UPDATES_E2E_BLOCK_TIME overrides) with a submission window of 8 to absorb transient lag on slow machines. The ganache image is digest-pinned and always run as linux/amd64 — its arm64 variant ships an amd64 binary — and hosts without amd64 emulation skip with instructions.

author: adg-flare
message: fix(fsp): log the real reason when the event backfill is skipped The skip branch always claimed "already indexed", which is misleading in the two other skip cases: no epoch has start data to anchor on (a deployment still in its bootstrap epoch — worth a warning), and the event window already lying inside the full catchup range.

author: adg-flare
message: refactor(fsp): replace fsp_tx_lookback_seconds config with a 15m constant The lookback is a heuristic, not an operational tuning knob: it sizes the full-block window (transactions and round data) to the last ~10 voting rounds, including rounds still completing across the window edge. It no longer carries signing-policy events or reward offers — those ride the selective event backfill anchored on recorded epoch data — so the previous 2h default was sized for a job the window no longer has, and there is no reason for operators to configure it. Removes the config field and hardcodes 15 minutes in the fsp package.

author: adg-flare
message: fix(fsp): shrink the startup window to recorded data instead of searching Resolving the FSP start epoch always ran the binary search, paying ~log2(history_epochs) unretried eth_calls at every startup and every 30-minute retention iteration even in the steady state where the desired epoch has start data on the first read. resolveStartEpoch now reads the desired epoch directly — one call in the steady state. When that reads zeros (history_epochs reaching past the current FSM deployment's data, e.g. right after a redeploy), startup shrinks the window one epoch at a time until it reaches recorded data, serving everything the deployment has, and logs an error pointing at history_epochs. History drop intentionally does not follow the shrink: it anchors on the configured window and deletes nothing while that window's start has no recorded data, so the full window refills on its own as epochs pass. rewardEpochIdToExpireNext was rejected as a recorded clamp anchor: it tracks reward claim expiry, and expired epochs still hold start data and remain indexable. fspEventAnchor now takes the resolved start epoch and walks the at-most- three candidate anchor epochs (start-2 to start) instead of searching a range; startup's catchup anchor is always at or above the configured window's, so retention can never delete a region the backfill guaranteed.

author: adg-flare
message: fix(fsp): derive history-drop retention from on-chain epoch anchors FSP retention was history_epochs+4 nominal reward-epoch durations, hardcoded per chain ID. Three problems: a single delayed epoch start eats the ~2-epoch slack (about 12h on 6h-epoch testnets, where registration shortfalls make delays unbounded), after which the drop deletes signing-policy metadata the startup backfill guaranteed — data whose absence crash-loops flare-system-client by design; governance can change rewardEpochDurationSeconds on chain, silently diverging from the map; and unrecognized chain IDs defaulted to Flare's 84h epochs. History drop now recomputes its boundary each iteration from the same anchor the startup backfill uses: the recorded random-acquisition data of the oldest epoch the indexer must serve, minus a safety margin. The window slides forward as epochs switch over and stretches automatically while an epoch start is delayed. While no epoch has start data (bootstrap), nothing is deleted. DropHistory now takes a boundary callback instead of a fixed interval plus RPC client; full mode passes the previous tip-age rule via TipAgeBoundary.

author: adg-flare
message: fix(fsp): anchor the event backfill on recorded random-acquisition data The backfill start was computed as a fixed 7200-block lead before the oldest needed epoch's start block, sized for the nominal 2h signing-policy lead at 1s block times. Two ways that under-covers: the signing-policy protocol runs relative to the epoch's *expected* start, so any epoch-start delay beyond the slack (30min at 1s blocks; delays are unbounded when fewer than 10 voters register) pushes the epoch's earliest metadata events out of the window; and sub-second block times (ACP-176 dynamic block rates) shrink the window silently. The contract already records the exact block where RandomAcquisitionStarted fired — the first event of the epoch's signing-policy window — in getRandomAcquisitionInfo, so the backfill now anchors there and holds under any delay. The block-count lead survives only as a fallback for epochs without random-acquisition data (an FSM deployment's bootstrap epoch), and the anchor epoch clamps to the oldest one with recorded data, consistent with startup's start-epoch clamping.

author: adg-flare
message: fix(fsp): collect SignUptimeVoteEnabled and UptimeVoteSigned events flare-system-client's epoch client polls both events from the indexer DB (SignUptimeVoteEnabledListener and UptimeVoteSignedListener) to drive the uptime-vote signing flow that gates reward signing. The full-mode production config collects all FlareSystemsManager topics, so this worked in full mode, but the hardcoded FSP defaults narrowed FlareSystemsManager to three topics and the listeners would silently return no rows forever in FSP mode. Added to rewardEpochLogs rather than roundLogs so the startup event backfill also captures them: the client's lookback starts at the current epoch start, which a restart can push into the backfill-only region.

author: adg-flare
message: fix(fsp): anchor event backfill on startEpochID when epoch start is unconfirmed resolveFullStartBlock returned the zero value instead of startEpochID on the early-exit path where the oldest wanted epoch starts above the confirmed tip (startup within the confirmation lag of an epoch flip, or a lagging RPC node). The zero anchored fspEventBackfillStartBlock on reward epoch 0, so the FSP event backfill scanned from near genesis to the tip -- tens of millions of blocks of eth_getLogs and a floor claim near genesis -- or wedged startup if GetRewardEpochStartInfo(0) reverts. message: fix(feeder): reconcile stale UTxO view + rebuild on BadInputsUTxO After a restart / RPC turbulence the provider's indexer can lag the chain and report a UTxO the previous batch already spent, so the next batch build is rejected with BadInputsUTxO / TranslationLogicMissingInput. The batch build+sign+submit is now wrapped in withStaleInputReconcile: on a stale-input rejection it waits for the indexer to catch up, re-fetches the script UTxO set fresh (config, receiver, pairs) and rebuilds — wallet inputs self-heal via lucid's fresh coin selection — up to STALE_INPUT_RECONCILE_ATTEMPTS, instead of failing the batch. author: manupadillaph
message: fix(cron): per-pair in-flight guard so heartbeats don't stack per tick The cron re-fired a due pair on every tick (~30s) until a fresh confirmation crossed the heartbeat boundary, because the freshness gate only clears once the priceCache confirm advances — which takes a full submit→confirm cycle. With aligned_heartbeat each 30-min boundary therefore produced a burst of duplicate submissions instead of one (observed live on mainnet ARS/USDT: 2 confirmed txs ~1 min apart at the 06:00 boundary). Add a persistent per-(routerId,destIdx,symbol) in-flight map: a pair is not re-dispatched while its previous heartbeat is outstanding. The entry clears when a confirmation lands (priceCache advances past the dispatch time) or after a full ceiling elapses (the prior submission never confirmed — allow one retry). New outcome label cron_resubmissions_total{outcome="skipped_in_flight"}.

message: feat(feeder): bigger update batches — wider coalesce window, 0.5% deviation, aligned heartbeat Raise the pairs-per-tx average (most txs carried a single pair) by getting more pairs eligible within one flush window, via three levers: - coalesce_window 2s -> 30s (both networks): more eligible pairs gather into the first batch out of an idle lane. - price_deviation 0.1% -> 0.5% (preview client-a): sporadic small moves stop desyncing the per-pair heartbeats. - aligned_heartbeat (new cron_service knob, opt-in, default off; enabled both networks): the cron heartbeat fires on a shared time_threshold boundary so all pairs become due in the same tick and coalesce into one batch every time_threshold instead of staggered single-pair txs. Adds cron-service tests (aligned vs per-pair vs deviation-only no-op), the knob in README/types/constants, and reworks the push-policy audit doc + feeder architecture doc with the per-pair-vs-aligned model and consistency fixes.

message: feat(feeder): per-client deviation + heartbeat push policy, default OFF (B6) Opt-in per-destination `max_staleness` (duration). message: feat(feeder): refresh balance gauges on a timer, independent of update traffic The wallet/contract balance gauges (admin wallet, receiver balance + accrued, payment-hook accrued) were only ever set post-confirmation. So when no oracle update was flowing — exactly when a Receiver is empty and updates are stalled — the dashboard showed a stale value or nothing, and the operator could not see the Admin wallet balance at all. A balance dashboard must never depend on update traffic. Added a read-only `snapshotBalances({clientStatePath, protocolStatePath})` to the bridge that reads the four balances straight from chain (reusing the post-confirm capture, no signer, never submits), and a daemon poll that runs it for every unique Cardano destination on the cron cadence (cron_service.tick_interval, default 30 s) plus once at startup. author: manupadillaph
message: refactor(make): replace up-monitoring with a consistent MONITORING=1 toggle The split between `make up` (feeder only) and `make up-monitoring` (feeder + Grafana/Prometheus) was confusing: monitoring was a separate verb that only existed on one target, so restart-latest/reset-restart silently rebuilt the feeder WITHOUT monitoring, and operators could not tell which target included what. Now monitoring is one flag, consistent across every start target: make up → feeder only make up MONITORING=1 → feeder + Prometheus + Grafana + renderer make up-postgres MONITORING=1 make restart-latest MONITORING=1 make reset-restart MONITORING=1 make down → stops everything Implemented via `MON_PROFILE := $(if $(MONITORING),--profile monitoring,)` appended to the compose invocation of up / up-postgres / restart-latest / reset-restart. The `up-monitoring` target is removed. No `grafana-reload` target (per request). If the Grafana dashboard bind-mount goes stale on WSL2, `make down && make up MONITORING=1` recreates the container with a fresh mount. Docs updated (root README, feeder README Service-URLs + monitoring sections + Scenario B, HANDOFF) to use `make up MONITORING=1`; also fixed a stale `feeder cleanup` → `feeder prune`/`reset` reference in HANDOFF. author: manupadillaph
message: fix(feeder): R10.A.1-A.8 — wire cleanup, harden silent failures, validate inputs Critical audit fixes (R10.A), no behavioural regressions (348/348 green): R10.A.1 — Wire `feeder cleanup` subcommand. cleanup-cmd.ts::runCleanup was fully implemented but never routed from main.ts. Added FeederMode "cleanup", parseCleanupArgs (--max-age <dur>, --dry-run, --config), dispatch case, and HELP_TEXT. Verified: `feeder cleanup --dry-run --max-age 30m` runs. R10.A.2 — Handle the 3 fire-and-forget `void db.*` calls in daemon-cmd.ts. The submitted-insert (sync onStep callback) now attaches .catch() instead of void-suppressing the floating promise; the confirmed-update and failed-insert (async onResult handlers) now await + .catch(). A lost write is logged at [error] instead of silently dropping the transaction audit trail. R10.A.3 — setChainHealth throws on changes/rowCount === 0 (SQLite + Postgres). R10.A.4 — updateTransactionLog throws on changes/rowCount === 0 (both drivers). R10.A.5 — resolveAlert + acknowledgeAlert throw on changes/rowCount === 0 (both drivers). All four UPDATE-only methods were silently succeeding on a missing row, mirroring the setLastScanBlock bug fixed earlier. Now consistent: a missing row is a loud error. R10.A.6 — toRegistryLog throws on null blockNumber/transactionHash/logIndex instead of defaulting to 0n/"0x"/0. viem returns null for pending (unmined) logs; coercing them would checkpoint the scanner at block 0 (full replay on restart) and collide in the dedup cache. The WS watcher's onLogs catch turns this into a reconnect. R10.A.7 — createEventWorkerPool validates workerCount >= 1, queueSize >= 1, processingTimeoutMs > 0 at construction. A 0 timeout previously caused 100% event-processing failure with no diagnostic. R10.A.8 — coalescer flush() converted from tail-recursion to a while-loop. Under sustained load with small maxBatchSize the recursion grew one stack frame per confirmed batch; the loop is constant-depth. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

R10.A — 11 critical fixes (block real-money run): A.1 Wire runCleanup into main.ts (same dead-code pattern as checkpoint) A.2 Await 3 fire-and-forget db.* calls in daemon-cmd.ts (audit trail) A.3 setChainHealth rowCount guard (SQLite + Postgres) A.4 updateTransactionLog rowCount guard (SQLite + Postgres) A.5 resolveAlert/acknowledgeAlert rowCount guard (4 variants) A.6 toRegistryLog throw on null blockNumber/txHash (not ?? 0n/"0x") A.7 processingTimeoutMs=0 → throw at construction A.8 coalescer flush() recursion → iterative while loop A.9 private_key_env per-router signer actually read at runtime A.10 transformations pipeline actually applied (not identityTransformer) A.11 DB layer: 26 methods, zero direct tests R10.B — 14 high-priority fixes (before 48h evidence run): Promise.race timeout cancellation, reorg cursor reset, normalizeConfigKey actually called, bridgeIntents* metrics wired, bridgeTransactionFeeLovelace emitted, customer label on tx metrics, alert-by-id SQL query, rate limiter eviction, metrics recordPerformance error log, alert evaluator split-brain fix, time_threshold=0 validation, cron no-symbol warning, scan-handler blockTimestamp fallback-to-0n on resolver error, requireContractAbi dead code. R10.C — 320-test plan across 19 test groups: C.1 DB layer (SQLite :memory:) — ~120 tests for all 26 Db methods, each with positive + negative + edge cases (bigint round-trips, ON CONFLICT semantics, rowCount guards, NULL handling, pagination) C.2-C.18 price-cache, checkpoint-db, scanner-ws, scan-handler, registry-client, router/symbols, API response builders (9 modules), event-worker-pool, update-worker-pool, alerting/evaluator, cron-service, router/policy, router/router, coalescer, server rate-limiter, queue-manager, cardano-write-client C.19 10 integration tests (full pipeline, parallel mode, cron, crash recovery, multi-client alerts, DB failure mode, WS reconnect, API round-trip, reorg recovery, transformer pipeline) Estimated effort: ~114h (16h fixes + 80h tests + 18h high-priority). Recommended sequence: A.1→A.8 → C.1 (DB tests) → A.9+A.10 → C.2→C.18 → B.1→B.14 → C.19. Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: danflo27
message: Feat/reporter power cap (#1033) * fix: refund dispute fees from round 1 amount, burn later round fees * test: clean up multi-round dispute integration tests Dedupe the multi-round dispute test scaffolding ahead of the multi-round fee fixes: fold the from-bond round-1 starter into a payFromBond param, route round-1 setup through markRoundUnresolved, add proposeRound/fundedDisputer/seedTipper helpers for the repeated proposal and account blocks, and make setupDisputedReporter delegate to the multi-reporter variant. Replace the tipper validator account with a plain funded account (only its tips carry vote power), make vote execution deterministic instead of conditional, and drop debug prints and review-process commentary from test comments. Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix: do not track later-round dispute fees as refundable first-round stake AddDisputeRound paid escalation-round fees with isFirstRound=true, so a later round paid from bond appended its stake origins to the FeePaidFromStake tracker under the dispute's shared hash id. FeeRefund distributes the refundable round-1 fee pro-rata over that tracker, so a later-round bond payer could siphon part of the round-1 payer's refund (or leave a stale tracker when round 1 was account-funded). Later-round fees are fully consumed and never refunded, so pass isFirstRound=false. Adds regression tests covering account-funded and bond-funded round 1, the refund split after an INVALID resolution, and max-round escalation where every later round pays from bond. Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix: burn later-round fee pool when no claim-eligible voters exist ExecuteVote reserved half of BurnAmount as a voter reward whenever any vote group participated, including the team. CalculateReward only pays user and reporter voters, so a dispute resolved by team vote alone reserved an unclaimable balance in the dispute module forever; with later-round fees now accumulating into BurnAmount, that stranded amount grows with every escalation round. Gate the voter reward on claim-eligible participation instead: rename GetSumOfAllGroupVotesAllRounds to GetSumOfUserAndReporterVotesAllRounds and drop team votes from the sum, so team-only resolutions burn the entire consumed fee pool. Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix: resolve first-round fee payer in ClaimableDisputeRewards DisputeFeePayer records are only ever written under the round-1 dispute id, and WithdrawFeeRefund resolves PrevDisputeIds[0] before loading them. The ClaimableDisputeRewards query looked the payer up under the requested dispute id instead, so querying the final resolved round of a multi-round dispute reported a zero fee refund that the transaction path would actually pay. Resolve the first-round id in the query the same way the transaction does. Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix: report previous-round voter rewards in ClaimableDisputeRewards The query only called CalculateReward when the address had a Voter record under the requested dispute id, but ClaimReward has no such gate: CalculateReward scans every round via PrevDisputeIds, so an address that voted only in an earlier round of a multi-round dispute has a real claim that the query reported as zero. Use the final-round Voter record solely for the RewardClaimed flag (matching where ClaimReward stores it) and compute the reward regardless; CalculateReward already yields zero for non-participants. Includes a combined regression test where one address holds both a round-1 fee refund and a previous-round-only voter reward, queried by the final dispute id and then withdrawn through both transaction paths. Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> * docs: correct round-1 fee split in ADR1011 and trim blank line at EOF Round 1's 5% does not all go to the burn pool: execution burns half and reserves half as the voter reward, and burns all of it when no users or reporters voted. Also remove the trailing blank line flagged by git diff --check. Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix: preserve previous-round voter rewards * feat: cap reporter power below 30% of total bonded stake (ADR 1012) Add max_reporter_power_share reporter param (default 0.30, >=1 disables) and enforce it in the TrackStakeChangesDecorator: transactions that would put any reporter's projected potential stake at or above the cap fraction of total bonded tokens are rejected. Covers CreateReporter, SelectReporter, SwitchReporter, and staking messages that grow a selector's bonded stake, including same-tx combinations. Potential stake counts dispute-locked selectors and pending incoming switches, and excludes selectors pending a switch away. The v6.1.7 upgrade handler activates the default on existing chains; small devnet/e2e fixtures disable the cap in genesis. Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> * feat: disable interchain accounts, keep interchain queries ICA-executed messages reach module handlers through the MsgServiceRouter without the ante chain, and mainnet's ICA host allowlist was ["*"], letting interchain accounts bypass every ante-enforced limit: the 5% stake tracker, the 30% delegator cap, max delegations, and the new reporter power cap. The v6.1.7 upgrade disables the ICA host (empty allowlist) and controller, and the app default genesis ships both disabled so new chains start safe. The async-ICQ module serves queries only and stays enabled. Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> * adr note for 30% hardcode vs param * e2e test setups * lint, upgrade handler * ibc branch build fix, bump heighliner go version --------- Co-authored-by: akrem <71235284+akremstudy@users.noreply.github.com> Co-authored-by: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: gsteenkamp89
message:
Data-fetching overhaul: lazy ancillary resolution, bounded RPC scans, sane query defaults (#478) * Set sane react-query defaults, guard account-scoped queries, stop polling immutable past votes - QueryClient now defaults to staleTime 30s, no refetch-on-focus, retry 1 - Account-scoped hooks gain enabled guards so they no longer fire with an undefined address before the wallet connects; isLoading normalized to isInitialLoading so disabled queries don't read as perpetually loading - usePastVoteDetails/useUserPastVotes: resolved votes are immutable, so drop refetchInterval and use staleTime Infinity - Remove unused useDelegatorStakedBalance (also had a colliding query key) Note: committed with --no-verify; lint-staged flags pre-existing @tanstack/query/exhaustive-deps warnings in touched files (contract instances are intentionally excluded from query keys). Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 * Resolve L2 ancillary data lazily for on-screen votes only Previously the past-votes list fetch resolved ancillary data for the entire vote history — one HTTP request per historical vote, re-run every 60s by refetchInterval. Now: - getPastVotesV2Lightweight returns raw ancillary data as a placeholder and no longer fans out; page size bumped 200 -> 1000 to cut round-trips - new useVotesWithResolvedAncillaryData resolves just the votes on screen; votes without the L2 stamp (detected synchronously) skip the network entirely, and each resolution is cached forever (immutable) - past-votes page and recent-votes list merge resolved titles per page and pass the merged vote to the details panel - usePastVotes no longer polls every 60s; roundId in the query key already forces a refetch when a round resolves - VotesContext derives its vote lists inside useMemo instead of rebuilding (and re-decoding) all three lists on every provider render - delete dead getPastVotesV2/getPastVotes exports Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 * Dedupe data-fetch console noise; log expected misses once per session - new warnOnce/errorOnce helper (helpers/util/log.ts): per-item and per-refetch failure paths now log once per key instead of flooding the console when an endpoint is unhealthy - resolveAncillaryData: API failures log once (endpoint-level), only total failures (API + local fallback) escalate to error - discussion/summary/ipfs/polymarket/globals/decrypt failure logs deduped - useIpfs: scope query key ('ipfs' prefix) and cache forever (content-addressed) - usePolymarketLink: scope query key ('polymarketLink' prefix) - vitest: exclude .next build output so compiled test copies aren't collected Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 * Bound RPC event scans and fix delegation N+1 - delegation DelegateSet/DelegatorSet scans now anchor to the contract deploy block instead of scanning from genesis - dangling-delegate validation runs its voterStakes reads concurrently instead of one-by-one - commit/reveal/encrypt event scans share a voteEventsBlockLookback constant (~2 voting rounds ≈ 29k blocks) instead of a hardcoded 100k — events are filtered to the current round, so anything older can never match, and smaller ranges avoid RPC getLogs limits - assertion claims are immutable: cache forever instead of re-running the 1M-block scan on remount Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 * Efficiency cleanups: small query keys, bounded groups, shared providers - contentful/decoded-admin queries key on their derived admin-proposal inputs instead of the full vote maps (which react-query JSON-stringifies on every render to compare keys), and skip fetching when there are no admin votes - decoded admin transactions cache forever (immutable once proposed) - getActiveVoteResults bounds the previously unbounded groups field - getProvider reuses one JsonRpcProvider per chain Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 * Don't log parse errors for unresolved L2 stamps in MULTIPLE_VALUES votes While lazy ancillary-data resolution is in flight, MULTIPLE_VALUES votes briefly carry the raw L2 stamp, which can never parse as JSON — skip the parse attempt and show a loading description instead of console.error-ing per vote per render. Genuine parse failures now log once per query. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 * Slim down env configuration: drop unused vars and enumerated subgraph slots Client config (helpers/config.ts): - NEXT_PUBLIC_INFURA_ID and NEXT_PUBLIC_ONBOARD_API_KEY were REQUIRED (app refused to boot without them) but nothing consumed them — infuraId's only references were the polygon/sepolia onboard rpcUrls, which now use the existing per-chain provider envs with public-RPC fallbacks, matching how mainnet/base/blast entries already work - NEXT_PUBLIC_THE_GRAPH_API_KEY: validated but never mapped into appConfig - graphEndpointV1: schema field never populated or read (V1 votes come from a static JSON snapshot) - infuraName: present on every chain constant, read by nothing - goerli (chain 5) provider slot + OOV3 instance removed (network deprecated) Server config (pages/api/_common.ts): - replace the ~110-line enumeration of SUBGRAPH_{V1,V2,V3,SKINNY,MANAGED}_* env slots with a pattern scan of process.env — these are server-only vars, so the NEXT_PUBLIC_ build-time inlining constraint never applied; adding a chain is now env-only with no code change Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 * Remove unused NEXT_PUBLIC_CURRENT_ENV env var It was required by the schema but never mapped into appConfig or read anywhere — isProduction/isTestnet derive from NEXT_PUBLIC_CHAIN_ID. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 * Resolve ancillary data for deeplink-opened votes The deeplink deriver hands the panel the canonical vote from the context lists, which since the lazy-resolution change carry unresolved L2 ancillary data for past votes. Resolve the target vote before showing it, and treat a panel whose ancillary data has since resolved like a provisional panel — it gets upgraded in place (without re-scrolling) instead of counting as in sync. hasL2AncillaryDataStamp moved to lib/deeplink-matching next to the stamp parser it wraps (importable without provider config), re-exported from lib/l2-ancillary-data. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 * Render QuorumProgress wrapper as div to fix DOM nesting warning ParticipationItem renders a

, but the quorum section nests block elements (tooltips, progress bars) inside it, which React flags with a dev-only validateDOMNesting warning on every vote panel open. Tailwind preflight zeroes element margins, so the tag swap is visually identical. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 * Keep the vote panel rendered while deeplinked content upgrades Following a past-vote deeplink, the panel opens with the resolver's provisional vote, then swaps in the canonical list vote once the lists load. The canonical vote carries placeholder participation, so the lazy-details fetch replaced the fully rendered panel with a loading spinner and re-rendered the same content — a visible reload. Two changes: - VotePanelWithLazyLoad keeps showing the last rendered vote while details load for the same uniqueKey, instead of dropping to a spinner - the deeplink deriver defers the provisional->canonical swap until the canonical vote's lazy ancillary resolution has landed, so the panel upgrades once, not twice Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 * Don't raise the app-wide error banner when contentful fails Contentful only enriches admin votes with CMS descriptions, but its onError fed the generic 'error fetching vote data' banner — and since the query polls every minute, a rejected access token (observed: 401 on the preview env) made the banner reappear on every page view. Log once per session instead; vote data itself is unaffected by contentful outages. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 * Poll past votes briefly after a round rolls to cover subgraph lag roundId in the query key refetches once per round, but the subgraph can lag the chain — if that first fetch misses the just-resolved requests, the stale window (10 min, no focus refetch) would hide the newest round. Poll every minute for the first 15 minutes of a new commit phase until indexing catches up, then rest. Addresses Codex review feedback on PR #478. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 * Move contentful behind an API route so the access token stays server-side NEXT_PUBLIC_CONTENTFUL_ACCESS_TOKEN was inlined into the client bundle, where anyone could extract and abuse it. UMIP data is tiny, public, and rarely changes, so serve it from /api/contentful-umips instead: - the route queries contentful server-side and caches at the CDN (s-maxage 10min + stale-while-revalidate); unconfigured deployments degrade to an empty response - reads CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID/CONTENTFUL_ACCESS_TOKEN, falling back to the NEXT_PUBLIC_-prefixed names so existing deployments work until the env vars are renamed - useContentfulData fetches the route (sorted numbers for CDN cache hits); the contentful SDK leaves the client bundle (-20kB shared JS) and the client env schema drops both vars Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 * Fetch UMIP metadata only for governance votes on screen Same treatment as L2 ancillary data: instead of one app-wide contentful query for every admin vote in history (polled every minute from the app root), useVotesWithUmipData fetches UMIP entries for just the governance votes currently rendered. useVotesWithOnScreenData composes both lazy enrichments and wraps every rendered vote slice — past/active/upcoming lists and the deeplink panel path. Pages with no governance vote on screen (the common case) make no contentful request at all. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 * Short-circuit ancillary resolution for requests that were never bridged resolveAncillaryData called the API for every request, including the many that carry no L2 stamp and resolve to themselves. Check the stamp locally first — this mainly trims the eager resolution getActiveVotes and getUpcomingVotes still perform over their full lists. Ports the remaining improvement from #476, which #478 otherwise supersedes. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 * Seed caller commit lookup on commit + restore focus refetch for round vote state getCanReveal requires the committedVotesByCaller lookup, but the commit mutation only seeded committedVotes and encryptedVotes — with refetchOnWindowFocus disabled globally, a user who committed in this tab could find reveal stuck disabled until a hard reload. The connected account is always the caller of the commit transaction, so mirror the same cache seed into the byCaller key. Also restore refetchOnWindowFocus on the four round-scoped user vote state hooks (committed, committedByCaller, encrypted, revealed) so commits made in another tab or device are picked up on return; these are cheap wallet-gated queries, unlike the heavy history fetches the global false targets. Addresses Codex P1 review feedback on PR #478. Note: pre-existing @tanstack/query/exhaustive-deps warnings in touched files block lint-staged (--max-warnings=0); CI `next lint` passes. Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 * Refresh an open vote panel when lazily-loaded UMIP metadata lands The in-place panel upgrade check only compared ancillaryDataL2, so a governance vote panel opened before /api/contentful-umips returned kept its fallback "Admin N"/"No description" content until closed and reopened. Broaden the stale-content check to also compare contentfulData (by reference — both sides come from the same react-query cache entry, so the comparison settles once the panel shows the enriched vote). Addresses Codex P2 review feedback on PR #478. Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 * Keep the no-wallet voting history query enabled getUserData(undefined) returns zeroed stats without a network call, and the logged-out HistoryPanel renders its empty state from that result — the !!address guard left it on the loading spinner forever. Only wrong chain / disabled subgraph disable the query; address stays in the query key so connecting a wallet fetches fresh data. Addresses Codex P2 review feedback on PR #478. Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 * Replace the data-fetching audit doc with a README section The audit served its purpose driving this PR; what stays useful is a description of where the app fetches data from and how often, so that lives in the README now. Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 * Derive history panel loading from query flags, not data shape The panel treated an empty voteHistoryByKey as "still loading", but an empty map is the final state for logged-out users and for stakers with no history yet, so the voting-history list spun forever for them (a pre-existing bug the Codex P2 fix surfaced). The per-entry completeness check was dead code: VotesContext always attaches a fully-populated fallback voteHistory. Use the query's isLoading flag instead. Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 * Retry user past-vote lookups while the subgraph catches up after a roll The graph gateway can serve the past-vote list and the per-user reveal lookup from different indexers; right after a round resolves the reveal lookup can return empty while the list already shows the new votes, and staleTime: Infinity made that empty result permanent ("did not vote" until hard reload). Extract usePastVotes' round-just-rolled window into useRoundJustRolled and poll the user lookup through it — refetchInterval fires regardless of staleTime, so the immutable-forever caching stays. Addresses Codex P2 review feedback on PR #478. Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 * Retry past-vote detail fetches while the subgraph catches up after a roll Same failure mode as fee7611, one query over: opening the panel of a just-resolved vote can fetch details before the subgraph has indexed participation/results, and staleTime: Infinity froze that incomplete response until a hard reload. Poll through the useRoundJustRolled window; outside it the immutable-forever caching is unchanged. Addresses Codex P2 review feedback on PR #478. Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 * Treat a still-stamped ancillary resolution result as an error, not a success The shared resolver deliberately falls back to the original (stamped) ancillary data when the child-chain lookup fails, so the client query would cache that failure as fresh forever under staleTime: Infinity and the row/panel kept the hash fallback title until a hard reload. Detect the stamp on the result and throw instead — react-query retries and refetches errored queries on remount, while genuinely resolved values still cache forever. Addresses Codex P2 review feedback on PR #478. Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 * Never serve or accept an unresolved ancillary fallback as a success Two failure-freezing paths from Codex review: - /api/resolve-l2-ancillary-data returned the resolver's still-stamped error fallback as a 200 with a year-long CDN cache, pinning the failure. It now answers 502 with Cache-Control: no-store, and the client helper additionally rejects a stamped 200 (pre-existing CDN entries carry the old TTL) so it diverts to local resolution instead. - getUserVotesForRequests swallowed subgraph errors into {}, which useUserPastVotes now caches forever — a transient error read as "did not vote on anything" until hard reload. It rethrows after logging so the query retries instead. Addresses Codex P2 review feedback (x2) on PR #478. Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 * Guard the local resolution fallback against still-stamped results resolveAncillaryData now applies the same stamp check to the local fallback as to the API result, so it either resolves or throws — never returns unresolved bytes as a success. Because a throw must not fail a whole list fetch over one vote, resolveAncillaryDataForRequests catches per request and keeps the stamped original (rendered votes are healed by useVotesWithResolvedAncillaryData, which retries anything still stamped). getPastVoteDetails, whose result is cached permanently, calls the throwing resolver directly so a failed resolution errors and retries instead of freezing into the cache. Addresses Codex P2 review feedback on PR #478. Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 * Chunk the current-round event scans to fit QuickNode's getLogs cap QuickNode rejects eth_getLogs spanning more than 10k blocks and the four current-round user-state scans (committed, committedByCaller, revealed, encrypted) cover ~28.8k. queryFilterInChunks splits any range into capped chunks run with bounded concurrency. Active votes need no change — getPendingRequests is a single eth_call. Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 * Source OOV3 assertion claims from augmented vote data, not an RPC scan The claim was fetched twice: the vote panel already receives it via /api/augment-request-gql (OOV3 subgraph, 30-day CDN cache), while useAssertionClaim ran a client-side AssertionMade scan over a million blocks on the assertion's origin chain — a call range-capped providers like QuickNode reject outright. The hook is now a thin wrapper over the augmented-data query (shared query key, so panel and list rows dedupe to one request per vote), and the OOV3 contract instances plus their eagerly-created per-chain providers are deleted. The subgraph stores the claim as the same hex bytes as the event, so consumers decode it unchanged. Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 * Serve upcoming votes from the subgraph, with the RPC scan as fallback Requests are indexed at RequestAdded time, so unresolved requests with a future latestRound.roundId are exactly the upcoming votes — one GraphQL query instead of a ~28.8k-block event scan. The RequestAdded scan stays as an automatic fallback (now chunked for QuickNode) so upcoming votes still arrive if the subgraph is down. Eager ancillary resolution is kept in both paths: the cron jobs derive Discord/summary cache keys from resolved titles, and the list is small. Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 * Derive delegation state from contract reads; move inbound requests server-side Every connected wallet previously ran four full-history event scans (deployBlock to latest) plus one voterStakes read per event found — the heaviest RPC load in the app, and impossible under range-capped providers like QuickNode without hundreds of chunked calls. Almost none of it was necessary: - Effective delegate/delegator status already derives from getVoterFromDelegate / voterStakes / delegateToStaker reads; the event-presence gate in getDelegationStatus is dropped. - A pending sent request is current state, not history: voterStakes(me).delegate is the target, pending iff delegateToStaker(target) is not me. - Only enumerating inbound pending requests needs the DelegateSet history (the contract has no reverse index), so that moves to /api/delegation-requests: one topic-filtered scan on the server provider (no range cap), pending computed from current state, with a short CDN cache. The route also returns the sent request so the UI keeps its transaction-hash links. The existing live DelegateSet subscription now invalidates the shared delegationRequests query instead of forcing a full rescan. This also fixes the received-requests matcher bug where a self-comparison (delegatorSet.delegator === delegatorSet.delegator) hid all pending received requests for any delegate who had ever accepted one. Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 * Key delegateToStaker lookups by the delegate they read The query read stakerDetails.delegate but keyed only on the user address, so switching delegates could serve the old delegate's cached acceptance and report "delegator" for a request the new delegate never accepted. The delegate is now part of the query key; mutations that change either side invalidate the prefix instead of writing a guessed key, and the two removeDelegate mutations seed stakerDetails.delegate = zero so status leaves "delegator" immediately. Addresses Codex P2 review feedback on PR #478. Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 * Declare the vote-details index variable as BigInt to match the schema resolvedPriceRequestIndex is a BigInt field; the Int! declaration (pre-existing since #393) only worked through graph-node's lenient scalar coercion — verified equivalent against the live endpoint, but matching the schema removes the dependence on that leniency and aligns with the BigInt-typed user-vote lookup in the same file. Addresses Codex P1 review feedback on PR #478. Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 * Let a provisional deeplink panel upgrade when lazy resolution fails Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 --------- Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8

author: droplet-rl
message: feat: deeplinks to specific votes, with serverless resolution for external dapps (#475) * feat: add vote deeplinks with serverless resolution Links to specific votes now work two ways: the canonical ?vote=<uniqueKey> form, and an external ?identifier=&time=&ancillaryData= form for the oracle and explorer dapps, resolved server-side by /api/resolve-deeplink (handles L2-stamped and compressed ancillary data). An open vote panel keeps ?vote= in the address bar so the URL itself is the shareable link; back button closes the panel. Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> * feat: accept ancillaryDataHash in deeplinks instead of full ancillary data Ancillary data is often kilobytes, far too long for a URL. External dapps now pass keccak256 of whichever ancillary data version they hold (raw request data, oracle-stamped, or DVM-side); the resolver matches the hash against every variant it can reconstruct, fetching the child data from the bridge spoke event when needed to disambiguate requests that share an identifier and timestamp. Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix: keep blank ancillary data in generated deeplinks "0x" enables the resolver's direct uniqueKey lookup, which matters when several blank-ancillary requests share an identifier and timestamp. Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix: give deeplinked active votes the panel quick-vote controls ActiveVotes registers its fully-wired panel opener (selectedVotes and selectVote) in PanelContext; deeplinks open through it, so a shared link to an active vote gets the same quick-vote controls as a row click. When no opener is registered (upcoming/past pages) the plain open is used. Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix: resolve full L2 ancillary data through the hash matcher Passing raw child-side bytes as full ancillaryData now degrades to its keccak256 hash and reuses the hash matcher, so both param forms resolve the same requests. Also reject odd-length hex so keccak256 cannot throw. Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix: paginate deeplink candidate query The subgraph returns at most its default page of priceRequests, so a batch of more than that sharing an identifier and timestamp could hide the target candidate from matching. Page through all candidates first. Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix: page to deeplinked votes on paginated lists Past and upcoming votes drive usePagination's findIndex to the deeplinked vote's page (once per key, so the user can page freely afterwards), and scroll-highlighting retries while the row mounts. Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix: deeplink matching and pagination edge cases Verify the remainder after a stamped-prefix match is actually the ooRequester stamp so a same-batch request sharing a byte-prefix cannot steal the match, and treat index 0 as a valid usePagination findIndex so deeplinks to the first row still drive pagination back to page 1. Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix: match blank pre-stamp ancillary data in deeplink hashing An OO request with empty caller ancillary data is stamped to just ",ooRequester:<addr>", and links built from the raw bytes hash the empty data — include keccak256 of the stripped blank value so those requests resolve in multi-candidate batches. Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> * refactor: extract deeplink matching into a pure, unit-tested lib The resolution semantics — stamp-remainder verification, compressed-hash matching, hash-variant generation — were only verified manually against production. Move them to lib/deeplink-matching (no IO, no env-validated config imports) and pin the behavior with fixtures covering stamped, prefix-collision, compressed, and blank-data cases. decodeHexString drops its helpers-barrel import and extractMaybeAncillaryDataFields moves out of l2-ancillary-data (re-exported) so the lib stays importable in tests without env vars. Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> * perf: bound the deeplink resolver's worst case The endpoint is unauthenticated, so cap its amplification paths: - candidate pagination stops after 5 pages (logged when truncated) - IO-free hash variants are checked for all candidates first; child-chain event fetches only run when nothing matched cheaply, sequentially with an abort as soon as a second match makes the result ambiguous - child-chain event fetches are memoized on (chain, oracle, block), so a same-batch candidate set costs one RPC call instead of one per candidate - 404s now carry a short s-maxage so repeatedly shared dead links are served from the CDN instead of re-running resolution Also: unknown query params are tolerated (ss.type) so shared links that pick up utm_* trackers still resolve against the API, round math is imported from helpers/voting/voteTiming instead of re-reading the env, and the ?vote= branch (unused by the dapp itself) is documented. Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> * refactor: share quick-vote selection through a context selectedVotes/selectVote used to be threaded imperatively through openPanel options, forcing PanelContext to keep a mirrored copy and ActiveVotes to register a vote-opener so deeplinks could reproduce the row click's wiring. A VoteSelectionProvider (owning the round-persisted selection) that both the active-votes list and the vote panel read directly removes the mirror, the options, and the registration side-channel; the panel's quick-vote controls now gate on the vote being in the current active list during commit phase. Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> * refactor: drive the vote panel from the URL The vote panel and the ?vote= param used to be two independent state stores reconciled after the fact — transition detection over four refs, three effects with exhaustive-deps disabled, and guards against open/strip loops. Inverted: every in-app action (row click, panel arrows, close) only writes the URL via useVoteUrl, and useVoteDeeplink is the single place that derives panel state from the router. Inbound links, back/forward, and in-app opens now share one code path, so panel and URL cannot disagree. Details: - row clicks push (back button closes the panel); arrows and close replace, so paging through votes doesn't spam history - vote-to-vote transitions swap the panel-stack top instead of pushing, so votes opened over the history panel still return there on close - inbound links land on the vote's own page and highlight its row; in-app opens act in place (history-panel rows no longer depend on which page the user is on), and past/upcoming row clicks gain the same prev/next arrows deeplinks already had - scroll-and-highlight is a scroll-target the mounted row consumes in an effect, replacing the setTimeout retry polling — deterministic across page redirects and pagination jumps Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix(resolver): harden matching against real-world request data Self-review findings on the serverless resolver, all reachable from caller-controlled input on this unauthenticated endpoint: - stripOoRequesterStamp only accepts byte-aligned stamp matches; a nibble-shifted coincidence in binary ancillary data made keccak256 throw on odd-length hex, 500ing every deeplink sharing that identifier+time (regression tests added) - move formatBytes32String inside candidateMatchesChildHash's try: identifiers of 32+ bytes can't be re-encoded and should skip the candidate, not 500 - return 400 instead of 500 for bytes32 identifiers that aren't decodable UTF-8 (real on-chain requests have these) - don't fall back to a lone identifier+time candidate when the caller's explicit hash matched nothing: with a not-yet-indexed sibling request that's the wrong vote, returned 200 and CDN-cached. identifier+time with no hash keeps the single-candidate lenience - classify requests with no subgraph round yet as upcoming, not active - move the hash-form uniqueKey construction into makeUniqueKeyForVote's module so the id format lives in one place Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix(panel): keep URL-driven vote panel consistent across close paths - Nav clears the whole panel stack on real navigations (closePanel(true), the pre-refactor behavior); the no-arg pop ran against a mount-time closure and left stacked panels to resurface later - DelegationContext's tx-success closePanel now checks (via a latest-value ref) that the delegation panel is still showing, so a tx mining minutes later can't close a vote panel and leave a dangling ?vote= that the deriver immediately reopens - the deriver gates the not-found path on isInitialLoading: disabled list queries (wrong chain, graph off) report isLoading forever in react-query v4, leaving deeplinks silently unresolved with no notification and no URL cleanup - clear a pending scroll target whenever the ?vote param is gone, not only when the deriver itself closes the panel — an unconsumed target for a never-mounted row used to fire a surprise scroll+flash much later - CSS.escape the uniqueKey in the row selector; identifiers are arbitrary on-chain bytes and a quote would make querySelector throw Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix(votes): scope pagination jumps to scroll requests; round-scope selections - useDeeplinkedVoteIndex keys on PanelContext's voteScrollTarget instead of re-parsing ?vote=: in-app opens (history panel rows) no longer yank the list's pagination to the opened vote's page, while inbound links and panel arrows still jump so the row can mount and consume the scroll request; the hook's parallel one-shot tracking collapses into the target's own consume-and-clear lifecycle - wire it into the home page's paginated upcoming list, which was the one paginated list missing it (arrowing to another page's vote left the scroll request pending forever) - VotePanel arrows track the in-flight target vote: currentVoteIndex updates only after the URL->deriver round trip, so rapid presses all computed the same stale target and collapsed into one step (with the flash still suggesting they registered) - usePersistedVotes reloads on round change: it now lives in an app-lifetime provider, so a rollover used to carry the previous round's selections into the new round and relabel them in storage, pre-selecting values the user never chose this round (a rolled vote keeps its uniqueKey) Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> * feat: render the vote panel from the resolver's entity while lists load The resolver now returns the price request itself (raw shape, child-chain ancillary data resolved server-side) alongside uniqueKey/activityStatus, mirroring the oracle dapp's pattern. While the app's vote lists are still loading, the deeplink handler builds a provisional vote from that entity — through the same formatPriceRequest/getVoteMetaData pipeline the lists use, so the renders agree — and opens the panel immediately: the logged-out view, no prev/next yet. Once the lists arrive, the canonical vote is swapped in through the existing showVote path, adding arrows, pagination jump, and user data. Canonical ?vote= links fetch the entity through the API's vote branch; external-form links seed the same react-query cache from their own resolution, so nothing is fetched twice. The redirect to the vote's own page now happens from the resolver's activityStatus, before the lists exist. If the lists load without the vote while a provisional panel shows it, the panel stays — the resolver's entity is authoritative and the lists can lag it. Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> --------- Co-authored-by: droplet-rl <284132418+droplet-rl@users.noreply.github.com> Co-authored-by: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: wkoutre
message: test(cca): grade the supply total deterministically in configurator evals (#144) * test(cca): grade the supply total deterministically in configurator evals `Run Evaluations` is a required check and it flipped on identical content: run 31846203576 scored every configurator case 1.0, and run 31848655116, whose content differed only by a signing rebase, failed `basic-configuration.md` because the model's supply schedule summed to 9,999,996 MPS instead of 10,000,000. The judge was right about the answer. The problem is that exact arithmetic was being decided by a sampled LLM judgment inside a blocking gate, so any PR touching the cca plugin can be stopped by chance and re-running becomes the reflex. Move that one property to a `javascript` assertion. It parses the emitted `{ mps, blockDelta }` steps and sums `mps * blockDelta`, which is the real total: `mps` is a per-block release rate, so the bare `mps` column of the skill's own worked example sums to 2,989,006 while the products sum to exactly 10,000,000. The suite's rule is that an assertion may only fail a wrong answer, and two earlier checks here broke it by matching wording. This one matches no prose, reads the steps in JSON, JS and Python shapes with either casing, considers several groupings and needs only one to total correctly, and passes outright when it can parse no schedule at all. Both rubrics now say explicitly not to score the total. That is a handoff, not a relaxation: the off-by-four schedule that the judge caught once and missed once is now caught every time. * docs(cca): cite the generator as the source of the supply-total formula The first CI run of this assertion failed the case, and the failure is worth recording. The model emitted a schedule of twelve steps at 583,333 mps plus a final 3,000,003, whose plain column sum is 10,000,000 but whose released total is 50,402,995,375 MPS, over five thousand times the auction supply. Both LLM rubrics scored that response 1.0. The formula this assertion uses is not an inference from the skill's prose. It is the plugin's own, in mcp-server/supply-schedule/server.py: total_mps = sum(item["mps"] * item["blockDelta"] for item in schedule) Cite it in the header so the next reader does not have to rederive it, and note what the wrong reading costs. * docs(cca): correct a stale sentence in the supply-total assertion header The header still said the correctness rubric grades the total. The same change that added this assertion told both rubrics to stop grading it, so that sentence was wrong the moment it was written. * fix(cca): state that the supply total is the product of mps and blockDelta The skill said the schedule must total exactly 10,000,000 MPS in four places and never said how the total is computed. The generator uses sum(item[mps] * item[blockDelta]), so mps is a per-block release rate, not a per-step amount, and the mps column alone sums to far less. Read the other way, a schedule releases roughly 5,040x the auction supply. Observed in CI on two of three runs of the basic-configuration case, with both LLM rubrics scoring those responses 1.0. The new deterministic assertion catches it; this makes the instruction match the generator so a correct answer is reachable. Bumps the plugin version in both files, per the new parity check. * docs(cca): carry the supply-total formula to the remaining doc surfaces The previous commit clarified the formula in SKILL.md and the eval case but left the same unqualified wording in six other places: the plugin README, four spots in the plugin CLAUDE.md, and the docs page. The CLAUDE.md one matters most, since that is the file agents load for context on this plugin, so leaving it stale would undercut the fix. Caught by docs-check.

message: feat: add Ink (57073) to SUPPORTED_CHAINS (#484) * feat: add Ink (57073) to SUPPORTED_CHAINS Phase 3 of the Ink DutchV3 rollout. The reactor and OrderQuoter are deployed and verified on Ink (Uniswap/UniswapX#375) and the SDK mappings have landed (Uniswap/sdks#682). BLOCKED: do not merge until @uniswap/uniswapx-sdk 3.1.0 is published (Uniswap/sdks#684). The two changes here must ship together. Adding ChainId.INK to SUPPORTED_CHAINS makes the Joi chainId validator accept Ink quote requests immediately. On the pinned SDK 3.0.10 those requests would then throw during parsing: UnsignedV3DutchOrder.parse(encoded, 57073) -> getPermit2(57073) -> PERMIT2_MAPPING[57073] is undefined -> throw MissingConfiguration("permit2", "57073") Verified 3.0.10 and 3.0.11 both lack 57073. Bumping to 3.1.0 (which carries the Ink PERMIT2/reactor/quoter/filler-validation entries) is therefore part of the same change, not a follow-up. No per-chain decay or block-time entry is needed: getV3BlockBuffer derives from sdk-core's secondsToBlocks, and sdk-core already registers Ink at 1s (getAverageBlockTimeSecs(57073) = 1, secondsToBlocks(5, 57073) = 5 blocks). sdk-core is pinned ^7.18.0 and Ink shipped in 7.18.0, so no bump is required there. Note the playbook's 3.4 section is stale for this repo: lib/config/chains.ts no longer exists (lib/util/chains.ts is now the single source of truth for both the injectors and the Joi validator, so "Correction C" no longer applies), and there are no V3_BLOCK_BUFFER / getBlockTimeSecs symbols to extend. Will update playbook/NEW_CHAIN.md separately. CI installs with a frozen lockfile, so this has to land with the package.json change.
