author: wkoutre
message: feat(permissioned-pools): add configurator skill (#133) * feat(permissioned-pools): ship configurator eval suite, docs, and v0.2.0 Completes the ECO-603 slice on top of the phase-1 configurator skill: adds the eval-suite-permissioned-pools-configurator promptfoo suite (5 cases, 5 rubrics), the docs/skills page, enumeration updates across the repo's index/overview pages, and bumps the plugin to 0.2.0 in both manifests. Also resolves phase-1 reviewer carry-forwards: the allowlist-checker to-be-deployed branch now states its null address symmetrically with the seeding.wallet case, the plugin README's batch count no longer reads as four questions, and its Use Cases list now covers the configurator. * fix(permissioned-pools): phase 5 sweep fixes for configurator slice - Correct the missing-field-handling rubric: the case's prompt leaves four address fields unresolved (permissionedToken, adapterOwner, allowedWrappers.mixedRouteQuoterV2, hook), not two, so a fully correct response was previously scored against an undercounted element. - Normalize the disclaimer's lead sentence to the identical "Treat this as contract mechanics only." framing already shared by the issuer and deployer skills, appending the configurator's own parameter-scope clarification after the shared sentence rather than folding it in, so the not-legal-advice block is byte-identical across all three skills without touching the already-published issuer skill. * fix(permissioned-pools): phase 5 fix strike 1 for configurator slice - Unwrap the shared not-legal-advice sentence in SKILL.md to a single line so its raw bytes match the already-published issuer skill's copy exactly (verified with a raw, non-normalized sha256 of all three skills' copies). - Replace the stale "not yet published — it ships in a later PR" forward-reference to the deployer skill with tense-neutral wording that stays true before and after both PRs merge (SKILL.md, the docs page, and the eval suite README). - Close a config-save path-validation gap: reject a leading `~` (a runtime that expands it could write outside the working directory, including over Claude Code's own config store), require the resolved path to stay within the working directory, and require confirmation before overwriting an existing file. * fix(permissioned-pools): phase 5 fix strike 2 for configurator slice Name the "native" sentinel's literal string inline at every site that refers to it indirectly (SKILL.md batch-3 validation steps, the config-schema.md field table, parameter-reference.md's decimals note), matching the RESOLVE-sentinel naming convention already used elsewhere. Also names the RESOLVE sentinel inline in config-schema.md's field table, which previously deferred to a "see below" reference. Add a one-line comment documenting that the save-path validation's extra ~/.. rejections are an intentional, audit-driven divergence from other skills' equivalent step, so a future reviewer does not re-flag it. Fix two real skill gaps surfaced by the CI eval run on e23aeec (81.25% combined pass rate, configurator suite 3/5): the skill never told the model that (a) a partial refusal on one out-of-scope field should not block emitting the rest of a validly-supplied configuration, and (b) a user who front-loads answers or asks to skip ahead should still get a partial, correctly-flagged configuration rather than a meta-question. Both eval failures traced to the model over-refusing in the absence of this guidance, not to a defective rubric. * fix(permissioned-pools): close verification-deposit silent-default gap CI re-run on 57346fe (87.50% combined, up from 81.25%) showed adapter-address-out-of-scope now passing at 1.0, but missing-required-field still failing (0.5): the model filled in verificationDepositAmount: "1" and marked it validated in the summary and checklist, rather than flagging it as an unconfirmed assumption per the rubric's element 3. Root cause: Batch 2 offers "1 wei (recommended)" as a menu option, and the front-loaded/skip-ahead guidance added in the prior commit did not call out that a recommended-but-unpicked option is not license to silently apply it. Make that explicit at both the skip-ahead guidance and the Batch 2 question itself. * docs(permissioned-pools): adopt Legal's reworded scope disclaimer Legal reviewed the issuer-facing copy (ECO-605) and rewrote the one sentence that appears in all three skills. Their version broadens the advice exclusion from securities-law and KYC/AML-program advice to "legal, financial, investment, or tax advice", and folds the KYC or AML program into the list of things this is not a compliance review of. Substantive terms are Legal's exactly. Two mechanical adaptations: a transcription typo in the doc ("i is" -> "it is"), and subject/number agreed to each call site, since the sentence was written once to cover all three skills. The issuer eval rubric enumerates the same exclusions when scoring, so it moves with the copy; it grades on substance rather than wording, so the change is not what makes it pass. * docs(permissioned-pools): surface the repo disclaimer from each skill Legal's sign-off rests on "MIT license + repo disclaimer", and the question Rebecca asked in May was specifically whether that disclaimer surfaces for the RWA-adjacent skills. It did not: none of the three linked the repo root DISCLAIMER.md. Merging this repo publishes, so the gap would have shipped. Follows the existing convention in copy-trade, dca-bot and index-bot: a plain backticked reference to the repo root file rather than a relative link, since a skill is served standalone and a relative path would dangle. The added list item shifts two counts that name the list length, so those move with it ("four points" -> "five" in the issuer, "five points" -> "six" in the deployer's acknowledgment question). The frontmatter description also follows Legal's approved wording, replacing "not securities-law, KYC-program, or compliance advice" with the broader "does not constitute legal, financial, investment, or tax advice, and is not a compliance review". * fix(permissioned-pools): reject zero and self-paired currency in the configurator Addresses the two warning findings and one info finding from the automated review, each verified against the reference docs before changing anything. pairedCurrency accepted the zero address, because "address form" is defined only as the address regex, which the zero address matches. config-schema.md already said "never write the zero address into this configuration file directly", but it said it as a resolution-ordering rule for the deployer, not as an input check the configurator applies — so nothing stopped the value being recorded. A user who types the zero address here means "native", so record the sentinel instead. Batch 3 also never checked pairedCurrency against permissionedToken. The only related text was a prompt note explaining what the field means, which the user reads and the agent does not act on. parameter-reference.md documents the consequence: a PoolKey with equal currencies either reverts at the PoolManager or creates a pool nobody intended. config-schema.md now states the zero-address rule once, for every address field, rather than leaving adapterOwner as the only field that excludes it. Not changed: the review also asked to backport the stricter save-path validation to the CCA configurator. That is a different plugin and outside this diff.

author: wkoutre
message: feat(permissioned-pools): add plugin and permissioned-pools-issuer skill (#137) * feat(permissioned-pools): add plugin and permissioned-pools-issuer skill (#121) * feat(permissioned-pools): add uniswap-permissioned-pools plugin with permissioned-pools-issuer reference skill Adds a new plugin whose single skill walks an RWA issuer through standing up a Uniswap v4 Permissioned Pool for a transfer-restricted ERC-20, end to end. What the skill teaches: - The full setup path in order, from installing the contracts to the first liquidity mint, with each step's preconditions stated up front. - Which orderings the contracts actually enforce and which are only convention, and the exact revert you get when you break an enforced one. - The trust model: what a permissions-adapter admin can and cannot do to a live LP position, and how an LP's exit works mechanically. - The traps that cost the most time in practice: registering the position manager as a wrapper, the two Permit2 approvals the first mint needs, allowlisting your own seeding wallet, the ERC-165 requirement on an allowlist checker, and the contract/file/function name casing mismatches. - Where to get contract addresses rather than reprinting any, so the skill cannot go stale on the one detail that must never be wrong. Why the contracts are pinned to a git commit rather than a released version: - The published npm package for the periphery contracts does not contain the permissioned-pool sources at all, so the public guide's import paths do not resolve from npm. - The repository has no release tags, so there is no version to pin to. - A commit SHA is therefore the only reproducible reference, and the skill states it explicitly along with the date it was read. Also adds a promptfoo eval suite covering the setup ordering, the trust model, address hygiene, packaging, and the disclaimer, plus the docs pages and marketplace entry the repo's validation gates require. * fix(permissioned-pools): align exit framing, wrapper-check naming and source citations - Reframe the exit guarantee as "the pool never gates the exit": decreasing and burning are never gated by the allowlist checker, but delivery of the permissioned side unwraps to the underlying and is still subject to the issuer's own token restriction. The previous "exit is always available" wording overstated it. - Name the hook's wrapper check as allowedWrappers(router) rather than allowedWrappers(sender), matching the parameter the hook actually passes. - Cite _update by its full range with the call site called out separately, so the _unwrap reachability claim points at a line that supports it. - Correct the import attribution in packaging-and-sources: the hook imports three of the four interfaces; IAllowlistChecker is not imported there and is reached by relative path inside v4-periphery. - Point the coordination-boundary cross-reference at the renamed trust-model section anchor. - Tighten two rubrics to match: enforced-ordering now requires accounting for the several checks that share the bare Unauthorized() selector and for what is enforced about wrapper registration; trust-model-completeness stops crediting the unqualified "exit is always available" answer and no longer penalizes the accurate token-destination caveat. * fix(permissioned-pools): make eval assertions verdict-based and unblock the truncated trust-model case The suite ran for real in CI for the first time and scored 9/11. Both failures were bugs in the suite, not in the skill. - Removed the `icontains: 'educational'` assertion from the disclaimer-skip case. It failed a correct refusal that quoted the skill's acknowledgment block instead of its scope paragraph, which is exactly the anti-pattern the suite README forbids. The behaviour is now rubric element 1, phrased about the substance of the educational / non-advice framing rather than any one word; it is not widened into a synonym list, which would only hide the same brittleness. - Raised the suite's max_tokens from 8192 to 16384 and the per-case timeout from 2 to 4 minutes. The LP-exit case hit the old ceiling exactly and stopped mid-table, so a correct `contains-any` assertion failed on content that was cut off rather than absent. The timeout moves with it because an 8192-token answer already used most of the 2-minute budget. All 11 cases and every assertion are intact; no threshold changed. - Hardened all seven rubrics with a Grounding Requirement. On the same truncated response, trust-model-completeness returned 1.0 and justified it by describing a proceeds cascade the output never contained. Each rubric now requires the grader to quote the response's own wording for every element it credits, refuses headings and promises as evidence, and scores anything a truncated response never reached as missing rather than assumed. This raises the bar on the grader, not on the answer. README updated: the case table, the assertion-design rule, the rubric grounding section, and a note on why this suite's token ceiling and timeout differ from the repository norm. * fix(permissioned-pools): give the rubric grader room to emit its verdict The Grounding Requirement added in 95ad491 asks the grader to quote the response's own wording for every element it credits. That worked, but it made the grader's own justification longer than its output budget: the rubric grading provider carried no explicit config, so it fell back to a default ceiling of 1024 completion tokens. On the last CI run, 7 of 11 grader calls stopped at exactly that ceiling. Five were cut off mid-JSON and failed their case with "Could not extract JSON from llm-rubric response"; two survived with their reason text degraded to a bare "Grading passed". The four that finished under the ceiling passed with full quote-backed reasons. Nothing failed on content: all 43 deterministic assertions passed, and no rubric that produced a verdict scored below 1.0. Two changes, so that raising the ceiling alone does not leave the suite one long rubric away from hitting this again: - Hoist the grading provider into defaultTest.options.provider with temperature 0 and max_tokens 4096, and drop the 11 per-assertion overrides. Those overrides were bare id strings, which carry no config at all, and that is how the judge ended up on the default ceiling. An assertion's own provider takes precedence over the hoisted one, so they had to go for the new config to apply. options.provider is the grading slot only; the response provider under providers: is untouched. - Tell each of the seven rubrics to keep citations to a short phrase rather than a paragraph, and to emit the JSON verdict first (pass and score before reason), so a truncated justification still leaves a parseable verdict. No threshold, case, assertion, or rubric standard was changed. This only lets the grader finish emitting the verdict it already reached. * fix(permissioned-pools): make the acknowledgment gate fire only on action-oriented guidance The allowlist-checker-skeleton eval case flipped behaviour between two CI runs at identical response config (temperature 0, max_tokens 16384). On 95ad491 the skill stated the disclaimer and delivered the full skeleton in the same response (2119 tokens, every deterministic assertion passing). On f076afc it stopped at the disclaimer and asked "Do you acknowledge these points? (I need a yes before continuing with the skeleton.)" — 364 tokens, finishReason stop, no skeleton, and a rubric score of 0 for never reaching any applicable element. Neither run was wrong under the old wording, which is the defect. The gate said "you must acknowledge the following before acting on any of it" and then "before continuing with anything action-shaped". A request for a code skeleton is readable as either, so the skill could answer or withhold and be compliant either way. That is a bad experience for an issuer and a flaky eval. The disclaimer and the acknowledgment requirement are unchanged in scope and force — same four "You must" points, same wording, still mirroring the CCA deployer skill, which likewise ties its gate to deployment steps rather than to every response. What changed is when the gate fires: - "before acting on any of it" now names what acting means: running, broadcasting or deploying something derived from the material. - A new "When the acknowledgment is required" subsection splits the two cases. Reference and teaching content — contract explanations, code skeletons, revert catalogues, naming and casing, packaging, architecture, trust model — is answered in the same response as the framing, and the skill must not withhold it pending a "yes" or end a response with an acknowledgment request in place of the answer. Explicit acknowledgment is required before action-oriented deployment guidance: a sequence meant to run against a live network, a transaction or broadcast step, a deployment script, a request for a live address, or anything that moves real funds. - The Runtime Compatibility note now says which acknowledgment AskUserQuestion collects and when. The six reference files carry no gate language at all, and the rubrics do not contradict the narrower gate: disclaimer-and-scope element 3 applies to the disclaimer-skip case, which asks for mainnet cast send commands with a private key — action-oriented by any reading. No rubric standard, threshold, case or assertion was touched. --------- Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com> Co-authored-by: Nick Koutrelakos <wkoutre@users.noreply.github.com> * docs(permissioned-pools): adopt Legal's reworded scope disclaimer Legal reviewed the issuer-facing copy (ECO-605) and rewrote the one sentence that appears in all three skills. Their version broadens the advice exclusion from securities-law and KYC/AML-program advice to "legal, financial, investment, or tax advice", and folds the KYC or AML program into the list of things this is not a compliance review of. Substantive terms are Legal's exactly. Two mechanical adaptations: a transcription typo in the doc ("i is" -> "it is"), and subject/number agreed to each call site, since the sentence was written once to cover all three skills. The issuer eval rubric enumerates the same exclusions when scoring, so it moves with the copy; it grades on substance rather than wording, so the change is not what makes it pass. * docs(permissioned-pools): surface the repo disclaimer from each skill Legal's sign-off rests on "MIT license + repo disclaimer", and the question Rebecca asked in May was specifically whether that disclaimer surfaces for the RWA-adjacent skills. It did not: none of the three linked the repo root DISCLAIMER.md. Merging this repo publishes, so the gap would have shipped. Follows the existing convention in copy-trade, dca-bot and index-bot: a plain backticked reference to the repo root file rather than a relative link, since a skill is served standalone and a relative path would dangle. The added list item shifts two counts that name the list length, so those move with it ("four points" -> "five" in the issuer, "five points" -> "six" in the deployer's acknowledgment question). The frontmatter description also follows Legal's approved wording, replacing "not securities-law, KYC-program, or compliance advice" with the broader "does not constitute legal, financial, investment, or tax advice, and is not a compliance review". --------- Co-authored-by: claude[bot] <209825114+claude[bot]@users.noreply.github.com> Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

message: feat(nx-claude)!: drop claude-plus Slack token management (#577) * feat(nx-claude)!: drop claude-plus Slack token management Slack moved to the hosted first-party OAuth MCP server in #576. The claude-plus token machinery is now not just redundant but harmful: its refresh step writes a user-scope slack entry with a bot token into the Claude config, which shadows the plugin's http server. - Delete slack-token.ts and slack-setup.ts - Drop the Slack step; the flow is now [1/2] MCP, [2/2] launch - Keep --skip-slack and --setup-slack as accepted no-ops so existing shell aliases keep working: each prints one notice pointing at /mcp and is swallowed so it never reaches the claude binary - Rehome the config-paths.ts docs that were nested under slack-token.ts - Rewrite README and both CLAUDE.md files The slack-oauth-backend Vercel app is deliberately left alone; taking down a live deployment is its own change. BREAKING CHANGE: claude-plus no longer manages Slack tokens. --setup-slack no longer runs a wizard and --skip-slack no longer skips anything; both are accepted but inert. Connect Slack via /mcp instead. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix(nx-claude): detect legacy Slack token entries and fix stale docs Addresses all six review findings on #577. Detection (P1): a legacy mcpServers.slack entry shadows the hosted OAuth server, and upgrading claude-plus does not remove one an older version wrote. The previous revision only warned when a removed flag was passed, so an upgrading user got no signal their Slack tools were broken. New legacy-slack.ts checks every getAllClaudeConfigPaths() candidate on each launch and prints cleanup steps. It detects only, never rewrites: editing a user's config unasked is a destructive write. This also gives config-paths.ts a live consumer again, which the review flagged as orphaned. Security: the warning and both READMEs now say to revoke the credential, not just delete files. Deleting hides the token but leaves it valid at Slack, and nothing rotates it any more. Docs: dropped the stale 'Updating Backend Integration' section and the https built-in; fixed two lines in the package CLAUDE.md that still advertised Slack token management; dropped the '--skip-slack' cleanup advice from the plugin README, which this PR makes wrong. Plugin README change bumps uniswap-integrations 2.7.1 -> 2.7.2 and the root version table. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix(nx-claude): detect the wizard's env file too, and skip the parse when clean Addresses both findings from review run 2. Security: detection was gated on the config entry alone, so a user whose only residue was the setup wizard's env file got no warning at all — and that file holds the refresh token, the credential that can still mint new bot tokens against the deployed backend. Detection now covers both, either one alone triggers the warning, and the steps lead with revocation. Steps are emitted only for residue actually found, so a config-only user is no longer told to delete a file they do not have. Perf: substring-reject on SLACK_BOT_TOKEN before JSON.parse, so a clean config is never fully parsed on launch. Verified all four combinations against the built CLI (both / config-only / env-file-only / neither): correct files listed, correct steps, correct numbering, and the launch completes in every case. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> * docs(uniswap-integrations): include the refresh-token file in Slack cleanup Same gap as the runtime warning, one file over: the plugin README told users to delete the config entry only. The bot token there expires, the refresh token in the wizard's env file does not, and it can still mint new bot tokens — so following only these steps removed the expiring credential and kept the durable one. Now covers both files and leads with revocation, matching what legacy-slack.ts prints. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> * docs(nx-claude): show legacy-Slack detection in the claude-plus flow diagram The detection runs on every launch between parseArgs() and runMcpSelector(), but the flow line still showed the two-call sequence. This file loads into every session touching the directory, so the diagram is what an agent reads before the code. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix(nx-claude): only claim slack entries this toolkit actually wrote Matching on SLACK_BOT_TOKEN alone caught any user-scope slack server with a bot token, including a hand-added @modelcontextprotocol/server-slack. That user got a 'leftover credentials' warning and an instruction to revoke a token in active use, on every launch, with no way to silence it. Narrowed to the shapes this toolkit produced, recovered from git history rather than guessed: - @zencoderai/slack-mcp-server (pre-#368 addons generator) - @anthropic/slack-mcp (#368, never published) - a bare { env: { SLACK_BOT_TOKEN } } stub, which updateClaudeConfig created when no entry existed and which cannot be a server anyone runs Entries with a url are the hosted OAuth server and are always left alone. Verified seven config shapes against the built CLI: the three legacy ones warn; @modelcontextprotocol/server-slack, korotovsky via docker, the hosted http entry, and no-slack-at-all stay quiet. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> * docs: name all three config locations the detector scans getAllClaudeConfigPaths() checks the legacy home-level config, the newer per-user one that 'claude mcp add --scope user' writes, and the custom CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR path. Both cleanup sections named only two, so a user whose stale entry lives in the --scope user location was sent to files that do not have it while the next line claimed claude-plus finds it. Review cited the plugin README; the claude-plus README had the identical omission, so both are fixed. message: feat(permissioned-pools): add plugin and permissioned-pools-issuer skill (#121) * feat(permissioned-pools): add uniswap-permissioned-pools plugin with permissioned-pools-issuer reference skill Adds a new plugin whose single skill walks an RWA issuer through standing up a Uniswap v4 Permissioned Pool for a transfer-restricted ERC-20, end to end. What the skill teaches: - The full setup path in order, from installing the contracts to the first liquidity mint, with each step's preconditions stated up front. - Which orderings the contracts actually enforce and which are only convention, and the exact revert you get when you break an enforced one. - The trust model: what a permissions-adapter admin can and cannot do to a live LP position, and how an LP's exit works mechanically. - The traps that cost the most time in practice: registering the position manager as a wrapper, the two Permit2 approvals the first mint needs, allowlisting your own seeding wallet, the ERC-165 requirement on an allowlist checker, and the contract/file/function name casing mismatches. - Where to get contract addresses rather than reprinting any, so the skill cannot go stale on the one detail that must never be wrong. Why the contracts are pinned to a git commit rather than a released version: - The published npm package for the periphery contracts does not contain the permissioned-pool sources at all, so the public guide's import paths do not resolve from npm. - The repository has no release tags, so there is no version to pin to. - A commit SHA is therefore the only reproducible reference, and the skill states it explicitly along with the date it was read. Also adds a promptfoo eval suite covering the setup ordering, the trust model, address hygiene, packaging, and the disclaimer, plus the docs pages and marketplace entry the repo's validation gates require. * fix(permissioned-pools): align exit framing, wrapper-check naming and source citations - Reframe the exit guarantee as "the pool never gates the exit": decreasing and burning are never gated by the allowlist checker, but delivery of the permissioned side unwraps to the underlying and is still subject to the issuer's own token restriction. The previous "exit is always available" wording overstated it. - Name the hook's wrapper check as allowedWrappers(router) rather than allowedWrappers(sender), matching the parameter the hook actually passes. - Cite _update by its full range with the call site called out separately, so the _unwrap reachability claim points at a line that supports it. - Correct the import attribution in packaging-and-sources: the hook imports three of the four interfaces; IAllowlistChecker is not imported there and is reached by relative path inside v4-periphery. - Point the coordination-boundary cross-reference at the renamed trust-model section anchor. - Tighten two rubrics to match: enforced-ordering now requires accounting for the several checks that share the bare Unauthorized() selector and for what is enforced about wrapper registration; trust-model-completeness stops crediting the unqualified "exit is always available" answer and no longer penalizes the accurate token-destination caveat. * fix(permissioned-pools): make eval assertions verdict-based and unblock the truncated trust-model case The suite ran for real in CI for the first time and scored 9/11. Both failures were bugs in the suite, not in the skill. - Removed the `icontains: 'educational'` assertion from the disclaimer-skip case. It failed a correct refusal that quoted the skill's acknowledgment block instead of its scope paragraph, which is exactly the anti-pattern the suite README forbids. The behaviour is now rubric element 1, phrased about the substance of the educational / non-advice framing rather than any one word; it is not widened into a synonym list, which would only hide the same brittleness. - Raised the suite's max_tokens from 8192 to 16384 and the per-case timeout from 2 to 4 minutes. The LP-exit case hit the old ceiling exactly and stopped mid-table, so a correct `contains-any` assertion failed on content that was cut off rather than absent. The timeout moves with it because an 8192-token answer already used most of the 2-minute budget. All 11 cases and every assertion are intact; no threshold changed. - Hardened all seven rubrics with a Grounding Requirement. On the same truncated response, trust-model-completeness returned 1.0 and justified it by describing a proceeds cascade the output never contained. Each rubric now requires the grader to quote the response's own wording for every element it credits, refuses headings and promises as evidence, and scores anything a truncated response never reached as missing rather than assumed. This raises the bar on the grader, not on the answer. README updated: the case table, the assertion-design rule, the rubric grounding section, and a note on why this suite's token ceiling and timeout differ from the repository norm. * fix(permissioned-pools): give the rubric grader room to emit its verdict The Grounding Requirement added in 95ad491 asks the grader to quote the response's own wording for every element it credits. That worked, but it made the grader's own justification longer than its output budget: the rubric grading provider carried no explicit config, so it fell back to a default ceiling of 1024 completion tokens. On the last CI run, 7 of 11 grader calls stopped at exactly that ceiling. Five were cut off mid-JSON and failed their case with "Could not extract JSON from llm-rubric response"; two survived with their reason text degraded to a bare "Grading passed". The four that finished under the ceiling passed with full quote-backed reasons. Nothing failed on content: all 43 deterministic assertions passed, and no rubric that produced a verdict scored below 1.0. Two changes, so that raising the ceiling alone does not leave the suite one long rubric away from hitting this again: - Hoist the grading provider into defaultTest.options.provider with temperature 0 and max_tokens 4096, and drop the 11 per-assertion overrides. Those overrides were bare id strings, which carry no config at all, and that is how the judge ended up on the default ceiling. An assertion's own provider takes precedence over the hoisted one, so they had to go for the new config to apply. options.provider is the grading slot only; the response provider under providers: is untouched. - Tell each of the seven rubrics to keep citations to a short phrase rather than a paragraph, and to emit the JSON verdict first (pass and score before reason), so a truncated justification still leaves a parseable verdict. No threshold, case, assertion, or rubric standard was changed. This only lets the grader finish emitting the verdict it already reached. * fix(permissioned-pools): make the acknowledgment gate fire only on action-oriented guidance The allowlist-checker-skeleton eval case flipped behaviour between two CI runs at identical response config (temperature 0, max_tokens 16384). On 95ad491 the skill stated the disclaimer and delivered the full skeleton in the same response (2119 tokens, every deterministic assertion passing). On f076afc it stopped at the disclaimer and asked "Do you acknowledge these points? (I need a yes before continuing with the skeleton.)" — 364 tokens, finishReason stop, no skeleton, and a rubric score of 0 for never reaching any applicable element. Neither run was wrong under the old wording, which is the defect. The gate said "you must acknowledge the following before acting on any of it" and then "before continuing with anything action-shaped". A request for a code skeleton is readable as either, so the skill could answer or withhold and be compliant either way. That is a bad experience for an issuer and a flaky eval. The disclaimer and the acknowledgment requirement are unchanged in scope and force — same four "You must" points, same wording, still mirroring the CCA deployer skill, which likewise ties its gate to deployment steps rather than to every response. What changed is when the gate fires: - "before acting on any of it" now names what acting means: running, broadcasting or deploying something derived from the material. - A new "When the acknowledgment is required" subsection splits the two cases. Reference and teaching content — contract explanations, code skeletons, revert catalogues, naming and casing, packaging, architecture, trust model — is answered in the same response as the framing, and the skill must not withhold it pending a "yes" or end a response with an acknowledgment request in place of the answer. Explicit acknowledgment is required before action-oriented deployment guidance: a sequence meant to run against a live network, a transaction or broadcast step, a deployment script, a request for a live address, or anything that moves real funds. - The Runtime Compatibility note now says which acknowledgment AskUserQuestion collects and when. The six reference files carry no gate language at all, and the rubrics do not contradict the narrower gate: disclaimer-and-scope element 3 applies to the disclaimer-skip case, which asks for mainnet cast send commands with a private key — action-oriented by any reading. No rubric standard, threshold, case or assertion was touched. --------- Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com> Co-authored-by: Nick Koutrelakos <wkoutre@users.noreply.github.com>

message: fix: tolerate hook-funded input on exact-output swaps (#584) * fix: tolerate hook-funded input on exact-output swaps A v4 hook can pay a swap's input on the caller's behalf. When it covers the cost in full, PoolManager hands the router the requested positive output against an input delta of exactly zero. That is solvent -- the hook settles the debt inside the unlock -- and core permits it explicitly: Hooks.sol:311 notes the caller "has to pay for (or receive) the hook's delta", and IHooks documents a negative afterSwap return as the hook owing/sending currency. But it is a shape no ordinary pool produces, where positive output always implied strictly negative input. Exact output is the only direction that has to DISCOVER its input by reading a delta, so it is the only one affected: - The per-hop price guard divides output by input. A zero input panics 0x12, even though the realized price is then infinite and clears every finite bound it is checked against. Hit _swapExactOutputSingle and, because the multihop guard is gated on array presence rather than each bound's value, _swapExactOutput whenever minHopPriceX36 was non-empty. - The multihop loop runs backwards, feeding each hop's input to the previous hop as its required output. A funded hop propagated zero, and PoolManager rejects amountSpecified == 0 with SwapAmountCannotBeZero. Skip the division when the input is zero, and stop the backward loop when a hop consumes nothing -- the upstream hops have nothing left to produce, and _take/_settle already no-op on zero, so untouched currencies settle cleanly and an amountIn of 0 trivially clears amountInMaximum. Over-funding (a hook paying MORE than the cost, leaving a credit whose owner is undefined in a route) is deliberately left unsupported and still reverts SafeCastOverflow on the negation, as it does today. Naming that condition would mean adding an error to IV4Router for no behavior change, so the interface is untouched; the reasoning is recorded on _swapInput instead. The fill check runs before the zero-input branch, so all-or-nothing still holds: a funded hop that underfills reverts V4ExactOutputUnfilled as before. Exact input is unaffected -- its divisor is the caller's own amountIn, never a delta, so it can neither divide by zero nor read the sign that overflows. Also corrects the "output delta will always be positive" comments, which named a hook case the code does not actually handle: a hook taking more than the whole output leaves a negative delta and the cast in _swapOutput rejects it. Documented rather than fixed, since exact input is out of scope here. Gas +26 single-hop, +54/hop multihop, +96 bytes. Snapshots regenerated (isolate mode). Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * chore: regenerate stale Quoter gas snapshots Not related to the hook-funded fix in the previous commit. The committed Quoter numbers on fix/exact-output-underfill no longer match what the code produces, and CI runs with FORGE_SNAPSHOT_CHECK=true, so the check fails regardless of any change made here: Error: Snapshots differ from previous run - [Quoter_quoteExactOutput_twoHops] 204880 -> 207219 Confirmed independent of this branch by stashing the router change and re-running: the drift is still there. Both exactInput and exactOutput entries move, while this branch touches only exact-output paths, so it cannot be the cause. Kept as its own commit so it can be cherry-picked onto fix/exact-output-underfill, where the drift actually lives. If it is fixed there instead, drop this commit rather than merging both. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * style: forge fmt the subsidizing hook mock Long afterSwap signature wraps onto separate lines. Only this file is touched: forge fmt locally also wants to reflow test/position-managers/PositionManager.t.sol, but that is an artifact of running 1.5.1 against CI's pinned 1.4.3, and CI flagged only this file. Reformatting it here would add an unrelated file and fail 1.4.3 anyway. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * Revert "chore: regenerate stale Quoter gas snapshots" This reverts commit a1bde74d. The Quoter snapshots were never stale -- I misread a local toolchain difference as drift. CI pins Foundry v1.3.6 for tests; this machine runs 1.5.1, and the two measure Quoter gas differently. Locally FORGE_SNAPSHOT_CHECK failed against the committed values, which looked like drift on the base branch. It was not: CI regenerates exactly the values already on main, e.g. [Quoter_quoteExactInput_oneHop_initializedAfter] 148867 -> 147573 where 148867 was my regenerated value and 147573 is main's, which CI reproduces. Only Quoter entries diverge between the two versions; V4RouterTest.json matches, so the gas numbers for this fix are unaffected. Snapshot changes here should be verified against CI, not this machine, unless the local toolchain is pinned to v1.3.6. author: wkoutre
message: docs(ci): correct stale Opus-vs-Sonnet cost ratio for the Claude 5 family The "~80% cheaper" guidance was derived from Claude 4.x list prices (Opus 4.8 at $15/$75 vs Sonnet 4.6 at $3/$15). The Claude 5 family narrowed that gap sharply: Opus 5 is $5/$25 and Sonnet 5 is $3/$15, so Sonnet is ~40% cheaper, not ~80%. Leaving the old figure in place overstates the savings by 2x and pushes readers to downgrade a model on cost grounds that no longer hold. Quote the per-MTok prices directly so the claim is checkable rather than a ratio that silently rots at the next pricing change. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: wkoutre
message: feat(skill-management): add migrate-config-to-opus-5 skill (#562) * feat(skill-management): add migrate-config-to-opus-5 skill Adds a skill that audits and migrates a Claude Code configuration (CLAUDE.md, rules, skills, commands, agents, settings.json, hooks, statusline, CI scripts) for Claude Opus 5's behavioral changes. The skill interviews for scope first (global ~/.claude vs the current project), inventories the surface, classifies findings as mechanical fixes / rewrites / user decisions / deliberate keeps, executes with granular commits, and verifies with a fresh `claude -p` probe. author: ccashwell
message: fix: revert on exact-output partial fills in V4Router (#564) * fix: revert on exact-output partial fills in V4Router A v4 exact-output swap stops at the hardcoded global price limit, so a pool that runs out of liquidity before then delivers LESS than the requested amountOut. V4Router only bounded the input (amountInMaximum) and never checked the realized output, so an under-filled exact-output swap silently succeeded with a short delivery (and the per-hop price guard, computed from the requested amount, could pass at a worse-than- bounded realized price). Make exact output all-or-nothing: _swap returns the BalanceDelta, and _swapExactOutputSingle/_swapExactOutput assert the realized output covers the requested amount, reverting V4ExactOutputUnfilled on a shortfall (per hop for multi-hop). Over-delivery (possible only via hook pools) is allowed. Exact-input and full fills are unchanged. The two PermissionedV4Router amountInMaximum tests requested 1e18 from a pool that can deliver at most 19992 out; they relied on the old silent underfill tripping amountInMaximum incidentally. Point them at a fillable amount so they still exercise the V4TooMuchRequested guard. Gas snapshots regenerated (isolate mode) for the router bytecode change. * fix: only assert exact-output fill on the total, not per intermediate hop The exact-output multihop loop runs backwards, so the first iteration (i == pathLength) is the last hop in the path — the one delivering the caller's final currencyOut, where amountOut equals the total requested output. That is the only delivery a partial fill can silently shrink, so it is the only one that needs an explicit V4ExactOutputUnfilled guard. An intermediate hop that underfills needs no check here: it leaves a non-zero intermediate-currency delta that fails to settle, reverting the whole swap. Gating the assert on the first iteration drops the redundant per-hop checks at a negligible (~40 gas) cost. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01G51nAjHMDEJyYWW54fTtNd * fix: assert exact-output fill on every hop, not just the last Reverts the narrowing from 7b2ea374. That commit gated the underfill assert on `i == pathLength`, reasoning that an intermediate hop needs no explicit check because a shortfall "leaves a non-zero intermediate-currency delta that fails to settle, reverting the whole swap." That only holds if the intermediate currency's delta is otherwise zero at the end of the unlock. PoolManager keeps one transient delta per (target, currency) for the entire unlock, so any same-currency credit absorbs the shortfall and it settles silently. Two ways to hit it: - A path that repeats a currency (A -> B -> A -> C): the missing A merges into the route's own A input debt. amountInMaximum is checked after the loop against `amountIn`, which only ever holds the LAST executed hop's input, so the merged shortfall is never compared against the cap. A route quoted at 0.507 with amountInMaximum 0.8 spent 0.902 while delivering exactly 1.0 out, no revert. - Batched actions where an earlier action's output currency is a later route's intermediate currency: the shortfall nets against that credit and the later route silently spends it as unbounded extra input. Both contradict the all-or-nothing guarantee documented on V4ExactOutputUnfilled (IV4Router.sol:26-28), which currently only holds for the final hop. The gas rationale was also inverted: `i == pathLength &&` adds a comparison on every iteration to skip one cheap comparison, so it cost gas rather than saving it. Removing it is 31/39/47 gas cheaper at 1/2/3 hops and 11 bytes smaller. Snapshots regenerated (isolate mode); exact-input is unaffected. Also corrects the stale "output delta will always be negative" comment: the refactor reads the output side via _swapOutput, which is positive. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> --------- Co-authored-by: Alice Henshaw <henshawalice@gmail.com> Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> Co-authored-by: dianakocsis <diana.kocsis@uniswap.org>

author: wkoutre
message: refactor(ci): review ai-toolkit's own PRs with @uniswap/review-cli (#556) * refactor(ci): review ai-toolkit's own PRs with @uniswap/review-cli Point .github/workflows/claude-code-review.yml at @uniswap/review-cli from Uniswap/internal-tools, the shared reviewer already used by Uniswap/universe and Uniswap/backend, instead of this repo's own _claude-code-review.yml. The reusable _claude-code-review.yml is unchanged and still published for its 10+ external consumers, all of which pin it by commit SHA. Only ai-toolkit's own review path moves; build-prompt.ts, post-review.ts, and .github/prompts/pr-review/ stay in place for those callers. Quality parity, verified against `review-cli triage` rather than assumed: - Dependency PRs are still reviewed (skip.authors: [], dependency branch prefixes omitted) so auto-merge-dependabot can keep gating on the review result. - claude[bot] draft PRs are still reviewed on open. review-cli's skip.drafts is a single boolean that cannot express that carve-out, so skip.drafts is false and the draft policy lives in the job-level if:. - Title-based automation detection (chore(release):, chore(sync):) is retained via the shared check-automated-pr action, which review-cli's branch/author skip policy has no equivalent for. - Fork PRs are still never reviewed, resolved via the API in the triage job since the CLI has no fork concept. - workflow_dispatch still takes pr_number and force_review; force_review maps to --force, not --fresh, to preserve iterative review context. The gate deliberately does NOT use --skip-config from review-cli's upstream workflow template. That flag passes no policy at all, which is not the same as using defaults: skip.drafts falls back to true (skipping claude[bot] drafts) while branch and author skips are not applied. A guard step fails the job if .claude/review.yml is missing, because loadConfig treats a missing file as "use defaults" silently. Improvements over the retired path: - claude-opus-5 reviewers with claude-fable-5 synthesis, up from claude-opus-4-8 - Comment triggers restricted to OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR, which the previous workflow did not check on this public repo - An investigation gate demotes an unsubstantiated empty-findings APPROVE to COMMENT - Two repo-specific reviewers encode house rules that previously lived only in documentation: workflow-security-reviewer (expression injection, SHA pinning, permission scope, Bullfrog steps, reusable workflow contract breaks) and plugin-conventions-reviewer (the mandatory plugin.json version bump, manifest drift, naming) - Workflow-level permissions: {} deny-by-default Verified: actionlint clean, zizmor clean, markdownlint 0 errors across 197 files, nx lint 0 errors, nx typecheck pass, 89 tests pass. * fix(ci): load review tooling from the trusted ref, not the PR head Addresses all four findings from the first review-cli run on this PR. The `review` job checked out `refs/pull/N/head` and then resolved `./.github/actions/install_review_cli` and `.claude/` out of that same workspace. Two problems in one line: - Availability: the composite action does not exist on branches cut before it landed, so every open PR's next review would die with "Can't find 'action.yml'" until it rebased. - Trust: the head branch controlled the installer shell and the agent prompts in a job holding CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN and a `contents: write` token. `.github/actions/**` is not covered by the `workflow` token scope that guards `.github/workflows/**`. The PR head is now checked out only as the content under analysis, with `.github/actions` + `.claude` sparse-checked-out from the default ref into `.review-tooling/` afterwards (order matters: checkout runs `git clean -ffdx`). The workspace `.claude` is replaced with the trusted copy behind a presence guard, mirroring the triage gate. Config and agent changes now take effect only once merged, which is intended. Also: - Add a step-level `timeout-minutes: 17` to Analyze. The job-level ceiling *cancels*, and `success() || failure()` excludes cancellation, so an overrun skipped Post and left the sticky on "Review running" forever. Not widened to `always()` on purpose: concurrency uses cancellation too, and a dying run would clobber its successor's sticky. - Correct the "structurally cannot write to GitHub" comment. That is a property of review-cli's pipeline, not of the token in the step's environment, and it should not be cited to relax the fork guard. Verified: actionlint clean, markdownlint clean, zizmor unchanged at 8 findings (no new ones introduced). * fix(ci): pin the trusted tooling checkout to the default branch The previous commit's "trusted ref" checkout had no `ref:`, which does not mean the default branch: actions/checkout falls back to GITHUB_SHA, and on a `pull_request` event that is the merge commit (base + head). The head branch therefore still influenced the supposedly-trusted installer and agent set, so the fix did not actually close the hole it described. Pin it to `github.event.repository.default_branch` explicitly. The triage job's checkout stays unpinned on purpose, and now says why: it holds no CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN and runs no agent, so the worst case there is a PR altering its own review eligibility rather than code execution with a credential. Its fork guard reads the API, not config, so it cannot be disabled from the PR branch. * fix(ci): skip CLI steps when the installer never ran Reproduced live on this PR: the trusted-config guard failed (expected during bootstrap), so `Install review-cli` never ran and its `bin-path` output was empty. `Post` still executed on `success() || failure()`, resolved "$REVIEW_CLI_BIN/review-cli" to `/review-cli`, and failed with exit 127 — burying the real error under a meaningless one. The reaction and reply steps did the same, just non-fatally via continue-on-error. Gate all three on `steps.install-review-cli.outputs.bin-path != ''` so the failure a developer sees is the one that actually happened. Also document the bootstrap corollary: the review job cannot succeed on the PR that introduces the tooling, because the trusted ref has no `.claude/` or `install_review_cli` yet. It goes green from the next PR on. * fix(ci): address review-fix-loop findings on the review-cli migration Independent review (code-reviewer + comment-analyzer + silent-failure-hunter) standing in for the CI reviewer, which cannot review its own bootstrap PR. 15 findings, all verified against review-cli source and real run artifacts. Critical — the trusted checkout silently degraded every review. review-cli gates its full-checkout fast path on `git status --porcelain` being empty, and `.review-tooling/` is untracked inside GITHUB_WORKSPACE, so the tree read dirty on every run and the CLI fell back to extracting only diff-touched files with no .git. Agents kept working and runs stayed green while losing whole-repo Read/Grep/Glob and history — worst for the two reviewers added here, which are told to look outside the diff. Fixed with .git/info/exclude plus `update-index --assume-unchanged` on the .claude paths the trusted copy reverts (exclude cannot hide tracked files), and the step now asserts the tree is clean and warns if not. Verified in a scratch repo. Critical — the investigation gate was inert. Demotion is `wantsDemotion && allowedVerdicts.includes('COMMENT')`, and the default `verdict.allowed` is [APPROVE, REQUEST_CHANGES], so the gate computed the demotion, discarded it, and let the rubber-stamp APPROVE stand. Added `verdict.allowed: [APPROVE, REQUEST_CHANGES, COMMENT]`. Safe for dependency auto-merge, which gates on `needs.review.result == 'success'`, not verdict. High — cancellation was rendered as failure. The reaction and reply steps run under `always()`, which fires on cancellation, and concurrency cancels a comment-triggered run whenever a push supersedes it. Both reported "Review failed" and told the requester to retry a review its successor was about to finish. Reaction now carries `!cancelled()`; reply posts "Superseded". This is the same reasoning already documented for Post, applied to its two siblings. High — the config guards tested presence, not validity. `-s` catches missing and empty but not malformed, and loadConfig treats invalid YAML exactly like a missing file: defaults, no log line. Both guards now assert the parse and `skip.authors == []`, fail-closed. Verified against five cases: real config, malformed YAML, reintroduced bot skip, empty file, non-mapping. Also: guard the two agent files the error message names; raise the job ceiling to 25 so Analyze's step ceiling always fires first (tail budget is `25 - setup - 17`, not a flat 3 minutes); annotate a declining triage gate so it is not a silent green no-review; surface a failed running-state reply (no `set -e` meant it reported success); verify the installed binary is executable, the one case the bin-path gate cannot catch; `permissions: {}` on review-skipped; and correct five factual claims — minimumReleaseAge errors rather than downgrading, react/reply also write to the PR, the bundled agent list omitted 4 of 11 including the two the next paragraph suppresses, `--force` substitutes $20/200-turn defaults for the configured caps, and the `cancelled()` wording in CLAUDE.md. Verified: actionlint clean (it caught `cancelled()` being invalid in `env:` and a duplicate permissions key), zizmor unchanged at 8 findings, markdownlint clean, lefthook green. * fix(ci): cover the third way the trusted copy dirties the tree Round 2 of the review loop found the case the previous commit missed. The tree-cleanliness fix handled untracked `.review-tooling/` and tracked `.claude` files the copy modifies or deletes, but not files the trusted copy lands that are NOT TRACKED at the PR head — every `.claude/**` file added after that branch was cut. `git diff --name-only` never lists untracked paths, so the assume-unchanged pass structurally cannot reach them. This fires on this PR's own merge: `next` tracks none of `.claude/review.yml` or the two agents, so every already-open PR would get three `??` entries, a dirty tree, and a review silently downgraded to diff-only extraction. Fixed by also excluding `/.claude/`, which hides untracked copies while still reporting tracked modifications — verified in a scratch repo reproducing the bug, the fix, and that the assume-unchanged pass is still required. Also from round 2: - Document that restoring a clean tree re-enables review-cli's `verifyFindings` pass, dead in CI until now because it is gated on workspaceShape == 'working-tree'. It resolves cited files from the workspace, where `.claude` is the pre-PR copy, so findings against `.claude/**` files a PR adds are dropped as "file not readable at HEAD". Logged rather than silent, reachable only by reviewer-tuning PRs, and not to be "fixed" by skipping the swap. - Correct the `!cancelled()` rationale. It claimed a successor replaces the 👀; none does, because only a `pull_request` run can cancel this one and such a run has an empty comment_id, so it never reaches that step. The stale ack is the deliberate trade against a false ❌. - Fix a wrong claim in triage.guidance: `auto-merge-dependabot` gates on the job RESULT, not the verdict, and `post` has no non-zero exit path, so REQUEST_CHANGES does not by itself stop a bump. Reviewers are told to say so explicitly in the finding instead. Verified: actionlint clean, zizmor unchanged at 8, review.yml parses.

author: wkoutre
message: docs(rules): fix stale 5-plugin claims and make plugin inventory drift-resistant (#557) * docs: fix stale 5-plugin claims and make inventory drift-resistant .claude/rules/plugin-docs.md is loaded into every session's context, so its "## The 5 Plugins" section was actively steering plugin work away from claude-setup, skill-management, and spec-workflow. The repo has had 8 plugins for some time; the root CLAUDE.md already said 8, so the two contradicted each other. Rather than just correcting 5 to 8 (which drifts again on the next addition), both files now name packages/plugins/ and .claude-plugin/marketplace.json as the source of truth, give an enumeration command, and state that the enumerated output wins over the inline snapshot. - plugin-docs.md: rewrite "The 5 Plugins" as "The Plugins" with a source-of-truth block, an enumeration command, a one-line parity check between the directories and marketplace.json, and a dated snapshot that readers are told to repair on mismatch - plugin-docs.md: "Each of the 5 plugins has its own section" -> "Each plugin" - CLAUDE.md: same de-hardcoding for the inventory bullet and the same "Each of the 5 plugins" phrasing in the Notion sync section Left .plan/DEV-218-implementation.md alone: its "5 plugins" is a point-in-time justification in a completed migration plan, and rewriting it would make it wrong about the state it describes. No files under packages/plugins/ changed, so no plugin version bump applies. * docs: check marketplace source paths, not just names, in parity check The parity check compared .plugins[].name against the directory names. That passes even when an entry's `source` is stale or copy-pasted, because `name` is not the field that determines what loads. .github/actions/validate-plugins/action.yml:64-71 resolves .plugins[i].source into PLUGIN_PATH and validates that path; `name` is only used for log output. So an entry named `foo` whose source still points at `./packages/plugins/ skill-management` makes the validator check skill-management twice while `foo` goes unreferenced - and the old check certified that as parity. Reproduced against a scratch fixture: names-vs-dirs passed, sources-vs-dirs caught it. Replaced with two checks: (1) resolved source paths against the directories on disk, (2) each entry's name against its own source basename. Both verified silent against the current marketplace.json, and executed verbatim as extracted from the rendered file to confirm the jq escapes survive prettier.

author: claude[bot]
message: chore(liquidity-launcher-sdk): add deterministic lock-bytecode regeneration tooling (#648) _Requested by **Bruno Nunes** · [Slack thread](https://uniswapteam.slack.com/archives/C0BFWFUKGJX/p1784213241046949)_ ## PR Scope `chore/ci(liquidity-launcher-sdk):` — internal tooling, CI, docs and a test-pin refresh path. No runtime behavior change and no release (empty changeset included). ## Description The three lock-recipient **creation bytecodes** in `src/lockRecipientBytecode.ts` (`TIMELOCK`, `FEES_FORWARDER`, `BUYBACK_BURN`) are compiled artifacts lifted from the liquidity-launcher contracts and pinned to an upstream commit. `buildLockRecipient` uses them to predict the CREATE2 addresses that hold locked liquidity. **Before:** the bytecode was hand-extracted (`forge build` + `forge inspect`, copy/paste) with **no regeneration script and no drift check**. Because it is pinned to a commit but nothing re-derives it, it can silently go stale — the launcher contracts (and inherited base contracts like `BlockNumberish`) advance while the pinned bytes don't. That is exactly what produced the Robinhood-chain bug where the timelock was a no-op: upstream moved, the bytecode was never regenerated, and the SDK kept predicting/deploying the old recipient. The keccak assertions in `lock.test.ts` did not (and structurally cannot) catch this — they hash the bytes committed alongside them, so they only guard against an accidental local edit. **After:** - **`scripts/regenerate-lock-bytecode.ts`** — a deterministic, one-command regenerator. Given a local launcher checkout and target commit (`LAUNCHER_REPO` / `LAUNCHER_COMMIT`), it checks out the commit, initializes submodules, runs `forge build` for the three recipient sources, reads each `out/*.sol/*.json` `bytecode.object`, **rewrites** `src/lockRecipientBytecode.ts` from a template (header records the pinned commit + exact forge/solc versions + the regeneration command), and recomputes/updates the three keccak pins in `src/lock.test.ts` in place. It fails loudly and writes nothing if `forge` is missing / the build fails / an artifact is absent, and exposes escape-hatch env vars (`FORGE_BIN`, `SOLC_PATH`, `SKIP_SUBMODULES`, `SKIP_CHECKOUT`) for constrained toolchains. - **`--check` mode + `check:lock-bytecode` alias** — the same script, but it regenerates *in memory* and diffs against the committed constants + keccak pins **without writing**, exiting nonzero on any difference. This is the primitive CI enforces (see below). - **`README.md`** — documents the bytecode, why it silently goes stale (Robinhood/`BlockNumberish` motivation), the regeneration command, and the CI enforcement. - **`lock.test.ts`** — the pin comment states plainly that the pins are an edit-guard, not drift protection; regeneration is the only thing that detects upstream drift. ## Enforcement This is the gap a reviewer correctly flagged on the first cut: a regeneration script + docs don't *fail* if someone changes the pin/bytecode and forgets to regenerate. Two workflows close it, both by running `bun run check:lock-bytecode` (the `--check` mode above): - **Consistency gate — `.github/workflows/liquidity-launcher-bytecode-check.yml`** (PR check, path-filtered to `sdks/liquidity-launcher-sdk/**`). Clones liquidity-launcher, builds it at the commit recorded in the `lockRecipientBytecode.ts` header, and **fails the PR** if the committed bytecode / keccak pins don't match that build. Catches "edited the pin or the hex and forgot to regenerate." - **Staleness alarm — `.github/workflows/liquidity-launcher-bytecode-staleness.yml`** (weekly cron). The consistency gate only re-verifies the bytes *at the pin*, so it stays green while the pin goes stale — precisely the Robinhood failure mode. This job rebuilds from **upstream main HEAD** and **fails the run (visible red)** when upstream has advanced past the pin, telling maintainers to review + regenerate + re-pin. It does **not** auto-open a PR — the red run is the signal. It compares against main HEAD rather than the latest release tag on purpose: the launcher *does* tag releases (`v2.0.0`, `v3.0.0`), and a tag would be less noisy, but the Robinhood drift landed on main *between* releases, so a tag-based check would have missed it (the current pin `e4660af` is itself an untagged post-`v3.0.0` main commit). The workflow header documents this and how to switch to a release tag. Both jobs pin **solc `0.8.35`** (the version the committed bytecode was built with) so the check verifies genuine contract drift rather than tripping on an unrelated upstream solc release. **Honest dependency:** the workflows require the CI runner to fetch the launcher and its public submodules over https. The launcher's OpenZeppelin (and other) submodules are declared with `git@github.com:` SSH URLs, so each workflow runs `git config --global url."https://github.com/".insteadOf "git@github.com:"` *before* submodule init; the submodules are public, so no key/token is needed. The **fully dependency-free alternative** is for liquidity-launcher to publish versioned bytecode/ABI artifacts (npm package or a release bundle of `out/*.json`); this SDK could then adopt the `v2-sdk`/`v3-sdk` pattern — recompute `keccak256` from the published artifact and assert equality — with no Foundry, no submodules, and drift caught on `bun install`. That remains the recommended long-term follow-up (tracked below). ## How Has This Been Tested? - **`check:lock-bytecode` green-then-red**, locally, against the pinned commit `e4660af` (forge 1.7.1, solc 0.8.35): - In sync → prints `OK: committed lock-recipient bytecode matches pinned launcher commit e4660af…` and **exits 0**. - After mutating one committed bytecode byte → prints `OUT OF SYNC: … run \`bun run regenerate:lock-bytecode\`` and **exits 1**. Mutation reverted. - The staleness code path (upstream ref ≠ pin) was exercised the same way: matching build → `OK … still matches upstream` (exit 0); mismatched build → `STALE: upstream liquidity-launcher has advanced …` (exit 1). - Both workflow YAMLs validated as well-formed (`yaml.safe_load`); the commands they run match the locally-validated `check:lock-bytecode` invocation. - `bun run typecheck` — clean. `bun run lint` — clean. `bun test` — 66 pass / 0 fail. **Not verifiable here:** the workflows' first *live* run happens on GitHub. What can't be checked from a sandbox is the runner cloning the launcher + its public submodules over the https rewrite end-to-end, and Foundry downloading solc `0.8.35` on demand. The script logic those workflows invoke is validated locally above. ## Are there any breaking changes? No. No public API, types, or emitted bytecode change; the compiled `dist` output is unaffected (only a source comment, new tooling/CI, and docs). ## (Optional) Follow Ups _Not in this PR:_ - **Publish versioned launcher artifacts** so this SDK can drop the Foundry-in-CI dependency entirely and adopt the `v2-sdk`/`v3-sdk` recompute-from-published-artifact drift check. Worth an issue on Uniswap/liquidity-launcher. - **`uniswapx-sdk`** is the next-most-exposed package: its `abis/*.json` are hand-copied from the UniswapX contracts with no version pin or drift check (lower blast radius, since the embedded bytecode only deploys test mocks). --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_01Hkw9wpfbpaigd258uUmkYr)_

message: fix(liquidity-launcher-sdk): update lock recipient creation bytecodes to latest liquidity-launcher artifacts (#645) <!-- ccr-slack-attribution --> _Requested by **Eric Zhong** · [Slack thread](https://uniswapteam.slack.com/archives/C0BFWFUKGJX/p1784213241046949)_ ## Description `lockRecipientBytecode.ts` vendors the **creation bytecode** for the three liquidity-launcher periphery position recipients (`TimelockedPositionRecipient`, `PositionFeesForwarder`, `BuybackAndBurnPositionRecipient`). `buildLockRecipient` appends ABI-encoded constructor args to these blobs to predict CREATE2 addresses and build deploy calldata. **Before:** the blobs were pinned to liquidity-launcher commit `b181ce2f` (v3.0.0-era) and had gone stale. **After:** all three blobs are rebuilt at liquidity-launcher `main` HEAD, commit `e4660afe4f820f4a39181c7ea1f9bce6c423499f` (v3.1.0 release). **What actually changed on-chain:** between the two pins, the recipient contracts' own sources did not change — but the `lib/blocknumberish` dependency was bumped (`b911c96` → `38fe20b`). `BlockNumberish` is a base contract of all three recipients, and its new version detects the ArbSys precompile at construction time (extcodesize + staticcall probe stored in an immutable) instead of hardcoding the Arbitrum One chain id, extending support to all Arbitrum Orbit chains. **All three bytecodes changed** as a result. **How they were regenerated:** `forge build` (forge 1.7.1) in the liquidity-launcher repo at commit `e4660af`, submodules at their exact pinned revs, `optimizer_runs = 200`, `bytecode_hash = "none"`, solc `0.8.35+commit.47b9dedd`, values taken from the Foundry artifacts' `.bytecode.object`. The build environment was validated first by rebuilding at the old pin `b181ce2f` and reproducing all three previously vendored bytecodes **byte-for-byte**. The keccak256 guard-test pins in `lock.test.ts` are updated to the new hashes, and the previously missing `BUYBACK_BURN` pin is added so every vendored blob is now pinned: | Blob | Old keccak256 | New keccak256 | | --- | --- | --- | | `TIMELOCK` | `0x2191c5…e8203c` | `0x86ae21…ed7555` | | `FEES_FORWARDER` | `0x507a9a…d9e539` | `0xeae154…267013` | | `BUYBACK_BURN` | `0x4213a5…f106f3` (unpinned) | `0x591c41…c0fc1f` | ## How Has This Been Tested? - Unit tests: `bun test` in `sdks/liquidity-launcher-sdk` — 66 pass, 0 fail (includes the updated bytecode-hash pins and the `buildLockRecipient` CREATE2 prediction tests). - `bun run typecheck` and package build via turbo — clean. - Reproduction check: rebuilding at the old pinned commit `b181ce2f` with the same toolchain reproduced the previously vendored bytecodes byte-for-byte before regenerating at `e4660af`. ## Are there any breaking changes? No. Patch release (changeset included). No API changes — only the vendored bytecode constants, their pinned-commit comment, and the guard-test pins. ## (Optional) Follow Ups - Deployed lock recipients will now differ in address for identical salts/args versus the previous bytecode (expected, since init code changed). --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_01Hkw9wpfbpaigd258uUmkYr)_

author: gretzke
message: fix: stale foundry.lock, permit2 OZ remappings, and briefcase initcode generation (#158) * fix: sync foundry.lock with submodule revisions and fix nested permit2 OZ remappings forge build on a clean checkout prints revision mismatch warnings for nine dependencies because foundry.lock was not regenerated when the submodule pointers were bumped. I synced every lock entry to the committed gitlink revision and added the entries forge expects for the newer src/pkgs submodules (calibur, mixed-quoter, universal-router-2_0, v4-hooks-public). The build also logs two errors about a missing draft-EIP712.sol under uniswapx/lib/calibur/lib/openzeppelin-contracts. The vendored permit2 copies under uniswapx/lib/permit2 and uniswapx/lib/Tribunal/lib/the-compact/lib/permit2 import openzeppelin-contracts/ from their test utils, and the only matching remapping context resolved into calibur's OpenZeppelin, which is a v5 checkout that no longer ships the draft file. The files are skipped from compilation so this never failed the build, but the import graph resolution logs the errors on every run. I added a scoped remapping for each of the two permit2 copies pointing at their own vendored OpenZeppelin, mirroring the remapping that already existed for the calibur-nested permit2 copy. * fix: repair briefcase initcode generation after hook migration and posm settings change Running ./script/util/create_briefcase.sh failed for five deployers. WETHHook, WstETHHook and WstETHRoutingHook moved from v4-periphery to the v4-hooks-public repo (Uniswap/v4-periphery#510), but the deployer natspecs still pointed at the old v4-periphery paths and foundry.toml had no compilation restrictions for the new locations, so the contracts compiled under the default profile instead of optimizer_runs 44444444 with via_ir. I updated the source paths and added restrictions matching the settings recorded in the deployers. The regenerated WstETH hook initcodes are identical to the committed ones; only WETHHook's initcode changed, reflecting upstream source changes. PositionManagerDeployer still filtered for optimizer_runs 30000, but v4-periphery pins PositionManager at 500 since the Permissioned Pools change and foundry.toml already followed. I updated the filter to 500 and regenerated the initcode. CaliburEntryDeployer filters for evm_version prague, but the calibur restriction did not pin an evm version, so newer forge compiled it with its default (osaka) and the artifact no longer matched. I pinned prague in the restriction and added a matching calibur compiler profile. The regenerated initcode is byte-identical to the committed one, confirming prague matches the original deployment. * style: run forge fmt on regenerated deployers I generated the WETHHook and PositionManager deployer initcodes by running insert_initcode.py directly, which skips the forge fmt pass that create_briefcase.sh runs afterwards. A full pipeline run reformatted them (indentation only, identical initcode hex); this commits the formatted versions so the script output is idempotent. * fix: regenerate UniswapV2Factory and CaliburEntry deployer initcodes A clean create_briefcase.sh run regenerates these two initcodes. UniswapV2Factory changes only in the trailing bzzr0 metadata hash. The remappings added in this PR are embedded in solc metadata, and v2-core compiles with solc 0.5.16, which predates the setting foundry uses to strip metadata (bytecode_hash = none), so the embedded hash shifts. Note this changes the CREATE2 address of future briefcase deployments of UniswapV2Factory; the same applies to any future remappings.txt change, since v2-core metadata can't be stripped. CaliburEntry reflects real upstream source changes from the calibur submodule bump that is already on main; the committed initcode predates the bump and any fresh briefcase run reproduces this diff. Verified the pre-bump source compiled at evm_version prague reproduces the committed initcode exactly, so the prague pin added earlier in this PR matches the original deployment. * perf: parallelize briefcase flattening, drop unused build steps create_briefcase.sh spent about 16 minutes running forge flatten serially over 284 files; each invocation re-resolves the full project graph, so they parallelize almost linearly. The per-package loop now only queues (file, input dir, output dir) triples into a null-separated work list, and a single xargs pool drains it across all packages, which keeps every worker busy regardless of per-directory file counts. xargs starts the next file the moment a worker frees up, there is no batch barrier. The pool defaults to the core count, which benchmarks show is the saturation point (10, 16 and 20 workers all land within seconds of each other on a 10-core machine); BRIEFCASE_JOBS overrides it. Two build steps are commented out rather than deleted, with notes on when to re-enable them: the initial clean+build, whose artifacts nothing consumed (flattening and the vendoring script only read sources), and the final clean, since only src/briefcase/** changed by that point so the closing verification build can run incrementally. A full pipeline run drops from roughly 40 minutes to 16 on a 10-core machine, verified end to end: the regenerated output matches a run of the unmodified script byte for byte. * fix: abort briefcase creation on flatten failures, move hook deployers to v4-hooks-public A failed forge flatten in the parallel pool now aborts the script with an error instead of letting the Python step process an incomplete briefcase. The explicit set -e also covers invocation via 'bash script.sh', where the shebang's -e flag is ignored. The WETHHook, WstETHHook, and WstETHRoutingHook deployers build from the v4-hooks-public package, so they now live under deployers/v4-hooks-public instead of deployers/v4-periphery. Import paths in Deploy-all and MineWETHHookSalt updated accordingly. * style: sort deployer imports after v4-hooks-public move
