author: codyborn
message: feat: trigger circuit breaker on Laplace-smoothed fade rate (#454) * feat: trigger circuit breaker on Laplace-smoothed fade rate, not raw count The V2 circuit breaker blocked a filler on ANY new fade in a 10-minute window, which structurally over-penalizes high-volume fillers (more orders -> more absolute fades). Switch the trigger to a fade *rate* with Laplace smoothing so volume is accounted for. - fadeRate = (fades + 1) / (total + 20) [LAPLACE_ALPHA=1, LAPLACE_BETA=20] Prior mean ~4.8%; block when the smoothed rate exceeds FADE_RATE_BLOCK_THRESHOLD = 12%. Smoothing pulls small samples toward the prior so a couple of early fades don't trip the breaker, while sustained high rates on real volume still do. - Rate is measured over the filler's "post-block window" (orders whose deadline is after their last blockUntilTimestamp). This is the clean-slate recovery mechanism: a returning filler is scored only on orders completed after the block ended, not on stale pre-block fades. To support this, the decay branch now preserves the (past) blockUntilTimestamp instead of resetting it to 0 — the provider already treats any past timestamp as unblocked, so behavior at the quoter is unchanged. - Recovery is driven by the block timer (a blocked filler receives no RFQs, so it cannot improve its rate while benched); the clean slate prevents instant re-block on return. consecutiveBlocks still escalates/decays for repeat offenders, and in-flight fades while blocked still extend the block (via newFades). - Block duration now backs off purely on consecutiveBlocks (2^n); dropped the per-fade 1.2^(n-1) multiplier so block length no longer scales with absolute fade count either. getFillersNewFades -> getFillersFadeStats (returns {fadeRate, newFades}). Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix: guard against non-finite stored timestamps in fade-rate logic TimestampRepository builds rows via parseInt, which yields NaN for a missing/malformed attribute. A NaN blockUntilTimestamp made `deadline > NaN` always false, zeroing the fade-rate window so the filler's rate stayed at the prior (~4.8%) and could never exceed the 12% threshold — a fail-open that let a corrupted row escape the breaker entirely (the old count-based code blocked such fillers). Add a finiteOr() helper and apply it to the window floor, the newFades lastPostTimestamp comparison, and the decay-branch write (so a NaN floor is normalized to the unblocked sentinel instead of being re-persisted). Add tests covering both getFillersFadeStats and calculateNewTimestamps with NaN state. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * chore: set LAPLACE_BETA=19 for a clean 5% prior mean alpha/(alpha+beta) = 1/(1+19) = 1/20 = 5% exactly. Update comments and the hardcoded denominators in tests accordingly. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * feat: widen fade window to 24h / latest-100 to catch chronic low-volume fading A 1h window with a latest-50 cap let two classes of fader escape the 12% smoothed threshold indefinitely (flagged in review): - a low-volume filler fading every order (1/hr => 2/21 = 9.5%, never blocked) - a high-volume filler chronically fading ~14% (7 of 50/hr => 8/70 = 11.4%) Widen the view window to 24 hours and the per-filler cap to 100. The cap makes the lookback adaptive: high-volume fillers are judged on their latest 100 orders (fast acute response, ~12 fades to trip from a clean history), while low-volume fillers accumulate up to 24h of orders (2 fades => 3/22 = 13.6% trips). The chronic 14% fader now holds ~14 fades in its latest 100 => 15/120 = 12.5% > 12%. A legitimate sustained ~10% filler stays clear. Trigger, smoothing, threshold, clean-slate floor, and the state machine are unchanged — the entire behavioral change is the SQL window and cap. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix: exclude in-flight orders before computing the per-filler latest-N cap ROW_NUMBER() was computed over all posted orders and the completed-orders filter (deadline < now) applied afterwards, so still-fillable in-flight orders consumed latest-N slots and were then discarded. For a very active filler this shrank the effective sample below ORDERS_PER_FILLER_LIMIT, overweighting recent fades in the smoothed rate (flagged in review). Move the deadline filter inside the windowed subquery so the cap counts completed orders only. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * feat: score during-block cohort as a rate; document idle-drift block decision Two review follow-ups: 1. The extend-while-blocked path triggered on newFades > 0 — an absolute count with no denominator, so a high-volume filler's single statistical in-flight fade extended their block while clean in-flight fills counted for nothing (the volume bias this PR removes elsewhere). Replace newFades with duringBlockRate: the Laplace-smoothed rate over orders completed since the last cron run with deadline on/before the block end (i.e. in flight during the block). Extending now uses the same threshold as tripping. Because cohort membership is defined by timestamps rather than "is the filler blocked right now", this also fixes the slip-through edge case: in-flight fades landing after the last blocked-state cron run but before blockUntil are scored on the next run and re-block from now, even though the block expired in between. 2. Idle-drift blocks (rate crossing the threshold with no new completions, as clean orders age out of the 24h window) are deliberately left in place: gating on new completions would just move the surprise to right after a completed — possibly cleanly filled — order, which is stranger filler UX. Documented at the block branch. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * docs: clarify UNBLOCKED_BLOCK_UNTIL_TIMESTAMP is only for never-blocked fillers Post clean-slate change, the sentinel is no longer written for fillers coming off a block — the decay branch preserves their expired blockUntilTimestamp as the fade-rate window floor. Overwriting it with the sentinel would erase the floor and re-score the filler's entire 24h history, including the pre-block fades that got them blocked (raised in review). Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * refactor: coerce non-finite timestamps at the TimestampRepository parse boundary Rows are legitimately written with optional attributes (blockUntilTimestamp: undefined), which parseInt turns into NaN on read — poisoning downstream comparisons. Per review, coerce at the parse boundary (parseFiniteInt) so every consumer sees finite numbers: blockUntilTimestamp falls back to the unblocked sentinel, lastPostTimestamp/consecutiveBlocks to 0. Move UNBLOCKED_BLOCK_UNTIL_TIMESTAMP (and its clean-slate-floor docs) into the repository that owns the stored value's semantics; re-export from fade-rate-v2 for existing importers. The cron-side finiteOr guard stays as defense-in-depth for timestamps arriving from other sources. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix: gate consecutiveBlocks decay on new completions (idling must not reset escalation) With the 24h view, a filler's stale rows keep them in the stats every cron run long after their block expired, so the decay branch fired every 10 minutes while they simply idled — resetting consecutiveBlocks 3 -> 0 in ~30 minutes with zero demonstrated clean fills, and letting a serial fader dodge the 2^n escalation entirely (raised in review). The old count-based code implicitly froze escalation for idle fillers because the stats map only included fillers with completions since the last run. Restore that semantic explicitly: getFillersFadeStats now reports newCompletions (orders completed since the last cron run, any cohort) and the decay branch only decrements consecutiveBlocks when newCompletions > 0 — otherwise the counter carries forward unchanged. Working off escalation once again requires demonstrated clean activity. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix: raise fade-query row cap 5000 -> 20000 to match the 24h window The LIMIT 5000 caps predate the fade window; widening 1h -> 24h (and the per-filler cap 50 -> 100) multiplied row volume ~24x, making 5000 easy to exceed. Above the cap, rows are silently truncated (the inner CTE LIMIT has no ORDER BY; the outer ORDER BY rfqFiller deterministically drops the highest addresses) and those fillers escape scoring entirely. Extract FADE_QUERY_ROW_LIMIT = 20000 (~200 filler addresses of headroom at the 100/filler cap) and use it for all three V2 caps, with a comment tying it to ORDERS_PER_FILLER_LIMIT and the CIRCUIT_BREAKER_V2_FILLERS_EVALUATED alarm as the tripwire if it's ever hit. Does not fix the truncation mechanism (a follow-up will paginate/aggregate); this restores safe headroom now. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * refactor: clean V2 circuit-breaker state schema on a fresh table Rolling the rate-based breaker onto a new DynamoDB table (FillerCBTimestampsV2, created alongside the V1 table for clean rollback) lets us fix the stored schema, not just the name. Three legacy-driven awkward spots retired: 1. Numbers, not strings. All CB fields were stored as type:'string' and read with parseInt; with wrapNumbers this was the source of the NaN-guard complexity (parseFiniteInt/finiteOr). Store native numbers, read via a wrapNumbers:false client the repo builds itself; a missing attribute is undefined (?? sentinel), never NaN. Both guard helpers dropped. 2. De-overload blockUntilTimestamp. It meant both "block expiry" and "clean-slate floor", forcing the "preserve past value, don't reset to 0" trick. Split out fadeWindowStart as the floor; blockUntilTimestamp resets cleanly to 0 on decay while fadeWindowStart independently holds the last block end. 3. Rename lastPostTimestamp -> lastExaminedTimestamp (last cron-run boundary). State is derived (recomputed each run from Redshift), so the new table starts empty — no migration. Behavior unchanged. jest-dynamodb creates the V2 table. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix: first-writer-wins filler-address ownership + per-filler address cap The circuit breaker attributes fades to a filler (webhook endpoint) via the address->filler map, populated from the caller-supplied `response.filler` on every OK quote. Two holes (flagged in the #454 security review): 1. Poisoning: `addNewAddressToFiller` did an unconditional last-write-wins put, so a filler could claim an address owned by another filler — binding a competitor's high-volume clean flow to their own hash to dilute their fade rate (or grief the competitor). Now first-writer-wins: a claim on an address already owned by a different filler is ignored. 2. Unbounded squatting: no limit on addresses per filler. Add MAX_FILLER_ADDRESSES (3); registrations beyond the cap are ignored. Both rejections are safe no-ops — the order still quotes/fills, the address just isn't attributed — so this can't break quoting. Mirrored in the mock repo. NOTE: caps the attribution map (what the breaker reads). Fully bounding postedorders.filler diversity additionally needs cosign-time enforcement (follow-up); MAX_FILLER_ADDRESSES should be calibrated against the real per-endpoint distribution before tightening further. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * docs: tighten circuit-breaker comments to present-tense intent Remove references to prior state and in-process/temporary decisions (e.g. the old row cap, the 1h->24h change, 'raised in review', 'remove V1 in a follow-up', 'tune before tightening'); keep concise comments describing current behavior. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * feat: require filler address in the RFQ response The filler address is the circuit breaker's attribution key. When it was optional, a response without it posted with no exclusive filler and never entered the fade view, so those fades escaped scoring. Make `filler` required in RfqResponseJoi: a response omitting it is now rejected as a validation error. validatePermissionedTokens keeps its own `!data.filler` guard, so its param is typed PostQuoteResponse (filler optional) rather than RfqResponse. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * feat: circuit breaker observability — metrics + dashboard (#460) * feat: add circuit breaker observability metrics and dashboard widgets New metrics (Service=CircuitBreaker, emitted each fade-rate cron run): - CIRCUIT_BREAKER_V2_FADE_RATE_{filler}: per-filler smoothed rate so the distribution can be charted against FADE_RATE_BLOCK_THRESHOLD - CIRCUIT_BREAKER_V2_NEW_BLOCKS / EXTENDED_BLOCKS: trips and extensions per run (the existing V2_BLOCKED counts all row updates incl. decays, so it cannot distinguish these) - CIRCUIT_BREAKER_V2_ACTIVE_BLOCKS: fillers currently benched, including benched fillers with no completions this run (countActiveBlocks helper) - CIRCUIT_BREAKER_V2_FILLERS_EVALUATED: sample-health denominator Dashboard: replace the "Blocked Filler On Average" widget (charted row-update counts) with three widgets — breaker activity (new/extended/active/evaluated), per-filler fade rates via SEARCH with a horizontal annotation at the 12% threshold, and per-filler consecutive blocks (metric existed but was never charted). Drive-by: fix pre-existing no-useless-escape lint errors in the failing-RFQ-logs query. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix: chart circuit-breaker recovery and during-block rate Two observability gaps from the #460 review: - Consecutive-blocks was emitted only in the block/extend branches, so the "escalation" widget could show climbs but never decay. Emit the resulting level in every branch (skipping never-blocked 0->0 fillers) so the chart steps down through recovery and plots the 0. - The "fade rates vs threshold" widget charted only the post-block fadeRate, which sits at the prior while a filler is benched. Emit and chart the during-block rate (the signal that drives extend/re-block) so a benched filler shows above the threshold line. author: gretzke
message: fix(deployments): final-review fix pass — containment, honesty, provenance Fork containers are created lazily (tier-1 success no longer leaks a container + concurrency permit) and the fork URL rides a 0600 bind-mounted tmpfile instead of Env (docker inspect showed credentials). bundledInImage builtins hash their staged bundle into the image label (stale-bundle images now flagged; staging reordered before hash so registry and label agree). Deployment-type params validate strictly against the described contract (required/type/select-options; exact-key result envelopes); plugin failure envelopes are capped + control-stripped before reaching API errors, validation items, or artifacts. Failure-skipped steps no longer resolve pointers via their dead predicted address (dedicated regression); POINTER_ UNRESOLVED classifies to its own pause reason (was broadcast); successful plain-create receipts without contractAddress pause needs-review instead of confirming addressless; created-code-missing recheck enqueues verification on late confirmation. Simulation only treats acknowledged steps as existing after OBSERVING code (execution deploys when absent); tier-3 marks calls after any earlier call unestimable (cross-contract state effects). Library bindings must match the compiler reference set exactly; artifact library sources use the canonical per-chain merge and portable lib keys. Edits reject inapplicable target/library/arg step ids whole and prune stale acknowledgments after prediction refresh; pointer pauses persist {stepId, path} details and the run view routes the edit dialog to the exact field (never writing path strings as literal arg keys). Frontend: canonical sourcePath:Name library keys, per-chain call target/value/gas + salt + library surfaces, call-arg pointer mode, viem-canonical tuple signatures. D3-era run-record fixture pins parse + deterministic v2 artifact regen.

author: gretzke
message: test(deployments): D5 exit-criteria integration proofs; fix ladder + hook plugin delivery Four Docker proofs green: linked create2 plan with pointers, calls, and a per-step signer override across two anvils with field-by-field artifact v2 assertions; acknowledged re-run (skipped-with-address, zero attempts, no nonce consumed); forward create2 reference + prediction-cycle rejection; hook mined and deployed through the REST prepare route incl. commitment- stale detection. Fixes exposed by the proofs: eth_simulateV1 create calls omit 'to' and tier-1 infrastructure errors always fall through with reasons (anvil cannot simulate creation calls; only simulation RESULTS block); tier-3 marks sequence-dependent calls (target created or called earlier in the schedule) unestimable instead of mis-estimating against pre-sequence state; fork container overrides the foundry image entrypoint and rewrites loopback fork URLs to host.docker.internal (host-gateway alias); create2 validation fallback code is CREATE2_PREDICTION_FAILED, not proxy-missing; deployment-type param keys allow camelCase (flagsOverride). The 480KB hook bundle exceeds MAX_ARG_STRLEN (128KiB/arg), so bundledInImage builtins bake their bundle into their image at /plugin/index.js (build-all stages it into the docker context) and execute installed-style; args-walk pointer paths now use the args.-rooted vocabulary collectRefs and the artifact expect.

author: gretzke
message: feat(deployments): engine execution branches, provenance, hardened edits, artifact v2 executeStep executes call steps (merged targets, canonical-signature ABI lookup, plain transfers) and create2/plugin strategies (pre-tx collision check honoring fresh acknowledgments as attempt-free skips; proxy tx; predicted-address code confirmation with created-code-missing pause since proxy receipts carry no contractAddress). Attempt.expected persists in the provider's built phase; confirm-hash verifies from/to/dataHash/value plus a success receipt against that durable intent (getTxOrigin -> getTxForProvenance). accept-deployed records a fresh acknowledgment + predicted address into the run's plan snapshot; created-code-missing recheck re-polls code. Edits validate on a clone (dependency rules, resolvability, ABI), refresh predictions for unexecuted steps, and reject prediction-affecting edits on mined plugin steps (EDIT_REQUIRES_REMINE). Launch persists predicted addresses and simulation tiers. Verification enqueue/reconciliation decompose calldata per strategy against linked bytecode; tasks snapshot the library map at enqueue and inject settings.libraries into a copy at submit (LIBRARY_SETTINGS_CONFLICT on mismatch). Artifact v2 renders strategies, salts, predicted addresses, library/pointer resolutions from expected, call targets, simulation tiers, acknowledged-skip notes. Integration: pinned- image harness + ensureCreate2Proxy (presigned canonical deploy) + forge fixtures (MathLib, LinkedCounter, OwnedBox, MiniHook); stale D4-era assertions updated (artifact v2; RETRYABLE detail carries explorer message per 8097740).

CoW order and CoW EVC-permit signing ignores it and is gated separately by cowSwapForcedOff. - Only the queuing of failed restorations is sequential-only; the restorePendingBeforeRetry gate runs before the bundled branch and so blocks bundled Safe migrations too. - Label the lens convertToAssets(balanceOf(address(1))) subtraction as an upstream on-chain invariant that cannot be verified in this repo, and state what can be: the SDK adapters pass lostAssets through unchanged. - Name createRaceGuard alongside runGuarded in the race-guard reference. - Drop the stale 'unavailable' return from the sendMigrationAsSafeBundle docstring; the function throws rather than falling back to sequential grants.

author: kasperpawlowski
message: fix: admit deployment manifest per entry, gated on enabled chains Rejecting the whole manifest when any single entry failed validation meant a routine euler-interfaces commit adding a sparse new chain (e.g. no permit2 yet) would freeze refreshes and turn into a total 502 on both realms once the 7-day stale window expired. Admission is now per entry: invalid entries for chains this deployment does not enable are dropped with a warning listing their chainIds, and the remaining valid entries are cached. Every enabled chain must still be present and valid — an unusable payload for a chain users are actually on is exactly the poison the stale window exists to outlive, so that still rejects and preserves last-known-good.

author: kasperpawlowski
message: fix: validate manifest and ABI payloads before cache admission An array-shaped but unusable 200 ([], entries missing chainId/addresses, ABI items without a type) could overwrite the last-known-good cache entry and reset its timestamp, turning the 7-day stale window into a long-lived poison cache. Both refresh paths now admission-check the payload shape and throw on failure, so the resolution chain falls back to the existing stale entry. Regression tests cover valid seed -> past TTL -> 200 [] -> stale value served, for both deployments and ABIs.

author: kasperpawlowski
message: refactor: drop committed manifest snapshots The app should not hold static copies of EulerChains.json or ABIs. Resilience now rests on the 7-day stale window (a running instance outlives any realistic upstream outage, which covers the actual incident scenario) plus the explicit URL env vars as emergency repoint levers. An instance cold-started mid-outage 502s until upstream recovers or the env repoints it — an honest, documented failure mode instead of baked-in data.

author: kasperpawlowski
message: feat: make deployment manifest and ABI fetching resilient to upstream outages During the 2026-08-17 GitHub incident the app went down because the euler-chains proxy's stale cache expired after 15 minutes and every SDK build then failed to load the deployments manifest. This makes the manifest pipeline survive arbitrary-length upstream outages: - createTtlCache: an explicit maxStaleMs is now honored above the 30-min default ceiling (the ceiling still applies when no explicit value is set) - /api/internal/euler-chains: 7-day stale window plus a committed build-time snapshot as cold-start last resort (fresh -> upstream -> stale -> snapshot); explicit NUXT_PUBLIC_CONFIG_EULER_CHAINS_URL now takes precedence over the branch env vars so it works as an emergency repoint lever - new /api/internal/abis/[contract] proxy with the same resilience chain for the runtime ABIs (AccountLens, VaultLens, UtilsLens); browser SDK wired via setQueryABI, raw.githubusercontent.com removed from CSP connect-src - server-side SDK builds (vault snapshots, token-list, SSR) now resolve deployments through the same chain via DeploymentService.setQueryDeployments instead of fetching GitHub directly - warm-cache refreshes the ABI manifests each global cycle - npm run snapshots:update refreshes the committed snapshots

author: cursoragent
message: docs: correct plan-time snapshot bounds and invalidation wording Three corrections from review: 1. sdk-integration.md said a preloaded `input.account` from useFreshAccount() is bounded by its refresh cadence "not by FORM_STALE_TIMES". Wrong: useFreshAccount's fresh task calls getEulerSdkFresh() then fetchAccount(), so those reads go through the shared QueryClient too. It is bounded by the trigger cadence *and* the applicable form windows. Also notes the parallel fast task uses the browsing windows and that the fresh result wins. 2. vault-labels-and-verification.md still claimed the path handler's header describes a shared read-through pipeline and called the behavior a known divergence. Since #720 the header documents the force-refresh, in-flight joining, and stale-fallback behavior directly, so the divergence framing is dropped and the paragraph points at the header and the endpoint-level guide instead. 3. "Evicted" was wrong throughout: invalidateSdkQueries calls TanStack's invalidateQueries, which flags entries stale and refetches active observers rather than removing them. SDK queries go through fetchQuery and have no standing observers, so the practical effect is that the next read re-fetches. Corrected in sdk-integration.md and in the matching comments in sdk-query-policy.ts, useEulerSdk.ts, useEulerTx.ts, useEulerAccount.ts, and the policy test header. Source changes are comment-only; no executable lines changed.

author: kasperpawlowski
message: feat: bundle batch prerequisites into the cart's safe proposal A Safe executing a cart with migration entries previously paid three signature ceremonies: standalone grant proposals, the batch proposal, standalone revocations. Entries now provide buildBundledExecution — the simulation-variant plan (no live authorization reads) plus grant/revoke calls — and executeBatch wraps everything into one atomic wallet_sendCalls proposal via executePreparedPlanWithPlainCalls. The standalone gas estimate is skipped on this path (grants are unmined until the proposal executes; the cart's continuous simulation with authorization overrides is the pre-flight validation) and unwind bookkeeping disappears (atomicity). Degraded Safes throw the reconnect error rather than silently degrading to the sequential ceremony; non-Safe wallets and mixed carts keep the sequential path. The review modal derives its ceremony display from the same predicate: prerequisite rows show bundled-in-proposal, expanded rows drop the Separate-tx badge.

author: kasperpawlowski
message: fix: abort loudly when the reviewed safe bundle cannot run The review promises one atomic proposal; a Safe whose provider cannot be acquired at confirmation now fails with a clear reconnect error instead of silently degrading into the sequential grant/migration/revoke ceremony the user never reviewed (non-Safe wallets still take the sequential flow). The migration success paths route through the detachment gate so a proposal that confirmed after its modal was closed marks success for the completion toast and no longer redirects mid-flow.

author: kasperpawlowski
message: fix: withhold uncovered losses until the coverage read settles Addresses PR review from Cursor, CodeRabbit and Leonard. useEarnLossCoverage kept exposing the previous vault's coverage shares while a new vault's balanceOf was in flight. The race guard stops a stale response landing later but cannot retract an already-committed value, so the overview netted one vault's shortfall against another vault's shares and understated the uncovered loss. Clear the shares before each read. That clearing makes the in-flight state indistinguishable from a failed read at the value level, so the stats row now gates on isCoverageLoading and renders a placeholder until the read settles; the conservative undefined -> full lostAssets fallback is reserved for a settled failure. Previously a covered vault briefly showed its gross shortfall. The formatter effect now runs through runGuarded so a slow first formatAssetValue cannot overwrite the fresher value produced once coverage arrives. Adds a useEarnLossCoverage regression suite (vault switch mid-read, out-of-order response, failed read), runGuarded ordering tests, and a computeUncoveredLosses fixture built from live mainnet TelosC Surge USDC state.

author: cursoragent
message: docs: align source comments with the shipped cache behavior The guide describes plan-time reads as bounded by FORM_STALE_TIMES with no form-mount invalidation, but several source comments still promised something stronger. Comment-only edits; no executable line changes. - useEulerSdk.ts: getEulerSdkFresh() no longer claims a zero stale time or that planning reflects the latest block. Pinning the adapters selects the data source; the windows are 1 min / 15 s per row. Also drops queryPythUpdateData from the list, which has no formStaleTimeMs and inherits its 30 s staleTimeMs. - useEulerTx.ts: freshPlanContext() no longer claims a live latest-block account. The fetch resolves through the shared QueryClient at each row's form stale time. - sdk-query-policy.ts: formStaleTimeMs is a stale time, not a forced refetch, and no row uses 0. invalidateAfterTx evicts after a successful tx only, naming the three call sites; nothing evicts at form mount. Two more instances of the same drift, beyond the three flagged: - tests/utils/sdk-query-policy.test.ts repeated the form-mount claim. - useEulerAccount.ts said portfolio reads via the fresh instance "always reflect the latest block", which is the same conflation of data source with freshness. sdk-integration.md drops the note recording the contradiction, now that there is no contradiction to record.

author: cursoragent
message: docs: flag the three source comments that still overstate freshness useEulerSdk.ts and useEulerTx.ts both describe a zero stale time on plan-critical reads, and sdk-query-policy.ts says invalidateAfterTx evicts at form mount. Neither is true any more, and this PR is docs-only so the comments stay as they are; point the reader at the document instead of leaving a silent contradiction.

author: cursoragent
message: docs: keep this PR docs-only and document the labels cache divergence Revert the non-documentation changes made while responding to review: the path-shape labels handler, the read-through helper export, the new route test, and the comment edits in useEulerSdk.ts, useEulerTx.ts, and sdk-query-policy.ts. Those files are byte-identical to their previous state again. Instead of changing behavior, describe it. The path-shape labels route backs the SDK's default `eulerLabelsBaseUrl` template and calls `refreshLabelFile`, the force-refresh primitive, so it bypasses the fresh-entry check: every request reaches upstream unless it coincides with an in-flight fetch for the same key, and the warm-cache entry acts as a stale fallback rather than a read-through cache. Only the query-shape handler short-circuits on a fresh entry. vault-labels-and-verification.md now contrasts the two handlers in a table, server-side-caching.md scopes its read-through claim to the handlers that actually short-circuit, and the warm-cache section's "requests read the still-fresh previous entry" note is qualified the same way. The divergence is flagged as such rather than presented as design.

author: cursoragent
message: fix(labels): read the path-shape route through the shared TTL cache The path-shape handler backs the SDK's default `eulerLabelsBaseUrl` template, but it called `refreshLabelFile` — the force-refresh primitive reserved for warm-cache cycles. That sent every SDK label read upstream and left the warm-cache prewarm useful only as a stale fallback, despite the handler comment, docs/server-side-caching.md, and docs/vault-labels-and-verification.md all describing a shared read-through cache. Export the existing `getOrRefresh` read-through helper and use it in both handlers. Warm callers keep calling `refreshLabelFile` directly so each cycle rewrites the entry before it expires.

message: fix: keep the in-flight owner resolution when a pending spy address is re-activated Re-activating the address already awaiting owner resolution bumped the resolution request id without starting a new lookup (the same-value ref write never re-triggers the watcher), so the only in-flight result was discarded as stale and the candidate stayed unresolved forever. Treat an identical pending candidate as idempotent and leave the in-flight resolution authoritative.

author: Seranged
message: feat: enrich liquidation activity rows with historical valuations Joins displayed liquidation events with the standalone /v3/liquidations endpoint (SDK fetchLiquidations) by chain, transaction, vault, violator, collateral, and repaid amount. Matching rows gain the event-time USD value of the repaid debt, the seized collateral converted to underlying units with its USD value, and the liquidator bonus (negative when unprofitable). The join is fail-soft: rows without a matching record keep today's share-quantity display, and an unavailable endpoint never degrades the feed. Queries batch per chain+vault over the displayed time window with bounded offset pagination, cached under the activity stale-time policy. The /v3/liquidations path joins the server proxy allowlist; violator and liquidator query params are excluded from proxy log fields since they identify wallets. Requires the euler-v2-sdk release with fetchLiquidations — the branch currently builds against a local SDK overlay until the version bump.

author: Seranged
message: fix: classify SDK 1.1.4 migration and rewards queries in the cache policy SDK 1.1.3 added six PositionMigrationService queries (queryListPositions, queryListTargets, queryGetPosition, queryGetAuthorization, queryEulerTargetVaultData, queryEulerSourceVaultAssets) routed through Lite's buildQuery. None had an SDK_QUERY_POLICY row, so both the browsing and the plan-time SDK served them from a 5-minute default cache and no post-tx eviction applied: migration planning could reuse stale external position balances and authorization state, and a completed migration kept serving the pre-migration position. Classify all six: position/authorization reads get balance-class windows (1 min browse / 15 s plan-time) plus invalidateAfterTx; discovery lists get 5 min / 1 min plus invalidateAfterTx; Euler-side vault data gets the governance-config class. Also classify queryFuulClaimChecks, queryFuulTotals, queryTurtleMerkleProofs and queryTurtleStreams, which had been silently defaulting since SDK 1.1.2, and add queryFuulClaimChecks to the post-claim reward invalidation list. Bump the SDK to 1.1.4, which adds PositionMigrationService to the EulerSDKQueryName union so the new rows typecheck without local widening. Add a completeness test that builds the real SDK with a recording buildQuery and fails when any wrapped query name lacks a policy row (or a row matches no wrapped name), so future SDK bumps cannot introduce queries that silently inherit the default stale time.

author: cursoragent
message: fix(analytics): restore V3 TVL/volume when DefiLlama backfill lags Protocol Metrics attributed 100% of CORE−COW to v2 whenever the chart window had no DefiLlama V2/V3 rows. The hourly api-v3 cron never writes those splits, and backfill was manual-only, so after the last DefiLlama day aged out of the 90D window Balancer v3 rendered as $0 despite ~$22M on DefiLlama. Forward-fill V2/V3 onto api-v3 snapshot points from the latest known ratio at read time, and schedule the DefiLlama backfill daily so the gap cannot grow silently again. author: Xeonus
message: fix: Github Oauth handling Root cause: Individual users (e.g. 0xDanko) got a persistent "error checking fork status" 500 because their stored GitHub OAuth token was stale/revoked. The token is only written to the DB in the linkAccount event, which fires only on first login — so returning users' tokens were never refreshed, and no cache clear, re-login, or fork sync could recover it. Changes: 1. auth.ts — Now refreshes the encrypted GitHub token on every sign-in (added a signIn event alongside linkAccount, sharing a persistGithubToken() helper). A stale/revoked token now heals when the user reconnects. This is the core fix. 2. app/api/github/check-status/route.ts — Hardened error handling so failures return clear, actionable responses instead of a generic 500: - Undecryptable token → 401 (TOKEN_DECRYPT_FAILED) - Revoked/expired token → 401 (GITHUB_TOKEN_INVALID) - Uses the fork's own default branch (handles old master forks) - Fragile cross-fork compare now degrades to non-blocking statusUnknown instead of blocking PR creation 3. components/modal/PRModal.tsx — Deduplicated the fork-status fetch logic and added a "Reconnect GitHub" button that appears on a 401, giving stuck users a self-serve fix instead of a dead-end toast.

author: Xeonus
message: chore: fix array parsing from balancer/backend What was wrong _to_json only rewrote spreads of inline array literals (...[ ] → [ ]). When balancer/backend added workerJobs: [...activeChainWorkerJobsGeneric, ...] (spreads of imported identifiers), those tokens reached json.loads and raised JSONDecodeError for every chain. Subgraph.get_subgraph_url_from_backend_config() swallowed it (bare try/except → None) and silently fell back to stale studio.thegraph.com URLs — which regressed the bal_addresses scheduled PR with outdated sources This change fixes the issue by adding two regexes right before the existing one to properly handle the new data structure in the backend.

author: tiago-hansen
message: add fork test for PRIME (#140) * add PRIME fork test * make setup skip time configurable; use 30 min for PRIME PRIME reads its rate from a Hastra FeedVerifier (Chainlink Data Streams) with a 1-hour staleness window. The base test's hardcoded skip(1 days) pushed the cached report past that limit, reverting the rate path and failing 13/17 tests. Add a `skipTime` field to ERC4626SetupState (defaults to 1 day, so all existing tokens are unchanged) and override it to 30 minutes for PRIME to keep the feed fresh. All 17 PRIME tests now pass. author: aoikurokawa
message: Steward: Fix directed rebalance ix (#306) ## Problem When an external withdrawal occurs (e.g. a JitoSOL redemption via `decrease_validator_stake_with_reserve`), the undirected rebalance may run before the directed rebalance and sync `validator_lamport_balances` to the current on-chain validator stake. However, it does **not** update the directed stake accounting fields (`total_staked_lamports`, `directed_stake_lamports`). When directed rebalance subsequently runs, neither existing branch fires: - The **withdrawal branch** (`validator_list < steward_state`) does not fire because `validator_lamport_balances` was already synced. - The **deposit branch** (`validator_list > steward_state`) does not fire because there was no new deposit. As a result, `total_staked_lamports` and `directed_stake_lamports` remain stale - far above the actual on-chain validator stake - causing incorrect scoring and rebalance calculations downstream. This was observed in production with LEVMA at epoch 956, where validator stake dropped from ~49,785 SOL to ~5,166 SOL but directed accounting remained at ~49,612 SOL. Epoch 956 Big withdrawal: https://solscan.io/tx/3DUfFxgajcCs1ZL5y9Hd6D8iJcKeujcSDoDg7YVNNwHm9k7SZCfw8MYVmQXEw65dy5fBroPgcSYMp17S4PKvux3k ## Solution - Add a third branch (`else if directed_stake_applied_lamports > validator_list_staked_lamports`) to `adjust_directed_stake_for_deposits_and_withdrawals` that caps `total_staked_lamports` and `directed_stake_lamports` down to the actual on-chain validator stake. `validator_lamport_balances` is left unchanged since it is already correct after the undirected rebalance. - The same branch is mirrored in `simulate_adjust_directed_stake_for_deposits_and_withdrawals` in `steward_state.rs` to keep scoring and rebalance calculations in sync with what the on-chain instruction writes.

author: stablebits
message: scheduler priority floor mechanism (load-shedding via published priority floor) (#12263) scheduler priority floor: load-shedding low-priority transactions in sigverify Adds a saturation-detection + priority-floor mechanism to banking-stage's central scheduler. When the scheduler is saturated, it publishes a priority floor — derived from the lowest-priority transaction in its queue — to a shared atomic. Sigverify reads the floor and drops incoming transactions whose priority is at or below it, ahead of signature verification. Saturation triggers (either): - the retained scheduler buffer crosses the saturation watermark - on-capacity drops in the just-completed receive_and_buffer call Desaturation requires both the buffer below the desaturation watermark and no on-capacity drops in this tick. SaturationState clears the shared floor on Drop so a stale value doesn't outlive the controller. Floor drop in sigverify happens in each non-vote worker thread, post-dedup and pre-signature-verify. Workers parse the transaction priority from raw packet bytes using the same priority formula the scheduler queue uses, so a packet drops on the same comparison value it would face at the queue's tail. Simple votes are detected at parse time and exempted from the floor — vote priority is governed by a separate policy in banking stage. The PacketFlags::SIMPLE_VOTE_TX flag can't be used for this exemption because it's set during sigverify, which runs after the floor check.

author: sam0x17
message: Geyser contact info (#12267) geyser: opt-in plugin notifications for validator contact info Adds a new pair of Geyser plugin methods so plugins can subscribe to push-based delivery of validator contact info instead of polling `getClusterNodes` over RPC. Closes the last gossip-side prerequisite for consumers that aim to operate entirely off Geyser (e.g. Triton's gRPC framework). Geyser is not covered by the SIMD process so this lands directly in Agave; the design discussion lives at https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-improvement-documents/discussions/511. - `ReplicaContactInfoV0_0_1<'a>` + `ReplicaContactInfoVersions<'a>` following the existing `ReplicaAccountInfo*` enum-of-references convention. Pubkey is `&[u8]` to match the convention on the other Replica types. Version is exposed as plain binary fields (`version_major`/`minor`/`patch`/`commit`/`feature_set`/`client_id`) rather than a formatted string, so the dispatch path is allocation free; consumers can format to a string themselves if they want one. - Three new methods on `GeyserPlugin`, all with safe defaults so existing plugins compile unchanged: - `fn contact_info_notifications_enabled(&self) -> bool` (default `false`) - `fn notify_contact_info(&self, info, is_startup) -> Result<()>` - `fn notify_contact_info_removed(&self, pubkey: &[u8]) -> Result<()>` - New module `contact_info_notifier` containing: - `ContactInfoSnapshot` — owned, `Copy`, no heap, 17 fields covering pubkey/wallclock/outset/shred_version, all version components, and every advertised socket including Alpenglow. - `ContactInfoEvent::{Updated(snapshot), Removed(pubkey)}`. - Channel type aliases (`ContactInfoSender`/`Receiver`). - `Crds::contact_info_sender: Option<crossbeam_channel::Sender<...>>` plus a `set_contact_info_sender` setter and a convenience accessor on `ClusterInfo`. - Three emit sites in `Crds`: - The two post-dedup acceptance arms in `Crds::insert` (vacant + occupied-overriding) emit `Updated`. - `Crds::remove` emits `Removed(pubkey)` for ContactInfo entries — covers both timeout-based purges (`CrdsGossipPull::purge_active`) and size-based trims (`ClusterInfo::trim_crds_table`) so consumers can invalidate cached endpoints rather than relying on a wallclock-staleness heuristic. - Drop-on-full by design (the dropped-event counter `gossip_contact_info_dropped` is bumped via `solana_metrics::inc_new_counter_warn!`); gossip rebroadcasts on a multi-second cadence so consumers self-heal on the next republish. `Removed` drops are less self-healing but bounded by consumer-side wallclock checks. - `ContactInfo::outset()` getter added; `ContactInfo::version()` made `pub` (was `pub(crate)`) so the snapshot's `From<&ContactInfo>` can read them. - New module `contact_info_notifier` owning the dispatch thread. - Single-shot startup replay: caller-supplied initial state is delivered with `is_startup=true` before the live stream begins. Mid-run plugin reload does *not* trigger fresh replay (documented caveat — operators reconfigure by restarting the validator). - Semantic dedup via a per-identity bounded `lazy_lru::LruCache<Pubkey, u64>` (cap 4096, ~2× the validator admission cap). Fingerprint covers sockets, shred_version, version components, and outset — *not* wallclock, so routine republishes are suppressed. Outset is in the hash so a node restart / identity transfer always surfaces a notification even if no other field happens to differ. - `semantic_fingerprint` uses an exhaustive destructure pattern, so adding a new field to `ContactInfoSnapshot` becomes a compile error unless the field is also added to (or explicitly skipped in) the fingerprint. - Single-thread dispatch: plugin callbacks run only on this thread; the gossip thread never invokes plugin code. - On `Removed`, the fingerprint cache entry is cleared so a later rejoin reliably fires an `Updated` rather than getting suppressed. - `attach()` helper returns `None` when no plugin opts in (channel never created, thread never spawned). Otherwise it sets up the channel, walks the current CRDS for initial state, and spawns the dispatcher. - `core/src/validator.rs` calls `attach()` immediately after `Arc::new(cluster_info)` and stores the resulting `Option<ContactInfoNotifier>` on the `Validator` struct so the dispatch thread lives for the validator's lifetime. When no plugin opts in: - The hot path in `Crds::insert`/`Crds::remove` adds one branch on `Option::is_some` against a sender field that stays `None`. Branch predictor pins it after the first iteration. - Zero allocations, atomics, hash lookups, or extra threads. - The new `Option<Sender>` field is 8 bytes at the end of `Crds`, on a different cache line from the hot fields. When at least one plugin opts in: - Gossip emit cost per accepted contact info insert: ~250 bytes stack memcopy + one bounded-channel `try_send` (lock-free CAS path). - Dispatch thread: one channel `recv`, one LRU lookup/insert, a semantic-fingerprint hash over plain ints, then for each opted-in plugin one `notify_contact_info` / `notify_contact_info_removed` call. No allocations on the dispatch path — version is emitted as binary fields rather than a formatted `String`. - No locks anywhere on the data path. The fingerprint cache is owned by a single thread; the channel is lock-free; the plugin manager handle is `Arc<ArcSwap<...>>`. Plugin-manager dispatch tests in `geyser-plugin-manager::contact_info_notifier::tests`: - `delivers_startup_then_live` — initial-state entries deliver with `is_startup=true` before any live updates surface. - `semantic_dedup_skips_identical_republish` — wallclock-only updates are suppressed; only socket/version changes propagate. - `skips_disabled_plugins` — plugins that didn't opt in receive no calls. - `any_plugin_opts_in_returns_correct_value` — gating helper is correct. - `removal_event_invokes_removed_callback_and_clears_fingerprint` — the Removed dispatch path delivers to the plugin's `notify_contact_info_removed` and clears the dedup cache so a subsequent rejoin re-fires `Updated`. Gossip-side tests in `gossip::contact_info_notifier::tests` and `gossip::crds::tests`: - `snapshot_from_contact_info_preserves_pubkey_and_versions` and `snapshot_from_contact_info_resolves_advertised_sockets` exercise the `From<&ContactInfo>` mapping. - `test_contact_info_sender_emits_on_insert_and_overriding_update` verifies both vacant + occupied-overriding insert arms produce `Updated` events. - `test_contact_info_sender_emits_removed_on_crds_remove` verifies `Crds::remove` produces a `Removed` event for ContactInfo entries. - `test_contact_info_sender_unattached_is_zero_overhead` guards the no-plugin case at the unit level. End-to-end verification: a separate test plugin loaded into a 2-node `LocalCluster` confirms STARTUP and LIVE events flow with real cross-validator gossip; the REMOVED dispatch path is covered by the unit tests above (CRDS timeout-based purge takes longer than the test harness's local-cluster setup). - Mid-run plugin reload does not replay current state: a plugin loaded after the dispatch thread started sees only live updates from that point forward. Documented in the public docs on `ContactInfoNotifier::spawn`. - No CLI override for channel capacity (defaults to `DEFAULT_CHANNEL_CAPACITY = 4096`); easy follow-up if operators ask. - No additional Geyser-side metrics beyond the `gossip_contact_info_dropped` overflow counter; further metrics could be added in a follow-up.

author: alessandrod
message: xdp: improve routing (#11945) * xdp: route monitor: actually drain the socket After polling for notifications, we were reading the first notification then going back to polling. We have to keep reading until we get EWOULDBLOCK instead. Fixes some cases where the table was getting stale after a notification burst. * xdp: netlink: detect truncated messages Detect truncated messages so we can trigger a full reset. * xdp: router: handle NLM_F_DUMP_INTR NLM_F_DUMP_INTR is set in flags when the dump we're parsing has been invalidated mid request. Handle it by propagating io::ErrorKind::Interrupted to callers. Make RouteMonitorState::reset handle the error by sleeping and retrying. This fixes an issue where if DZ updates their tables while we're dumping them, we used to end up with inconsistent internal state. * xdp: router: harden routing state Always rebuild the whole routing state when we detect updates, instead of trying to apply deltas on top of the previous state. This is more robust as netlink is fundamentally lossy. For example it's been observed on mnb that when running `doublezero disconnect ibrl`, sometimes the GRE link is removed without getting the corresponding RTM_DELROUTE notifications for the routes belonging to it, which used to leave routing in an inconsistent state. * xdp: router: log the routing table * xdp: netlink: turn on strict checking Without NETLINK_GET_STRICT_CHK, RTM_GETROUTE returns all the route exceptions not just the FIB table. Route exceptions are not real routes, they are internal entries kept by the kernel to keep track of per destination PMTU overrides, expiration times and other kernel-internal metadata. On mnb with DZ on, without this change the kernel returns 8k+ routes. * xdp: router: track what events trigger router rebuilds

message: Keeper, CLI: Fix Don't skip validators missing from list during directed rebalance (#290) ## Summary - Remove the skip logic in both the keeper and CLI that filtered out validators not found in the validator list during directed rebalance - The on-chain `rebalance_directed` program already handles missing validators by updating `staked_last_updated_epoch` and checking `all_targets_rebalanced_for_epoch` to advance the state machine - Skipping these validators prevented `REBALANCE_DIRECTED_COMPLETE` from being set, which could stall the steward state machine ## Test plan - [x] Verify directed rebalance completes for pools with stale entries in `DirectedStakeMeta` (validators removed from pool but still in targets) - [x] Confirm steward state transitions past `RebalanceDirected` when all targets include validators not in the validator list

author: aoikurokawa
message: Keeper: Re-upload BAM status on every run within an epoch (#281) ## Problem - The `is_uploaded` filter in `CopyIsBamConnectedOperation` prevented re-submitting a validator's BAM status once it had been written for the current epoch. Since a validator's BAM connection can change mid-epoch and the keeper runs 3 times per epoch (at 30%, 60%, 90%), the filter caused stale data — a validator that disconnected from BAM after the first run would still appear connected for the rest of the epoch. ## Solution - Remove the `is_uploaded` filter so every keeper run re-submits the latest BAM status from the Kobe API for all validators. This ensures mid-epoch BAM status changes are captured on-chain, which is important now that BAM scoring uses a "X of last Y epochs" window rather than requiring continuous connectivity.

author: AvhiMaz
message: fix: re-enable test_scheduler_drop_idle by resolving race condition (#9042) * fix: re-enable test_scheduler_drop_idle by resolving race condition Remove #[ignore] attribute and fix timing to eliminate race condition in test_scheduler_drop_idle, which was disabled in PR #8278. The test verifies the scheduler pool's cleaner thread correctly removes idle schedulers while preserving recently-pooled ones. Root cause: The original test used a 100ms idle threshold with 1000ms sleep, but timing was still unreliable due to system variations. The race occurred when old_scheduler and new_scheduler had unclear age differences. Fix: - Use explicit 300ms idle threshold for this test (instead of 100ms) - Sleep 350ms before returning new_scheduler (provides 50ms+ safety margin) - This guarantees old_scheduler is idle while new_scheduler is not Result: - old_scheduler: 350ms old (> 300ms threshold) → definitely idle → removed - new_scheduler: ~0ms old (< 300ms threshold) → definitely not idle → kept - Test is now deterministic and matches expected checkpoint sequence Fixes #8279 Signed-off-by: AvhiMaz <avhimazumder5@outlook.com> * Address all reviewer feedback on test_scheduler_drop_idle - Move SHORTENED_MAX_POOLING_DURATION constant to test_scheduler_drop_stale where it's used - Convert test_max_pooling_duration from let to const TEST_MAX_POOLING_DURATION following conventions - Create TEST_WAIT_FOR_IDLE constant (500ms) with explicit safety margin tied to TEST_MAX_POOLING_DURATION - Increase safety margin from 50ms to 200ms for CI reliability - Add detailed comments explaining 300ms pooling duration tradeoff (speed vs race condition window) - Update assertion comment with explicit timing guarantees: old_scheduler ~500ms old (exceeds 300ms threshold), new_scheduler ~50ms old (below threshold) Signed-off-by: AvhiMaz <avhimazumder5@outlook.com> * refactor: tie test duration constants together and improve comment accuracy Signed-off-by: AvhiMaz <avhimazumder5@outlook.com> * fix: cargo fmt Signed-off-by: AvhiMaz <avhimazumder5@outlook.com> --------- Signed-off-by: AvhiMaz <avhimazumder5@outlook.com>

author: haydenshively
message: feat(stores): add TtlStore decorator (#46) Closes APPS-583 ## What Adds `TtlStore`, a decorator that gives any wrapped `Store` an **absolute TTL**. This upstreams the ad-hoc `TtlLruStore` that was duplicated verbatim across the `curator-v2-app` and `markets-app` (whose `stores/index` carried a `// TODO: Add TtlStore`), and hardens it into a general-purpose primitive. ```ts import { HierarchicalStore, LruStore, TtlStore } from '@morpho-org/viem-dlc/stores' // TTL-bounded in-memory tier fronting a shared remote const store = new HierarchicalStore( [new TtlStore(new LruStore(100_000_000), { ttlMs: 60_000 }), remote], { populateOnMiss: true }, ) ``` ## Why upstream / what the ad-hoc version got wrong The ad-hoc copies kept a parallel `insertedAt: Map` for TTL stamps. That map was only pruned when a key was read again or explicitly deleted — but the wrapped `LruStore` evicts values internally under byte pressure **without notifying the wrapper**. Under high-cardinality keys, stamps for evicted/expired entries accumulate **indefinitely**, growing memory outside the intended cache cap. That defeats the whole point of a store built for bounded memory in prod. ## Design - **Leak-free by construction.** The write timestamp rides *inside* the value as a small header, so it is counted against — and evicted with — the wrapped store's own cap. No side table; nothing to prune. Memory is bounded by the wrapped store alone. - **Framing-robust.** `get` reassembles values that the wrapped store rechunks or collapses (`UpstashStore.get` returns a single buffer; `CompressedStore` collapses framing), with a **zero-copy fast path** when framing is preserved (`LruStore`/`MemoryStore`) so even massive values are copy-free on read. - **Foreign-value safe.** The header carries a magic marker, so a value this store didn't write (a pre-existing entry in a persistent store, or one from another consumer sharing the wrapped store) is recognized and reported as a miss rather than misread. - **Sync/async passthrough.** Wrapping a synchronous `LruStore` stays synchronous; wrapping an async store returns promises. - **No delete on expiry.** A read past `ttlMs` reports a miss and leaves the stale bytes for the wrapped store to overwrite/evict. Deleting on expiry could race a concurrent `set` on an async store and clobber a fresh write (the `Store` interface has no compare-and-delete). Cleanup is free (overwritten on next `set`) and bounded (wrapped store's cap). - **Absolute TTL.** Stamped at `set`, never refreshed on `get` — bounds how long this tier may diverge from a fresher source behind it. Uses `Date.now()`, so a serverless freeze/thaw safely expires warm entries early — the exact behavior APPS-583 asks for. - **Robust config.** Rejects non-finite `ttlMs` (`NaN`/`Infinity` would silently disable expiry). - Best-effort and non-throwing, per the `Store` contract. ## Tests `test/stores/ttl.test.ts` (18 tests): core TTL behavior, the `> ttlMs` boundary, `ttlMs` validation (incl. `NaN`/`Infinity`), the zero-copy fast path (by-reference return), framing reassembly over a byte-per-buffer rechunking store, too-short/foreign entry → miss, no-delete-on-expiry (sync + async), sync/async passthrough, and the `HierarchicalStore`-fronting-a-remote coherence scenario. Full store suite green (86 tests); `tsc` and biome clean. ## Follow-up (separate, in the apps) Migrate the apps off the local copies: replace `new TtlLruStore({ maxBytes, ttlMs })` with `new TtlStore(new LruStore(maxBytes), { ttlMs })`, import from `@morpho-org/viem-dlc/stores`, and delete both local files + specs. (Their sync-only copies are race-free today; the migration hands them the race-free no-delete behavior automatically.) 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- --------- Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context)

author: haydenshively
message: fix(midnight-liquidation): address review findings on the whitelist union Keeps production single-source (the public endpoint) and lets staging hold the superset — staging then exercises the endpoint production depends on without production spending real capital on markets whitelisted for testing. The union mechanism stays; only the intended deployment differs, and the README no longer tells operators to set the same value everywhere. Silent-failure fixes: - Report `markets.whitelist_expired` per tick from `discover` again, instead of once per refresh. The whitelist expires on LISTED_MARKETS_MAX_AGE_MS but was only re-checked on MARKETS_REFRESH_MS, which is unbounded — a longer interval (or a wedged refresh loop) left a total liquidation halt unreported for most of each interval, visible only as `discover.filtered { listed: 0 }`. - Throw when no markets source is configured. An empty union lists nothing, logs nothing, and is indistinguishable from a working fail-closed whitelist. - Warn `markets.listed_empty` when a source goes from some listed markets to none. A successful-but-empty response is authoritative, so it replaces last-known-good — and in a union a healthy peer would mask it entirely. - Restore the startup `tryCatch`: a first-fetch failure must not be fatal, and the comment claiming "non-fatal by construction" contradicted the code. - Emit `markets.refresh_error` at error, not warn — it means the union's non-throwing contract broke, which is not an API blip. Correctness and observability: - `current()` freezes the fresh-source set for one discovery pass, so a pass is judged against one staleness reading rather than re-deriving it per candidate. - Log the deduplicated union size as `markets.whitelist`. Per-source `markets.listed` counts overlap, so they can be neither summed nor maxed into the combined number. - Label a source by host AND path, so two sources on one host stay distinguishable; de-duplicate `MARKETS_API_URL` on the parsed URL so trivially different spellings of one endpoint are not polled and counted twice. Docs: correct the claim that EXCLUDE_COLLATERALS vetoes an added source (it is collateral-scoped, and every listed market shares one collateral), note that LISTED_MARKETS_MAX_AGE_MS is a build-time constant rather than a knob, and warn that rolling back past this release with a list-valued var will crash-loop. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: haydenshively
message: feat(midnight-liquidation): union the market whitelist across sources Staging and prod pointed at different Midnight markets APIs (api.morpho.dev vs api.morpho.org), so the two deployments disagreed about which external service defines the market whitelist. The dev list is a strict superset of prod's — the same 6 markets plus 13 daily-maturity test markets — and the liquidation-candidates endpoint is byte-identical across both hosts, so the whitelist was the only real difference. `MARKETS_API_URL` now accepts a comma-separated list of endpoints, and the whitelist is the union across them. Both deployments can then hold the same value: the difference becomes which markets are listed, not which API is trusted, and staging finally exercises the endpoint prod depends on. The max-age staleness rule is applied PER SOURCE, which is what makes reading two endpoints safe in both directions: a source that goes down or goes stale drops out of the union (markets.source_expired) instead of either emptying the whitelist and halting all liquidations, or letting a stale set keep a since-delisted market in scope. Only when every source is stale is the whitelist empty (markets.whitelist_expired, fail-closed). `refresh` fans out concurrently and never throws — a per-source failure keeps that source's last-known-good and still lands its healthy peers, because a partial refresh must not read as a total one. The default stays the single public endpoint: an additional source widens what the bot will spend real capital on, so it is opt-in per deployment rather than shipped in the default. A single-URL value parses exactly as before. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: jinmel
message: feat(monitor-bot): poll make orders from the global book (#7) * feat(monitor-bot): poll make orders from the global book The make-orders poller read /v0/midnight/users/{user}/offer-groups, a per-maker endpoint that forced a WATCH_MAKERS allowlist and registered no poller at all when the var was unset — so out of the box the bot watched no make orders. It now reads the protocol-wide book: /v0/midnight/books supplies the active-market universe plus top price levels, and each market's populated sides expand through books/{id}/{side}/takeable-offers into individual signed offers. No maker allowlist; MARKET_IDS still scopes it via the books `ids` filter. WATCH_MAKERS is removed. Takeable offers carry no server-side id and an offer is an immutable EIP-712 signature, so identity is the tuple that survives a re-sign: (market, side, maker, group, tick), with offers sharing it summed into one bucket. A re-sign at a new size therefore reads as `resized` rather than closed+created. Expiry and the takeable `units` field are excluded from the comparison — both churn constantly, and takes are already the transaction pollers' surface. Introduce BootSnapshot as a state concept distinct from Cursor. The book has no change feed, so there is no position to resume from: the state IS the previous observation and items come from diffing it. Calling that a cursor was wrong. The base Poller now depends on a neutral PollerStateStore; CursorStore (resume position) and BootSnapshotStore (boot-scoped observation) keep separate types and DI tokens, because a boot snapshot must never be persisted — a stale one diffed against live data would report every change made while the process was down as if it had just happened. Truncation is treated as failure rather than data, since a truncated snapshot fabricates `closed` events and re-fabricates `created` next tick: takeable-offers at its 1000-offer cap fails that market, a runaway books listing aborts the tick, and the `ids` path asserts no cursor came back. The empty-side skip is conditional on the side also being empty last tick. Levels are aggregated *executable* liquidity from a different endpoint than the offers, and takeable-offers retains non-executable offers with units 0, so a side can report zero levels while its offers still stand — skipping unconditionally would close every bucket on it and re-open them all next tick. Known limitation, documented rather than hidden: the books list response carries only the top 3 levels per side, so FILTER_MIN_ASSETS can size unit-capped offers only at those ticks. Unpriced buckets pass the filter rather than being dropped — a wrong drop loses an alert permanently, a wrong pass is only noise. * test(monitor-bot): unit-test the snapshot diff directly Cover the diff between the stored and freshly fetched snapshot on its own, independent of fetching, pagination and alert formatting: only buckets absent from the stored snapshot surface as `created`, and ones present in both with identical signed caps are filtered out. Export diffSnapshots (plus OfferBucket/MarketSnapshot) for this, the same way format.ts and filter.ts expose their pure helpers. The poller remains its only production caller. Cases: new-only extraction from a multi-bucket snapshot, an identical snapshot producing nothing, an empty stored snapshot making everything new, non-cap churn (count/expiry) producing nothing, created/resized/ closed separated in one mixed diff, same group at a different tick counting as new, and assets sizing present/null by tick price.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> * feat(midnight-liquidation): backport typed openapi discovery client Rewrite midnight discovery from hand-built URLs + manual parseJsonResponse to typed openapi-fetch clients over two generated, dependency-free spec files (src/generated/markets-api.ts, src/generated/midnight-api.ts). State lives under BOT_STATE_DIR (default ~/.morpho-bots), namespaced by bot + chain. - onSettled hook + outcome journal: terminal settlements (confirm / revert / drop) append as JSONL to outcomes-<chain>.jsonl. - sendAborted latch: a hashless TxSendError blocks further sends until the next onBlock settlement pass clears the latch. - value threaded into the pre-send simulation call so the sim matches the broadcast byte-for-byte. - Periodic signer.balance metric (BALANCE_EVERY_BLOCKS=30, ~60s) so operators see EOA gas drain. Persistence + journal are on by default with sensible default paths. Existing settled-cooldown dedup and backoff are preserved. Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> * feat(bot-kit): backport default-deny signing policy guard Re-embed the daemon-era signer's default-deny authorization as an in-process pre-broadcast guard. Between prepare and send, every transaction is checked against the bot's policy and rejected — logging signer.policy_violation (error) and throwing, never broadcasting — unless it: - targets the configured Executor (`to` == executor), - calls exec_606BaXt (selector 0x00000001), - carries zero value (hard invariant), - and stays under the maxFeePerGas / gas / calldata-size ceilings. The fee ceiling reuses the bot's existing MAX_FEE_GWEI (config.maxFeeWei); gas (15M) and calldata (65536 bytes) ceilings are constants matching the daemon-era defaults. A violation means an upstream encoding bug, not a retry case, so the claimed nonce is rolled back and nothing is sent. Both bots thread their Executor + ceilings in. The daemon-era recovered-sender and prepared-vs-signed field assertions are skipped: in-process there is no remote signer to distrust, so the prepared-request guard covers the same fields as cheap defense-in-depth. Unlike the retired single-image (evm-kit, all-stderr) design, @repo/bot-kit's createLogger splits levels: info/warn/debug -> stdout, error -> stderr. Almost every operational event (tx.sent, tx.confirmed, signer.balance) is info/warn, so BOTH streams are spooled. Vector's VRL stamps bot/chainId/RAILWAY_* per line; blue's two chains share one source discriminated by those fields. LIQUIDATOR_PRIVATE_KEY is scrubbed from Vector's env so the shipper never sees the signing key; the spool stays off any persistent volume. Each Dockerfile bot stage bakes the pinned Vector 0.57.0 binary, a build-time `vector --version` link check, and a `vector validate` step (dummy creds + --no-environment) so a config/VRL typo fails the build. vector.yaml lives per-bot to match the per-bot Dockerfile/ compose philosophy. compose and deploy-railway.ts pass BETTERSTACK_* through (host = plain var, token = secret) when set. Machinery only, inert without the token: creating BetterStack sources/dashboards remains a deploy-time step (TIB-2026-07-14 phase 2). Settlement audit is already covered by the structured tx.* log events (now shipped to BetterStack in-process via loglayer), so the file-based outcomes journal was redundant. Return to the baseline design: queue state is in-memory only and chain truth wins on restart. - Remove src/state.ts (saveState/loadState/botStatePaths, BOT_STATE_DIR, QUEUE_STATE_VERSION/QueueState) and src/queue/journal.ts (createOutcomeJournal), plus their tests. - Remove dump(), initialState, onSettled, PendingQueueState, Settlement, and SettlementStatus from the pending queue; simplify settle() back to the baseline (blockNumber-only). Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix(bot-kit): latch sends after dropping an unconsumed nonce replaceStuck retires entries on fee_ceiling, max_bump_attempts, and reverts_on_replace while the ORIGINAL broadcast still sits unconsumed at that nonce in the mempool. The signer's cursor keeps allocating N+1, N+2..., none of which can mine until the hole is filled, and nonce resync only happens on an empty queue — so a hole below a still-pending entry accumulates unminable future-nonce sends. Add a nonce-hole latch, independent of the sendAborted latch: - The three replaceStuck drop paths record the dropped-but-unconsumed nonce as a hole (span [low, high]). Reconciler drop(_, 'nonce_consumed') retirements are by definition already consumed, so they never latch. - While latched, submit() refuses NEW first-sends (queue.nonce_hole) and returns; replacement/fee-bumps of existing entries reuse their own nonce and continue. - Clears every onBlock once the chain's consumed nonce advances past the HIGHEST dropped nonce (proving every dropped nonce is mined), OR when the queue empties and syncNonce re-derives the cursor from chain truth. Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix(bots): run queue maintenance independently of tick work Pending-queue maintenance (queue.onBlock) ran at the END of each bot's tick, after discovery/lens/quotes/simulation/submission. A sustained discovery-API / database / lens-RPC outage throws the tick, and the runner swallows it without driving the queue — so receipt checks, fee replacement, nonce reconciliation, and latch clearing all starve exactly when infrastructure is degraded and transactions are already in flight. Make maintenance an independent block-lifecycle phase: - createRunner accepts an optional `maintain(height)` run BEFORE the tick in its own try/catch; its failure logs queue.maintenance_failed and is swallowed, and the tick runs regardless. Before-the-tick ordering makes the guarantee structural rather than a per-bot convention. - Both bots move queue.onBlock + balanceMonitor.maybeLog off the tick (dropping the pendingOnBlock dep) and into `maintain`. Ordering note: maintenance now sees a block before that tick's new submissions (previously after). Stuck-detection ages absolutely (blockNumber - submittedAtBlock), so a tx submitted at H is first maintained at H+1 with age 1 and its bump timing is unchanged; only the inert age-0 pass is dropped. Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix(bot-kit): warn loudly on partial betterstack config betterStackTransport returned null silently when exactly one of BETTERSTACK_SOURCE_TOKEN / BETTERSTACK_INGESTING_HOST was set, so a provisioning mistake would silently drop external observability while the bot looked healthy. TIB-2026-07-14's opt-in contract requires token-without-host (and vice versa) to FAIL LOUD. Both-unset stays fully inert (the opt-out). Exactly-one-set now emits a structured logship.misconfigured stderr line naming the missing var and still returns null (ship nothing; never crash the bot over observability config). Written via console.error like the transport's onError to avoid recursing through loglayer. TIB addendum updated to note partial config now fails loud in-process. Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix(swaps): pin 1inch swaps to the known per-chain router The 1inch adapter accepted the API-supplied swap `tx.to` verbatim, so a compromised/misdirected response could point the swap — and its token approval — at an arbitrary contract, even though the repo already knows the expected AggregationRouterV6 per chain (ONEINCH_ROUTER). After parsing a quote we now assert `tx.to === ONEINCH_ROUTER[chainId]` (isAddressEqual). A mismatch is treated like any other invalid response: throw QuoteError with both addresses, which the quoting layer logs as `quote.failed` detail — never past the venue seam. `spender` was already pinned (hardcoded to the static router, never read from the response); 1inch semantics make tx.to === spender, so pinning tx.to keeps the call target and approval in lockstep on the known contract. No lookup tables added for 0x / LiFi / LiquidSwap, which route through per-chain/per-quote contracts with no static expectation. Also documents two review-acknowledged scopings that belong with this code: policy.ts is an outer-envelope guard (does not decode the inner bytes[] program — inner-call integrity rests on venue handling, quote validation, and pre-send simulation); pending-queue treats a one-block receipt as terminal, accepted for the target L2s (Base, Robinhood / Arbitrum-Orbit). Both recorded in TIB-2026-07-16. author: haydenshively
message: feat(swaps): add pendle pt unwrapper (#70) Pendle Principal Tokens now unwrap to their underlying before the venue swap: expired PTs redeem (yt-addressed, aggregator off), active PTs swap through the Pendle AMM — both as fixed-amount Router steps with a USDT-safe approve pair. Detection rides a per-chain markets list (6h TTL, success-only caching with stale-on-failure, dump/restored via the op cache) and the unwrapper is only constructed on PENDLE_CHAIN_IDS. The downstream sell is sized by amountOut x (1 - PENDLE_SLIPPAGE_BPS) as a conservative floor estimate; simulation stays the real guarantee. Pendle joins the HTTP client as an HttpVenue host, not a Venue. CRTR-2804 (PR 2 of 2, stacked on the unwrap seam). Co-authored-by: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: Foulks-Plb
message: fix(evm-simulation): block native ETH retained by bundler3 on Tenderly (#865) `assertNoBundlerRetention` only inspected parsed `Transfer` logs, so native ETH retained by a bundler3 address slipped through the guard on the Tenderly primary backend: native ETH emits no event log, and Tenderly derives it into `assetChanges` rather than synthetic transfer logs (Cantina finding 1440). The check now reads native ETH from `assetChanges` (the cross-backend source of truth) while keeping ERC20/WETH retention from transfer logs. Native transfer logs (the `eth_simulateV1` synthetic sentinel) only backfill bundler endpoints absent from `assetChanges`, so native moves are never double-counted on `eth_simulateV1`. Adds regression tests proving the Tenderly-only path throws and the `eth_simulateV1` path counts native ETH exactly once. Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
