author: haydenshively
message: feat(blue-liquidation): add Morpho Blue ecosystem-backstop liquidator (#21) * feat(blue-liquidation): add Morpho Blue ecosystem-backstop liquidator A non-competitive, backstop liquidator for Morpho Blue on Base, mirroring the midnight-liquidation bot's architecture with Blue-specific deltas: - Discovery via a co-located rindexer indexing CreateMarket + Borrow. - A soltag deployless lens that simulates IRM accrual (borrowRateView + Taylor) and re-derives id = keccak256(abi.encode(params)) before health. - Seize-exact sizing (min(collateral, seizeForFullDebt)); the repaidShares <= borrowShares underflow safety is proved by a brute-force sweep. - Multi-venue callback swaps (uniswap-v3 / 0x / 1inch) via the vendored generic Executor's native onMorphoLiquidate; dual-skim full-drain. - Signer + in-memory nonce queue with EIP-1559 bumps; Railway topology. Also vendors IMorpho.sol + MorphoAbi into @repo/contracts, and hoists the deployless batch-lens helper into @repo/utils (repointing midnight). Read path validated against 256 live Base positions; lens gas model measured on a Base fork. Full liquidate-broadcast fork suite is fixture-gated (needs a live-unhealthy position). Includes the design TIB. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix(blue-liquidation): align discovery SQL with rindexer schema Fixes surfaced by the first Railway deploy to the bot.liquidation.blue project (the startup discovery.schema diagnostic did its job): - discovery: rindexer flattens the CreateMarket MarketParams tuple with a market_params_ prefix (market_params_loan_token, ...), not the bare field names the join assumed. Every tick failed with "column cm.loan_token does not exist". Select the prefixed columns, aliased back to the bare names so parseCandidate is unchanged; lock the real names into the test. - discovery: probeTable now parses a string row count (Bun returns count(*)::bigint as a decimal string), so discovery.schema reports real row counts instead of null. - deploy-railway: pass -e/-p explicitly to `railway up` and `railway deployment list` -- `railway link` does not carry the environment into the non-TTY subprocess, so `up` failed with "No environment specified". - bunfig: preload blue-liquidation's soltag transform for `bun test` at the repo root (was only midnight's), so the deployless lens tests compile there. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix(blue-liquidation): recover market params via idToMarketParams no-code rindexer cannot decode the CreateMarket event's nested MarketParams struct (it panics "CustomStruct ... not supported" and crash-loops), so the bot can no longer index CreateMarket. Verified on the live Base singleton that idToMarketParams(id) exists and returns the exact params, so: - rindexer indexes ONLY Borrow (rindexer.yaml); the distinct (id, onBehalf) set is the full candidate universe. - state/market-params.ts recovers each market's immutable params on-chain via a Multicall3 batch of idToMarketParams(id), cached by id (params never change per id), so steady-state ticks make no extra RPC calls once markets are known. - discovery/borrowers.ts: discoverBorrowerIds (distinct id+borrower, no join) + discoverCandidates (composes ids with the injected resolver); diagnostics simplified to the borrow table only. - The lens is UNCHANGED: it still re-derives keccak256(abi.encode(params)) as an id-commitment check, so on-chain-sourced params are belt-and-suspenders safe. This revises the TIB's Alternative-1 (params ARE retrievable from the singleton). rindexer.yaml also sets max_block_range: 150000 for the /cache backfill endpoint (avoids the /realtime range-limit fallback that starved indexing). Reviewed via the reviewer agent (must-fix stale lens comment addressed). Also includes a documentation/comment pass across the bot, a TIB revision, and a fork-fixture test harness (test/fork/harness.test.ts). Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * feat(blue-liquidation): add multi-chain support (robinhood) Run the bot across chains from one shared rindexer + Postgres, adding Robinhood (4663) beside Base. rindexer indexes all chains into one borrow table with a network column; discovery and the lag query filter candidates by network. One bot-<chainId> service per chain (chainId-suffixed secrets), and the legacy single-chain bot service is retired after cutover. 0x serves Robinhood, so example.json wires its four market collaterals. Also polls getCode after deploy:executor to avoid an RPC read-lag false negative. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix(blue-liquidation): scope deploy volume check to the service ensureVolume matched only the mount path against the environment-wide volume list, so every bot after the first — and after a deleted service left an orphaned /config volume — skipped provisioning and got no volume. Match (serviceName, mountPath) so each bot gets its own /config. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix(blue-liquidation): route base collaterals via 0x instead of 1inch The example config routed 4 Base collaterals through 1inch, which needs ONEINCH_API_KEY; with only a 0x key set, the bot fails loud at startup. 0x covers Base broadly, so route them via 0x (no new key); unrouted pairs still fail-closed at simulate. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * docs(blue-liquidation): document multi-chain deploy in readme Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> --------- Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: Foulks-Plb
message: feat(morpho-sdk)!: native ETH wrapping in Blue repay (#840) * feat(morpho-sdk): native ETH wrapping in Blue repay actions Add optional native (wNative) wrapping to the two Blue repay flows (actions + entity). Assets mode is additive like blueSupply; shares mode carves native out of transferAmount. Replaces validateRepayParams with the pure resolveRepayAmounts helper; adds a new typed error. Adapts wdk-protocol-lending-morpho-evm to the renamed amount field. Breaking: major bump. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * refactor(morpho-sdk): share repay test permit fixture, deprecate dead error Dedupe the makePermit fixture from both repay action tests into test/helpers/permit.ts. Mark the now-unthrown TransferAmountNotEqualToAssetsError @deprecated; assets mode is additive. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * refactor(morpho-sdk): flatten repay action args, resolve amounts upstream blueRepay / blueRepayWithdrawCollateral now take a flat, pre-resolved RepayActionAmountArgs: { amount?, shares?, nativeAmount?, transferAmount }. The action does no amount arithmetic. Assets mode: repay transferAmount (= amount + native), pull amount. Shares mode: repay shares, pull transferAmount (net of native), skim residual. MorphoBlue.repay / repayWithdrawCollateral derive these from live state and pass them flat. Remove resolveRepayAmounts; deprecate NonPositiveTransferAmountError (no longer thrown). Entity public API (RepayAmountArgs) unchanged. Docs + major changeset updated. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix(morpho-sdk): reject negative repay amounts consistently across entity + action The flatten refactor left the negative-amount guards asymmetric. The entity's assets mode never checked `amount < 0n`, so a negative amount masked by a larger nativeAmount reached getRequirements as a negative approval while only buildTx threw. The action never checked shares-mode `transferAmount < 0n`, silently skipping the ERC-20 pull and returning a malformed frozen tx. Both now raise NonPositiveRepayAmountError. Also broadens the `@throws` docs and corrects the `@example` scale comment (0.5/0.2, not 500/200), per the PR review. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * test(morpho-sdk): add native ETH repay fork integration tests Adds Anvil fork round-trips for a fully-native repay and repayWithdrawCollateral on WstethWethBlue (loanToken === wNative), mirroring the supply native fork test. The native wrap+repay path was previously covered only by transport-mocked unit tests; per AGENTS.md §5 the onchain round-trip must be Anvil-verified at a pinned block. Requires MAINNET_RPC_URL (archive) — runs in CI, not offline. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * test(wdk-protocol-lending-morpho-evm): align repay assertion with renamed amount field The Blue repay reshape renamed the entity's `assets` param to `amount` and the adapter source was updated to match, but this mock assertion still expected `{ assets: 100_000n }`. Update it to `{ amount: 100_000n }` so the asset-repay unit test matches the call the adapter now makes. Test-only; no changeset. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * docs(morpho-sdk): align repay README example with the renamed amount arg The repay reshape renamed the entity arg `assets` -> `amount`, but the README Repay section still showed `market.repay({ assets: ... })`, so the public example no longer compiled. Rename it to `amount` and note the optional `nativeAmount`. The Withdraw section keeps `assets` (unchanged). Docs-only. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * test(morpho-sdk): cover native repayWithdrawCollateral + shares-native repay at the entity Mirrors the four repay-native entity tests for repayWithdrawCollateral (non-wNative rejection, assets-mode wrap buildTx, fully-native no-requirement, shares-mode exceeds rejection) and adds a positive shares-native repay buildTx case, closing the entity-layer coverage asymmetry the local review flagged. Tests-only. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * docs(tibs): record Blue repay native-wrapping + flat-args design (TIB-2026-07-02) Retrospectively documents the design shipped in PR #840: native ETH wrapping in blueRepay / blueRepayWithdrawCollateral, the entity-resolved flat action args (RepayActionAmountArgs), the additive assets mode vs shares-mode native carve-out, and the removal of validateRepayParams in favour of arithmetic-free actions. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix(morpho-sdk): validate repay action funding to prevent stranded/underfunded bundles blueRepay / blueRepayWithdrawCollateral are exported builders; a direct caller passing self-inconsistent pre-resolved args could strand over-pulled loan tokens on GeneralAdapter1 (assets mode has no skim) or encode an under/unfunded repay that reverts. Restore the guard the flatten reshape dropped: assets mode requires transferAmount === amount + nativeAmount (TransferAmountNotEqualToAssetsError, un-deprecated), shares mode requires positive funding (transferAmount + nativeAmount > 0n). The entity path already satisfies both. Addresses the Codex review P2 comments on PR #840. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * docs: fix repayWithdrawCollateral README example + record action funding guards in TIB The README repayWithdrawCollateral example still used the pre-rename `assets` arg (the repay example was fixed earlier); update it to `amount`. Update TIB-2026-07-02 so the action-level funding/consistency guards read as adopted (not deferred) after the Codex + local review corroboration. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * docs(tibs): correct stale deprecation note for TransferAmountNotEqualToAssetsError The action funding guard added in a04a17aa re-wired TransferAmountNotEqualToAssetsError to be thrown in assets mode (transferAmount === amount + nativeAmount), but the TIB's "Why validateRepayParams is removed" section and Phase 1 note still listed it among the "dead" @deprecated errors. Only NonPositiveTransferAmountError is deprecated/unthrown; correct both mentions so the design doc matches the shipped error surface. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * chore(liquidity-sdk-viem): bump morpho-sdk peer to ^5.0.0 for the SDK major Per root AGENTS.md §7 peer-dependent audit: the morpho-sdk major bump in this changeset requires updating maintained dependents that peer on it. liquidity-sdk-viem consumes morpho-sdk at runtime (PublicReallocation / ReallocationData in loader.ts) but its peer range was stuck at ^3.0.0 (predating the 4.x line and not admitting the new 5.x). Widen to ^5.0.0 to match the released major, matching the single-caret convention used by its sibling peers, and add a patch changeset entry for liquidity-sdk-viem. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * refactor(morpho-sdk): extract shared repay funding helpers Deduplicate the funding block that was byte-identical (modulo comments) between blueRepay and blueRepayWithdrawCollateral into two encode-only @internal helpers colocated in actions/blue/: - resolveRepayFunding: shared guards + assets/shares mode discrimination + funding validation, returning { isSharesMode, repayAssets, repayShares, erc20Amount }. - buildRepayFundingActions: the nativeTransfer -> wrapNative -> ERC-20 pull composition, returning a fresh Action[] (mirrors buildReallocationActions; no input-argument mutation, per AGENTS.md section 2.4). Removes the correctness-sensitive divergence risk flagged in review (a funding-math fix could land in one builder but not the other). Behavior-preserving: single source of truth, same bundle ordering, same thrown errors. Addresses PR #840 review discussion_r3518583363. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * test(morpho-sdk): cover native-mix repay round-trips e2e Add Anvil fork round-trips for the native repay funding paths that were only build-tested until now, on WstethWethBlue (loan token = wNative): - repay / repayWithdrawCollateral, assets mode, partial native + ERC-20 (additive): asserts the approval covers only `amount`, tx.value is the native part, Morpho receives amount + nativeAmount, and only the ERC-20 portion leaves the user's WETH balance. - repay / repayWithdrawCollateral, shares mode, partial native (net of native): asserts a positive ERC-20 remainder is still pulled, tx.value is the native part, the position fully closes (and all collateral is withdrawn for the repayWithdrawCollateral case). testInvariants also enforces that bundler3 holds no stranded tokens. Only the assets + fully-native path was exercised e2e before. PR #840. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * test(morpho-sdk): pin entity shares+native repay carve-out Address the coverage gap on the shares-mode native carve-out (erc20Amount = borrowAssets - nativeAmount) in the entity tests: - Strengthen the repay shares+native happy path: assert the action transferAmount equals borrowAssets and getRequirements() approves exactly borrowAssets - nativeAmount (was the weak transferAmount > nativeAmount). - Add the mirror repayWithdrawCollateral shares+native happy path, which had no build-level coverage at the entity layer. borrowAssets is computed as toBorrowAssets(shares, "Up") on the snapshot; the fixture has no rateAtTarget so accrual is a no-op, keeping the expectation deterministic. PR #840 review discussion_r3518708483. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * refactor(morpho-sdk): unify Blue funding prefix in buildAssetFundingActions Rename buildRepayFundingActions -> buildAssetFundingActions and generalize it to the shared native-wrap + ERC-20-pull prefix that every bundled Blue funding path emits before its Morpho call. The helper now takes `asset: Address` instead of `marketParams`, and drops the redundant explicit erc20TransferFrom branch: getTokenRequirementActions already emits that action itself when no permit/permit2 signature is supplied. Wired into all 5 Blue builders (previously 2), making it the single source of truth for the funding prefix: - blueSupply / blueSupplyCollateral / blueSupplyCollateralBorrow - blueRepay / blueRepayWithdrawCollateral Behavior-preserving: each builder emits a byte-identical Action[] for all inputs, so the encoded bundles are unchanged (76 unit + 52 fork e2e green). Vault deposits are intentionally left out — they throw the distinct public NativeAmountOnNonWNativeVaultError, so folding them in would change that error contract. The two repay unit tests that asserted getTokenRequirementActions was not called without a signature now assert the unified routing (called once, with requirementSignature undefined); the observable erc20TransferFrom is proven by the fork round-trips. Internal @internal helper, public surface unchanged: no changeset. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * test(morpho-sdk): typecheck repay funding spy assertions The two rewritten repay / repayWithdrawCollateral spy assertions indexed `spy.mock.calls[0][0]` directly, which fails `tsc --noEmit` under noUncheckedIndexedAccess (TS2532: object possibly undefined). The CI build step type-checks test files, so it broke the build even though vitest — which strips types rather than checking them — ran green locally. Read the first call's args through optional chaining (`spy.mock.calls[0]?.[0]`) instead. No behavior change; the assertions themselves are unchanged. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * chore(morpho-sdk): release Blue repay native wrapping as a minor Downgrade the repay-native-wrapping changeset from major to minor. With #821 already shipping morpho-sdk 5.0.0, this is now the sole pending changeset, so the next release is 5.1.0. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> --------- Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: Foulks-Plb
message: feat(morpho-sdk): integrate setAuthorizationWithSig with array buildTx (#833) * feat(morpho-sdk): integrate setAuthorizationWithSig and array buildTx Add offchain setAuthorizationWithSig support for Morpho Blue bundled paths. When supportSignature is enabled, the authorization requirement becomes a signable Requirement folded into the bundle as setAuthorizationWithSig, replacing the standalone setAuthorization transaction. Entity buildTx now accepts an array of signatures (permit + authorization). Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * test(morpho-sdk): cover signed-authorization path + fix changeset/docs Address PR review feedback: - Add fork test for the in-bundle setAuthorizationWithSig borrow path (sign authorization requirement -> buildTx([sig]) -> single bundle tx). - Add colocated unit tests for isPermitSignature / isAuthorizationSignature. - Include @morpho-org/liquidity-sdk-viem in the changeset and bump its morpho-sdk peer range ^3.0.0 -> ^5.0.0 (the prior range no longer matched the published major). - Fix stale @returns JSDoc on getBorrowRequirements. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * feat(morpho-sdk): harden buildTx signature array + pin authorization to GeneralAdapter1 Address the risk of an arbitrary, unvalidated signature array driving GeneralAdapter1 transfers: - getAuthorizationAction(chainId, signature) now pins `authorized` to the chain's GeneralAdapter1 and throws BundlerErrors.UnexpectedSignature for any other target — the bundle can never grant Morpho operator rights to an unintended address (the previous guard only blocked Bundler3). - selectRequirementSignatures replaces the silent `.find` split in every entity buildTx: it rejects more than one signature of a kind, or a kind the path does not consume, via the new AmbiguousRequirementSignaturesError / UnexpectedRequirementSignatureError instead of dropping extras silently. - Unit tests for both guards and the new selector; getAuthorizationAction test covers the non-GeneralAdapter1 rejection. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * feat(wdk-protocol-lending-morpho-evm): plumb borrow authorization signature into buildTx getBorrowRequirements advertised a signable authorization requirement when supportSignature is enabled, but borrow/quoteBorrow built the bundle with a bare buildTx() and no way to feed the signed authorization back. Add a requirementSignature field to MorphoBorrowOptions, plumbed through _getBorrowTransaction, mirroring the supply/repay paths, so the signed setAuthorizationWithSig is folded into the same bundle instead of requiring a separate setAuthorization transaction. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * test(morpho-sdk): fix supplyCollateralBorrow fork tests for signable authorization With supportSignature: true, getMorphoAuthorizationRequirement returns a signable Requirement (action.type "authorization", carries sign()), not a standalone setAuthorization transaction. The two supportSignature:true supplyCollateralBorrow fork tests still asserted isRequirementAuthorization on the last requirement and submitted it as a separate transaction, then built the bundle with only the permit signature — so they threw "Authorization requirement not found". Sign the authorization requirement and fold both the permit and authorization signatures into buildTx, matching the borrow fork test. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * perf(morpho-sdk): parallelize nonce read with isAuthorized on the signable authorization path getMorphoAuthorizationRequirement serialized the Morpho nonce read behind the isAuthorized check because nonce was only needed when not authorized. On the supportSignature path the nonce is needed in the common case (enabling supportSignature signals intent to authorize), so fetch isAuthorized and nonce together via Promise.all, sharing a single round-trip (batched into one multicall when the client enables batching). The supportSignature:false branch keeps a single read and never fetches an unused nonce. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix(morpho-sdk): reject revocation auth signatures and fix array buildTx docs - getAuthorizationAction now throws BundlerErrors.UnexpectedAuthorizationRevocation when handed a revocation signature (isAuthorized: false), which would otherwise leave GeneralAdapter1 unauthorized and revert the following on-behalf Morpho op. - Update README/ARCHITECTURE buildTx examples and API text to the array contract (buildTx([signature])) so documented permit flows no longer break. message: feat(morpho-sdk): public-allocator liquidity metrics on ReallocationData (#796) * feat(morpho-sdk): shared-liquidity target-utilization metric + opt-in Add read-only metrics computeMaxBorrowToUtilization and computeAvailableSharedLiquidity (plus MorphoBlue methods), and a maintainSupplyTargetUtilization opt-in that holds the target market at its supply target instead of relaxing to 100% in the aggressive phase. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * refactor(morpho-sdk): standalone shared-liquidity metric, drop borrow helper Per review: the shared-liquidity metric must be an independent helper that returns a reallocatable-liquidity amount, decoupled from any borrow amount and from the Blue entity. - Remove MorphoBlue.getAvailableSharedLiquidity / getMaxBorrowToUtilization. - Remove computeMaxBorrowToUtilization (borrow-amount metric). - Keep computeAvailableSharedLiquidity as the sole standalone helper. - Update changeset, AGENTS.md, and tests accordingly. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * feat(morpho-sdk): add computeAvailableLiquidityToTargetUtilization Borrow-free read-only metric: returns the target's own borrow headroom to the supply-target ceiling plus the shared liquidity reallocatable from source markets (drained to 100% utilization), or 0n once the target is at/above the ceiling. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * refactor(morpho-sdk): drop maintainSupplyTargetUtilization opt-in The read-only metric computeAvailableLiquidityToTargetUtilization does not go through computeReallocations, so the maintainSupplyTargetUtilization write-path flag is unnecessary for this PR's scope. Reverts computeReallocations.ts, sharedLiquidity.ts, and computeReallocations.test.ts to main; the PR is now purely the two read-only shared-liquidity metrics. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * docs(morpho-sdk): add tib for shared-liquidity target-utilization metric Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * refactor(morpho-sdk): reshape liquidity-to-target-utilization metric Rename computeMaxBorrowToUtilization to computeLiquidityToTargetUtilization (and the matching MorphoBlue method) and reshape its result: - Return the market's own borrow headroom plus reallocatable shared liquidity. - Return only own headroom when supplyTargetUtilization > targetUtilization. - Return only shared liquidity when targetUtilization equals current utilization. - Pass discovery options through unchanged (no forced 100% withdrawal override). Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * refactor(morpho-sdk): refine available-liquidity-to-target-utilization metric Apply the requested metric semantics to computeAvailableLiquidityToTargetUtilization: - Return only shared liquidity when targetUtilization equals current utilization. - Drop the forced 100% source drain; pass discovery options through unchanged. - Return only own headroom when supplyTargetUtilization > targetUtilization. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * refactor(morpho-sdk): move liquidity metrics onto ReallocationData Address review feedback (Rubilmax): - Move the two read-only metrics off the helpers layer onto the ReallocationData class as getAvailableLiquidity / getAvailableLiquidityToUtilization (drop the "shared" qualifier; "utilization" rather than "target utilization"). - Extract getSupplyTargetUtilization, shared by computeReallocations and the new metric, removing the duplicated per-market supply-target resolution. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * refactor(morpho-sdk): rename metric to getAvailableLiquidityToTargetUtilization Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * refactor(morpho-sdk): rename getAvailableLiquidity to getPublicReallocationLiquidity Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * docs(morpho-sdk): rewrite shared-liquidity metric TIB to match shipped design Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * refactor(morpho-sdk): rename utilization param to targetUtilization Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix(morpho-sdk): exact borrow limit for getAvailableLiquidityToTargetUtilization Address Codex review: the metric returned ownHeadroom + reallocatableLiquidity, which overstated the borrow limit by (1-U)*L and reported positive liquidity for markets already above the target. It now measures the borrow headroom to the target on the supply augmented by the reallocatable liquidity, i.e. getBorrowToUtilization({ supply + L, borrow }, targetUtilization): 0n when over-target, and reallocated supply counted at the target utilization. Keeps the supplyTargetUtilization gate (fix #3) and the friendly source cap (fix #2). Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * refactor(morpho-sdk): revert metric to ownHeadroom + reallocatable sum Reverts ea128b02 per request; restores the additive ownHeadroom + reallocatable-liquidity form (no targetUtilization scaling). Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * refactor(morpho-sdk): scale reallocatable liquidity by target utilization getAvailableLiquidityToTargetUtilization now returns ownHeadroom + targetUtilization * L instead of the un-scaled ownHeadroom + L. Reallocated supply L raises the market's supply denominator, so borrowing against it only adds targetUtilization * L of headroom -- this matches getBorrowToUtilization({ supply + L, borrow }, targetUtilization). Tests, changeset, and TIB updated to match (Alternative 4 now documents the un-scaled sum as the rejected option). Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix(morpho-sdk): clamp liquidity metric to 0 when above target utilization getAvailableLiquidityToTargetUtilization returned positive liquidity when the market was already above the requested target and the reallocatable liquidity L was too small to bring it back under (Codex P2): the exact equality check only caught util == target, not util > target. Replace the scaled-sum + equality branch with the single canonical form getBorrowToUtilization({ supply + L, borrow }, targetUtilization) = zeroFloorSub(wMulDown(supply + L, targetUtilization), borrow). Below target this equals own headroom + targetUtilization * L (preserving the scaling); at or above target, zeroFloorSub clamps to 0n. This subsumes the removed util == target special case. Add two over-target tests (insufficient L -> 0n; sufficient L -> 130). Changeset and TIB updated to the unified two-rule form. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * docs(morpho-sdk): trim verbose inline comments on the liquidity metric The JSDoc already carries the full borrow-to-utilization math; collapse the two multi-line inline comments to one short line each. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * docs(morpho-sdk): address Codex review on liquidity metrics - add required @example blocks to getPublicReallocationLiquidity and getAvailableLiquidityToTargetUtilization (AGENTS.md §6) - narrow TIB "never-throws" wording to "never throws on insufficiency"; both metrics still throw UnknownReallocationMarketError on absent market - drop the stale unused ownHeadroom line from the TIB implementation snippet - add absent-market error tests (UnknownReallocationMarketError) for both metrics Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * Update packages/morpho-sdk/src/entities/reallocationData.ts Co-authored-by: Romain Milon <rmilon@gmail.com> Signed-off-by: Foulk plb | Morpho <71005796+Foulks-Plb@users.noreply.github.com> * fix(morpho-sdk): align getAvailableLiquidityToTargetUtilization name The method declaration used getAvailableLiquidityToUtilization with a `utilization` parameter, while the JSDoc example, AGENTS.md, and tests all referenced getAvailableLiquidityToTargetUtilization with `targetUtilization`, which the method body also read. This broke `tsc --noEmit` (build job). author: Foulks-Plb
message: feat(morpho-sdk): add MarketV1.refinance() (#749) * feat(morpho-sdk): add MarketV1.refinance() for Blue → Blue position migration Migrates a borrower's collateral and debt atomically from one Morpho Blue market to another sharing the same loan and collateral tokens. Implemented as a flash-collateral bundle via onMorphoSupplyCollateral: GA1 deposits on the target, borrows inside the callback, repays the source, then withdraws the source collateral to settle the deferred transfer — no user-side prefunding required. Shares mode is immune to mid-tx accrual; collat-only and partial migrations are supported. Adds the MarketV1RefinanceAction discriminant, seven typed errors, colocated unit tests for action + entity, and a minor changeset. * fix(morpho-sdk): clamp refinance accrual timestamps and cover mode-exclusive error - Replace `Date.now()` with `Time.timestamp()` and clamp both source and target accrual timestamps via `MathLib.max(now, market.lastUpdate)` so a stale clock or simulated future position never produces a negative elapsed interval (the pattern already in `repay()` / `repayWithdrawCollateral()`). - Add a missing entity test for `BorrowAmountAndSharesExclusiveError`. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix(morpho-sdk): tighten refinance preflight per Codex review Address five P2 findings from the Codex review on PR #749: - Assets-mode now caps `borrowAssets` at the source position's outstanding debt via the new `RefinanceExceedsBorrowAssetsError` (mirrors the existing `RefinanceExceedsBorrowSharesError` and `validateRepayAmount`), so we can't return an unexecutable bundle that underflows Morpho's repay path. - The source residual health check now (1) accounts for shares burned by an assets-mode repay via `accruedSource.toBorrowShares(requestedAssets, "Down")`, and (2) uses the forward-accrued source market so the projected residual debt reflects on-chain accrual. Partial assets-mode refinances that should be safe no longer falsely throw `BorrowExceedsSafeLtvError`. - The target LLTV check now runs against `borrowAssetsAdjusted` (the overshot amount actually borrowed) rather than `projectedBorrowAssets`, so a target near its LLTV buffer can no longer pass preflight but revert on-chain on the shares-mode overshoot. - The action layer now rejects `borrowShares > 0n` with `borrowAssets <= 0n` via the new `RefinanceSharesMissingBorrowAssetsError` — direct action callers (bypassing the entity) must provide the overshoot computed by the entity from `slippageTolerance`, otherwise the encoded `morphoBorrow(target, 0n, 0n, …)` would revert. The fifth Codex finding (`Date.now()` without `max(now, lastUpdate)` clamp) was already addressed in 32790582. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix(morpho-sdk): tighten refinance preflight per second Codex review Address three more P2 findings from Codex on commit eb6f6351: - Reject negative `borrowAssets` / `borrowShares` up front in the entity rather than letting them fall through the `> 0n` mode checks as if no debt were being migrated. Without the early check, `getRequirements()` would prompt the user to authorize GA1 before `buildTx()` later threw on the action's `< 0n` guard. - Reorder the action callback so the shares-mode `maxUint256` target sweep runs BEFORE `morphoWithdrawCollateral`, not after. In same-token markets (`loanToken === collateralToken`), the trailing sweep would otherwise consume the just-withdrawn collateral that the outer `morphoSupplyCollateral`'s deferred `safeTransferFrom` still needs to pull, reverting the bundle. - Gate the target LLTV health check on `shouldMigrateBorrow`. Collat-only refinances only supply target collateral and withdraw source collateral — neither degrades target health — and running the helper unconditionally would reject markets whose oracle is unavailable or whose collateral value is below the helper's `+1` rounding guard. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix(morpho-sdk): refine refinance per third Codex review Address three more findings from Codex on commit d1800194: - Shares mode now forward-accrues the source market by 2h (same buffer as `repay()` / `repayWithdrawCollateral()`) so `projectedBorrowAssets` and `maxRepaySharePrice` absorb signature→exec accrual. Low-slippage or delayed shares-mode refinances no longer under-borrow the target leg or hit the source repay cap on-chain. - The action layer rejects `maxRepaySharePrice <= 0n` whenever a repay leg is encoded, via `NonPositiveRepayMaxSharePriceError` — matching the `marketV1Repay` / `marketV1RepayWithdrawCollateral` contract. The zero sentinel remains legal in collat-only refinances. - Parameter JSDoc on `borrowAssets` / `borrowShares` / `maxRepaySharePrice` now describes the shares-mode overshoot requirement and the repay-cap contract, so direct action callers won't be misled by the "mutually exclusive" wording in generated API docs. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com> * chore: untrack .claude/scheduled_tasks.lock harness runtime state The lock file is written by the Claude Code harness for scheduled task coordination — it is per-machine runtime state, not project source. Accidentally committed in the previous commit; add an explicit gitignore entry alongside the removal. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix(morpho-sdk): derive refinance minBorrowSharePrice from encoded borrowAssets Pre-fix, `MorphoMarketV1.refinance()` computed `minBorrowSharePrice` from `projectedBorrowAssets`, while the encoded `morphoBorrow` carries the larger `borrowAssetsAdjusted` (the shares-mode slippage overshoot). The GA1 on-chain check `mulDivDown(borrowedAssets, RAY, borrowedShares) >= minSharePrice` derives `borrowedShares` from the encoded assets, so the guard must be derived from the same input or `toBorrowShares("Up")` rounding can revert a bundle that passed preflight. Also adds a fork e2e test (`test/actions/marketV1/refinance.test.ts`) covering assets-mode, shares-mode overshoot sweep, and collat-only paths, asserting via `testInvariants` that every bundler3 component (incl. GA1) ends with zero balance — no loan or collateral residue. The `loanToken === collateralToken` case is documented as a follow-up because it requires deploying a custom 1:1-oracle market on the fork. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com> * test(morpho-sdk): stabilize refinance fork coverage Address carapulse review feedback (PR #749, second review). The fork e2e file fails locally with MAINNET_RPC_URL set because: - the `borrow()` setup helper already authorizes GA1, so debt-mode refinance has zero auth requirements rather than exactly one; - the pinned fork block drifts behind wall-clock `Time.timestamp()`, so the share-price guard on the migrated borrow leg can revert with SlippageExceeded before the refinance path is exercised. Make the auth check tolerant to a pre-authorized wallet (length <= 1, iterate) and pass `MAX_SLIPPAGE_TOLERANCE` on the debt-mode cases so the pinned fork stays deterministic against wall-clock drift. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com> * feat(morpho-sdk): wire shared liquidity into MarketV1.refinance() Add optional `targetReallocations` to `MarketV1.refinance()` and the underlying `marketV1Refinance` encoder. When provided, each entry is encoded as a top-level `reallocateTo` action prepended before the outer `morphoSupplyCollateral`, mirroring the pattern in `marketV1Borrow` / `marketV1SupplyCollateralBorrow`. The PublicAllocator moves liquidity into the target market so the in-callback `morphoBorrow` on the target finds enough on-chain liquidity. Reallocation fees accumulate in `tx.value` and on `action.args.reallocationFee` (new field on the discriminant). No new error classes — validation is delegated to `buildReallocationActions` / `validateReallocations`, which throw the same five typed errors already exported for borrow. Coverage: - Unit (action): fee in `tx.value` + discriminator; empty/omitted produce identical calldata; reallocate ordered before supplyCollateral; collat-only refinance still accepts reallocations; `ReallocationWithdrawalOnTargetMarketError` for self-withdraw. - Unit (entity): pass-through to action. - Fork e2e for the non-empty path: tracked as a follow-up TODO in `test/actions/marketV1/refinance.test.ts` (requires a refinance-eligible market pair publicly allocated by a vault at the pinned block). Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com> * chore(morpho-sdk): trim verbose comments on refinance reallocations Drop inline narration that paraphrased the JSDoc or the code itself, and tighten the new JSDoc sentences. No behavior change. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com> * test(morpho-sdk): cover refinance + reallocation on fork Add a mainnet fork test that refinances a cbBTC/USDC position from `CbbtcUsdcMarketV1` (oracle 0xA6D6...) to a second cbBTC/USDC market (oracle 0xc7BE7593..., new `CbbtcUsdcMarketV1Alt` fixture) and uses the Yearn USDC vault (new `YearnUsdcVaultV1` fixture) to reallocate 2000 USDC from the wstETH/USDC source market into the target before the in-callback borrow. Verifies: - `tx.value === 0n` and `action.args.reallocationFee === 0n` at fee=0. - Target `totalSupplyAssets` grew by ≥ the reallocation amount. - Migrated collateral / debt landed on the target. Both markets and the Yearn vault flow caps to both were verified present at the pinned block 24_593_903 via the Morpho API. Removes the prior TODO that asked for this coverage. author: divhead
message: confirm a relay switch before one replica acts on it The flags arrive from whichever keeper replica the fallback tracker elected, and it elects on price health — a replica can serve good prices and a stale flag, and stay elected for as long as its prices are fine. That is how express went off for real users yesterday: one fallback host served isExpressAvailable false for half an hour while the other three served true. Survivable for a banner, not for a switch that takes express away. Before acting on either relay switch, ask the configured keeper directly. Nothing changes while the switches are at rest, so the common case costs no request, and a switch someone actually threw still works within one interval. This narrows the window rather than closing it: the flag is only as reliable as the fleet serving it, and the opposite failure — a replica still serving true during a real incident — is not something the client can fix.

author: qwinndev
message: Rewrite legacy hash urls opened in place The rewrite only ran during module evaluation, so following a legacy /#/... link while already sitting on its path did nothing: only the fragment changes, the document is not reloaded and nothing re-reads the url. The landing page is the exposed one since it always sits on /, so pasting gmx.io/#/builders from gmx.io left you on home with a stale hash. Watch hashchange and navigate onto the real path. Navigating rather than rewriting the history entry is what makes the router follow. Plain anchors like #bridge are untouched, and the rewritten url carries no legacy hash so the handler cannot loop. message: Fix Support button blinking and unread counter after refresh - useShowSupportChat: @privy-io/wagmi hardcodes reconnectOnMount: false, so on page load wagmi reports plain "disconnected" (never "reconnecting") while Privy restores the session — the last-connected-state cache never engaged and was overwritten to false on every load, hiding the Support button until the wallet reconnected. author: cursoragent
message: Fix memoized staleness check that ignored time Remove useMemo wrapper from isMarketsDataStale calculation so that the staleness check runs on every render. The hasStaleMarketValues function compares Date.now() against market updatedAt timestamps, but the useMemo only recalculated when configData/valuesData changed, not when time passed. This caused the API to stay marked as healthy for up to one refresh interval beyond the 10s stale threshold. Now the staleness check recalculates on every render, which happens periodically due to the forceStaleCheck interval in useApiDataRequest.

This ensures positions/orders see the updated health state immediately during the same render cycle when staleness is detected.

We add a script to make it fairly easy to deploy a new Starport implementation. * Derive Types This patch adds a set of macros to derive types.json automatically. This is, all in all, a little complicated because the best way to analyze the code is through macros (since we can easily mark types that need to be exported) but macros, for obvious reasons, are run at compile-time and are not _meant_ to be side-effecty. That is, you can't easily just store a bunch of global data and when you're finished just emit it. Instead, we truncate and re-write a file-system temp file each time we encounter a new type and eventually we stop encountering new ones and we're good. We do this separately for each project in `scripts/build_types.json` since partial compilation and project-by-project compilation makes this even harder to do. We also need to clean and rebuild each time to ensure every macro is run. _Also_ there is some compile time slowness added here since I can't seem to remove the macros via features or other settings since this runs in the same layer as those types of tools. All-in-all, it's significantly fast enough and hopefully will make the process of updating our types.json trivial going forward. Note: some of the code is pretty spaghetti in the derive code itself and can be upgraded over time. The issue is that there is a ton of possibilities that could occur in the syntax and we probably don't want to handle all of them. The most complex one that we need to consider is `WIDTH` which, as a const, is not very easy to determine its value, so for now, we just use its value directly, since literals are fairly easy. We add an `EventTracker` module that handles tracking events without using global vars (which was probably messing up test cases). Events are hard because they come in from a subscription in PolkadotJS, but our scenarios often ask "Have you seen any Substrate `Lock()` events?" and we have to say something like "Yes, we saw one more recently than the last time you asked." It's important to merge this quickly as it touches a lot of random lines of code. * Fix initialization of starport parent block (#297) * Fix initialization of starport parent block * Scen debugging tweaks * Change auth requires supermajority (#300) * change auth supermajority * fmt * camelcase * add comment * add more data about cash to the cashdata rpc (#289) * add more data about cash to the cashdata rpc * delete unused params * fix rebase * add trx request to the and_provides to fix stuck nonces on failed trx… (#301) * add trx request to the and_provides to fix stuck nonces on failed trx requests * fix test * Resolve some open questions / standing issues in rates (#303) * Minimum blocks wait for all events (#304) * Fix substrate coverage (#305) * Add rudimentary filter on worker side of already signed blocks (#307) * Add rudimentary filter on worker side of already signed blocks Still need to determine worker's identity before this can take effect. * Add ability for workers to get current validator, unlock filtering * Event Fixes (#309) * Start to test scenarios * Debugging improvements * Better handling new Web3 revert without reasons * Fix test failures due to more blocks being fetched * Add missing check for already signed reorg (also fixes warnings) Co-authored-by: Geoffrey Hayes <hayesgm@gmail.com> * Debugging Reorgs (#311) * Debugging Reorgs * Some cleanup / notes Co-authored-by: Geoffrey Hayes <hayesgm@gmail.com> * Debugging Reorgs (#310) * Fix Cash RPC, Add Max Ingression Blocks, and Misc. Scenario Fixes This patch fixes the Cash RPC which was double adding interest to the cash results. We've also added a max ingression blocks since certain scenario tests attempted to lock unpriced assets and thus failed. I would debate after a sufficient number of blocks, we should always just take in a given event from the queue (e.g. 50 or 100 blocks). Finally, we fix a large number of scenarios, including making sure we use `types.json` from earlier versions for upgrade tests. We are still facing a number of issues testing upgrades, and thus those are marked as skipped for now. Finally, we switch back from 1-second blocks to auto-mine for the majority of test cases. This is because they run about 50% faster when auto-mining. To handle the ingression queue code, we just mine 100 blocks whenever we're waiting for Eth events. * Resolve some XXXs Co-authored-by: Jared Flatow <jflatow@gmail.com> * Add checks for Extract, Liquidate and Transfer events (#312) * Fix m8 Failure (#313) This patch fixes failures running m8 due to the enum shifting between versions. We add a reserved filler into the enums that can later be set to a different value, e.g. for another chain. We try to fill all of the slots since we would prefer that the numbering of chains stays constant and doesn't shift (e.g. it's #0 for ChainAccounts but #1 for ChainAssets and #5 for ChainBlocks). Currently we cannot run m7 wasm in the native shell. This is likely due to some incompatability in the host functions versus the previously built wasm code. This new test shows off that behavior (it was broken with a Wasmi Trap). We fix the issue by changing the Dot/Eth order in chains.rs (not sure why this is the fix, but it worked). Note: this test now traps on missing a host function for getting cash data, but this is **not of any concern**. The original error was that blocks could not form, and we have a partial fix here that warrants more follow up. That is: why did this fix work? How can we make it work without changing the enum orders? Again, the current error in the test is not the issue. The issue is "fixed" as we can mine blocks, but we need to figure out why this fix worked and if we can fix it without the "hack". * Miner cumulative, asset modified events, and some other fixes (#315) * Miner cumulative, asset modified events, and some other fixes * MinerPaid events; initialize events; appease the tests * Unit test reorg (#317) * unit test reorg * fmt * fmt * fix rebase * Fix substrate tests ? (#316) * Run benchmarks on digital ocean instance (#276) Roughly matches the original substrate benchmarking hardware. * Move deadline to const (#318) * bump spec version (#314) * Start to get upgrade to m9 test going (#321) This patch gets the upgrade tests working. They are pretty crazy due to the stateful API connections that make it quite difficult to send an RPC that changes the encoding/decoding scheme, since they can't really be on version 1 (since they crash after changeover as soon as they see an event) nor version 2 (since they crash trying to init with an old types.json). You can try to blend the types.json from both versions (we do this) but you'll still get truly conflicting decoding schemes. It's just a mess so we actually mostly try to disconnect the APIs and reconnect them after the change. It's a bit flakey but it works somewhat okay. With this strategy, we fix the previous upgrade scenarios and we add an m8 -> m9 scenario. We were unable to get into the state seen on test-net (not sure how to repro), and thus we still don't have full confidence this upgrade will fix the issue, but we see no reason that it should specifically break it, either. * Native m8 Shell (#324) This patch adds a scenario where we run a native m8 binary and upgrade _it_ to m9 (as opposed to running an m9 binary with m8 WASM runtime and then do the upgrade there). This can detect anomolies in the node runtime that wouldn't be found by other tests. author: dbeal-eth
message: Forkability improvements (#2335) * add fork detector contract * forkability improvements This PR introduces a new core utility contract, `ForkDetector`, which provides a way for developer forks (such as Tenderly, Anvil) to distinguish themselves from the canonical chain safely. This can be useful as there are some functionalities which are difficult to operate on a fork (ex. offchain prices or precompiled contracts), and the behavior in those places can be selectively mocked to prevent interruption of testing. Design Considerations: * The idea of these changes is to provide a one-line way for integrators or anyone trying to fork the synthetix system a way to make Synthetix fork-friendly setup. In the future, who knows, this functionality could be enabled by default. * Original functionality of the chain can be restored by removing or modifying the code at `0x1234123412341234123412341234123412341234`, in case your tests require it Specific changes: * add `ForkDetector` library * in op gas price oracle, replace calls to the OP precompiled contract with mock values or skip * in arb gas price oracle, replace calls to the arbitrum precompiled contract with mock values or skip * in pyth ERC7412 adapter proxy, use whatever the latest price available on-chain is regardless of its staleness. Additionally, prices can be overridden by calling the contract (note: it was previously possible to simply switch out the oracle node on the oracle manager as well, but sometimes this lever is much more convenient to pull) Tests to be written tomorrow * add tests * set reasonable mock values reccomendation from audit * misc audit fixes * add events for fork-only write operations * misc lint/solidity style warnings * move definition of contractCode variable * fix abstract proxy is not effectively used by the pyth wrapper audit note * add flag * undo storage changes * fix yarn lock

message: refactor(collateral-return): match ts-sdk plan shape and execution behavior - Rename the plan model to CollateralReturnPlanResponse with the ts-sdk field set: wire names (starting_pusd, net_pusd_out, final_pusd, required_pusd_input), restored operation_count, estimated_cost, and candidate_position_ids, and ts-matching required fields (only position_summary stays defaulted). - Apply the 120s request timeout to submit as well as plan; submit re-validation also recomputes wallet state server-side. - Drop CollateralReturnPlanRejectedError and the client-side empty-plan gate: stale and empty plans surface the service rejection as RequestRejectedError, matching ts-sdk. - Share one gasless submit retry helper between prepare_gasless_transaction and collateral return execution instead of four copies of the loop. - Move the decimal-string validators to a shared models module under public names; e6 amounts serialize back to base-unit strings in JSON mode so dumped plans re-validate to the same amounts, and signed amounts are rejected. - Narrow client execute return types to the gasless handles. author: kartojal
message: feat(streams): surface unknown frames without closing connections Realtime streams previously dropped unrecognized frames silently, and on the RFQ quoter surface an unrecognized or malformed frame ended the whole session. Servers may introduce frame types and status values ahead of a client release that understands them, so: - Add an optional on_unknown_frame callback (UnknownFrame(frame, stream)) on PublicClient/SecureClient async clients and every stream surface: clob_market, clob_user, rtds, sports, perps_market, perps_session, rfq_quoter. Unknown frames never close the connection; without a callback they are ignored, and the SDK no longer logs them - observing them is the consumer's choice. The dropped_events counters stay. - The RFQ quoter treats unknown message types, non-object frames, and known types with unreadable payloads as unknown frames instead of failing the session; callers waiting on an unreadable acknowledgement fail through their acknowledgement timeout. Well-formed uncorrelated RFQ errors still fail the session deliberately. - Status vocabularies now parse any string so known frames carrying new lifecycle values are delivered instead of dropped: user trade/order statuses and order event types, RFQ execution status, and perps TP/SL, deposit, withdrawal, and order statuses. Known values stay enumerated as Known* aliases for narrowing; frame-type discriminators and trading sides stay strict. - Expected control frames (perps request-id acknowledgements and heartbeat pongs) are not reported as unknown.

author: kartojal
message: feat(client): surface unknown websocket frames via onUnknownFrame Unrecognized frames on any websocket stream (CLOB market/user, RTDS, sports, perps subscriptions/session, RFQ quoter) were silently dropped. They still never close the connection, but are now observable: an optional `onUnknownFrame` client option receives the raw frame and the stream that produced it. The SDK itself never logs; whether and how to record unknown frames is up to the consumer. Expected control frames (perps request acks and heartbeat pongs) are not reported. Regression tests cover the unknown-frame path per stream through a shared expectSurfacesUnknownFrame helper, plus delivery of known frames carrying newly introduced status values.

author: cesarenaldi
message: feat(client): add perps support Port Perps support from the TypeScript SDK to the async clients: - Public reads on AsyncPublicClient and AsyncSecureClient: instruments, tickers (with statistics merge), book, fees, and paginated candles, funding history, and trades with SDK-owned opaque cursors. - Perps market data streaming through subscribe() with per-topic specs (trades, bbo, book, candles, tickers, statistics), channel dedupe, and reconnect with resubscribe. - Delegated credential lifecycle: open_perps_session creates or resumes credentials (CreateProxy typed-data signature, validation, default 7d expiry) and revoke_perps_credentials signs deleteProxy ops. - PerpsSession trading over WebSocket with EIP-712 signed msgpack ops: place_order (gtc/ioc/fok overloads, optional TP/SL triggers), post_orders, place_position_tp_sl, cancel_order(s), update_leverage, session account reads, and an async-iterable event stream with sequence-gap and reconnect resync events. - Funds: deposit_to_perps (EOA broadcast or gasless relayer call) and withdraw_from_perps (owner-signed Withdraw typed data). Signing is pinned byte-for-byte against golden vectors generated from the TypeScript implementation (msgpack encoding, Op data hash, and signatures). Verified with ruff, pyright, the unit suite, and the live integration suite including a 10 USDC deposit/withdraw roundtrip and GTC and TP/SL order place/cancel against production.

message: feat(client): add RTDS manager close Implement RtdsWebSocketManager.close() as an idempotent resource teardown that stops the heartbeat, ends active subscriber queues, clears subscription state, and closes the current socket even if a connection is still opening. Update subscription tests to clean up the shared public client's RTDS manager between tests and assert that closing the manager stops future heartbeat PINGs.

author: cesarenaldi
message: feat(client): add RTDS heartbeat coverage Keep RTDS connections alive by sending a non-blocking PING heartbeat from the shared WebSocket manager. Add a shared setNonBlockingInterval helper so Node timers do not keep processes alive solely because of heartbeat work. Cover the heartbeat through the public client subscribe interface using MSW WebSocket interception, forwarding traffic to the real RTDS endpoint while spying on outbound frames. Narrow the Node-entry restricted-import rule so msw/node can be used in tests without matching the SDK's node entrypoint restriction.

author: cesarenaldi
message: feat(client): implement shared-socket RTDS WebSocket manager Split the websockets module into a folder — `types.ts` for the WebSocketManager interface and aggregate manager types, one file per concrete manager (CLOB, RTDS, sports), and a barrel `index.ts`. The CLOB and sports managers remain no-op stubs. The RTDS manager now opens a single shared upstream socket lazily on the first subscribe and multiplexes subscribers grouped by topic. Each topic carries one server-side subscription; all narrowing by symbol, comment type, or parent entity happens client-side because the RTDS server treats `filters` as an opaque lowercase substring. Add an integration test that validates independent filters fan out correctly on the same shared socket. Record two new RTDS boundary notes: the `crypto_prices` filter regex actually required by the server, and the authoritative `(connection, topic, type)` subscription model derived from the RTDS service source. Remaining followups in inline TODOs: 5s PING heartbeat, refcount handle lifecycle with unsubscribe frames, manager-level close(), and reconnect + resubscribe on socket drop.

author: liby
message: fix: Config::default() zero heartbeat_interval (#290) ## Summary - `Config` derived both `Default` and `bon::Builder`, but their defaults diverged: the builder set `heartbeat_interval` to 5 seconds while `derive(Default)` produced `Duration::ZERO`, which panics at runtime in `tokio::time::interval`. - Replace `derive(Default)` with a manual `impl Default` that matches the builder defaults, consistent with the pattern already used in `ws::Config`. Closes #289 ## Test plan - [x] `cargo build --all-features` passes - [x] `cargo test --all-features` passes (49 passed, 0 failed) - [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` passes with zero warnings <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Low Risk** > Low risk: changes only `Config::default()` initialization to prevent a zero-duration heartbeat interval that could panic when the `heartbeats` feature is enabled. > > **Overview** > Fixes a mismatch between `bon::Builder` defaults and `derive(Default)` for `clob::client::Config`. > > `Config` no longer derives `Default`; it now has a manual `impl Default` that sets `heartbeat_interval` to 5 seconds (and keeps other fields at their intended defaults), avoiding runtime failures from a zero-duration interval when automatic heartbeats are used. > > <sup>Written by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/dashboard?tab=bugbot) for commit cf2be7eca8faf875577716e0647df6db2805c8b3. author: chaz-polymarket
message: feat(heartbeats)!: add heartbeats (#113) Introduces a new feature flag `heartbeats` for the CLOB which automatically creates a new Tokio task on `authenticate` which will send heartbeats to the Polymarket server every five seconds (configurable via CLOB `Config` struct). When the `Client` is dropped, then the heartbeat task will be cancelled. This is a breaking change because previously non-async methods are now async (`deauthenticate` and `promote_to_builder`).

author: Haut
message: feat: add RTDS (Real-Time Data Socket) client (#56) Add a new WebSocket client for streaming real-time data from Polymarket's RTDS service, including cryptocurrency prices (Binance and Chainlink) and comment events in the style of the CLOB WS. - New `rtds` feature flag for optional compilation - Stream-based API with subscribe_crypto_prices, subscribe_chainlink_prices, subscribe_comments methods - Automatic reconnection with exponential backoff - 5-second PING/PONG heartbeat for connection health - Lazy deserialization via InterestTracker for performance - Authenticated subscription variants using existing Credentials type

author: denys-cb
message: Solana/mint controller (#26) * feat: add Solana mint-controller program Implements P/PS: Mint rate limiting and onchain allowlisting for Solana (https://docs.google.com/document/d/10EEjJ_m3b8Hj61fkNGqmjIh5d9ZxKkQo0eoYzbMOAMY). Adds a new Anchor program at solana/programs/mint-controller/ that takes ownership of an SPL stablecoin's mint authority and gates mint_to behind per-(mint, minter) rate limiting and per-(mint, minter) recipient allowlisting. Mirrors the EVM RateLimit.sol semantics from evm/src/lib/RateLimit.sol exactly (linear replenishment, mulDiv math). Roles match the EVM Stablecoin contract: a per-mint MintRoles PDA holds admin / rate_limit_admin / allowlist_admin; MINT_ROLE is granted implicitly by the existence of a per-(mint, minter) MintRateLimitConfig PDA, eliminating the EVM "grant role then configure" two-step gap. Also adds a Solana build job (cargo fmt --check + anchor build) to the existing CI workflow alongside the Foundry job. (cherry picked from commit f6ffad3d701ac249ab438343cffef50037caf41f) * review fixes: drop Solana CI job, trim function docs, preserve rate-limit state on reconfigure - Revert .github/workflows/test.yml to main (drop the Solana CI job added earlier in this PR; it can land separately). - Trim secondary doc paragraphs from each pub fn in the mint-controller program; keep only the one-line primary summary. - configure_minter: on reconfigure, only update `limit` and `interval`; preserve `remaining` and `last_consumed` so an in-flight rate-limit window survives an admin re-config. Use `config.bump == 0` to detect fresh init (matches the existing pattern in `add_to_allowlist`). - Update the reconfigure test + README + PR-body table to describe the new preserve-on-reconfigure semantics. Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com> (cherry picked from commit df21457f5fe19d5cf0ffe0e2e46f19ab06b4320d) * refactor(solana): address mint-controller PR review feedback Collapse allowlist management into admin, rename rate_limit_admin to rate_limit_authority, rename allowlist instructions to add/remove_allowed_mint_recipient, and reshape mint_tokens to mirror SPL mint_to by checking the destination token account owner and dropping the separate recipient and payer accounts. Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com> (cherry picked from commit 1889aeaf07364e356ea0e8915b33a67d37ebd101) * feat(solana): add global pause and address remaining PR review feedback Add a program-wide GlobalConfig PDA with admin-gated pause/unpause so all minting can be halted without redeploying. revoke_minter now also closes the allowlist PDA when present, and configure_minter uses an explicit is_initialized flag instead of bump==0. Tests and README updated. Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com> (cherry picked from commit 7f6d69e8c8b3e932b5ac43bc125a807efda65b51) * fix(solana): gate initialize on hardcoded global admin Hardcode INITIAL_GLOBAL_ADMIN at compile time so initialize_global cannot be front-run, and require the global admin signer for per-mint initialize. Adds localnet feature for tests and updates docs. Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com> (cherry picked from commit cdbb14689f1b20cdb5fba45ac2fd808cc1a76fa9) * fix(solana): reject zero-address inputs and guard minter on reconfigure Add non-zero (default pubkey) checks to update_global_admin, initialize (admin + rate_limit_authority), update_admin, update_rate_limit_authority, configure_minter (minter), and add_allowed_mint_recipient (recipient) via a new InvalidAddress error. Also assert the loaded config PDA matches the provided minter on reconfigure. Adds negative tests for each check. Generated with Claude Code Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix(solana): snapshot rate-limit capacity on minter reconfigure On reconfiguring an existing minter, snapshot the currently-available capacity into remaining (capped at the new limit) and reset last_consumed to now, so reducing the interval can no longer retroactively refresh a minter's capacity earlier than intended. Update the reconfigure test to assert the new snapshot/reset behavior. Generated with Claude Code Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com> * feat(solana): dedicated allowlist_authority and eager allowlist lifecycle Add a per-mint allowlist_authority role (separate from admin) that gates add/remove of allowed mint recipients, with an update_allowlist_authority instruction to rotate it. The allowlist PDA is now created together with the rate-limit config in configure_minter and always closed in revoke_minter (no longer optional/lazy), so a re-granted minter can never inherit a stale allowlist. Update tests for the new initialize signature, allowlist authority, and eager allowlist creation. Generated with Claude Code Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com> * chore(solana): document owner-based allowlist, test allowlist-authority guard, add yarn test - Clarify in code that the allowlist stores token-account owners and that the destination is validated at mint time (typed TokenAccount + token::mint), so no add-time token-account/mint check is needed. - Extend the wrong-signer test to assert a non-admin cannot call update_allowlist_authority. - Add a `yarn test` script that builds with the localnet feature and runs the suite in one command. Generated with Claude Code Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix(solana): enable no-idl by default Anchor injects IDL instructions unless `no-idl` is set. The Create handler takes any funded signer and the account can't be reclaimed after. Default-on so a release build can't miss the flag. Build is byte-identical to --features no-idl; IdlCreateAccount absent from the .so; anchor idl build unaffected. Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com> * test(solana): assert exact Anchor error codes in negative tests assert.fail sat inside the try whose catch matched the error string, so a chai AssertionError satisfied its own catch. 22 of 25 sites could pass without the program rejecting anything. expectAnchorError captures only errors from the awaited thunk, throws outside the catch if it resolves, and checks the exact code rather than a substring. Mint-path negatives also assert the destination balance and remaining capacity afterwards, so an unexpected success that moves value fails even if the error oracle were wrong. All 34 pass. Mutation-checked: a wrong code and a resolving thunk both fail. Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix(solana): configure the mint before handing over authority initialize required the PDA to already hold the SPL mint authority, so the irreversible handoff had to happen first. Any failure during setup then stranded the mint, since the program can't give the authority back. Drop the check. Roles, minters and allowlists are configured while the original key still controls the mint. MintTokens enforces the authority, so minting stays disabled until the handoff. Also fail the build when INITIAL_GLOBAL_ADMIN is the placeholder. initialize_global is permissionless and GlobalConfig can't be re-initialized, so shipping it would let anyone pin an unsignable admin. Non-localnet builds need a real key now. README preflight reordered to match, plus the recovery posture. Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com> * docs(solana): correct the allowlist authority and lifecycle The README credited the per-mint admin with allowlist management, but add/remove enforce allowlist_authority. Same drift elsewhere: no allowlist_authority row, no update_allowlist_authority entry, MintRoles listed as two keys, and the allowlist described as lazily created when configure_minter makes it and revoke_minter always closes it. Key types are now Cold and Hot. The internal system names meant nothing to a reader of this repo. Also rename a revoke test that still said "when one exists". Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com> * docs(solana): document who pays and reclaims minter PDA rent configure_minter pays from rate_limit_authority, revoke_minter closes to admin, so rent moves between the two keys each cycle. The refund goes to whoever holds the admin role at close time, not the original payer. Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com> * docs(solana): add August 2026 Cantina audit report Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com> Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com> --------- Co-authored-by: Forest Hu <forest.hu@coinbase.com> Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com> Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: adrienzheng-cb
message: fix: upgrade vulnerable transitive dependencies (#841) * fix: upgrade vulnerable transitive dependencies Ports the security fixes from cds-internal#187. Every range that declares these packages already permitted the patched version, so the vulnerable copies were held in place only by a stale lockfile. Refreshing the affected subtrees clears all 12 advisories with no resolutions entries added, which avoids pinning us below upstream and going stale again. Also covers three advisories the original PR left open: form-data (which it fixed incidentally, so omitting it would regress), plus the pre-existing svgo and websocket-driver issues. Removes five resolutions that were provably no-ops - elliptic, ip, koa and bn.js are absent from the dependency tree entirely, and nothing declares ajv@^6.0.0 - verified by reinstalling without them and getting a byte-identical lockfile. The remaining minimatch and tar entries are load-bearing and were left alone. Drops the unused axios devDependency, which had no importers and was the only source of the EOL axios 0.18.x line. Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com> * fix: dedupe lockfile The refresh left duplicate ranges that could be consolidated, which tools/ci/validators/validateLockfile.mjs rejects. Re-verified that every advisory floor still holds after deduping, since consolidation can pick a different version. author: hsiuhsiu
message: fix: harden crypto helpers and add coverage tooling (#121) Simplify error reporting by removing stack trace emission from ordinary error paths and trimming unused string/error helpers, while keeping API argument validation on structured error returns. Fix several crypto helper edge cases: mod_t assignment now drops stale Montgomery contexts, mod_t::mod(int) handles negative values and INT_MIN without signed overflow, ElGamal /= performs division, and Paillier batch cipher validation runs in an explicit variable-time scope. Tighten ECC behavior by validating curves and signature scalars during ECDSA verification, asserting same-curve point operations, preserving variable-time scalar multiplication when requested, and enforcing Ed25519 point storage alignment. Harden protocol paths by checking Schnorr nonce points before proof verification, using explicit variable-time evaluation in HD EdDSA derivation, simplifying HD root K-share helpers, and preserving empty access structures during deserialization. Add Clang/LLVM coverage configuration and Make targets for text and HTML coverage reports, and ignore generated PDF diff artifacts from internal tooling.

author: lakshaysharma-cb
message: fix(app2app): self-heal stale App Attest key + reset control, and TestFlight build docs (#43) * feat: self-heal stale App Attest key + manual reset control The App Attest keyId lives in the iOS keychain, which survives app delete/reinstall for the same bundle id, and a key is bound to its App Attest environment (dev sandbox vs production). A key created by a local/dev build can be reused and then rejected at the assertion (signature) step by a later TestFlight build on the same device. - Add clearAllAppAttestKeys() (scoped + legacy entries). - Add an AppAttestReset button on Home to force a fresh key. - Self-heal in the app2app flow: on a signature/attestation error, reset the key, re-register, and retry the hand-off once. * docs: document TestFlight build + app2app env vars /ios and .env are git-ignored, so a fresh clone needs a real .env and an expo prebuild. Add a "Building for TestFlight" section and clarify the app2app env vars (USE_EXPO_CRYPTO must be false; BASE_URL needs /api on Vercel; ONRAMP_PROJECT_ID / APP_ATTEST_APP_ID requirements). * feat: open the app via iOS Universal Link on onramp return Replace the custom-scheme onramp redirect with an https Universal Link so the Coinbase app reliably reopens this app (domain-verified, with a web fallback) instead of relying on the onrampdemo:// scheme. - Serve the AASA at /.well-known/apple-app-site-association on the backend domain (server/api/aasa.js + vercel.json rewrite). - Add ios.associatedDomains (applinks:<murex host>) so prebuild registers the Associated Domains entitlement. - Derive REDIRECT_URL as https://<api-origin>/onramp-return; fall back to onrampdemo://onramp-return for local/non-https backends. Expo Router auto-routes the matching /onramp-return file route. Note: the redirect must be added to the CDP Onramp allowlist, and iOS caches the AASA at install time (reinstall to test).

author: lakshaysharma-cb
message: fix(app2app): correct Vercel /api/app2app routing + prod parity, App Attest env scoping, retail-app detection (#42) * fix(server): expose app2app onramp routes as Vercel functions The /app2app/mobile/{challenges,sessions} and /app2app/mobile/attestation/{challenges,registrations} routes are defined on the shared Express app but had no corresponding serverless function under server/api/. Vercel uses file-based routing, so production requests to those paths returned a static 404 without ever invoking (or logging) the Express handler. Add a single catch-all api/app2app/[...slug].js that forwards every /api/app2app/* request to the Express app, unblocking the app-to-app onramp + App Attest flow against the deployed backend. * fix(server): route all /api/app2app/* via single function + vercel.json rewrite Vercel zero-config only matched a single path segment for the api/app2app/[...slug] catch-all, so multi-segment routes like /api/app2app/mobile/attestation/challenges returned a platform 404 and never reached Express. Replace the bracket catch-all with a single api/app2app.js and add a vercel.json rewrite funneling /api/app2app/(.*) to it; the function strips the /api/app2app prefix and delegates to the shared Express app. * feat: detect Coinbase retail app install + use production App Attest Add useCoinbaseAppInstalled + CoinbaseAppStatus to surface whether the Coinbase consumer app is installed (partner signal), register the com.coinbase.consumer query scheme, and switch the App Attest entitlement to production for TestFlight/App Store builds. * fix: scope App Attest keys per onramp project and purge legacy keys Scope the stored keyId/attested/registered SecureStore entries by the onramp project id so dev and prod provision independent keys on the same device, and clear pre-scoping (un-scoped) keys on the app2app entry path to avoid a stale dev registration breaking prod assertions. * chore: ignore .vercel local project link

author: hsiuhsiu
message: fix: make MODULO macro safe for early returns and nesting via RAII scope guard (#107) Replace the raw for-loop MODULO macro with an RAII-based modulo_scope_t that saves and restores the thread-local modulus on scope exit. This fixes a latent bug where early return, break, throw, or goto inside a MODULO block would leave a stale modulus set for subsequent operations on the same thread, and enables safe nesting of MODULO scopes. Add unit tests for early-return restoration and nested modulus scoping.

message: feat: Color pairing tool (#524) * feat(ColorPairingTool): add color pairing tool with spectrum token matching Adds a Color Pairing Tool to the docs site that extracts colors from uploaded images (or manual hex input) and maps them to CDS spectrum tokens with WCAG contrast compliance. Includes drag-and-drop upload, k-means color extraction, hue-aware token matching, light/dark mode previews, and a component playground. Rewrite payload serialization as converters (#56) * Refactor serialization to converter. This follows the patterns of the Go and Java SDKs and allows interoperability between Ruby and the other SDKs by converting arguments to/from payloads in the same way. Serialisation of protobufs has been left as-is because it is not affected by interoperability issues. * Add some more payload specs. * Add mixed payloads test case. * Missed some callsites. * Make converters compatible. * PR feedback. Still need to bring a few specs back across. * Add legacy encoder. More specs. * Add legacy require. * Remove redundant parantheses. * Use a constant. * Add requires. * Add composite spec. * Remove attempt to migrate from legacy encoding. * Fix adding an extra array wrapper. Thanks to @gvieira for the report! * Produce a single payload for the error message. * Use a single payload for results and heartbeats. Ruby doesn't let us disambiguate `return 1,2` from `return [1,2]` so enforce a single payload for all cases. This makes things predictable albeit sometimes a little surprising if returning multiple values. However I think returning multiple values will be unusual, and is not supported by other SDKs so this is probably fine. * Also restrict workflow result and markers to single payloads. * Activity and child workflow results should only include the first payload. This is to get sane round-trip behaviour in Ruby without results always being an array. * Create nil payloads where applicable.
