author: UnbornAztecKing
message: (fix) improve handling of unhealthy websockets connections (#2854) Before, publishing errors were caught on each attempt to send a message from a batch to a subscriber. Now, encountering an error in publishing will stop publishing to that subscriber, minimizing redundant error generation. Before, when a websocket client would fail to respond to pings, it was disconnected by termination and cleanup. Now, the websocket is closed with an error appropriate for heartbeat timeout. In the event the websocket is healthy but the subscriber is not responding to pings, they will receive the informative error. Remove unnecessary typed buffer conversions. Minimize connection lookups by passing Connection and not ConnectionId. Add connectionId to `Connection` for use in logging and error generation. Extract metrics to methods for clarity in critical code segments. Simplify error handling in wss send. Add constants for websocket error codes. Remove ad-hoc listener removal in InvalidMessageHandler.

author: Ri-go
message: fix(subscription): apply review fixes to engine/adapter split Important: - ReplaySubs now returns the first write error (abort-on-first-error behavior unchanged in both adapters; inj's local Warn removed). The engine run loop logs the failure once at Warn under the adapter tag and carries a TODO to treat replay write failure as upstream death. - Narrow the adapter-facing engine surface to a documented sessionIO interface (upstreamWrite/clientWrite/clientReplyResult/clientReplyBool/ clientReplyError); HandleClientFrame/HandleUpstreamFrame/ReplaySubs take sessionIO instead of *engine. Conns, locks, channels, and goroutines stay engine-private. Lifecycle-test wrapper seams unchanged. Minor: - Bind the upstream reader's terminal error in the run loop and attach it (nil-safe errString, replicated locally from health) to the "upstream gone, evaluating resume" log line. - Honor SessionConfig/InjSessionConfig.HandshakeTimeout: when Dialer is nil the default dialer uses it (> 0), else 5s; fields documented as used only when Dialer is nil. - Unify JSON-RPC id unquoting: move unquoteID to wire.go and switch the eth adapter's pending-ack match from strings.Trim(`"`) to it. unquoteID handles escaped JSON strings correctly where strings.Trim did not; ids on this path are stitch-minted ("stitch_%d"), so the escaped-quote edge is unreachable in practice and the change is a strict correctness improvement on a path stitch controls. - Pin InjStreamURL's path-preserving append for path-carrying http URLs (http://x/foo -> ws://x/foo/injstream-ws) in wsurl_test.go. - Document in both adapters' ReplaySubs that stale pending entries from never-acked epochs are deliberately retained (late-notification fallback window; ids never collide; memory-only, bounded by flap count).

author: Ri-go
message: fix(health/selector): gate EVM-only backends on eth_ws stream health EVM-only backends (no CometBFT rpc endpoint) were never health-gated: the selector mapped EthRPC/EthWS/ChainStream to the ProtoRPC snapshot, which the RPC prober never writes for such backends, so the "no probe yet" optimistic default applied forever — even with the head stream down. - EthWSProber: a dropped stream now writes an unhealthy ProtoEthWS snapshot to the registry (last known height carried forward, drop error recorded), not just a zeroed gauge; the per-frame update flips it back to healthy on reconnect. The whole drop-path bookkeeping is membership-guarded so a natural drop after a hot-reload prune cannot resurrect pruned state. - Selector: healthProtocol becomes healthProtocols, an ordered witness chain — ProtoRPC (authoritative height/lag) first, ProtoEthWS (WS head stream) as fallback for the three EVM/stream protocols. The optimistic default remains only for backends no prober covers. - Dead code: Weights.CircuitOpen (circuits are hard-filtered at the Allow gate) and the constant Health score term (unhealthy backends are filtered before scoring) are removed. Ordering is unaffected for every weighted-preference case in the tree: all differing-weight test rigs use identical coverage and zero lag, where weight ordering is invariant to the removed constant. - Drop the var _ = (*backend.Backend)(nil) import anchor in subscription/session.go (last anchor outside _test files).

author: Ri-go
message: health: verify bounded backends once, skip periodic probes Bounded coverage is static: a backend declared [Lower, Upper] doesn't follow head, so its latest_block_height isn't a routing signal. The RPC/REST/GRPC/EthWS probers were waking up every probe_interval to fetch it anyway, and for backends without an eth_ws endpoint the WS prober was looping reconnect storms against unreachable hosts. This change introduces BoundedVerifier: at startup it issues one CometBFT /status (or eth_getBlockByNumber fallback) per bounded backend, asserts latest_block_height >= declared Upper, and publishes a permanent healthy snapshot under ProtoRPC. Failures retry with exponential backoff and are then surfaced as unhealthy — operators see misconfigured Upper or unreachable archives instead of silently degraded routing. The four existing probers skip CovBounded backends in their tick loops. Live-verified against the Injective EVM-sharded archive config: - shard-119m, shard-139m verified on first attempt - shard-142m correctly marked unhealthy (RPC unreachable from this host) - eth_ws logs no longer show retries against bounded shards - by-height routing regression check: 3/3 valid balances at fresh head

message: feat: keep parallel syncing for the tip while filling historical gaps Controlled by WEB3INJ_PARALLEL_SYNC_TIP_AND_GAPS which is true by default now. Why this is important - certain methods like eth_getBlock may return stale blocks while indexer synces the gaps. We now advance tip forward as well, so the methods can query and get latest indexed block wihtout querying underlying RPC directly. In case you need old behaviour (syncing all gaps in sequence, then forward the tip) just set WEB3INJ_PARALLEL_SYNC_TIP_AND_GAPS=false. We don't recommend that.

author: lucasmaan
message: fix(derive): report the filtered unit in the CLI response, and drop the dead API off-topic field (#36) * refactor(derive,web): drop the off-topic count nothing behind the API can produce The PRECISION pass is off by default and the daemon exposes no prune switch, so report.offtopic_articles was always empty on the HTTP path and every carrier of the count reported 0 unconditionally: the daemon response key, DeriveResponse's Offtopic, the "derive: done" log pair, and DeriveResult's field. #34 stopped the dialog reading it; this drops the field it used to read. No migration, because nothing decodes a stored blob into the typed struct: runner.go marshals the response into derived_jobs.result and api/derive.go forwards that text as a json.RawMessage after a bare json.Valid check, so rows carrying "offtopic":0 keep serving unchanged and the browser ignores the extra key. The decode that does matter is the daemon hop in bridge.Derive, which is a plain json.Unmarshal -- an older engine still emitting the key deserialises into the smaller struct fine. The CLI keeps its own offtopic (spec F2): kb-ai derive --prune can reach the pass and report a real count. The guard test now pins the absence of the key rather than its value, and spec H5 records the wire-level half of the decision next to the UI-level half #34 added -- both have to be undone together if prune ever becomes reachable over HTTP. Refs #35 Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * docs(derive): record --select-from in the spec's CLI and HTTP criteria #29 added the flag to the derive CLI and #30 extended it to the HTTP path, but the spec still described the surfaces both predate: F1 listed the CLI invocation without it, and H1 still gave the request body as {topic, slug?, model?} even though the handler validates select_from and the web dialog sends it. Read together they said `articles` was the only catalog a derive can filter. F1 names the default and what `documents` buys, since nothing else in the spec explains the flag. H1 records the 400 on an unknown value and says the default is supplied on the Python side -- the Go handler forwards an empty value rather than substituting one, so stating it there would be the wrong place to change it. Refs #35 Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix(derive): count the unit the CLI filtered, not always articles Under --select-from documents the engine populates selected_documents and leaves selected_articles empty by design (derive/__init__.py:220), so the CLI's response reported selected: 0 for a run that had just matched documents. The volume gate in the same command already reports the right unit, which made the two disagree inside one invocation: the operator confirmed "2 documents matched" and the JSON that came back said nothing was selected. A scripted caller reading `selected` to decide whether the topic found anything would abandon a derive that worked. Fixed the way the daemon already does it (server_daemon.py:368) -- prefer selected_documents, fall back to selected_articles -- so the CLI, the gate and the HTTP path all report the same number. The fallback cannot mask a real miss: a run that selected nothing raises NoDocumentsError before a report is built. Spec F2 now says which unit `selected` counts, since the key alone cannot say. Refs #35 Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * docs(derive): true up F2's payload list and the stale HTTP off-topic note Three review follow-ups, no behaviour change. F2 claimed to enumerate the CLI response but listed 10 of its 15 keys, omitting bytes, dropped_invented_paths, compiled, cost and warnings. F2 is the criterion someone cites when asked what the CLI returns, and bytes in particular carries the volume-gate story (F5), so the gap was load-bearing. The list now matches commands/derive.py key-for-key, order included. Also says outright that offtopic is live on this path, since H5 now says the opposite of the HTTP one and the two criteria sit far apart. notes.md's HTTP smoke run cited `offtopic: 0` as evidence that pruning stays off behind the API. The evidence is still sound but the key is gone, so anyone reproducing that run would go looking for it. Appended a clause rather than editing the figure: notes.md is a dated verification log, and rewriting what a run reported would cost more than it buys. The prune guard test's docstring said only the first of the two assertions was guarded. Both fire, in order -- forwarding the flag trips the first, restoring the count trips the second -- which is a materially better story for whoever picks this up. Says plainly what still cannot be caught: deleting both. message: feat(extraction): give each document's extraction its own layer (#32) * docs: scope the language policy to artifacts, not conversation The policy listed "conversation" among the things that must be English. That reads as a rule about how a contributor talks to their coding agent, which is not something the repository can observe and not something it needs to: none of that text lands here. What matters is that every artifact — docs, comments, commit messages, PR text, identifiers, log strings, prompts — is English, including work that was discussed in another language. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * docs(extraction-layer): specify extraction as a named layer Records the design before the code: today's per-document extraction lives in a checksum-keyed `.extract-cache/`, which makes text staleness impossible to miss but model and prompt staleness impossible to detect, and it is written by only one of the two ingestion routes. The spec gives that stage a directory (`extraction/`), a path-mirrored filename, a provenance header, one serializer shared by both routes, and two independent gates in `compile` so a prompt edit costs one extraction pass instead of a full recompile. Includes the alignment questions that fixed the open decisions, the task-level plan, and the four-layer diagram. The diagram replaces the ASCII art the spec opened with; the Chinese translation carries the same diagram with translated labels. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * feat(extraction): give each document's extraction its own layer A knowledge base now has four named layers on disk. `extraction/` holds one markdown file per raw document at the same relative path, carrying a provenance header — source, source checksum, extract model, strategy, summarize model, prompt version, timestamp, schema version — so "is this stale, and why" is a field comparison instead of a guess. The old checksum-keyed `.extract-cache/` could only see text changes; editing `prompts/defaults/extract.md` or switching models silently reused every entry. One module owns the format. `storage/extraction.py` is the only place that serializes, parses, persists, loads and judges staleness, and both ingestion routes go through it: the CLI `compile` and the daemon's `_handle_extract` now write byte-identical files, verified by a test that runs both in one process. Previously only the CLI wrote a cache, so a UI-ingested document paid for extract again on the next derive. `ExtractRequest` carries `kb_dir`, `source` and `model` for that, and `PipelineItem.Extraction` is gone — the pipeline loads the extraction from disk by its `source_ref`. `compile` splits into two independent gates. The extraction gate is missing-or-stale against the header; the write gate stays on `.compile-state.json`. So a prompt edit re-extracts and writes nothing, and `--extract-only` stops after extraction for prompt tuning. The prompt version is a hash over the whole extract prompt set, including the five rendered type-split variants, so editing any one of them invalidates exactly the extractions that used it. Read paths get shorter. The document catalog reads a summary out of a file it can name instead of hashing the document to find a cache entry, and derive copies that file instead of a hash it has to reconstruct. `derive/_status.py` adds the parent-KB drift checks. `split_frontmatter` closes on `rstrip()` so an indented `---` no longer truncates a header — compared over 353 files in the reference KB and its derived KBs, this changes no existing verdict. Verified: 1407 Python tests pass at 99% coverage (`storage/extraction.py` and `derive/_status.py` at 100%), Go tests and `go vet` clean, 454 web tests pass. No test calls a real LLM. All 108 cache entries in the reference KB round-trip through the new serializer field for field, and the layer is smaller than the cache it replaces (2.14 MB against 2.54 MB). `notes.md` records the measurements, the decisions taken beyond what the spec fixed, and seven known gaps. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * docs(extraction-layer): record the Stage 4 run The real extraction run over data/kb-2026-06 was approved and executed on 2026-08-08. Extract cost 17.4280 USD against the 17.4541 USD baseline from the KB's own .compile.log, a 0.15% difference — which is what the run was for: confirming that figure with a second measurement rather than trusting one log line. 108 documents, 0 errors. Also recorded: all 108 freshly written files re-serialize byte for byte, the layer measures 2.05 MB against the cache's 2.42 MB on real files, the gate reports "nothing to compile" at zero cost on a re-run, F3 over the parent is 108/0/0, all seven derived KBs are in sync, and a derive of an existing topic reproduced its manifest exactly and then paid nothing for extract. Two things did not go to plan and are written down as such. The document-index selection comparison had no baseline: the reference KB was compiled before the document catalog landed, so this run created that file for the first time. And the 30% wall-clock drop is not attributable to this change — same work, different write target — so it is recorded as environmental, not as a performance claim. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix(extraction): close the gaps recorded after the Stage 4 run Six of the seven gaps the extraction-layer notes recorded were real. Each was reproduced before it was touched; the seventh — `ExtractResponse.Extraction` being unused on the Go side — did not survive its own verification (a 19 KB payload against an 8 MB response buffer, and deleting the field would not stop the daemon sending it), so that code is unchanged. `extract_strategy` is now one configured value that every ingestion route reads. The CLI gate compared against a literal `chunked` while the daemon recorded whichever strategy it routed to, so a `summarize` deployment had every UI-ingested extraction read as stale on the next compile — re-extracted once per document and silently downgraded, since `summarize` never shows the structured pass the original words. `plan_extraction` and `run_planned_extraction` are the only router, `llm.extract_strategy` (env `LLM_EXTRACT_STRATEGY`) reaches `ExtractRequest.Strategy` symmetrically with `model`, `kb-ai distill` takes `--extract-strategy`, and `derive_kb` passes it to the compile of the KB it just built — that third route would otherwise have re-extracted every byte-copied extraction and ping-ponged the strategy between the two KBs. Under `chunked` or `summarize` the gate still compares a constant and reads nothing; only `auto` resolves per document, at one read and a chunk count. An unrecognised strategy is refused at four points rather than falling back, and a non-chunked strategy with no `summarize_model` is refused before the run starts. `parse()` refuses any `schema_version` but its own, which routes a format bump into `load()`'s absent branch and re-extracts instead of composing an article from a payload this code cannot read. Before, a `schema_version: 99` file parsed as v1 and the gate called it fresh. `kb-ai check --kb <dir>` is the operator entry point the F3 and F5 checks never had. One command for both kinds of KB: F5 already degrades to `unknown` with a reason, so a parent gets an honest "not derived from anything". It spends nothing and writes nothing. The wiki-lag fold now skips compile-state entries whose document is gone from `raw/`; the orphan entry itself stays, because cleanup is a stated non-goal and a test pins it in place. The write phase records a `write_prompt_version`, covering all three write system prompts — the article creator's was an unhashable f-string and is now `_create_system()`, pinned by a test, because a version that omitted a third of the prompts would be worse than none. Reported, never gated: both merge paths only add, so re-composing on a prompt edit would layer content on top of the old rather than replace it. `storage/lag.py` holds the comparison for both callers and reports "cannot tell" over an unreadable prompt set. The first-run captions are per gate, so one gate's landing cannot excuse the other's real lag. The compile scan is metadata-only and a document's text is read only once the extraction gate has selected it — `list_raw_files()` retained 6.79 MB over the 108-document reference KB against 0.05 MB for `iter_raw_file_meta()`, roughly 62 KB per document. The two checksums were compared over every file of that KB first (0 differences), since a byte-different hash would have re-extracted the corpus. `persist()` is handed the hash of the text the extraction was actually made from, so the split cannot leave an extraction whose checksum matches the document while its payload describes text that is gone. Verified: 1477 Python tests pass at 99% coverage (`commands/check.py`, `storage/lag.py`, `storage/extraction.py`, `core/merge.py` and `derive/_status.py` at 100%, `commands/compile.py` 99%), Go tests and `go vet` clean, 454 web tests pass. No test calls a real LLM. A real `--extract-only` run over the reference KB reports "nothing to compile" at zero cost. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * docs(extraction-layer): record what happened to the seven gaps Replaces the "known gaps" list with what each one turned out to be: six real and fixed, one verified as not a defect with the evidence that settled it. Each entry keeps the original numbering and says how it was reproduced, since a gap list that only names symptoms cannot be audited later. The measurements the fixes rest on are written down where a re-reader will look for them: the corpus chunk distribution behind `auto`'s three-chunk switch (31 of 108 documents are a single chunk, median 24,534 characters, largest splits into 9), the memory retained per document by the old scan, the 0-difference checksum comparison, and the derive-route cost a missed strategy would have run up. `spec.md` and `alignment-questions.md` mark their write-phase provenance gap as superseded rather than deleting it — the gap is closed as *reported*, not as gated, and the reasoning for not gating is the part worth keeping. The Stage 4 artefact `derived/stage4-extraction-check/` is kept, decided today: it is the only derived KB in the corpus holding an `extraction/` directory rather than an `.extract-cache/`, so it is where the F5 path can be exercised against post-layer copies without paying to derive again. Verified on disk against the other seven. The cost is that an F5 sweep reports eight derived KBs where the table lists seven, which the note now says outright. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * refactor(extraction): drop the connections payload field `connections` held LLM-suggested wiki article titles a document "should link to", asked for by Question 5 of both extract prompts. Nothing ever turned one into a link. Its single consumer was one line of the classify user message (`- Connections (suggested links): ...`), free text no code validated against the article set. Compare `topics`, which drives four real paths: the `Tags:` line of a new article, the relevance sort deciding which existing articles reach the classify prompt, the section scoring deciding what survives merge truncation, and the union-find clustering in `_phase_classify`. So the field cost a question in two prompts, a slot in two type-split groups, two dedup passes and a line in every extraction file, and bought a hint. It goes; if suggested links are ever worth having they come back as a field that emits links. Removed from both extract prompts, `ExtractionResult` (and the dead duplicate in `_types.py`), `parse_extraction_result`, `extraction_to_dict`, `_FIELD_JSON_SCHEMAS`, `TYPE_SPLIT_GROUPS_K2["B"]`, `TYPE_SPLIT_GROUPS_K3["C"]`, both merge helpers, `classify_article`'s user message, merge's `_FIELD_PRIORITY`, and the extraction file's frontmatter. Classify's budget needs no retuning: the removed line was in the `prefix` whose length feeds `decisions_budget`, so the freed characters go to decisions. `SCHEMA_VERSION` stays at 1. Dropping a field reads cleanly in both directions -- `parse()` never asks for the `connections:` key old files still carry, and code that still asked would read an absent key as the empty list it already tolerates -- so the version records no incompatibility. Verified against a real pre-removal file from the reference KB: it parses, 19 topics and 18 concepts intact. The re-extraction this forces comes from `prompt_version`, which is the honest reason, and it holds for every deployment rather than only the default prompts: `_extract_stage_renderings` hashes the rendered type-split variants, so the group-table and schema-table edits move the hash even where `extract.md` is overridden through `KAAS_PROMPTS_DIR`. Measured 69f137466914 -> 40173bb799fc, and `staleness()` reports exactly that. `test_file_shape_is_frontmatter_plus_five_pinned_sections` now asserts the exact frontmatter key set. It named individual keys before, so a payload field could appear or vanish and every assertion still passed -- this change is the case that showed why that matters. Verified: 1477 Python tests pass at 99% coverage, unchanged from the baseline before this change, with `storage/extraction.py`, `core/classify.py`, `core/merge.py` and `_phase_classify.py` at 100%. `go build` and `go vet` clean, 454 web tests pass. No test calls a real LLM. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * docs(extraction-layer): mark the eight-field format superseded The spec, its Chinese mirror and the alignment record all describe a frontmatter carrying `connections`, and they are dated records -- rewriting them would falsify what was specified on 2026-08-07. This repo already answered that: `spec.md` and `alignment-questions.md` carry ten `[Superseded <date>: ...]` markers added in 083425a, which leave the original wording byte-intact and protect the reader. Same treatment here. Marked: `spec.md` background item 2 (the eight-field enumeration), B1's frontmatter field list, B17's sort, the B2 example frontmatter, the four-layer diagram, and the `spec.zh-CN.md` mirrors of all five; `alignment-questions.md` C3's determinism list and its example frontmatter. The pointer runs both ways now. `serialize()`'s docstring cites B1-B5, so a reader following it lands on the eight-field list; B17 is the sharper case, because its `serialize()` docstring counterpart *was* corrected, so spec and code disagree by design and only the marker says which is current. `assets/kb-four-layers.svg` and its `.zh` twin still render `summary, topics, connections, counts` and stay as drawn: an SVG cannot carry a bracketed marker, so the note sits in the caption line that embeds it. Neither file is referenced outside these two dated specs. Not fixed here, and pre-existing: `spec.zh-CN.md` never received the 2026-08-08 marker that `spec.md:125` carries, so the pair has been out of sync since 083425a. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * refactor(types): delete the two dead duplicate dataclasses in _types.py `_types.ArticleMeta` and `_types.ExtractionResult` had no importer in `py/src`. Every production site takes `ArticleMeta` from `storage.store` (eight modules) and `ExtractionResult` from `core.extract`; the only thing reaching into `_types` for either was `tests/test_types.py`, so four tests were the sole reason both survived. They read as a canonical type module and were neither. `ArticleMeta` had already drifted, which is the concrete harm rather than a tidiness argument: `storage.store.ArticleMeta` carries a `keys: str = ""` field that the `_types` copy never gained, so anyone who followed the module docstring and imported the "shared" type would have silently lost `keys`. `_types.py` keeps what it is actually for -- `MergeTarget`, `CreateTarget` and `ClassificationResult`, imported across `core`, `commands` and their tests. Its `dataclass` and `field` imports are still both in use. Verified: 1473 Python tests pass at 99% coverage, `_types.py` at 100%. The count drops from 1477 by exactly the four tests that covered the deleted duplicates; no other test changed. `go vet` clean. message: test: raise coverage on the untested failure paths (#27) * build: add a coverage target across all three components Coverage was measurable but not reproducible: nothing in the repo wired it up, and the Python figure required pulling pytest-cov in ad hoc with `uv run --with`. `make cover` now runs Go, Python and web in one go and prints one total per component. Declares pytest-cov as a dev dependency so the Python run needs no extra flag, and records the one caveat that remains: coverage.py traces only the test process, so lines executed inside the subprocess the `slow` tests spawn are not counted. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * test: cover the untested failure paths in bridge, derive, api and sqlite Every one of these is a path that only runs when something has already gone wrong, which is exactly when silent breakage is expensive: - NewDaemonClient had no coverage at all. Adds the startup handshake against a fake daemon script, plus the two ways it can fail — the process not spawning, and the daemon rejecting init — both of which must return a nil client rather than one with no LLM credentials loaded. - MultiplexStreamDaemon.Stop's force-kill escape hatch. A wedged daemon never exits on stdin close, so without the kill Stop would block shutdown forever. Costs the full 5s grace period by design; that timeout is the thing tested. - NewRunner's config fallbacks. A zero PollInterval panics time.NewTicker and takes the process down; a zero Timeout lets one derive hang forever behind the single-flight claim. - Migrate's per-stage error labels, so a startup failure names the schema at fault instead of just reporting "SQL logic error", and the two ALTER TABLE migrations' carve-out for an already-existing column stays narrow. - rollbackFiles' unremovable-file branch. It has no error return, so the log is the only signal that a stale raw file is now blocking re-upload. Go coverage 87.1% -> 88.4%; bridge 81.4 -> 86.6, derive 83.9 -> 89.3, sqlite 91.4 -> 92.7. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * test(web): stub jsdom scrolling so streaming views can be rendered jsdom implements no scrolling. ThinkingBlock keeps a live stream pinned to the bottom by calling scrollTo from an effect, where the resulting TypeError unmounted the entire React tree — a test would see an empty document instead of a useful failure. That is why Chat's mid-stream states had never been covered: they were unreachable, not overlooked. The stubs go on Element.prototype rather than HTMLElement.prototype because MessageList.test.tsx spies on Element.prototype.scrollIntoView, and a stub further down the prototype chain shadows that spy. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * test(web): cover the untested pages, components and error branches FilePreviewSheet and MermaidBlock had no test file at all, and the three pages were tested only along their happy paths, leaving the branches a user actually hits when something fails unverified: - FilePreviewSheet: the request lifecycle, the truncation warning, and the abort on task change — without which a slow first response could land after the second and show the wrong file's content under the new title. - MermaidBlock: a diagram that will not parse must degrade to a readable message, and a render that resolves after unmount must be ignored. - Chat: history loading and its dismissible error banner, session select/rename/delete including their failures, draft preservation across a session switch, first-message session creation, and every stream event kind — status, reasoning, role, mid-stream error, and the abort that must stay quiet because stopping is not a failure. - Tasks: status and stage colour coding, the unformattable-timestamp fallback, the delete flow including the page step-back after removing a page's last task, sorting, debounced search, and pagination elision. - Wiki: 404 vs generic load failure, a tree that fails independently of the article, breadcrumbs, the collapsed tag list, and the sources dialog. Extends the Tasks mock to cover deleteTask and getTaskContent, which the page and the preview sheet both call and the previous mock omitted. Web coverage 87.42% -> 95.64% statements, 86.18% -> 93.36% branches. Chat.tsx 60.4 -> 98.65; Tasks.tsx, Wiki.tsx, FilePreviewSheet.tsx and MermaidBlock.tsx to 100%. 415 -> 451 tests. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> --------- Co-authored-by: lucasmaan <305449091+lucasmaan@users.noreply.github.com> Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

message:
feat(derive): derive a topic-scoped knowledge base from the catalog (#21) * docs(derive): add brainstorm, spec, tech design and implementation plan Feature workflow artifacts for deriving a topic-scoped knowledge base from the catalog: brainstorm decisions, testable spec, tech design and the 20-task implementation plan across Python core, MCP and the web UI. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * refactor(storage): extract the shared catalog-line renderer * feat(derive): add derive error codes and shared value objects Define the DeriveError family (DeriveError, NoCatalogError, InvalidSlugError, SlugExistsError, NestedDeriveError, NoDocumentsError, UnknownDerivedKBError) in _errors.py with machine-readable codes. Create kb_ai/derive/ package with _types.py containing filter modes (MODE_RECALL, MODE_PRECISION), value objects (Skipped, SelectionResult, DocumentRef, DeriveReport), and the Selector callable type shared by the filter, source, and layout phases (spec A–E). Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * test(errors): cover the derive error codes in the uniqueness guard Add the seven new DeriveError subclasses (DeriveError, NoCatalogError, InvalidSlugError, SlugExistsError, NestedDeriveError, NoDocumentsError, UnknownDerivedKBError) to test_all_error_codes_are_unique so that a future task reusing one of those code strings will be caught. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * feat(derive): add derived-KB layout, slug rules and manifest I/O Implements py/src/kb_ai/derive/_layout.py (spec C1-C7, E1-E4, G4): - SLUG_RE + normalise_slug / validate_slug: lexical guard before any path is built; cross-language pair comment for Task 12 (Go) and Task 16 (Go). - assert_not_nested: manifest presence distinguishes a real derived KB from a directory that merely happens to be named 'derived'. - check_slug_available / create: --force replaces only directories derive itself created (manifest slug must match); shutil.rmtree only after that check, so a mistyped --kb cannot silently wipe unrelated directories. - copy_documents: copies raw documents and matching .extract-cache entries by value (not symlink) so the derived KB is independent of the source. - write_manifest / read_manifest / list_derived: provenance I/O; absent or unparseable manifests return {}. - resolve_kb_dir: shared read-path resolver for MCP ask and HTTP handlers; uses Path.resolve() containment check (matching KBStore._resolve) to reject symlinks planted under derived/ pointing outside the KB. 33 tests, all passing; full suite 1103 passed, 1 skipped, 1 xfailed. * fix(derive): confine the derived-directory delete to the KB Addresses all review findings from the first round of security and quality review on the derive layout module (task 3). Critical (finding 1): add _safe_create_target() which resolves the slug target and checks is_relative_to() against the unresolved derived/ base, matching KBStore._resolve. create() now calls this before check_slug_available so neither rmtree nor mkdir runs when a symlink is planted at <kb>/derived or <kb>/derived/<slug>. Two new tests plant real symlinks and assert the outside directory survives. Important (finding 2): copy_documents rejects rel_path that is absolute or contains '..' and rejects a checksum that does not match ^[0-9a-f]{16}$ (spec E4), raising DeriveError in both cases. Three new tests cover these guards. Important (finding 3): add parametrized hostile-slug test that asserts InvalidSlugError is raised before the filesystem is touched, plus the two symlink layout tests described above. Minor (finding 4): widen read_manifest except to (OSError, ValueError) so UnicodeDecodeError (invalid UTF-8) is also silenced. Make write_manifest atomic via a .tmp sibling + os.replace, matching the precedent in storage/store.py. New test plants a file with invalid UTF-8 and asserts read_manifest returns {}. Minor (finding 5): list_derived now skips children failing SLUG_RE and children whose resolved path is not relative to the derived/ base, so the set of slugs it advertises agrees with what resolve_kb_dir accepts. New test plants a symlinked child and asserts it is excluded. Minor (finding 6): correct the module docstring spec list from C1-C7,E1-E4,G4 to C1-C5,C7,E1,E2,E4,G4 (C6 and E3 belong to later tasks). Minor (finding 7): assert_not_nested parent-name comparison is now case-insensitive so a KB at <root>/Derived/<slug> is also caught. Naming (finding 8): rename dest_dir parameter to derived_dir in copy_documents, write_manifest and read_manifest for cross-task consistency with the plan interface list. * fix(derive): require the derived target to sit directly in derived/ Finding 1: replace is_relative_to(base) with target.parent == base in _safe_create_target. The old guard passed when slug resolved to base itself (<kb>/derived/<slug> symlinked to <kb>/derived), allowing force=True to rmtree the whole derived/ tree and destroy every sibling derived KB. The parent-equality check also closes the deeper-nesting variant (<kb>/derived/<slug> → <kb>/derived/a/b). Finding 2: switch _CHECKSUM_RE.match to fullmatch so a checksum string like 'deadbeefdeadbeef
' is rejected — re.match with $ allowed the trailing newline to slip through. Finding 3: reword the InvalidSlugError message in _safe_create_target to state the rule factually rather than accuse a symlink. New tests confirm both failures against the pre-fix guard. Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix(derive): accept only the exact derived/<slug> directory The old _safe_create_target guard required target.parent == base, which let two symlink layouts slip through: - sibling-symlink: derived/pricing -> derived/pricing-backup parent is still derived/, so rmtree deleted the sibling's real tree. - dangling-symlink: derived/pricing -> derived/ghost (nonexistent) parent is still derived/, so mkdir silently created derived/ghost, making create()'s return value diverge from derived_dir(). Replace the parent-equality check with an exact-path comparison: resolve the filesystem entry at base/slug and require it to equal base/slug itself. Any symlink produces a different resolved path and is rejected before rmtree or mkdir runs. Add two tests that confirm the pre-fix guard raised nothing for both layouts and verify post-fix behaviour plus data-survival assertions. Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com> * feat(derive): add the topic filter with prompt-budget batching Implements spec A1-A8: LLM-based article selection over a catalog listing with two modes (RECALL permissive, PRECISION strict) sharing one prompt template, greedy prompt-budget batching with line_over_budget skips, invented-path dropping, first-seen deduplication across batches, and a hard DeriveError on any malformed response to prevent silently empty KBs. Observed directly: CONTRIBUTING.md classified as decision in one KB and project in another, same source document, same 4-item menu. The fix is deterministic ordering, not temperature or retries. - Usage saturates at five categories. Going 6 to 8 added no distinctions and left three dead. Growing the menu re-partitions rather than extends: only 62% of documents kept their type across all three menus, so changing a KB's category set is a migration, not a config change. - Category definitions in the prompt help modestly — top bucket 62% to 50%, two documents moved, both correctly. The remaining concentration is probably the corpus, and settling that needs a human-labelled gold set that does not exist yet. Recommends six categories and notes that membership matters more than count: person fired zero times in 240 classifications while reference and guide, absent from the default, took the right four documents. Also records a gap found on the way: the classify cache key omits the prompt text, so editing classify.md leaves cached classifications in place and appears to do nothing. No code changed. The default menu is deliberately untouched — it would move roughly a third of articles in every existing KB. Why these six: over 240 classifications, `person` was chosen zero times and `decision` zero to two times, while `reference` and `guide` -- absent from the original four -- took the right documents, filing policy files as reference and how-to files as guide. Usage saturated at five categories in every menu tested, so six leaves one slot of headroom. `person` stays because core/people.py generates people articles from config, a path a docs-only corpus never exercises. Why definitions: the prompt passed bare words, leaving the model to infer what each meant, and `project` became the default bucket at 81% of a docs corpus. Definitions are keyed by category name in code rather than written into the prompt, so a caller passing a custom `categories` list gets no definitions instead of definitions for words it is not using. They reach the prompt through a new {category_definitions} placeholder; a user prompt override that lacks the placeholder still renders, since the registry allows extra variables. Verified live against the shipped classify_article with the default menu, 16 documents: project 8, concept 4, guide 2, reference 2, no off-menu types, top bucket 50% -- down from 81% on the original four and 62% on six bare names. Also corrects an overstatement in the findings doc. The 62% cross-menu re-partition applies to a KB classified from scratch. On a populated KB classification prefers merging into existing articles -- 16 of 16 did at every menu size -- so existing articles keep their paths and only new ones use the new set. The real cost is a mixed taxonomy over time plus one re-classification, not a migration. Landing this at v0.1.0 is the cheapest moment for it. Also collapses three duplicate copies of the default list onto the shared constant. 1206 passed, 1 skipped, 1 xfailed. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix(classify): emit results in input order, not completion order The parallel branch collected group results via as_completed() and flattened them in completion order, so classified_items came back in a different order on every run and the dedup and write phases downstream saw a different order each time. Collect into a dict keyed by the item's index in `items` and emit in sorted key order. Group crashes go into the same map so a dead group's per-item errors land in their input positions too, instead of jumping ahead of the groups that survived. This is one of three ordering defects behind the recorded 48-vs-98 article variance. The other two are still open and now recorded accurately in docs/classify-taxonomy-measurements.md: cross-group duplicate creation (dedup_create_new only sees one group's copy of `existing`), and the input `items` order. Worker scheduling and the clustering function are ruled out as sources -- each group gets an untouched copy of the baseline, and the clustering breaks ties on (i, j). Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix(classify): key the classify cache on the prompt, not just category names The third cache-key component hashed only the category names, so a prompt-only edit changed nothing the key could see. Editing classify.md left every cached classification in place and the edit appeared to do nothing on a KB that had already been compiled -- and the category definitions live in CATEGORY_DEFINITIONS in code, so editing a definition had the same silent-no-op problem. classify_inputs_hash() hashes the rendered system template instead, with the articles placeholder left unfilled since classify_cache_key carries the articles separately. It therefore moves when the prompt file, a category definition, or the category list changes. classify_article() now renders through the same helper so the hash cannot drift from the prompt actually sent. This also closes a mismatch it exposed. compile_kb hashed its own `categories or []` argument while classify_article substituted the defaults for a falsy list, so every kb-ai distill run -- which never passes categories -- wrote entries keyed as "no categories" for runs that used all six. effective_categories() is now the single definition of "what the run will actually use" and both call sites derive the hash from it. Verified end to end: two runs with an identical prompt make one LLM call, and a prompt-only edit forces a second. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * feat(classify): freeze the category set per KB DEFAULT_CATEGORIES is a measured default that can change between releases, and nothing tied a KB to the set it was built with. A KB compiled under one taxonomy would quietly start filing new articles under another, leaving a mixed taxonomy that re-running does not repair. kb-ai distill made this certain: it never passed categories at all, so it always used whatever the current default happened to be. resolve_categories() writes the effective set to <kb>/kaas.json on first use and later runs inherit it. Both entry points that classify -- compile_kb and the pipeline entry -- resolve through it, so the daemon and the CLI cannot disagree. kb-ai distill gains --categories to choose the set on that first run; omitting it stays None rather than becoming the defaults, which is what lets an existing KB keep its own set. An explicit set that conflicts with the frozen one is honoured, because the daemon accepts categories per request and refusing would break existing callers, but it warns: that is exactly the case that mixes a KB's taxonomy. A conflict does not re-freeze. Two cases deliberately do not write config: a read-only store, which the MCP server opens, and a KB directory that does not exist -- writing there would leave a mistyped --kb path looking like a real KB, the same trap 5d580b4 closed for distill's source paths. Verified end to end: a custom set freezes on creation, a later run with no flag inherits it, a conflicting set warns without re-freezing, and compiling a mistyped path creates nothing. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix(dedup): elect one creator per cross-group duplicate The cross-group dedup pass cancelled itself out. For each item it built the cross-group article list from every other item's creations, minus its own paths, which makes a collision symmetric: item A merged into B's path, B merged into A's path, both dropped their own create, and neither path kept a create to serve it. The write phase creates any merge target that does not exist yet, so both articles were written anyway -- with titles derived from the filename stem, because no CreateTarget survived to supply one. The pass reported "2 articles merged" and produced two articles. Identical paths were worse: the own-paths filter hid A's copy from B and B's copy from A, so nothing deduped at all. The pass now walks items in input order and dedups each against the creations accepted so far, so exactly one item keeps the create and every later collider points at it. An item's own creations join the pool only after that item is done, so a classification that deliberately split one document into two articles still gets both. Shared state in the classify workers would have fixed the same symptom by putting race-dependent context back into the parallel groups, which is what 6c147fc removed. This stays entirely after the join, and its outcome depends only on the input order -- which now decides which spelling of a title wins, not how many articles a collision produces. kb-ai distill never hit this: compile_kb classifies serially against an accumulating existing_articles, which already elects a first writer. It needs a pipeline request carrying enough items to form two groups, and the Go worker sends one item per request, so it was reachable through the daemon API rather than the CLI. Covered by a unit test per collision shape (near-duplicate title, identical path, three-way) and an end-to-end pipeline test that asserts one file on disk where two groups invented the same article. author: lucasmaan
message: feat(retrieval): advertise reference-table keys in the catalog line (#19) * feat(retrieval): advertise reference-table keys in the catalog line Page selection reads one 150-char summary per article, which cannot name the dozens of discrete values a config or API table defines. A question about one of those values ("how many entries may a zip hold?") had no signal pointing at the article holding the answer, so the selector fell back to whichever title sounded topical. Each catalog line now also lists the identifiers its tables define, as a `| keys:` column kept apart from the prose summary: classification reads `summary[:80]` and hashes it for its cache key, so folding keys into the summary would pollute that prompt and invalidate the cache. Capped at 500 chars per article, whole keys only. Measured on a 48-article compile of this repository -- 10 narrow factual queries phrased without naming the keys, 2 runs each, us.claude-sonnet-4-6: selection hit-rate 13/20 -> 20/20 on derived prose summaries and 18/20 -> 20/20 on written frontmatter summaries, while the mean number of articles selected fell from 3.80 to 3.50. The reported query now answers 200 from kaas-backend-configuration.md instead of reporting no limit. Refs #18 Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * feat(index): make the catalog summary budget configurable The whole catalog goes into every page-selection prompt, so the summary budget is really a trade between summary length and how many articles fit before the prompt limit. That trade belongs to the deployment, not to a module constant: at the current ~367 chars per catalog line the selection prompt alone reaches MAX_PROMPT_CHARS at roughly 218 articles. `update_markdown_index` takes `summary_max_chars`, threaded through `compile_kb` and both pipeline entry points from a `summary_max_chars` request key, mirroring how `topic_index_min_articles` is already plumbed. The default stays 150, now for a measured reason rather than by default. Sweeping the cap over 50/80/100/120/150/200/300/400/600 on a 48-article compile of this repository -- 14 prose-fact questions whose answers are in article bodies rather than in any table, 2 runs each, gold sets verified by grepping the answer token -- selection recall is flat at 26/28 across the entire range while the catalog grows from 13.0K to 29.5K chars. There is no recall optimum to pick, so the default matches what the write phase is asked to produce (one sentence under 150 chars) and stays at the cheap end. Refs #18 Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix(index): raise the catalog summary cap to what the write phase emits The cap was 150 because that is the length core.merge asks the write phase for. It is not the length the write phase produces: across 20 articles from two compiles of this repository, written summaries run 143-200 chars (median 159, p90 184). Capping at 150 clipped 13 of 15 in the larger sample, and the clipped tail was the last enumerated specific in the sentence -- "...and chat API implementation notes", "...orchestrated classify->dedup->write pipeline", "...with heartbeat and circuit-breaker support" -- which is exactly the routing signal a catalog summary exists to carry, discarded from 87% of articles. 200 is where that clipping stops (250 changes nothing, nothing exceeds 200) and it costs 5.6% more catalog on a declared-summary corpus. A cap of 160, the obvious guess from a 5-article sample, would still clip 7 of 15. The cap is a backstop bounding one catalog line, not the generator's target: the write prompt still asks for one sentence under 150, and the first-paragraph fallback (median 384 chars) is still cut hard. Selection recall was measured flat from 50 to 600 chars, so no recall claim is being made here -- this recovers written text that was being generated and then thrown away. Also defaults `summary_max_chars` late (None) rather than binding SUMMARY_MAX_CHARS at definition time, so the constant stays the single source of truth and patching it in a test behaves as expected. Refs #18 Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> --------- Co-authored-by: lucasmaan <305449091+lucasmaan@users.noreply.github.com> Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Correct — the previous verify was a facade. Three concrete bugs found, all fixed: 1. Schema mismatch: manifest-verify expected 'sha256' field, but the real manifest on ai-skill-manifest uses 'files' (matches mcp/manifest and skill/manifest sibling manifests). Updated to 'files'. 2. URL wrong: default was 'api.bybit.com/cli/manifest' but Bybit's mount convention (matches skill and mcp) is 'api.bybit.com/ai-manifest/cli/manifest'. Writes the manifest file to ../ai-skill-manifest/ai-manifest/cli/manifest for team B to review and push to internal GitLab. - 'pnpm build:manifest' shortcut in package.json - docs/release-flow.md rewritten with concrete step-by-step for both release lanes (Team A: npm publish, Team B: manifest publish) and order-matters warning (manifest must ship BEFORE npm). - tests updated for new schema; 5/5 pass.

author: APF20
message: Fix for reconnect stale data issues As Bybit still do not send through snapshot data for private topics, if the WS encounters an error (eg. ping/pong timed out) and restart_on_error (self.handle_error) is set to True, the WS will attempt to reconnect. If successful reconnect, the self.data dictionary entries for private topics can/will become stale in the time it takes to reconnect, as there is no snapshot on connect to overwrite with current data. Public topic subscriptions will be overwritten by the new snapshot data, so it is being cleared/updated in any case. This fix adds a common reset function for the state booleans and to clear the (potentially stale) dictionary.

author: varunjain15
message: Fix SBE parity script crash on Python 3.10 (#168) * Fix Py3.10 TimeoutError swallow in parity script; warn on unsupported public+SBE combo - scripts/check_sbe_parity.py: asyncio.wait_for raises asyncio.TimeoutError, which is only an alias for the builtin TimeoutError on Python >=3.11. On the repo's minimum supported 3.10, the bare `except TimeoutError` never fires and the script crashes instead of printing partial results. Catch both explicitly. - ws_client.py: sbe_enabled=True only takes effect against the direct endpoint — ws-public.api.{env} ignores the sbeSchemaId/sbeSchemaVersion query params and always sends JSON, so enabling it without direct=True silently no-ops instead of decoding binary frames. Warn at connect() time when that combination is detected, and document the constraint on ParadexWebsocketClient.sbe_enabled and Paradex.ws_sbe_enabled. * Revert incorrect SBE public-endpoint warning Verified with raw frame-type inspection that ws-public.api.{env} does send binary SBE frames when sbeSchemaId/sbeSchemaVersion are present, on both prod and testnet. The earlier warning was based on a flawed test: the JSON path and the SBE decode path both produce identically shaped {"params": {"channel": ..., "data": {...}}} dicts, so seeing a normal-looking dict out of the callback didn't actually prove which path ran. sbe_enabled=True works correctly on the public endpoint; only the check_sbe_parity.py Python 3.10 fix remains from this branch. * Update stale testnet chain id assertion in test_system_config Live testnet's starknet_chain_id has moved from PRIVATE_SN_POTC_SEPOLIA to PRIVATE_SN_PARACLEAR_TESTNET since this test was written, failing CI on every PR (unrelated to this branch's actual change).

author: sv
message: Add WebSocket order management with Cancel-on-Disconnect support (#143) * Add WebSocket order management with Cancel-on-Disconnect support Implements WS order management on ParadexWebsocketClient to mirror the server-side API added in tradeparadigm/mono#33320. Users can now switch from REST to WebSocket transport by calling `ws_client.*` instead of `api_client.*` — the method names are intentionally identical. New methods on ParadexWebsocketClient: - submit_order / submit_orders_batch (order.create / order.create_batch) - modify_order (order.modify) - cancel_order / cancel_order_by_client_id (order.cancel) - cancel_all_orders (order.cancel_all) - cancel_orders_batch (order.cancel_batch) - cancel_on_disconnect (order.cancel_on_disconnect) — OFF by default, session-scoped, resets on each reconnect Plumbing: - WsRpcError exception carries server JSON-RPC error code/message/data - _pending_requests dict correlates responses to callers via JSON-RPC id - _send_request helper registers a Future, sends the message, awaits reply - _check_subscribed_channel resolves pending futures before subscription acks - _close_connection cancels all in-flight futures with ConnectionError immediately on disconnect, avoiding silent timeout hangs on reconnect Tests: 26 unit tests covering all methods, error paths, timeout cleanup, concurrent requests, reconnect cleanup, and _process_message integration. Example: examples/ws_order_management.py * Simplify WS order management: safe IDs, async fixes, DRY tests - Replace microsecond timestamp IDs with itertools.count in _send_request to eliminate collision risk for concurrent requests - Use asyncio.get_running_loop() instead of deprecated get_event_loop() - Use existing time_now_micro_secs() utility for auth/subscribe/unsubscribe IDs - Remove unnecessary asyncio.shield() wrapper in wait_for call - Use direct dict key access (message["id"]) after "id" in message guard - Extract _run_with_response helper in tests, removing 13 copies of the inject-task-await pattern - Add WsRpcError to docs index so the public exception is rendered

author: yasir7ca
message: feat!(BET-3930): remove hardcoded DEFAULT_CONFIG fallback (#49) The SDK shipped a giant DEFAULT_CONFIG constant with every protocol's package + shared object IDs hardcoded. When /config fetch failed (Cloudflare blocks, transient network), the SDK silently fell back to this constant — building PTBs with whatever stale addresses were baked into the deployed bundle. This bit us today: an hour after Turbos's package was bumped and rolled out to the prod aggregator, a wallet still showed `0xd02012c7…::pool:: check_version` because the SDK fell back to its hardcoded constant during a fetch hiccup. Stale on-chain addresses are the worst kind of fallback. The new contract: if /config can't be fetched, throw — don't pretend. - Drop the entire DEFAULT_CONFIG constant (~180 lines of stale data). - getConfig() throws a clear error on fetch failure or non-2xx. - Bump SDK to 7.0.0 (semver-major: buildTx now throws under conditions where it previously returned a Transaction with stale addresses). Tests: - configOverride.spec.ts switched from importing DEFAULT_CONFIG to a small inline fixture. - New getConfig.spec.ts asserts the throw-on-unreachable behaviour (regression test for BET-3930). Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: agent-smith-k
message: feat: server-authoritative rate limiting with enriched errors (#9) Remove client-side rate throttling (SpotRateLimiter, FuturesRateLimiter, SpotTier config). Requests now flow directly to the Kraken API without artificial delays or hidden retry loops for rate-limit responses. When Kraken rejects a request due to rate limits, the CLI returns the error immediately with enriched fields: - suggestion: tier-specific guidance on what to adjust - docs_url: canonical Kraken documentation link - retryable: always true for rate_limit category This lets agents and automation layers read the error, consult the docs, and adapt their own pacing strategy rather than having the CLI impose opaque backoff delays that could stale time-sensitive orders. Also includes: - WebSocket reconnect hardening (12 attempts, paced exponential backoff with jitter, rolling window budget, token-refresh rate-limit integration) - Futures auth error classification (authenticationError, insufficientPrivileges mapped to Auth category) - Comprehensive integration and unit tests for all new behavior - Updated docs, skills, AGENTS.md, error-catalog.json

author: PDiogo
message: feat: rebuild the dashboard frontend on The Graph Design System Rebuilds the Rewards Eligibility Oracle dashboard on real GDS components, prerendered to static HTML and hydrated for interactivity. An /impeccable critique scored the previous dashboard 14/40. Its central finding was that the generic appearance was structural rather than chromatic: a gradient body with a floating white card wrapping a raw 98-row table, with a cookie emoji as the wordmark. A token swap could change which colours were used but not that shape, which is why this is a rebuild. A re-score using the same method gives 25/40. Architecture — two halves, one contract: generate_dashboard.py -> output/data.json -> React (SSG) -> output/index.html Python fetches on-chain data and writes JSON; React renders it. Neither half crosses the line: the frontend reads only data.json, and Python emits no markup. This remains a snapshot architecture — nothing is fetched in the browser, and freshness still comes from regenerating every ~5 minutes. GDS ships components only as React (gds-css is a Tailwind preset with no component classes), so consuming the design system properly required a React renderer. The SSR bundle is self-contained, so the runtime image needs a node binary but no node_modules. scheduler.py is unchanged: rendering hangs off main(), so the one-shot and scheduled paths cannot drift. Rendering is atomic and non-fatal, leaving the previous page serving if it fails. generate_dashboard.py drops from 4,105 to ~2,000 lines; generate_html_dashboard() and its ~1,100-line <style> block are deleted. What indexers get that they did not have: - The eligibility criteria on the page, above the roster, fetched at generation time from the oracle's ELIGIBILITY_CRITERIA.md so they cannot go stale. Provenance is named and linked: GIP-0079 (the specification), GGP-0058 (The Graph Council's vote ratifying it, passed 6-0), and the living criteria document the GIP delegates to. - A self-lookup resolving to a single-subject verdict card, with ?indexer=, ?network= and ?status= deep links, so a Telegram alert can point at the affected indexer rather than the top of the page. - The 14-day grace countdown, the defining number in GIP-0079, which was never computed anywhere before. Badges self-describe ("Grace · 3 days left"), so the detached legend card is gone. - A card per indexer on mobile, where the six-column table previously pushed Status off screen. Correctness fixes: - --graph-red was an invalid 7-digit hex that CSS silently dropped, removing the ineligible badge's border and rendering Expired and Unqualified identically. They now have distinct GDS Status variants. - Explorer links hardcoded chain=arbitrum-one on every network; the slug is now derived from network_id. - The GIP forum link 404'd; corrected to the thread the previous dashboard used. - Arbitrum Sepolia no longer publishes eligibility verdicts its oracle never made. Its last_oracle_update_time is 0 — the oracle has never run there — yet every indexer rendered "Unqualified · never renewed", a judgement about named third parties that no oracle issued. Availability is now gated on the oracle having actually run. - Oracle staleness is surfaced rather than swallowed. Mainnet last ran 30 days ago against a 14-day period, previously rendered as 48 healthy "Eligible" badges, making a stalled oracle indistinguishable from a healthy one on a page whose purpose is monitoring it. Accessibility, which the critique found broken throughout: every status colour failed WCAG AA in the default theme and now none do; 9 of 13 controls had no focus ring and now none lack one; sortable headers were mouse-only and are now real buttons with aria-sort; landmarks, heading order, table semantics, a skip link, live regions and labelled controls are all in place. author: MoonBoi9001
message: perf: stop querying the network subgraph on every TAP receipt (#1069) * perf(service): move allocation-redeemed check to a background watcher The TAP receipt path queried the network subgraph once per receipt to ask whether the allocation's escrow was already redeemed, blocking every paid query on an external round trip. A watcher now keeps a snapshot for the active allocations and the check reads it in memory. * perf(service): read RAV redemption from postgres, not the subgraph The redeemed check no longer polls the network subgraph at all. indexer-agent already records when a collection's closing RAV is redeemed on-chain; the check now loads those rows and stays current through a trigger with pg_notify, the same pattern the deny-list check uses. * fix(service): reject from redeemed_at so the check can fire in time The final flag is only set a finality window after redemption, past the default buffer in which receipts still pass eligibility, so the check never fired. Keying on last and redeemed_at fires at redemption time; rows are scoped per service provider and reconnects trigger reloads. * docs(service): state when the redeemed check can actually fire In the routine lifecycle redemption follows the same recently-closed buffer that gates the eligibility check, so by the time a closing RAV is redeemed, eligibility already rejects the receipt; the check's real role is insurance against out-of-band redemptions, not a routine gate. * fix(service): re-listen before resyncing redeemed RAVs after reconnect When the notification connection dropped, the watcher reloaded the redeemed set while still disconnected; sqlx only reconnects on the next receive call, so a redemption landing between the reload and the reconnect went unseen. Re-issue LISTEN first, then reload, as at startup. * fix(service): resync redeemed RAVs when a notification fails to parse The watcher used to log and skip a notification it could not parse. The payload comes from this repo's own trigger, so a parse failure means the trigger and the Rust code drifted apart and every later notification would fail too; reload the whole set from the table instead.

author: incrypto32
message: chain/ethereum: OR-merge receipt requirements in EthereumLogFilter (#6558) * chain/ethereum: add unit tests for EthereumLogFilter receipt merge Cover all six insertion sites (from_data_sources arms, from_mapping, extend) and assert OR semantics across the three internal collections (contracts_and_events_graph, wildcard_events, events_with_topic_filters). Tests use two assertion helpers (assert_from_data_sources_or_merges and assert_extend_or_merges) parameterized over the match-arm or collection variant. Each helper runs both insertion orders so order-independence is verified per variant. The OR-semantics property test catches any flag-sequence regression. * chain/ethereum: OR-merge receipt requirements in EthereumLogFilter Wrap the three EthereumLogFilter collections in MergeMap and MergeGraph newtypes whose only mutators (or_insert / or_add_edge) OR-combine the bool weight with any existing value at the same key. The inner HashMap and GraphMap are private, so callers cannot bypass the merge by going through HashMap::insert or GraphMap::add_edge. When two handlers collide on the same filter key with differing receipt flags, the merged value is now the logical OR rather than the last write. Handlers that declared receipt: true now reliably receive transaction receipts even when another handler at the same key declared receipt: false. * chain/ethereum: Remove obsolete topic-filter test TODO Topic-filtered events are now covered by the receipt-merge tests, so the stale TODO is no longer needed.

author: RembrandtK
message: feat(deployment): gather per-component upgrade bundles and gate governance execution The GIP-0088 upgrade orchestrator now gathers each component's upgrade-<Name>.json into one consolidated batch, and execute-governance requires explicit bundle selection when more than one bundle is pending. Gather model: each component writes its own upgrade-<Name>.json reflecting current on-chain state; the orchestrator reads whichever files exist, appends their TXs into the consolidated bundle, adds Group 2/3 cross-component config TXs, saves one batch, then moves the source bundles into txs/incorporated/<batch>/ so they're invisible to execute-governance. Components keep working standalone for hotfixes. createGovernanceTxBuilder claims ownership of its filesystem slot (public claimBundleSlot helper), clearing stale files left by prior runs. Execution gate: 0 pending bundles -> no-op; 1 -> execute; 2+ -> error listing the files and TX counts, requiring --name <basename> or --all. --name X with X missing now errors (--allow-missing restores the old silent no-op); --name with --all is rejected. Selection is a pure selectBundles() so the gate is unit-testable without an executor. executeTxBatchDirect writes the full enhanced bundle (_transactionMetadata, _gatheredFrom, meta) to executed/ via builder.saveToFile, so fork-mode audit trails match the testnet/mainnet shape.

message: test: describe expected behaviour instead of point-in-time bugs in regression tests Several regression tests narrated the bug they were born from ("THE BUG: with the original buggy code...", "Old code: A.sub(S).add(P) reverts...", "the old buggy ... approach") in comments and assertion messages. Once the underlying fix lands, that narration is stale and misleading: it describes code that no longer exists rather than the invariant the test guards. Reframe the comments and assertion messages to state the expected behaviour as a permanent property (snapshot-delta distribution regardless of same-block ordering; underflow-safe A.add(P).sub(S) under an inverted snapshot state; per-provider escrow deficit; pending-update escrow freed on cancel). author: RembrandtK
message: fix: prevent over-allocation double-collection in presentPOI auto-downsize When an over-allocated indexer presents a POI, presentPOI takes rewards and updates the allocation in storage (snapshotRewards / clearPendingRewards), but passed the stale memory snapshot captured at the top of the function into _resizeAllocation. That snapshot recomputed the reward accumulator delta from the pre-snapshot value and re-credited accRewardsPending with the rewards just paid out, letting the indexer collect them again on the next POI. _resizeAllocation now reads the current allocation state from storage itself instead of accepting a caller-supplied copy, so neither caller has to keep a memory copy in sync with storage. This removes the stale-snapshot hazard for both the auto-downsize and explicit-resize paths. Includes failing-then-passing unit and integration regression tests.

author: incrypto32
message: Decide load_related membership against final state (#6548) * graph: Fix load_related returning stale or phantom derived entities EntityCache::load_related decided derived field membership against intermediate cache layers, so same-block changes to an entity's parent reference could leave it in the wrong derived collection (or omit it from one it had moved into). Rewrite load_related to build a candidate set from the store baseline plus in-block writes, resolve each candidate's final state by layering store -> updates -> handler_updates the same way get() does, and apply query.matches exactly once against the final state. * graph, store: Add tests for load_related under same-block membership changes Cover six scenarios where an entity's parent reference or presence changes within a block: a single-handler reassignment that should remove the entity from the old parent's derived collection, a cross-handler reassign-then-revert that should leave the intermediate parent's collection unchanged, a cross-handler touch-then-reassign that should add the entity to the new parent's collection, a removal landing in updates and a removal landing in handler_updates that both drop the entity from its collection, and a fresh in-handler creation that should appear in the new parent's collection. * graph: Avoid cloning keys when building load_related candidate set Hold borrowed `EntityKey` references in the candidate `BTreeSet` instead of cloning into owned keys. The keys borrow from `stored`, `self.updates`, and `self.handler_updates`, all of which outlive the candidate set.

author: RembrandtK
message: fix(collector): persistent agreement.payer for independent cancellation (TRST-L-7) Persist agreement.payer (and dataService/serviceProvider) at offer time rather than waiting until accept(). _requirePayer is replaced by an inline payer check at the cancel() call site now that agreement.payer is the reliable authority — no more fallback decoding of stored RCA data on every cancel. Persistent agreement.payer makes cancelling a pre-acceptance RCA offer and cancelling a pending RCAU offer independent operations that may be performed in either order. Neither path leaves the other unreachable. _offerUpdate also simplifies: it reads agreement.payer/dataService/ serviceProvider directly (set by _offerNew) rather than decoding the stored RCA on every update offer. State guard relaxes to accept {NotAccepted, Accepted} so update offers work post-acceptance. cancel(by) clears any pending RCAU offer at cancellation time — pendingHash != activeTermsHash means the pending offer is now stale and can be reaped. offer() hoists the msg.sender == details.payer authorization out of both _offerNew and _offerUpdate now that details.payer is reliably populated by either path. accept() now stores the RCA offer idempotently (when not already present) so accept-without-prior-offer paths leave the same on-chain trail. update() does the same for RCAU storage.

message: fix(subgraph-service): validate update terms against RCAU rate, not stale agreement rate IndexingAgreement.update() validated new indexing terms against wrapper.collectorAgreement.maxOngoingTokensPerSecond (the current agreement's rate) instead of rcau.maxOngoingTokensPerSecond (the update's rate). If the RCAU decreased the rate, indexing terms exceeding the new cap would be accepted. accept() already validates against rca.maxOngoingTokensPerSecond — this makes update() consistent.

author: lutter
message: graph, node, store: Add max_contracts parameter to clear_stale_call_cache When --max-contracts is passed alongside --ttl-days, compute an effective TTL that limits eviction to at most that many contracts. The effective TTL is determined by looking at the (max_contracts+1)th oldest stale entry in call_meta; if it exists, the cutoff is set to its accessed_at date so that contracts at that date are excluded. When multiple contracts share the boundary date, fewer than max_contracts may be deleted since the cutoff operates at date granularity.

author: lutter
message: graph, node, store: Return eviction stats from clear_stale_call_cache Return a StaleCallCacheResult struct with effective_ttl_days, cache_entries_deleted, and contracts_deleted so the graphman command can report what actually happened to the user.

author: lutter
message: graph, store: Use ctid-based join delete for call cache eviction Replace the two-loop structure (fetch stale contracts, then delete their call_cache rows in tiny batches) with a single adaptive loop that joins call_cache to call_meta directly and deletes by ctid. The old approach did `WHERE contract_address = ANY(N addresses)` on the 6.9B row call_cache table repeatedly, which required expensive index scans. The new approach lets Postgres join the small filtered call_meta result against call_cache using the contract_address index, then deletes by physical row address (ctid), which is the fastest possible delete path. Also removes the GRAPH_STORE_STALE_CALL_CACHE_CONTRACTS_BATCH_SIZE env var since batch size is now fully controlled by AdaptiveBatchSize.

author: lutter
message: graph, node, store: Remove ttl_max_contracts from clear_stale_call_cache The ttl_max_contracts parameter limited how many contracts got processed per invocation. With the upcoming switch to a more efficient delete strategy that doesn't iterate by contract, this parameter no longer maps to anything meaningful. Remove it from the trait, CLI, and all implementations.
