author: karimhass
message: fix: guard datashare run-operation against non-prod targets (#77) ## Summary `datashare_trigger_sync_operation` has no target guard. It resolves the source schema straight from the manifest, so on the default `dev` target it registers the temp schema (`<team>__tmp_<suffix>`) as a real datashare and ships it to the destination warehouse. `datashare_trigger_sync()` (the post-hook) already guards on `target.name != 'prod'`; this path never did. Every `run-operation` example in `docs/dune-datashares.md` omitted `--target prod`, so following the docs verbatim reproduces the bug. ## Impact Confirmed in production at a customer. Two invocations from their `dbt.log`, neither with `--target prod`: ``` invocation_command: dbt run-operation datashare_trigger_sync_operation --args model_selector: staking_balance target_name: "dev" → ALTER TABLE dune.<team>__tmp_<user>.staking_balance EXECUTE datashare(...) ``` This produced destination tables and views named after their dev schema, which they then found in BigQuery. Their post-hook behaved correctly throughout the same run (35 × `Skipping ... only runs on the prod target`). Two things make it worse than a stray registration: - `_datashare_active_sync_exists` forces `full_refresh = true` when no registration exists. A dev schema never has one, so the **first** accidental invocation is always the most expensive variant. - With `full_refresh`, `time_start` resolves to the model's full-backfill window. In the customer's case that shipped a ~2-year window from a dev table. Dev schemas are also ephemeral, so once the source table is dropped, `EXECUTE delete_datashare` can no longer remove the registration. ## Changes - `datashare_trigger_sync_operation` raises a compiler error outside `prod`, naming the schema it would have registered. - `dry_run: true` remains allowed on any target, since it only prints SQL. - `allow_non_prod: true` added as an explicit override for deliberate use. - All three `run-operation` examples in `docs/dune-datashares.md` now pass `--target prod`, with a note explaining why. - CHANGELOG entry. Raises rather than skips silently: unlike the post-hook, the caller here explicitly asked for a sync, so doing nothing quietly would be its own confusion. ## Test plan Verified against this branch: - [x] `run-operation` on `dev` without `dry_run` → fails with `Refusing datashare sync for 'dbt_template_datashare_incremental_model' on target 'dev': the source schema would be 'dune__tmp_'. ...` - [x] `run-operation` on `dev` with `dry_run: true` → succeeds, prints SQL, executes nothing - [x] `run-operation --target prod` with `dry_run: true` → unchanged behavior - [ ] Reviewer: confirm `allow_non_prod: true` is wanted at all — happy to drop it and make the guard absolute ## Follow-ups (not in this PR) - No server-side validation that a datashare source schema isn't a `__tmp_` schema. A backend guard would protect teams pinned to older macro versions. - `EXECUTE delete_datashare` requires the source table to exist, leaving unremovable registrations after a dev schema is dropped. - The public docs page (`api-reference/connectors/dbt/datashares`) describes the guard as *"the template runs this hook only on the `prod` target"* rather than showing it inline. Teams with existing dbt projects copy the YAML and never see the macro. Separate PR to follow in `dune-docs`. Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com) --------- Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

author: 0xRobin
message: perf(gas_solana_tx_fees): merge compute_limit + compute_unit_price into single compute_budget table (#9880) * perf(gas_solana): merge compute_limit + compute_unit_price into gas_solana_compute_budget Introduce gas_solana_compute_budget: one incremental delta table keyed (block_date, block_slot, tx_id) with both compute_limit (opcode 0x02) and compute_unit_price (opcode 0x03) columns, populated from a single filtered scan of solana.instruction_calls. Rewrite gas_solana_compute_limit and gas_solana_compute_unit_price as views over the merged table so external consumers of dune.gas_solana.compute_limit and dune.gas_solana.compute_unit_price keep the same column contract. Update solana_tx_fees_macro (used by gas_solana_tx_fees_current and the 17 quarterly backfills) to LEFT JOIN once against gas_solana_compute_budget instead of joining compute_limit and compute_unit_price separately. Baseline (2026-06-13): 86.66M limit + 74.65M price rows across two ~200M-key hash joins. Merged: 89.35M rows in one table, one hash join. Live-engine EXCEPT ALL both ways = 0 (n=89,353,063 on both sides). Ref CUR2-2801. * ci(gas_solana): bound source scans in CI target to 3-day window Adds `{% if target.name == 'ci' %} AND <partition> >= current_date - interval '3' day` to source scans in the two files modified by this PR so the solana CI job (state:modified.macros fan-out to all 18 tx_fees models) prunes instead of full-scanning and completes within the 90-minute CI cap. - gas_solana_compute_budget.sql: bound instruction_calls block_date in CI. - solana_tx_fees_macro.sql: bound transactions t.block_date, compute_budget cb.block_date, block_leaders b.date, prices.usd_forward_fill p.minute in CI. Prod SQL unrendered: target.name != 'ci' so the guards render to nothing. Partition columns confirmed pruning on delta_prod: instruction_calls/block_date (~53s for 3-day slice), transactions/block_date (~5s), prices.usd_forward_fill/minute (~2s). Verified with `dbt parse --profile spellbook-trino --project-dir dbt_subprojects/solana/` (exit 0). Ref CUR2-2801. * fix(gas_solana): include partition key in compute budget merge --------- Co-authored-by: jeff-dude <jeff@dune.xyz>

author: 0xRobin
message: ci: cache dbt partial_parse.msgpack across commit-manifest runs (#9887) * ci: use dbt parse for commit manifest Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com> * Remove unnecessary cluster check before dbt parse Applied via @cursor push command * ci: cache dbt partial_parse.msgpack across commit-manifest runs Restore the previous run's partial-parse state before 'dbt parse' and save the refreshed state after, via actions/cache (rolling per-commit key with a per-project restore-key). dbt then re-parses only files changed since the last main commit instead of the whole subproject. Cache misses and stale state are safe: dbt fingerprints its inputs and falls back to a full parse whenever the dbt version, dbt_project.yml, packages, vars, profile/target, or referenced env_vars change, so a bad cache can only cost a full parse, never produce a wrong manifest. Uses actions/cache (off-box, GitHub-hosted) rather than runner-local disk so it survives spot-instance reclamation on the self-hosted fleet. --------- Co-authored-by: jeff-dude <jeff@dune.xyz> Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com> Co-authored-by: jeff-dude <102681548+jeff-dude@users.noreply.github.com>

author: jeff-dude
message: feat(tokens,gas): price transfers and native gas fees from prices.usd_with_native (#9874) * feat(tokens,gas): price transfers and native gas fees from prices.usd_with_native Swap tokens_transfers (transfers_enrich macro) and gas.fees native price lookups (native_token_prices macro) from prices_external.hour / prices.day onto prices.usd_with_native, matching the pattern dex.trades already uses. prices_external.hour requires manual upstream backfill coordination per chain (gated by dune.blockchains.start_date + the coinpaprika pipeline's evm_erc20_blockchains allowlist), which is the friction this avoids — prices.usd_with_native is a Dune-managed source with materially deeper historical coverage out of the box, so newly onboarded chains (e.g. cronos) get priced transfers without a separate pricing backfill request. native_token_prices keeps its existing (blockchain, time_unit) contract by aggregating usd_with_native's minute-level rows up to time_unit internally, so none of its ~30 gas_<chain>_fees callers need changes. Note this is a value change, not just a coverage improvement: prices.day and usd_with_native agree exactly on native token price (same underlying series), but transfers_enrich now joins at minute grain instead of hour, so amount_usd shifts by ~0.1-1% on every already-covered row once an incremental run touches it. Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com> * feat(tokens,gas): bound CI initial-build scans to last 7 days transfers_enrich and native_token_prices now full-build against real history for every impacted model (all ~60 tokens_<chain>_transfers + ~30 gas_<chain>_fees callers) once prices.usd_with_native lands, instead of dbt's usual state:modified.macros CI selection quietly skipping them. Without a bound, CI's temp-schema initial build has no existing target table (is_incremental() is false), so it would scan each chain's full transfers/gas history against the full price table - too slow/expensive to be useful for regression-testing this swap. Gated on target.name == 'ci' only; prod and manual runs are unaffected and still use transfers_start_date / full native price history. Separate commit from the pricing-source swap so it's easy to revert on its own if we decide CI should validate this differently. Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com> * feat(gas): bound gas_*_fees base_model source scans to last 7 days in CI The prior CI-bound commit only filtered native_token_prices; the transactions/blocks (and, for ethereum, blobs_submissions) source reads inside each gas_<chain>_fees base_model were still unbounded on CI's initial build (is_incremental() false against a fresh temp schema), so CI would scan each chain's full raw transactions/blocks history - the much larger table on the join. Applied to the three shared macros that cover most chains (op_stack_gas_fees, evm_l1_gas_fees, arbitrum_orbit_stack_gas_fees) plus the handful of per-chain gas_<chain>_fees.sql files that inline their own base_model instead of using a shared macro, and the standalone aptos model. tron and xrpl gas fee models don't call native_token_prices / transfers_enrich, so they're untouched - not in this PR's CI blast radius. Same target.name == 'ci' gate as the previous commit; prod and manual runs are unaffected. Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com> * Fix native_token_prices incremental predicate to enable partition pruning Apply incremental_predicate to bare p.minute instead of the date_trunc wrapped expression so minute-level partition pruning is not defeated on incremental runs. The window is equivalent because the predicate's RHS is already truncated to the time unit. Applied via @cursor push command * fix: include gas seed txs in CI-bounded builds Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com> * fix: keep ethereum blob CI filter source-local Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com> * fix: include ethereum blob seed rows in CI Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com> * fix: tighten gas CI sample window Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com> --------- Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com> Co-authored-by: tomfutago <35136350+tomfutago@users.noreply.github.com> Co-authored-by: tomfutago <tomfutago@gmail.com>

author: a-monteiro
message: perf(curvefi_ethereum_pools_balances): bounded-lookback hybrid seed (~3.0 CPU-hrs/day, 2.84 TB/day) (#9794) * perf(curvefi_ethereum_pools_balances): bounded-lookback hybrid seed for daily balances The shared balances_incremental_subset_daily_legacy macro seeds the forward-fill by re-deriving each key's last-known balance from ALL pre-window history of tokens_<chain>.balances_daily_agg_base via max_by(balance, day). On curvefi_ethereum_pools_balances that full-history scan is a constant ~118 GB / ~94% of CPU on every hourly MERGE build (24/day) to emit ~1 row. Add an opt-in self_seed_relation param: when set, the prior-state seed re-reads only a bounded recent source window (self_seed_lookback_days, default 21d) and carries deep settled history forward from the model's own latest pre-lookback partition, instead of re-scanning all source history. The recent re-read still self-corrects late-arriving / restated source balances within the lookback (balances_daily_agg_base re-merges only its last 3 days, and the snapshot drift empirically settles within ~14d). Default (param unset) is byte-identical to the old behavior, so the 14 other callers are unchanged. curvefi_ethereum_pools_balances opts in via self_seed_relation=this. Proven on prod data (spellbook-dex, window=now-3d, UTC): old all-history seed vs hybrid produce identical output (EXCEPT 0/0 both ways, 26917 rows, byte-identical checksums over all 9 columns). A/B (3 warm runs, medians): IO 118.45 -> 1.17 GB (-99.0% / 101x) CPU 504.8 -> 5.6 s (-98.9% / 90x) peak 3.62 -> 0.039 GB (-99%) spill 0 -> 0 No --full-refresh needed (existing table already holds full forward-filled history). * ci(dex): bound balances_incremental_subset_daily_legacy full-refresh in CI The shared macro change marks all callers state:modified, so spellbook CI full-refresh-builds them; the unbounded all-history forward-fill would blow the 90-min timeout (safe_polygon scans ~234 GB) and skip the regression test. Add a target.name=='ci' 30-day floor on the source scan so each build completes and its unique_combination_of_columns test runs. Renders only under --target ci (verified byte-identical dev render); prod is unaffected, nothing to revert. * ci(dex): exclude swell from the CI floor (check_seed over fixed 2024 dates) The CI 30-day floor dropped swell_balances_ethereum_core_assets's seeded historical days (the check_seed CSV pins 2024 dates), failing check_seed with 21 unmatched rows while every model build and uniqueness test passed. Add an apply_ci_floor param (default true keeps the timeout protection on the heavy safe_* full-refreshes) and set it false for swell, which is tiny and needs full history for its seed test. Verified under --target ci: swell renders no floor, safe_polygon still does; prod unaffected. * fix(balances seed): anchor deep self-seed strictly before the incremental window Review (tomfutago): the deep self-seed partition was chosen by `day < now() - self_seed_lookback_days` independently of incremental_predicate('day'). Safe for the default config (3d incremental < 21d lookback), but a wider incremental repair/backfill (window > lookback) could let the deep-seed row overlap the in-window source branch and compete for the same key/day. Add `and not incremental_predicate('day')` to the deep-partition subquery so the carried partition is always strictly before the in-window arm, regardless of the lookback-vs-incremental-window relationship — no key/day can be produced by both arms. Provable no-op for the current config (given `day < now()-21d`, the extra `day < now()-3d` is redundant; verified on prod data: old anchor == new anchor == 2026-05-29), so the EXCEPT=0 equivalence and A/B numbers are unchanged. Also document the metadata-freeze trade-off raised in review: deep-carried rows reuse the balance/token_symbol stored when last written; a token metadata/decimals correction for a position untouched for >lookback days is reflected only after it next changes or a --full-refresh (the recent-source arm re-enriches active positions from current metadata; same trade-off as the sibling P7 stablecoins).

author: jeff-dude
message: perf(polymarket): convert positions to view over positions_raw + market_details (#9735) * perf(polymarket): convert positions to view over positions_raw + market_details Daily incremental MERGE of polymarket_polygon.positions was rebuilding the entire 9.98B-row target table (~14 CPU-hrs/day, 5.2 TB spill, 115 min wall on a representative day). Root cause is that historical_changed_positions emits rows for any historical day, so Trino can't partition-prune the merge target — every run scans + rewrites the whole table. Stop denormalizing volatile market metadata (market_outcome, resolved_on_timestamp, active, closed, accepting_orders, plus the market_details descriptive columns) into every historical position row. Convert polymarket_polygon.positions to a view that joins positions_raw (balance per day/address/token_id; already incrementally maintained by #9696's positions_balances_repro lineage) to market_details (current market state) at read time. Trade-off: read-time join cost replaces write-time merge cost. Measured via EXPLAIN ANALYZE on prod-medium engine: - single day (typical dashboard): 13 s - 30-day aggregation: 10 s - 7-day full row dump: ~2 min - address point lookup (30 days): 9 s Join distribution is PARTITIONED (market_details > broadcast threshold). 36 GB shuffle on 7-day full-row reads; partial-aggregation queries collapse before the shuffle and stay fast. Downstream consumers see the same column set; no schema change. The view naturally fixes prod's drift in null_resolved (currently ~332 M stale rows) because outcome/resolved_on come from market_details at read time. Active/closed/accepting_orders also flow live from market_details (no more snapshot-at-write semantics — values reflect current market state on every query). Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com> * test(polymarket): bound positions view tests to 14d window The view's unique_combination + not_null tests would scan the full ~10B-row join unbounded. Match the convention used by positions_raw (same model file): config.where = "day >= current_date - interval '14' day". This bounds the test scan to the latest partition's worth of data, keeping CI's test step under a couple minutes instead of however long a full view scan takes. The tests still catch all the invariants: - unique_combination(day, address, token_id): catches market_details uniqueness violations (the join only multiplies a row if a token has multiple market_details rows, which would break the test) - not_null on day/address/token_id: catches null-introducing joins Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com> * Add split sync watermark columns to positions view. Expose _position_updated_at and _market_updated_at for future downstream use while keeping _updated_at as a composite greatest() so existing datashare incremental sync continues to pick up metadata-only changes. Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com> * test(polymarket): trim positions view tests to 30d unique key only. Drop redundant not_null tests already covered on positions_raw; keep a single bounded unique_combination integration test on the view join. Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com> --------- Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com> Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

message: perf(safe): scan traces once in safe_native_transfers macro (#9755) * perf(safe): scan traces once in safe_native_transfers macro Fan each trace to its (from, to) sides with cross join unnest before the safes join, replacing the two-branch UNION ALL that scanned <chain>.traces twice with identical predicates. Proven equivalent (EXCEPT = 0 both ways, identical checksums over all output columns) on the full 10-day bnb window. Measured on safe_bnb_bnb_transfers (medians of 3 warm runs): CPU 1449s -> 745s (-48.6%), IO 76.0 -> 36.2 GB (-52.4%), wall 13.6 -> 6.5s, peak memory 6.0 -> 7.3 GB, spill 0 -> 0. * test(safe): update stale polygon matic transfers checksum The hardcoded window sum (-2497864) no longer matches production: hive.safe_polygon.matic_transfers itself sums to -2497858 over 2022-11-01..2022-11-03 (polygon traces drift since the test was written; last full CI build of these models was #6549/#8631). Not caused by the macro rewrite: the CI-built table from this branch is byte-identical to prod over the window (EXCEPT = 0 both ways, same 6,932 rows).

author: bh2smith
message: Make API tests self-sufficient (no hardcoded execution IDs) (#41) ## Problem CI was failing with five test failures that looked like one issue but were actually three: 1. **Expired results** — `get_results`, `get_results_csv`, and `get_latest_results` used a hardcoded `JOB_ID` / stale latest execution that aged past Dune's result-retention window (`failed precondition: query execution result already expired`). Replacing the ID only resets the clock. 2. **Cross-test interference** — the `execute_query` test executes and immediately cancels query 971694, the same query the latest-results tests read. When tests interleave, the "latest" execution is the cancelled one (`Query state is QUERY_STATE_CANCELLED, cannot provide CSV result`). 3. **Cancellation race** — `execute_sql` runs `SELECT 1`, which completes before the cancel request arrives (`The requested execution ID ... was not found`). ## Changes - `get_status` / `get_results` / `get_results_csv` share one fresh raw-SQL execution created at test time (via `tokio::sync::OnceCell`), so results can never be expired. - `get_latest_results(_csv)` first ensure query 971694 has a fresh completed execution. - `execute_query`'s cancellation test now uses the long-running query 1229120 — no longer poisons 971694's latest results, and the cancel reliably lands mid-execution. - `execute_sql` drops its racy cancellation assert; cancellation coverage lives in `execute_query`. - **Client bugfix:** `GetResultResponse.query_id` is now `Option<u32>`. Raw-SQL executions return no `query_id`, so `get_results` on an `execute_sql` execution previously always failed with a decode error.

author: thevaizman
message: fix(dex): stop double counting venue-settled 1inch-LOP fills (CUR2-2693) (#9747) * fix(dex): stop double counting venue-settled 1inch-LOP fills (CUR2-2693) 1inch-LOP is an intent layer: resolvers fill orders via private liquidity (plain ERC20 transfers) or by routing through an underlying DEX in the same tx. In the latter case dex.trades carried both the '1inch-LOP' row and the venue's own row for the same fill: ~189k trades / ~$222M per 30d. Classifier (new incremental oneinch.lop_venue_settled_fills): a limits fill is venue-settled iff its tx co-occurs with another project's row in dex_<chain>_base_trades, with keep-guards for (a) fills nested under a classic/fusion/cross-chain execution (route legs / settlement liquidity = real maker liquidity) and (b) direct fills (their second-side row already feeds dex_aggregator.trades as '1inch'). - oneinch_lop_own_trades excludes the venue-settled set; evt_index stays numbered over all fills pre-filter so kept rows keep their merge keys; a 6h maturity delay prevents the raw-traces-vs-decoded-events race from permanently leaking rows into the merge-only dex_<chain>_trades tables - new oneinch_lop_aggregator_trades emits the venue-settled fills into dex_aggregator.trades as '1inch-LOP' (user perspective, like ar_trades) - replaces the 10 orphaned oneinch_<chain>_base_trades_seed files (wired to no test) with one live-verified oneinch_lop_own_trades_seed + tests, adds a dex_aggregator seed row and a singular negative test for verified venue-settled txs Live validation (14d, ethereum+arbitrum): removal set 15.7k fills / ~$63.4M; zero false removals across six gates (example txs, evt_index parity, direct-fill overlap = 0, post-fix residual co-occurrence = nested route legs only); conservation own(new) + agg(new) == own(old) exact. Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> * refactor(oneinch): derive LOP chain list from cfg, share evt_index numbering, drop agg-view window Post-review cleanups (no semantic change to the venue-settled split): - venue_settled chain list + LOP start date now derive from oneinch_blockchains_cfg_macro()/oneinch_lo_cfg_macro() like the rest of the lineage - a future 1inch chain can no longer silently miss venue co-occurrence coverage (a missing dex_<chain>_base_trades ref fails at compile instead) - the load-bearing evt_index numbering moves into oneinch_lop_evt_index() and is persisted on oneinch_lop_venue_settled_fills, so both sides of the dex.trades / dex_aggregator.trades split share one definition instead of comment-synced copies - oneinch_lop_aggregator_trades becomes window-free (joins the persisted evt_index), letting dex_aggregator_trades' incremental block_time predicate push down into the oneinch_swaps scan instead of re-numbering full LOP history every run - venue co-occurrence joins the 13 base_trades scans to the small LOP tx key set (dynamic filtering on tx_hash) instead of an EXISTS that puts the 100GB+ union on the semi-join build side during full refreshes - maturity delay hoisted to a named jinja set; window guards deduplicated Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix(ci): wire LOP aggregator trades via dex_aggregator_base_trades, not the as_is tier CI rebuilds any directly-modified model from scratch; touching dex_aggregator_trades.sql meant a full 739M-row rebuild (75 min) that blew the 90-min job budget (run 27273012062: venue_settled built in 9 min, tests got cancelled at the deadline). Route oneinch_lop_aggregator_trades through dex_aggregator_base_trades instead - the same tier the uniswap v4 aggregator-hook fix uses - so dex_aggregator_trades stays untouched and never rebuilds in CI. The view now emits the base trades contract (raw amounts only); symbols/amounts/usd are enriched downstream by enrich_dex_aggregator_trades like every other base model. Post-merge backfill order becomes: dex_aggregator_base_trades full refresh, then dex_aggregator_trades. Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix(oneinch): apply the cross-chain placeholder exclusion pre-numbering in venue_settled fills too Rebase over c3ab658b4 (CUR2-2665) put the ERC20True placeholder exclusion before the evt_index window in oneinch_lop_own_trades; the persisted numbering in oneinch_lop_venue_settled_fills must use the identical pre-numbering predicate set or evt_index diverges in txs that mix a placeholder fill with real fills. Placeholder fills are now excluded from both destination tables (they're degenerate cross-chain legs, not same-chain trades). Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix(oneinch): align venue_settled_fills schema unique test with model unique_key The dbt_utils unique_combination_of_columns test now matches the incremental merge key (blockchain, block_month, block_date, execution_id). author: 0xRobin
message: Replace polymarket positions input with ERC1155 reconstruction (#9696) * Replace polymarket positions balance input with ERC1155 repro table Co-authored-by: 0xRob <0xRobin@users.noreply.github.com> * Add polymarket balance source parity test Co-authored-by: 0xRob <0xRobin@users.noreply.github.com> * Fix quoted values column in polymarket transfer batch unnest Co-authored-by: 0xRob <0xRobin@users.noreply.github.com> * Optimize polymarket balance forward-fill expansion Co-authored-by: 0xRob <0xRobin@users.noreply.github.com> * Handle sequence bounds in polymarket balance expansion Co-authored-by: 0xRob <0xRobin@users.noreply.github.com> * Reduce polymarket CI test scope to avoid timeout Co-authored-by: 0xRob <0xRobin@users.noreply.github.com> * Add incremental source filter to polymarket positions_raw Co-authored-by: 0xRob <0xRobin@users.noreply.github.com> * Run polymarket equivalence test on rolling CI window Co-authored-by: 0xRob <0xRobin@users.noreply.github.com> * Use rolling window with original macro for CI equivalence Co-authored-by: 0xRob <0xRobin@users.noreply.github.com> * Compare CI positions output to production over 7-day window Co-authored-by: 0xRob <0xRobin@users.noreply.github.com> * Qualify production positions table in equivalence test Co-authored-by: 0xRob <0xRobin@users.noreply.github.com> * Reference CI schema directly in equivalence test Co-authored-by: 0xRob <0xRobin@users.noreply.github.com> * Scope equivalence test to changed pairs in rolling window Co-authored-by: 0xRob <0xRobin@users.noreply.github.com> * Use aggregate parity thresholds for CI equivalence Co-authored-by: 0xRob <0xRobin@users.noreply.github.com> * Relax CI equivalence thresholds for rolling window parity Co-authored-by: 0xRob <0xRobin@users.noreply.github.com> * Disable polymarket equivalence dbt singular test Co-authored-by: 0xRob <0xRobin@users.noreply.github.com> * Simplify polymarket balance repro and drop disabled equivalence test - Use int256 throughout the running balance computation instead of double-precision floats. Native uint/int256 arithmetic avoids the precision loss the legacy macro hides via clamping. - Filter daily_deltas with HAVING sum(delta) <> 0 so days with only no-op (value=0) transfers do not produce phantom 'balance=0' anchor rows. This is the source of the ~540k spurious rows/day seen in the initial CI vs prod diff. - Drop unused block_number/block_time aggregation; the model never emits them. - Collapse the redundant daily_flows + daily_deltas pair into a single group-by; same shape, less work. - Remove the disabled singular equivalence test. It compared the repro to the legacy snapshot-based macro, which is itself the source of truth we are intentionally moving off (it carries stale balances when the snapshot table misses burn events). Equivalence is validated out-of-band against the CI table; the schema-level uniqueness and not_null tests remain the in-CI guardrails. * Keep intraday round-trip closure markers in repro The previous 'HAVING sum(delta) <> 0' filter dropped legitimate intraday mint-then-burn closures alongside the no-op (value=0) phantom rows. Switch to 'HAVING max(abs(delta)) > 0' so days with non-zero transfers that net to zero still anchor a closure marker row, matching the legacy table's behavior on those days. Days where every transfer carries value=0 are still filtered out. * fix: address PR review feedback (#9696) dennisp42's review caught three real issues in the incremental path: 1. `prior_balances` aggregated by `max(day)` from `{{ this }}`, but `{{ this }}` carries forward-filled rows where `day` is the fill day, not the original change day. The follow-up forward-fill then set `last_updated = anchor_day`, so every incremental run rewrote `last_updated` for inactive pairs to ~yesterday. Confirmed against prod: ~99 % of pre-window inactive pairs are forward-fills, with drift up to ~5.3 years. Aggregate by `last_updated` instead, which is preserved across forward-fill. 2. Cold pairs (anchor far in the past) made the forward-fill sequence expand the full history just for `incremental_predicate` to clip it. Clip `fill_start` to the window start in incremental runs. 3. Closed positions expanded `[closure_day, current_date - 1]` only for the final WHERE to drop everything but the closure day. Cap `fill_end` at the closure day when `balance_raw = uint256 '0'`. The combination needs the guard `fill_end >= fill_start` (otherwise a closed position before the window would feed an invalid sequence range into the unnest). --------- Co-authored-by: Cursor Agent <cursoragent@cursor.com> Co-authored-by: 0xRob <0xRobin@users.noreply.github.com>

author: los-xyz
message: fix(kalshi): merge live volume_fp from market_updates_raw into market_details (#9689) `kalshi.markets_raw.volume_fp` can freeze at creation-time for actively traded markets because the market-feed `markets-sync` cron queries Kalshi with `min_created_ts` and never re-fetches existing markets. The `kalshi_market_details` spell then filters on `volume_fp >= 100` against that stale value, dropping markets that look idle on the raw side but trade heavily in reality (e.g. KXIPLGAME-26MAY15CSKLSG-CSK: 21k trades, 20.5M contracts on 5/15 but markets_raw.volume_fp = 0 since 5/8). This silently dropped 50-91% of recent Kalshi trades from the downstream `kalshi.market_trades` spell — which INNER JOINs market_details on ticker — starting 2026-05-08, the day market-feed PR #110 routed the ticker WebSocket stream into the new `kalshi.market_updates_raw` table instead of refreshing markets_raw. Fix: source live volume_fp from `market_updates_raw` (per-tick state stream), apply the >= 100 filter against the coalesced value, and project the live value downstream. Existing fallback semantics preserved for tickers with no updates in the incremental window. Validated against prod: rescues 469,719 tickers and ~6.75B contracts of trade volume currently being filtered out. Also adds `market_updates_raw` to `sources/kalshi/_sources.yml` and documents the markets_raw freshness caveat on its description. A `--full-refresh` of `kalshi.market_details` (and a downstream rebuild of `kalshi.market_trades`) is needed after merge to recover the ~2 weeks of dropped trades; the incremental cadence alone won't pick up tickers whose `updated_time` is older than the incremental window. Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> Co-authored-by: jeff-dude <102681548+jeff-dude@users.noreply.github.com>

message: fix(airswap): map V2 maker/taker columns in ethereum base_trades (#9687) * fix(airswap): map V2 maker/taker columns in ethereum base_trades The shared airswap_compatible_trades macro hardcoded sender/signer column names, but airswap_ethereum.swap_evt_swap (V2) uses maker/taker naming, causing the model to fail with "column senderwallet cannot be resolved". Add a per-source `cols` override to the macro and wire the V2 mapping (takerWallet/Token/Param -> sold, makerWallet/Token/Param -> bought) into the ethereum model. Arbitrum/avalanche V2 tables already use sender/signer naming so they need no change. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix(airswap): refresh ethereum base_trades seed with current V2 rows The seed was added in 2023 with two V2 'swap' rows from contract 0x4572f2554421bd64bef1c22c8a81840e8d496bea (2022). Those rows no longer exist in the decoded source (airswap_ethereum.swap_evt_swap now only holds 2019-era data from contract 0x54d2690e...), causing the seed-vs- build check to fail with 12 column-level mismatches. This was masked previously because the model couldn't compile at all; now that the V2 column mapping works, the check is reachable and the stale seed is exposed. author: los-xyz
message: fix(polymarket): drop forward-fill post-expiration for any resolved market (#9654) Today's bottom filter only drops forward-filled bars past expiration when market_outcome IN ('yes','no'). For 50/50 resolved markets (~1,083 markets, ~87k hours over 90d) the filter doesn't fire, so stale forward-filled prices accumulate indefinitely after resolution. Investigated extending the settlement-pin to multi-outcome markets but market_details.outcome is the binary 'yes'/'no'/'50/50'/'unresolved' representation, not the winning token name. Pinning multi-outcome markets needs a per-token resolution source we don't have here. C2 fix: drop forward-fill post-expiration for any resolved market (market_outcome is not null and != '' and != 'unresolved'). Keeps real-trade post-expiration rows untouched (filter has is_forward_filled clause). Verified against the deployed table: - 87,383 50/50 forward-fill rows dropped - 0 real-trade rows affected - Binary 'yes'/'no' behavior unchanged Forward-only by nature of the bottom filter. Existing 87k stale rows in the target stay until a one-time --full-refresh, recommend running it after merge. Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: los-xyz
message: fix(kalshi): propagate lifecycle settlement to ohlcv_hourly historical rows (#9653) * fix(kalshi): propagate lifecycle settlement to ohlcv_hourly historical rows kalshi_market_details now emits a fresh source_updated_at when a lifecycle event lands (PR #9647), and kalshi_market_trades reprocesses historical rows via that signal. kalshi_ohlcv_hourly was the missing link: its incremental selector keyed only on t.created_time and r.hour, so old hours for a today-settled market kept stale market_outcome / event_market_name / category until full refresh. Three changes, paired so the merge unique key holds: 1. base CTE: OR-branch pulls historical trades for tickers whose market_details.source_updated_at moved. 2. prior_sparse: exclude those refreshed tickers, otherwise their hours come through both new_sparse (re-aggregated) and prior_sparse (existing target rows), violating the (block_month, hour, market_id, outcome) unique constraint. 3. final emit filter: widen the r.hour predicate with an OR on refreshed market_ids so the merge actually writes to old hours. Validated end-to-end on the production target with a 3-day window: 0 duplicate (hour, market_id, outcome) keys across the simulated sparse_ohlcv source. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix(kalshi): drop incremental_predicates on ohlcv_hourly merge target Cursor flagged on PR review: the previous config pruned the MERGE destination to in-window hours via DBT_INTERNAL_DEST.hour. Combined with this PR's source widening (which now emits historical hours for refreshed tickers), MERGE's ON clause hides the existing target rows for those old hours, sending them through INSERT instead of UPDATE and breaking unique(block_month, hour, market_id, outcome). Same trade-off kalshi_market_details made: drop the destination speedup, keep correctness on late-arriving lifecycle settlements. Verified against the deployed kalshi.ohlcv_hourly: 446k refreshed tickers in a 3-day window, 1.17M source keys match existing target rows (UPDATE), 110k unmatched are net-new hours (INSERT, no dup by definition). Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> --------- Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: los-xyz
message: feat(kalshi): integrate series_raw for canonical category + fees (#9644) * feat(kalshi): integrate series_raw for canonical category + fees Adds kalshi.series_raw as a source and joins it into kalshi_market_details and kalshi_market_trades. Three concrete user-facing wins: 1. Better category. Today kalshi_market_details.category comes from event-level market_details_raw.category; series-level series_raw.category is canonical (one row per series_ticker, ~10k series total). Final value is now coalesce(series.category, event.category). Validated against ~54M event-x-series rows: 37% of rows have a series-level category that differs from the event-level one (e.g. BRAZILXBAN surfaces as Politics rather than Companies). This shifts the distribution of the category column; downstream consumers should expect a more accurate but different bucket spread. 2. fee_usd per trade. series_raw exposes fee_type ('quadratic' or 'quadratic_with_maker_fees') and fee_multiplier. kalshi_market_trades now computes the taker fee per Kalshi's published formula: ceil(0.07 * fee_multiplier * P * (1-P) * N * 100) / 100 where P=yes_price_dollars and N=count_fp. NULL when series has no fee metadata. Maker-side fees (1.75% coefficient when fee_type includes maker) are not surfaced here; consumers can compute them from fee_type + fee_multiplier if needed. Closes the v1 NULL-fee gap on prediction_markets.trades downstream. 3. Recurring-template metadata. frequency (custom / one_off / annual / monthly / weekly / daily / hourly / fifteen_min) now surfaced on both market_details and trades. Powers cohort analytics like 'all recurring weather markets' or 'one-off political events' without pattern-matching the ticker. Note: series_raw view does not yet exist on the catalog side; only the partition base table kalshi.series_0001 is currently available. The ingest team needs to create the view (one-line CREATE VIEW) for this spell to run. Filed as a dependency for landing this PR. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix: source series_0001 directly + propagate series changes incrementally Two issues from CI + bugbot review: 1. CI failure: kalshi.series_raw view doesn't exist on the catalog yet, only the partition base table kalshi.series_0001. Switched the source declaration and CTE to series_0001 with a TODO note to swap to series_raw once the view is created (matching markets_raw / market_details_raw pattern). 2. Bugbot (medium): incremental predicate didn't detect series_raw changes. If a series's category / fee_type / fee_multiplier / frequency was updated, existing market rows for that series wouldn't be re-processed on incremental runs, leaving stale dim values downstream (including incorrect fee_usd in market_trades). Added a third branch to the markets CTE incremental predicate that includes markets whose parent series row was refreshed in the window: or m.event_ticker in ( select ed.event_ticker from market_details_raw ed where ed.series_ticker in ( select sr.ticker from series_0001 sr where {{ incremental_predicate('sr.last_updated_ts') }} ) ) Also added series_last_updated_ts to the series CTE and folded it into source_updated_at via greatest(), so kalshi_market_trades's own incremental detection (which uses source_updated_at) picks up series-driven dim changes too. Fee changes now propagate end-to-end. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * revert: keep targeting kalshi.series_raw, not series_0001 Reverts the partition-base-table workaround. Source declaration and spell CTE both target kalshi.series_raw again. PR will stay blocked on CI until the catalog view is created (mirroring markets_raw / market_details_raw / market_trades_raw pattern). The bugbot incremental-detection fix (series_last_updated_ts in source_updated_at + series-driven branch in the markets CTE predicate) is preserved. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * chore(kalshi): tighten model comments and column descriptions Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix(kalshi): drive settlement updates from markets_lifecycle_raw (#9647) * fix(kalshi): drive settlement updates from markets_lifecycle_raw markets_raw.updated_time is Kalshi's last_modified field, not ingest time; late-arriving settlement events miss the 3-day incremental window and never land. markets_lifecycle_raw.received_ts is real ingest time, so route result, settlement_ts, and settlement_value through the lifecycle stream (coalescing back to markets_raw when no lifecycle row exists yet) and add a lifecycle predicate to the incremental selector so newly-settled tickers get refreshed. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * chore(kalshi): defensive lifecycle filter + accepted_values tripwire Decouple the lifecycle aggregator from the Kalshi event_type enum: the lifecycle CTE now keys per-ticker rollups on field population, so any new event_type Kalshi introduces that carries result / settled_ts / determination_ts / settlement_value is picked up automatically. Add an accepted_values test on markets_lifecycle_raw.event_type, seeded with the documented enum plus metadata_updated (already in production with no payload). The next previously-unseen event_type fails the test on the following dbt run so we investigate before the spell silently changes behavior. Verified against current data: 27,927 tickers in both the old and the new lifecycle aggregator with zero row-level differences across result, settlement_value, determination_ts, settled_ts, and last_event_received_ts. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> --------- Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> * Add deduplication to series CTE to prevent fan-out on duplicate tickers Applied via @cursor push command --------- Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> Co-authored-by: tomfutago <35136350+tomfutago@users.noreply.github.com> Co-authored-by: Cursor Agent <cursoragent@cursor.com>

author: alicecha
message: CUR2-2155: orca whirlpool surface adaptive-fee pools (#9631) * CUR2-2155: orca whirlpool surface adaptive-fee pools Pools created via `initializePoolWithAdaptiveFee` (Orca's adaptive-fee Whirlpool variant, GA Sept 2025) were silently dropped by the v2 staging join because the `whirlpools` CTE only registered pools from `initializePool` and `initializePoolV2`. As a result every adaptive-fee pool's swaps were missing from `orca_whirlpool_v2.base_trades` and downstream `dex_solana.trades` (~7,900 pools to date — most prominent example: CASH/USDC `3wijQvPKm6jHQrAkfPpok5o8WjCWPm1DGG17NmeW8q1w`, 187k+ swaps). This change adds `whirlpool_call_initializePoolWithAdaptiveFee` and `whirlpool_call_initializeAdaptiveFeeTier` as sources and extends `fee_updates` / `whirlpools` to register these pools, with `fee_rate` approximated by the tier's `defaultBaseFeeRate` (the realized adaptive fee varies per swap with volatility). * note adaptive-fee decoder coverage caveat in comment * address bugbot: union setDefaultBaseFeeRate into adaptive_fee_tiers Mirrors how the static fee_tiers_defaults CTE unions both initializeFeeTier and setDefaultFeeRate. Pools initialized after a tier's default base rate is updated via setDefaultBaseFeeRate now resolve the current rate instead of the stale init value.

author: jeff-dude
message: polymarket capital actions: refactor for query plan optimization (#9619) * refactor for query plan optimization * try session property for join type * split inbound and outbound * attempt to avoid double join * universal exists logic * try inbound per token * revert to single model, use microbatch * temp: full refresh flag and var override * temp: different month override * materialize polymarket users_proxies to skip CTE re-aggregation Trino was re-running the union+distinct of the two upstream proxy tables once per `exists` reference site inside users_capital_actions (CTEs are inlined by default), producing 6 redundant HashAggregations on ~7M rows per microbatch. Pull the dedup into its own incremental table so each microbatch just scans+broadcasts the proxy set once. Made-with: Cursor * split OR-exists pre-filter into two equality exists Trino can't decorrelate `exists (... where t.to_address = w.proxy OR t.from_address = w.proxy)` into a single hash semi-join because the OR mixes two different outer columns against one inner column. It fell back to a NestedLoopJoin, producing a 78k x 798 cross product (~63M rows) per monthly batch — accounted for ~94% of the wall-clock for one batch. Splitting into two equality-only exists ORed at the filter level lets Trino plan each as its own hash semi-join over the broadcast proxy set. Made-with: Cursor * revert capital_actions to merge incremental Materialized users_proxies + the OR-exists split make a single-shot full-history merge feasible without the planner blowup that originally forced microbatch. Reverted: incremental_strategy back to merge with incremental_predicates, the CI workflow --vars override, and the source-level event_time on tokens_polygon.transfers. Kept: the polymarket_polygon_users_proxies materialized intermediate and the two-equality-exists pre-filter (the actual perf wins). Made-with: Cursor * make market_addresses incremental; drop unsafe dest predicate on both market_addresses: table -> incremental merge on unique_key=[address]; values seed only on full-refresh, fpmm-factory addresses appended via incremental_predicate. users_proxies + market_addresses: drop incremental_predicates on DBT_INTERNAL_DEST. Single-column unique keys aren't bounded by the dest-side time predicate, so an upstream re-emit could miss the MATCH and INSERT a duplicate. Destinations are small enough that the full-table merge scan is fine. Made-with: Cursor * revert capital_actions back to microbatch The single-shot full-history merge fails at executor-time hash sizing: Too large (824300146 expected elements) even though the EXPLAIN plan is structurally clean. Trino sizes the build hash from the planner row estimate (~12B transfers across 5y of polygon history), not from the post-dynamic-filter probe set, so dynamic filtering doesn't help here. Microbatch keeps the per-batch source estimate small and avoids the sizing blowup. Kept: users_proxies + market_addresses incremental shape (independent wins). Did NOT bring back the temp --vars '{... month}' override; daily batches should fit CI's 90-min budget given the OR-fix and proxy materialization. Made-with: Cursor * temp: monthly batch_size override for CI test run Re-thread batch_size through var() and pass --vars in the CI workflow so the initial backfill runs monthly batches instead of ~2000 daily batches. Revert before merging. Made-with: Cursor * prep for merge

author: alicecha
message: CUR2-2163: add _updated_at column to dex_aggregator.trades (#9615) * Add _updated_at column to dex_aggregator.trades lineage Add _updated_at timestamp and merge_skip_unchanged=true to dex_aggregator_trades, dex_aggregator_base_trades, and the enrich_dex_aggregator_trades macro. Each model generates current_timestamp AS _updated_at directly in its SELECT. The merge macro skips unchanged rows, so _updated_at only advances when data actually changes — matching the pattern shipped for dex.trades (#9494) and dex_solana.trades (#9543). CUR2-2163 * Stamp _updated_at only in dex_aggregator_trades final SELECT Address Cursor Bugbot review on #9615: the prior pattern (stamp in dex_aggregator_base_trades, propagate through the enrich macro) wrote a stale base_trades timestamp on the enriched path, so rows re-merged in dex_aggregator_trades because amount_usd changed from price movement would carry an old _updated_at and slip past the customer's incremental sync watermark. Drop _updated_at from dex_aggregator_base_trades and the enrich_dex_aggregator_trades macro; stamp current_timestamp AS _updated_at once in the final union of dex_aggregator_trades. The merge macro already excludes _updated_at from change-tracking so merge_skip_unchanged still works. CUR2-2163 * Fix duplicate keys in velora delta v1 by using order_index as evt_index paraswap_delta_v1_safeSettleBatch unrolls a batch into N orders that share the same call_trace_address and have NULL evt_index. They were all coalesced to evt_index=0 in map_internal_to_dex, so within a single tx the orders collapsed on dex_aggregator.trades's unique key (block_date, blockchain, project, version, tx_hash, evt_index, trace_address) — producing 24 duplicates (verified pre-existing in prod) that were surfaced by slim CI when this PR first built dex_aggregator_trades. Coalesce evt_index to order_index instead of 0; delta v1 has no events, and order_index already distinguishes batch orders. Delta v2 is unchanged for the swap_settle_batch path (real evt_index from joined events takes precedence) and for swap_settle (single order, order_index=0, same as before). Note: prod cleanup of historical duplicates needs a full refresh of dex_aggregator.trades (or the upstream paraswap_delta_v1 model) — incremental MERGE on a unique key whose value is changing won't reconcile the existing rows. CUR2-2163 * Revert delta v1 fix; downgrade dex_aggregator_trades unique test to warn The previous attempt to give velora delta v1 batch orders distinct evt_index values worked at the paraswap_delta_v1_ethereum_trades level in CI, but slim CI's --defer mode resolves dex_aggregator_trades' ref to paraswap_trades (a view that wasn't selected by state:modified) back to prod, so the CI build of dex_aggregator_trades still saw the unfixed prod data and the test continued to fail with the same 24 dupes. Revert the macro change and downgrade the uniqueness test to warn until velora delta v1 is fixed properly upstream and prod is full-refreshed. Comment in _schema.yml notes the reason and the bump-back condition. CUR2-2163 * Revert "Revert delta v1 fix; downgrade dex_aggregator_trades unique test to warn" This reverts commit 62dfce98b63cd814285e20170e5a0f6b7abce07e. * Touch paraswap views so slim CI rebuilds them with the delta v1 fix map_internal_to_dex.sql is changed in this PR, so slim CI selects paraswap_delta_v{1,2}_*_trades. But dex_aggregator_trades refs paraswap_trades, which refs paraswap_ethereum_trades, both views — neither is selected by state:modified. With --defer, dex_aggregator_trades' ref chain resolves to prod and the test reads unfixed upstream data. Add a no-op header comment so dbt picks them up as state:modified.body and the ref chain resolves to CI-built tables instead. CUR2-2163

Downstream models (ohlcv_hourly, positions, market_prices_*) are not touched — they only read existing column contracts, which this change preserves. * chore(polymarket): temp 7-day scope on market_trades for CI dbt-test on #9586 was timing out at 1h30m. Note: V2 CLOB is not live yet on Polygon (launch date slipped past 2026-04-22), so this 7-day window contains only V1 trades. The V2 union branch compiles and the filter will scope it the same way once V2 traffic starts landing. TODO: revert before merge. The schema test already requires it (since V2 can emit rows with identical (block_time, asset_id, evt_index, tx_hash) under two different V2 exchange contracts), but the merge key lagged behind — so two legitimately-distinct V2 rows would have overwritten each other during incremental merges. 2. The row_number() dedup window in the incremental source_trades CTE partitioned by the old 5-column key, so the same collision would silently drop one of the two rows via `where rn = 1` before merge could even see them. message: Raydium v4 trades performance (#9386) * refactor: rebuild raydium_v4_base_trades for performance Refactored raydium_v4 models to match the lifinity_v1 design pattern (commit 1fd0435) for improved query performance: Staging model (raydium_v4_solana_stg_decoded_swaps): - Normalized column names (removed call_ prefix) - Applied COALESCE to inner_instruction_index - Switched to solana_instruction_key for surrogate_key - Updated incremental predicates to use block_date - Removed unused account columns Base trades model (raydium_v4_base_trades): - Separated transfer join logic using swap_transfer_keys pattern - Added swap_slots CTE for coarse block-level filtering - Added transfers_pruned CTE with EXISTS for fine-grained filtering - Pivoted transfer sides via MAX(CASE WHEN) with GROUP BY - Added HAVING clause to ensure exactly one match per side - All source tables now in upstream staging; base_trades focuses on heavy transfers join logic Schema: - Updated staging model test columns to match new names Co-authored-by: jeff-dude <jeff-dude@users.noreply.github.com> * add 7-day window filter on full refresh for fast CI run times Adds an upper bound of project_start_date + 7 days in the non-incremental (full refresh) path for both the staging model and base trades model, so CI only reads a narrow 7-day window instead of the full history. Co-authored-by: jeff-dude <jeff-dude@users.noreply.github.com> * remove hardcoded 7-day cutoff filter, prep for merge Removes the temporary upper-bound date filters (DATE + INTERVAL '7' DAY) that were added for fast CI testing. All three non-incremental paths now read from project_start_date onwards without a ceiling. Co-authored-by: jeff-dude <jeff-dude@users.noreply.github.com> * refactor: implement microbatch backfill pattern for raydium_v4_base_trades Mirrors the design from PR #9396 (raydium_v3): - Created raydium_v4_base_trades_backfill.sql: microbatch incremental model containing the core transfer-key join logic. Uses model.batch.event_time_start/end for batch windowing with batch_size=day and lookback=3. - Converted raydium_v4_base_trades.sql: now a simple view that selects from the backfill model, ensuring no downstream breakage. - Updated schema.yml: added backfill model entry with microbatch tag and tests, updated base_trades description to note it is a view over the backfill model. Co-authored-by: jeff-dude <jeff-dude@users.noreply.github.com> * simplify backfill model to use original join logic Since microbatch handles batching, the complex transfer-key aggregation pattern is unnecessary. Reverted the backfill model to use the original simple INNER JOIN logic: - swaps CTE reads from staging model (normalized columns) - transfers CTE reads from tokens_solana.transfers - all_swaps joins via direct offset matching (inner_instruction_index + 1/+2) The COALESCE in the staging model means the offset arithmetic works uniformly for both inner and non-inner instructions, simplifying the original conditional join to a single expression per side. Co-authored-by: jeff-dude <jeff-dude@users.noreply.github.com> * pull block_month and surrogate_key from staging instead of recomputing Instead of recomputing block_month via CAST(date_trunc(...)) and surrogate_key via dbt_utils.generate_surrogate_key, pull both directly from the upstream staging model which already provides them. These were the only two columns being recomputed; all other columns (block_slot, block_time, tx_id, etc.) were already pulled directly. Co-authored-by: jeff-dude <jeff-dude@users.noreply.github.com> * add block_date and block_slot to transfer join conditions Restores the block_date and block_slot join conditions from the original code that were dropped during refactoring. While tx_id is sufficient for correctness, these columns help the query optimizer with partition pruning on the large transfers table. The inner_instruction_index simplification (from conditional is_inner logic to simple offset arithmetic) remains correct because the staging model COALESCE's the value to 0 for non-inner instructions. Co-authored-by: jeff-dude <jeff-dude@users.noreply.github.com> --------- Co-authored-by: Cursor Agent <cursoragent@cursor.com> Co-authored-by: jeff-dude <jeff-dude@users.noreply.github.com>

Co-authored-by: jeff-dude <jeff-dude@users.noreply.github.com> * Fix Jinja microbatch condition: use truthiness check instead of 'is defined' model.batch is None outside microbatch execution (e.g. dbt compile). Use 'if model.batch' instead, which correctly treats None as falsy. author: sdaftuar
message: Periodically make block-relay connections and sync headers To make eclipse attacks more difficult, regularly initiate outbound connections and stay connected long enough to sync headers and potentially learn of new blocks. If we learn a new block, rotate out an existing block-relay peer in favor of the new peer. This augments the existing outbound peer rotation that exists -- currently we make new full-relay connections when our tip is stale, which we disconnect after waiting a small time to see if we learn a new block. As block-relay connections use minimal bandwidth, we can make these connections regularly and not just when our tip is stale. Like feeler connections, these connections are not aggressive; whenever our timer fires (once every 5 minutes on average), we'll try to initiate a new block-relay connection as described, but if we fail to connect we just wait for our timer to fire again before repeating with a new peer.

author: laanwj
message: Merge #18991: Cache responses to GETADDR to prevent topology leaks 3bd67ba5a4ef3c20ef1f873b63c9f53a6c8608b6 Test addr response caching (Gleb Naumenko) cf1569e074505dbbb9d29422803dd31bb62072d4 Add addr permission flag enabling non-cached addr sharing (Gleb Naumenko) acd6135b43941fa51d52f5fcdb2ce944280ad01e Cache responses to addr requests (Gleb Naumenko) 7cc0e8101f01891aa8be093a00d993bb7579c385 Remove useless 2500 limit on AddrMan queries (Gleb Naumenko) ded742bc5b96e3215d69c11fb3628d224e7ae034 Move filtering banned addrs inside GetAddresses() (Gleb Naumenko) Pull request description: This is a very simple code change with a big p2p privacy benefit. It’s currently trivial to scrape any reachable node’s AddrMan (a database of all nodes known to them along with the timestamps). We do have a limit of one GETADDR per connection, but a spy can disconnect and reconnect even from the same IP, and send GETADDR again and again. Since we respond with 1,000 random records at most, depending on the AddrMan size it takes probably up to 100 requests for an spy to make sure they scraped (almost) everything. I even have a script for that. It is totally doable within couple minutes. Then, with some extra protocol knowledge a spy can infer the direct peers of the victim, and other topological stuff. I suggest to cache responses to GETADDR on a daily basis, so that an attacker gets at most 1,000 records per day, and can’t track the changes in real time. I will be following up with more improvements to addr relay privacy, but this one alone is a very effective. And simple! I doubt any of the real software does *reconnect to get new addrs from a given peer*, so we shouldn’t be cutting anyone. I also believe it doesn’t have any negative implications on the overall topology quality. And the records being “outdated” for at most a day doesn’t break any honest assumptions either. Merge #13048: [tests] Fix feature_block flakiness c1d742025c [tests] Fix feature_block flakiness (John Newbery) Pull request description: feature_block.py occasionally fails on Travis. I believe this is due to a a race condition when reconnecting to bitcoind after a subtest that expects disconnection. If the test runs ahead and sends the INV for the subsequent test before we've received the initial sync getheaders, then we may end up sending two headers messages - one as a response to the initial sync getheaders and one in response to the INV getheaders. If both of those headers fail validation with a DoS score of 50 or higher, then we'll unexpectedly be disconnected. There is only one validation failure that has a DoS score bewteen 50 and 100, which is high-hash. That's why the test is failing immediately after the "Reject a block with invalid work" subtest. Fix is to wait for the initial getheaders from the peer before we start populating our blockstore. That way we won't have any invalid headers to respond to it with. Tree-SHA512: dc17d795fcfaf0f8c0bf1e9732b5e11fbc8febbfafba4c231b7c13a5404a2c297dcd703a7a75bc7f353c893e12efc87f424f2201abd47ba5268af32d4d2e841f

author: sdaftuar
message: [qa] Delete cookie file before starting node If a cookie file exists in a datadir prior to node startup, it must have been leftover from a prior unclean shutdown. As bitcoind will overwrite it anyway, delete it before starting up to prevent the test framework from inadvertently trying to connect using stale credentials.

author: sdaftuar
message: Shut down if trying to connect a corrupted block The call to CheckBlock() in ConnectBlock() is redundant with calls to it prior to storing a block on disk. If CheckBlock() fails with an error indicating the block is potentially corrupted, then shut down immediately, as this is an indication that the node is experiencing hardware issues. (If we didn't shut down, we could go into an infinite loop trying to reconnect this same bad block, as we're not setting the block's status to FAILED in the case where there is potential corruption.) If CheckBlock() fails for some other reason, we'll end up flagging this block as bad (perhaps some prior software version "let a bad block in", as the comment indicates), and not trying to connect it again, so this case should be properly handled.

author: sdaftuar
message: Connect to an extra outbound peer if our tip is stale If our tip hasn't updated in a while, that may be because our peers are not relaying blocks to us that we would consider valid. Allow connection to an additional outbound peer in that circumstance. Also, periodically check to see if we are exceeding our target number of outbound peers, and disconnect the one which has least recently announced a new block to us (choosing the newest such peer in the case of tie).

author: thaaddeus
message: Simplify MEXC futures derivative ticker sources Build derivative_ticker snapshots from push.ticker, using its lastPrice, holdVol, indexPrice, fairPrice and timestamp as the normalized ticker source. Stop using push.index.price and push.fair.price in this mapper so price-only streams no longer drive derivative_ticker state or emit separate snapshots. Keep push.funding.rate as the dedicated funding source because it provides nextSettleTime. Funding messages update pending funding state only, and that state is carried into the next push.ticker snapshot so normalized timestamps stay ticker-derived and stale ticker fundingRate values do not overwrite newer funding updates.

message: feat: terminal checkpoint and graceful shutdown for pipelines (#61) * fix(shutdown): coordinated front-to-back drain so bounded multi-source pipelines don't lose the tail Implements the core of the shutdown investigation (docs PR #11): make a multi-source/multi-sink pipeline (hybrid sources -> plugin/pubsub sinks) drain every record into every sink and exit cleanly, in both job mode (bounded completion) and streaming mode (SIGTERM), instead of racing plugins and losing the last buffered batches. Coordinator (checkpoint_management.rs) - Add a cloneable CheckpointControl handle over the coordinator's shared state: - begin_terminal_checkpoint(): mint the single final epoch a completing/ shutting-down bounded source emits after its last data; gate the timer producer so it can't clobber it. - await_terminal_finalized(): resolve once that epoch finalizes. - sink_completed(): drop a drained sink from a now-mutable expected-ack set and finalize epochs the remaining live sinks already acked (fixes the multi-source finalization stall). - stop() now unsubscribes the coordinator's own channel so it stops leaking a dead sender. Retry (retry.rs) - Add retry_forever_with_backoff_until_cancelled(): a shutdown-watch-aware variant that gives up between attempts instead of retrying a sick backend forever. Hybrid source (hybrid.rs) - Emit the terminal-checkpoint round-trip (marker after last data -> await finalize -> finalizer inline) on job-mode bounded completion, on unbounded stream end, and when the shared shutdown signal fires mid-phase. - A shutdown watcher stops the inner unbounded (Kafka) source so the loop drains instead of blocking forever on a live topic. Host run loop (lib.rs) - One top-level SIGTERM/SIGINT handler flips a shared watch signal (sources drain front-to-back) and replaces the per-component signal handlers. - Restructure the run loop: a plugin dispatcher finishing is terminal only on error; on clean completion the sinks are drained, then plugins are Terminated and their dispatchers are AWAITED (bounded) so the last buffered batches flush before the runtime is dropped -- the job-mode tail-loss fix. - Gate teardown on the terminal checkpoint finalizing (bounded), wire the control handle to hybrid sources and sink_completed into each sink future. - Add a shutdown budget (STREAMLING__SHUTDOWN_BUDGET_SECS, default 25s) and a watchdog OS thread that hard-exits at the budget edge so a wedged FFI/rdkafka teardown can never hold the process past the k8s grace period. Plugin lifecycle (plugin.rs) - Remove the competing one-shot plugin SIGTERM watcher (it killed plugins first, inverting the drain order); the top-level handler owns signals now. - terminate_plugins uses a bounded send_timeout and continues past a wedged plugin instead of blocking the shutdown path forever. Unit tests added for the coordinator (terminal checkpoint, sink_completed, idempotent begin) and the cancellable retry loop. Full build green; streamling-core (18) and hybrid (33) unit tests pass. A SIGTERM during a long bounded (ClickHouse) scan therefore sat in stream.next() until the whole table had been read, blew the shutdown budget, and the watchdog force-exited without a terminal drain. - hybrid: select on the shutdown watch while forwarding bounded-phase batches, ending the stream early on signal (the Kafka phase is exempt on purpose: its source drains the in-flight batch itself). Ending early is safe — nothing past the last emitted batch is checkpoint-covered, so a restart resumes from the last finalized cursor. - clickhouse source: check the shutdown signal between pages so the scan ends at a page boundary; the buffered-marker flush after the loop still runs. - checkpoint control: new pending_terminal_ack_sinks() diagnostic, and the finalize-timeout warning now names the sinks that never acked. Documented the lock discipline on the CheckpointControl impl. - e2e: SIGTERM mid-bounded-scan must exit 0 within the grace period with the drained prefix in the sink. * fix(kafka): flush buffered checkpoint messages before the source stops Markers/Finalizers that arrive after a batch has been built are buffered to ride the NEXT batch — but on shutdown (top-of-loop exit, drained-send exit) and on SourceComplete there is no next batch, so they were silently dropped: sinks never saw the marker, the epoch could not collect this branch's acks, and its offsets were never committed before teardown. ClickHouse, hybrid, and plugin sources all flush pending checkpoints before ending their streams; Kafka now does the same, reusing the ClickHouse synthetic-flush helper. * fix(shutdown): make ClickHouse retry backoff and plugin-source teardown shutdown-aware Two gaps in the front-to-back drain: - The ClickHouse scan's query-retry and timeout backoff sleeps (up to 30s) were uncancellable, so a SIGTERM landing mid-backoff outlived the shutdown budget on its own and rode the watchdog. Both sleeps now select on the shutdown watch and fall through to the page-boundary check. - On shutdown, PluginSourceExec drained only the plugin output channel before its synthetic final flush; coordinator Markers/Finalizers still queued on the source's subscription (e.g. the terminal epoch's Marker, broadcast during the shutdown window) were dropped, so sinks never saw those epochs and finalization stalled until the timeout. Still-queued messages are now folded into the final flush batch — the plugin is about to be terminated, but the sinks still need the Marker to ack. * fix(plugin): error instead of panic when the Init send hits a closed channel; count skipped terminal Finalizers - PluginSourceExec::execute unwrapped the Init send to the plugin input channel: a plugin that exited during startup panicked the executor thread instead of failing the query. Surface a DataFusionError. - The terminal-Finalizer skip path (finalize timeout on shutdown) only emitted a warn log; the silent tail replay after restart was undiagnosable from metrics. Record a checkpoint_terminal_finalizer_skipped counter under the coordinator's component id alongside the warning. * fix(checkpoints): remove timed-out epochs so a lost marker cannot wedge the producer The timer producer waits for the newest epoch to finalize before minting the next one, but the timeout checker only logged and counted stalled epochs — it never removed them. An epoch whose Marker broadcast reached no source subscriber (e.g. the first interval fires while a large plan — many sources, plugin UDF compilation — is still being built, so no source execute() has subscribed yet) can therefore never be acked, and the producer waits on it forever while data keeps flowing with no further checkpoints: markers_sent stays flat, the epoch sits in Started, and every offset from that point on is never committed. The timeout sweep now removes timed-out non-terminal epochs, so the producer mints a fresh epoch whose Marker reaches the (by then live) subscribers and checkpointing self-heals within one timeout. This is safe under the Finalizer consumer contract: Finalizers may be skipped and commit semantics are cumulative, so a removed epoch's offsets stay uncommitted until the next finalized epoch covers them (at-least-once preserved). It also restores the behaviour the next_epoch doc comment already promised ('even if previous epochs are removed due to timeout'). The terminal epoch is exempt: the shutdown path's bounded wait owns its lifecycle. The sweep cadence derives from the configured timeout (half, clamped to [1s, 30s] — unchanged for the production default) so the behaviour is testable with a short-timeout coordinator. --------- Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
