author: kroitor
message: feat(base): ws auth single-flight primitives (#29903) * fix(binance): prevent concurrent ws auth races via base single-flight guard - singleFlightAcquire/Wait/Resolve/Reject primitives on the Exchange base with per-language mirrors (py/php/cs/go/java), flight futures stored on the exchange because binance futures/delivery user-data urls embed the listenKey and no ws client exists before the fetch - binance authenticate(): per-type flight around the listenKey fetch - binance signature subscribe: waiters now block until the leader's subscribe confirms instead of returning onto an unauthenticated stream - binance listenToken: flight covers create+subscribe incl. the renewal timer re-entry, failure resets lastAuthenticatedTime so retries work - base ws unit test: leader election, shared result, rejection propagation, wait semantics closes #29393 * fix(binance): harden ws-api subscribe paths per review - listenToken: write the options cache and schedule renewal only after the subscribe confirms, so a late-entering caller cannot pass the staleness check while the flight is still in progress - signature: clear the subscriptions flag on transport-level watch failure so the next caller re-enters the leader path instead of treating the stream as authenticated * fix(binance): reject the auth flight on protocol-level subscribe failure - handleUserDataStreamSubscribe now rejects the request messageHash and returns when subscriptionId is missing, so the awaiting watch throws, the leader rejects the flight, and waiters retry instead of proceeding onto an unauthenticated stream - authenticate() rejects the flight when the listenKey response carries no key instead of caching an empty credential * fix(binance): address review nits on ws auth flight - reject the flight when the listenToken response carries no token - python: initialize authentication_flights once in the constructor - java: non-blocking thenApply chains instead of supplyAsync + join * fix(binance): guard the stock listenKey path with the auth flight - authenticateStock had the same unguarded staleness check as the main listenKey branch and was missed by the initial wiring - flight hash authenticate:listenKey:stock, empty-key rejection included - base test: assert a failed flight leaves the credential cache untouched (regression guard for the cache-before-confirm class) * fix(base): close the single-flight reject and shutdown holes addresses the three review findings before any exchange wires onto the primitives: - an alone leader rejecting a flight no waiter had awaited was an unhandled promise rejection that killed node - the flight now carries the same silent rejection handler Future.subscribe attaches (python retrieves the exception in a done callback, c# observes the task exception; go channel futures and java completable futures need no swallow, documented in place) - the c# acquire lost-add-race path could miss the winner's flight entirely when it had already settled and vanished, returning false as if a flight had completed and letting the caller proceed against an empty credential cache - the acquire is now a loop that either awaits the visible flight or elects the caller as the fresh leader - close() never settled the flights map, so in-flight waiters hung across a shutdown - every runtime now rejects all in-flight authentication flights with ExchangeClosedByUser at the top of close, mirroring client reset semantics the primitives test gains an alone-leader case: acquire, reject with no waiter, assert the process survives and the slot is clean for a fresh leader * fix(base): settle flights on the real c# teardown and pin close-in-flight - the settlement sweep lived on the camelCase close() wrapper while Close(bool) is the teardown every caller actually reaches - callers of Close() / Close(true) bypassed it and their waiters still hung. the sweep now lives at the top of Close(bool); close() inherits it - new test case pins the behavior on a fresh instance: acquire, spawn a waiter, close(), assert the waiter rejects with ExchangeClosedByUser and the slot is gone * fix(base): type the close-in-flight waiter error for the ts gate let x = undefined types as undefined and instanceof on it is TS2358 - the local tsx run transforms without typechecking, which hid it

message: fix(latoken): drop non-positive book levels and skip the stale-ticker median check (#29906) * fix(latoken): drop non-positive book levels and skip the stale-ticker median check latoken's rest book is an absolute snapshot - price, quantity, cost, accumulated - with no signed fields, unlike their websocket stream whose entries carry signed quantityChange deltas (official clients build books by summing them). during venue incidents a signed internal aggregate leaks into the rest quantity and a deleted level is served with a zero or negative quantity for long stretches: observed live on 2026-08-17, bestAskQuantity -0.1791852 from both the book and ticker endpoints for 30+ minutes, failing fetchOrderBook amount asserts in every language lane. such a level is a deleted level their aggregation failed to drop, so fetchOrderBook now removes non-positive rows before parsing - the semantically correct reconstruction of the book. the ticker side cannot be repaired by parsing - bestBid/bestAsk come from the venue ticker endpoint fields themselves, which served a dust bid and the ghost ask while trades printed 1.15% above the stale median - so latoken fetchTicker gets the purpose-built lastBetweenBidAsk skip entry with the incident as the reason * test(latoken): lock the incident-replay book fixture per review: the filter's parse path had no static response coverage - the poisoned 2026-08-17 payload (negative ask, zero ask, negative bid ghosts around real levels and a positive dust bid) is now a static response case, parsedResponse harvested verbatim from the response tester report block. 4 static response tests pass

message: fix(pro): java ArrayCache hashmap, getLimit, BySide, and move-to-end (#29873) * fix(pro): java ArrayCache hashmap, getLimit, BySide, and move-to-end Ports java/lib/src/main/java/io/github/ccxt/ws/ArrayCache.java back onto the ts/src/base/ws/Cache.ts contract. The Java cache is hand-written (not transpiled) and had drifted; javaTranspiler.ts:3077 leaves Java out of the shared test.cache.ts conformance harness that every other port runs, so the divergences below were silent. - hashmap: ArrayCacheBySymbolById/BySymbolBySide now write through to the public nested hashmap (symbol -> id|side -> item) instead of a private symbolMap. 17 generated call sites across 14 exchanges read .hashmap directly and were always getting {}, which among other things made the BitmexCore side carry-forward fix for issue #29001 dead code. - ArrayCacheByTimestamp.getLimit: own override counting distinct timestamps via a sizeTracker set (Cache.ts:134-140). OHLCV rows are Lists, so the inherited symbol-keyed getLimit returned 0 and watchOHLCV re-emitted the entire cache on every tick. - getLimit reset is deferred to the next append rather than eager, so two reads with no intervening append agree (Cache.ts:69,75,93-102). - getLimit honours limit via min, and returns limit verbatim for a symbol never seen; the return type becomes a nullable Integer to represent TS undefined. filterBySinceLimit already null-checks the limit. - ById/BySide re-append moves the row to the end (splice+push) and merges fields onto the stored object instead of replacing it positionally. - ArrayCacheBySymbolBySide is implemented rather than a stub: dedupes on (symbol, side) and never evicts, matching Cache.ts:237-286. - maxSize <= 0 means unbounded instead of being coerced to 1000, which is the .filter() copy-construction case called out at Cache.ts:88. - clear() wipes the hashmap and update counters alongside the contents so it cannot hand out rows that are no longer in the list. Every synchronized marker is retained; the JMM hazard documented at BaseExchange.java:1408-1412 is unchanged. ArrayCacheTest grows from 5 tests to 31, covering each divergence above plus reflective dispatch through Helpers.callDynamically (the path all 220+ generated call sites use) and concurrent appends. Verified the new assertions are load-bearing: run against the previous implementation 8 of 9 contract probes fail, against this one all 9 pass. ./gradlew :lib:test -> 204 tests, 0 failures. * test(pro): java ArrayCache remaining contract regressions * fix(pro): truncate Java OHLCV on shorter ByTimestamp update Incoming candle defines length. mergeInto used to copy only min(len) and leave a stale tail; that test locked the old JS for-in behaviour. Match the corrected TS contract: [100,1,2,3,4,5] then [100,9,9] → [100,9,9]. * refactor(pro): java newUpdatesBySymbol is ConcurrentHashMap<String, Integer> Distinct id/side tracking for ById/BySide moves to seenUpdatesBySymbol. getLimit now reads the int count directly.

author: carlosmiei
message: chore: add ws static tests to different exchanges (#29800) * chore: add ws static tests to different exchanges * fix php kraken * add more static tests * more tests * more test * trigger build * some fixes * fix tests * fix(tests): deterministic ws static frame injection across threaded runtimes - injector now waits for each consumed frame to settle before checking for the next pending future, so threaded runtimes (java/c#/go) cannot burn a frame against a stale future - sequence tests keep rejecting pending futures until the watch side flags completion (markWsTestCompleted/isWsTestCompleted helpers in all six languages), so a wrong fixture fails fast instead of hanging the run - java: sleep() blocks synchronously during ws static tests - joining a delayed future inside a ForkJoinPool worker could steal the pending watch task onto the injector's own stack (helpAsyncBlocker) and deadlock the run - go: disable poloniex watchTicker (injected frame does not resolve the future - parity backlog) - whitebit: skip timestamp/datetime (c# float ms rounding) Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix deribit * fix(tests): unbounded ws rejection loop + master-merge fixture updates - the sequential frame injector now rejects pending futures until the watch side flags completion, with no time bound - a watch call registering its future after the frames ran out is rejected on the next tick instead of hanging the run when it slipped past the old 5s window (intermittent java hang on slow/loaded runners) - deribit inverse ticker fixture updated for the new volume mapping from master (baseVolume=stats.volume, quoteVolume=volume_notional, vwap derived) - regenerate php/python kraken (array-length fix was committed in ts but the generated files were stale, crashing php with strlen(array)) Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> * fix hang * fix tests * fix(tests): eliminate forkjoin work-stealing deadlock in java ws static tests the java ci hang: joining an incomplete common-pool future from a forkjoin worker lets the pool execute queued tasks inline on the blocked stack (helpAsyncBlocker). the watch chain's joins could steal the still-queued frame injector task and run it on top of the very stack it needs to release — with the unbounded rejection loop that became a hard deadlock. three layers of defense: - java callExchangeMethodDynamically now returns a wrapper future joined on a dedicated plain thread pool, so the watch side's joins never steal - the injector is queued before the watch side in sequence mode, so it is already running (unstealable) by the time the watch chain first blocks - the rejection loop keeps a 30s backstop so even an inlined injector always unwinds instead of deadlocking verified: 97/97 in all six languages; java green 4x consecutively under the ci 4-core constraint (-XX:ActiveProcessorCount=4) Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> --------- Co-authored-by: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: kroitor
message: fix(cli): prefer the local typescript sources over built artifacts so new integrations work without any build steps (#29790) * fix(cli): prefer the local typescript sources over built artifacts so new integrations work without any build steps The cli loaded ccxt with import('ccxt') first, which resolves through the package exports map to built artifacts (js/ or dist/), and only fell back to the typescript sources on a hard import failure. For a developer working on a new integration inside the repository this silently loads a stale bundle that predates the new exchange and fails with 'ccxt[exchangeId] is not a constructor' until js and cjs build steps are run manually. The loader is now shared in helpers and detects the repository via the presence of ts/ccxt.ts: inside the repo it always loads the typescript sources (no build steps required, stale artifacts can never shadow the sources), outside it falls back to an installed ccxt package. The default export is unwrapped to survive cjs interop shapes whose namespace does not expose named keys (observed via dist/ccxt.cjs re-exporting ccxt['default']: namespace btse undefined while default.btse is a function). Deduplicating the loader also fixes a latent double-instance hazard where error classes destructured in cli.ts had different identities than those thrown by the exchange constructed in helpers, breaking instanceof checks. * fix(cli): only prefer the typescript sources when the cli itself runs as typescript Gates the ts-sources-first loading on the cli executing as typescript (import.meta.url ending in .ts, i.e. under tsx). The compiled ccxt-cli package runs under plain node, in-repo via npm run cli.js or installed from npm, where importing raw typescript would crash with ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION - those runtimes fall back to import ('ccxt'): the built js barrel in-repo, the installed ccxt dependency otherwise. The published ccxt npm package itself ships neither cli/ nor ts/ (verified against .npmignore), so it is unaffected in all cases. The repository detection is additionally wrapped so it can never throw (fs.existsSync is non-throwing by contract, but the loader owns the invariant explicitly) - on any detection error it degrades to the package import instead of taking the cli down. * fix(cli): normalize the exchanges export to an id array regardless of import shape The namespace's named exchanges export is a dictionary of exchange classes while the default export carries an array of exchange ids, so after unwrapping the default the cli registered numeric indices as command names (Object.keys over an array) and every exchange id was rejected by commander with 'unknown command'. The two existing usage sites already contradicted each other - cli.ts used Object.keys (dictionary shape) while printSupportedExchanges used .join (array shape) - so each only worked under one loader outcome. A single exchangeIds array is now derived in the shared loader, Array.isArray-guarded so both shapes normalize identically, and both usage sites plus the prediction-id filter consume it. pro and prediction need no changes: their .exchanges arrays are attached to the same objects under both shapes.

author: kroitor
message: test(php): guard the ws orderbook index invariant and replay the desync sequence (#29744) Hardening follow-up to https://github.com/ccxt/ccxt/pull/29603, which fixed the phantom index sentinels from https://github.com/ccxt/ccxt/issues/26967 but left the diagnosis scaffolding behind in the debugging session: 1. The tripwire that caught the bug is now a permanent debug invariant: a protected assertIndexAligned on OrderBookSide asserting count(index) equals parent::count() after every structural mutation, placed at all seven mutation exits across the plain, counted and indexed sides plus limit. A desync previously surfaced as book corruption only several mutations later; now it trips at the first desynced mutation with both counts named. Native assert, zero cost in production where zend.assertions is -1. 2. A transpilable regression test replaying the killing sequence in test.orderBook.ts: reset with a snapshot, depth trim via limit, then deltas landing on and beyond the trimmed tail, asserting the exact resulting book plus that every row is a well formed price and amount pair, the php corruption produced rows holding only an amount. Verified: ts test passes including the new sequence; php lint clean; healthy flow across all three side types keeps the asserts silent; a simulated pre-fix sentinel desync trips at the first mutation; with zend.assertions -1 the corrupted flow runs assert-free, confirming zero production cost. ts test sources only, ci regenerates the transpiled outputs; the php side file is hand-written base, no transpile surface.

author: kroitor
message: fix(python): guard ping loop transport writes and cancel keepalive before close (#29735) Two teardown defects in the aiohttp ws client left the ping task dying with ConnectionResetError, Cannot write to closing transport, as asyncio task exception was never retrieved noise, open since 2024 in https://github.com/ccxt/ccxt/issues/22075 1. aiohttp_close closed the transport first and cancelled ping_looper after, so a ping tick during the close await wrote into the closing transport. The keepalive is now cancelled before the close, matching the php client's teardown ordering, whose timer dies before the transport starts closing. 2. The raw connection.ping call carried no guard, unlike the custom text ping branch one line above it, so a server initiated close or a network drop between the loop condition and the write raised out of the task. It is now guarded symmetrically: a closed client exits the loop silently, a live transport death routes into on_error, which rejects futures and arms the standard reconnect path, then the loop exits since a dead transport has no keepalive to maintain. Hand-written python ws base, no transpile surface. Verified with a semantics simulation, deliberate teardown produces no error, live death routes exactly one error to on_error, and the base future suite green through the patched module.

author: kroitor
message: fix(python): retain ws results resolved without a waiter (#29720) Client.resolve on a message hash with no future in the map silently dropped the data. The consumer arriving a moment later waited on a fresh future for data that had already arrived, and in multi symbol subscriptions the drop window opens every time user code awaits between watch calls, quiet symbols pay the latency tail, see https://github.com/ccxt/ccxt/issues/28089 and https://github.com/ccxt/ccxt/issues/23251. Mirrors the go lane fix https://github.com/ccxt/ccxt/pull/29719. resolve now retains the latest value per hash in pending_results, future() drains it into an immediately resolved future kept out of the map so it is delivered exactly once and the next consumer waits for fresh data. Pending value and retained rejection are mutually exclusive per hash in both directions, resolve retention clears a retained rejection so a recovered stream never fails a later waiter with a stale error, reject clears retained values per hash and wholesale on broadcast so a post error consumer never receives stale pre error data. Regression tests in test_client_retention.py run against the real Client, wired into tests_init, covering latest wins delivery, drain once, reject clearing, resolve superseding a stale rejection, and broadcast wipe.

author: kroitor
message: fix(go): eliminate ws future resolve races and retain unconsumed results (#29719) Three related defects in the go ws client future plumbing, plus retention symmetry on both sides: 1. Lost wakeup: Future.Await checked resolved under f.mu and appended its subscriber under a second mutex. A Resolve landing in the unlocked gap fired sync.Once, notified the then empty subscriber list, cleared it, and the consumer subscribed to a future that never notifies again, blocking forever. On high frequency streams like binance bookTicker the gap is hit within minutes, the exact symptom of https://github.com/ccxt/ccxt/issues/29586. One mutex now spans the resolved check and the subscriber append against the state set and subscriber snapshot in Resolve and Reject, notification happens outside the lock on the snapshot. FutureRace carried the identical gap and gets the identical treatment. 2. Lost update: Client.Resolve on a hash with no future in the map silently dropped the data, the consumer arriving a moment later waited on a fresh future for data that already arrived, see https://github.com/ccxt/ccxt/issues/28089 and https://github.com/ccxt/ccxt/issues/23251. Resolve now retains the latest value per hash in PendingResults under FuturesMu, NewFuture drains it into an immediately resolved future kept out of the map, latest value wins matching watch coalescing semantics. 3. Data race: NewFuture read and deleted client.Rejections outside any lock while Reject wrote it. Rejections access now shares FuturesMu. 4. Retention symmetry: an error rejected while no consumer future exists is stored in Rejections and fails the next NewFuture fast, ts parity. Pending value and retained rejection are mutually exclusive per hash in both directions, reject retention clears the pending value and resolve retention clears a retained rejection, so a recovered stream never fails a later waiter with a stale error and a post error consumer never receives stale pre error data. Spent futures from both drains stay out of the map. Regression tests in exchange_future_resolve_test.go, all pass under the race detector, a window instrumented mirror of the previous Await hung 1975 of 2000 interleavings. Supersedes https://github.com/ccxt/ccxt/pull/29718

author: carlotestor
message: refactor(base): List-only parse* params + multi-lang implicit API return shapes (#29645) * refactor(base): take List, not Dict | List, on the toArray parse* family The nine parse* helpers that begin with this.toArray() were widened to Dict | List in 45788925 on the grounds that toArray normalizes both shapes. It does, but that made the *documented contract* of the public parse* surface "hand me either shape and I will guess", which is not a contract any caller should rely on: only the exchange method knows whether its venue answered with a bare array or with an envelope, and it is the one holding the key to read out of. So the parameter becomes an honest List and the extraction moves to the call sites that actually have a dict: kraken#fetchMyTrades result.trades is keyed by trade id -> toArray whitebit#fetchTransactions v4 main-account/history is the {records,...} envelope, read with safeList exactly as the fetchWithdrawals sibling already did coinbaseexchange#fetchAccounts GET /accounts is Endpoint<Dict> -> toArray mexc x3 contract answers {code,data}; safeValue on that payload becomes safeList Everywhere else the response was already a list and only its *local* was over-wide: 18 `let response: Dict | List` declarations collapse to `List` because every endpoint assigned to them is already declared Promise<List> in the abstract, and the 7 leftover `responseList` guards now normalize through this.toArray, matching the shape master already uses in binance#fetchDeposits. The two overrides follow the base so the ports stay compatible: derive#parseTrades and pro/hitbtc#parseWsTrades. Also teach build/transpile.ts that `List` maps to PHP `array` and to Python `List[Any]`. Without that entry `List` fell through the map and PHP would have kept emitting an untyped parameter. Verified by transpiling the base both ways: Dict | List -> public function parse_trades(mixed $trades, ...) List -> public function parse_trades(array $trades, ...) def parse_trades(self, trades: List[Any], ...) npx tsc --noEmit: 0 errors (probe-verified live). * feat(build): emit implicit API return shapes in PHP/Python/C#/Go/Java TS already carries per-endpoint Dict/List/string shapes from Endpoint assertions into ts/src/abstract. Extend generateImplicitAPI so the same storedReturnTypes map drives the other ports: - Python: Entry[T] generic descriptor + per-module aliases (_Dict/_List); subscript erased at runtime via __class_getitem__ so import cost stays flat - PHP sync: @return array<string,mixed>|list<mixed>|string (docblock only — native return types break async abstract children that already return PromiseInterface) - PHP async: same shapes wrapped in PromiseInterface<> - C#/Java/Go: prose shape docs (signatures cannot narrow without dropping panic/error multiplexing or sync/async method-text identity) Generated dumps are CI-owned and not committed here. * fix(build): import only used typing names in Python abstract modules Always importing Dict, List, and Union made ruff F401 fail the Python qa gate on every Dict-only (or List-only) exchange abstract. Build the from-typing line from the aliases and multi-member returns the module actually uses. * feat(build): emit implicit API return shapes in C# and Java signatures TS and Python already carry the per-endpoint Dict/List/string shapes declared by the `as Endpoint<...>` assertions on each api leaf. C# and Java were left with prose docs only, on the grounds that their generated signatures could not be narrowed. That was wrong: both have a generic async return, so the shape fits on the signature itself once callAsync stops hardcoding the root type. Base: - cs: add callAsync<T>, a guarded narrowing over the existing callAsync. The cast is `is T` rather than a hard cast because handleRestResponse hands back the raw string when a body fails to parse, so an error page yields default(T) instead of an InvalidCastException from inside the transport. - java: make callAsync generic (<T> CompletableFuture<T>). Erasure means the unchecked cast is free, matching how the rest of BaseExchange narrows. Generator (same storedReturnTypes map that already drives TS/Python/PHP): - csharpReturnType: Dict -> Dictionary<string, object>, List -> List<object>, string -> string. Those are exactly what JsonHelper.Deserialize builds, so the declared type is castable rather than merely descriptive. - javaReturnType: Dict -> Map<String, Object>, List -> List<Object>, string -> String, matching Jackson's Object binding. - A multi-member shape has no honest narrowing in either language (both generic returns are invariant and neither has a union type), so those endpoints keep object/Object and say why in the doc comment. Task<T> invariance fallout, fixed at the three hand-written sites that filter or cast an un-awaited task whose static type was erased to object. A narrowed Task<Dictionary<string, object>> is not a Task<object>, so `is Task<object>` returned false and the task was dropped with no error: - Exchange.TranspileHelpers.cs: add AsTaskOfObject and route PromiseAll, callDynamically and callDynamicallyAsync through it. - Exchange.cs: same normalization in the WS spawn path. Without this, promiseAll over two narrowed endpoints returned 0 results instead of 2 — silently, with no exception and no compile error. Also fixes two things the narrowing surfaced: - gemini's web/get/rest-api was declared Endpoint<Dict> but fetchMarkets reads it through fetchWebEndpoint with returnAsJson=false and splits it as text: it answers with the docs page markup. Declared Endpoint<string>. - java kept a Coinbaseadvanced and a Huobi tree after those aliases were removed upstream (#28787, #28788). They have no TypeScript source, so the generator cannot emit shapes for them, and every other port had already dropped them. Their stale untyped api classes were the only override conflicts in the Java build. Generated dumps are CI-owned and not committed here. Verified: tsc --noEmit clean; dotnet build of ccxt, tests and cli succeeds with the pre-existing 2 warnings and 0 errors; gradle :lib :tests :examples compileJava succeeds with the pre-existing 8 warnings; all six languages re-emit cleanly. Both builds are green with the committed sources against the old dumps and against freshly regenerated ones. * feat(build): native return types on sync PHP implicit API abstracts Sync php/abstract methods now carry `: array`, `: string`, or `: array|string` from the same Endpoint shape map as TS/Python/C#/Java. Fine Dict-vs-List detail stays in the @return PHPStan shapes. Async abstracts strip the native suffix when derived (request returns a Promise, not the body) and keep @return PromiseInterface<...>. * feat(build): PromiseInterface return types on async PHP implicit API Async abstracts (and async-only prediction) now match transpiled unified methods: native `: \React\Promise\PromiseInterface` plus generic `@return PromiseInterface<array<string,mixed>|list<mixed>|string>` for Psalm/PHPStan. PHP has no runtime generics, so the type argument cannot appear on the signature itself. Sync REST abstracts keep `: array` / `: string` body shapes. * fix(build): stop PHP/C# typed returns from breaking STATIC_RESPONSE PHP: drop native `: array`/`: string` on sync implicit abstracts. Transport can hand back a raw string (error page / fixtures); a hard array return TypeError'd in response tests. Keep @return shapes and async `: PromiseInterface` + generic @return. C#: generated api methods return Task<object> again (shape in XML docs). Task<T> + is-T filtering silently defaulted real JSON bodies when the declared leaf disagreed with the fixture, emptying balances/tickers. Keep generic callAsync<T> with IDictionary/IList coercion for opt-in use. Test harness awaits via AsTaskOfObject so Task<T> stays awaitable.

message: build: generate base types from ts/src/base/types.ts for all language ports (#29507) * build: add base-type IR extractor and transpile driver Shared scaffold for generating the port base type files from ts/src/base/types.ts instead of hand-maintaining them. * build: generate base types from ts/src/base/types.ts for all ports The per-language base type declarations were hand-maintained: nothing in build/ wrote them and nothing in CI diffed them against the TypeScript, so they drifted silently until a consumer hit a permanently-null field. PR Adds build/transpileTypes.ts, a shared IR over ts/src/base/types.ts (build/typesIR.ts) and one emitter per language. The emitters splice each type over its existing declaration instead of rewriting whole files, so the hand-written support code around them (the C# Helper class, Go's Safe*Typed helpers, Python's Entry/ConstructorArgs) is preserved byte-for-byte and the resulting diff is exactly the drift. C# regenerates byte-identical to the post-#29502 files, which is the correctness oracle for the other ports. Regenerate with `npm run transpile-types`; `npm run transpile-types-check` fails CI when a target is stale. * build: add standard generated-file banner to base type ports Use the same PLEASE DO NOT EDIT / CONTRIBUTING.md banner as the rest of the transpile pipeline on every file owned by transpile-types (Python, C#, Go, Java POJOs). Hand-written Java helpers (TypeHelper, OrderBook, Balances, Network*) stay unbannered. Placement matches sibling ports: file-top (Python), after namespace (C#), after package (Go), after imports (Java). Idempotent via ensureGeneratedBanner. * build: put generated-file banner on line 1 Move the PLEASE DO NOT EDIT banner to the top of every transpile-types output (Python/C#/Go/Java types). Java cores (javaTranspiler createJavaClass) and typed wrappers (generateJavaWrappers) now emit the same banner before package/imports so line 1 is always the marker. * build: recreate missing Java type POJOs; delete orphans npm run transpile-types now writes dictionary wrappers (Tickers, …) and other managed Java types even when the .java file was deleted. Generated POJOs whose TS source is gone are deleted; hand-written TypeHelper / SKIPPED files and unbannered files are left alone. * build: delete Java type POJOs not present in types.ts transpile-types now removes any java/.../types/*.java that is not owned by ts/src/base/types.ts (or the hand-written keep list: TypeHelper, OrderBook, Balances, Network, NetworkLimits). Banner is not required — unbannered orphans are deleted too.

author: carlotestor
message: feat(playground): runnable Java runner with REST + WebSocket proxy support (#29472) Makes Java the sixth runnable language in docs/playground (parity with TypeScript/Python/PHP/Go/C#). Provisioning: scripts/setup-runtimes.sh resolves io.github.ccxt:ccxt from Maven Central (latest release; pin via CCXT_JAVA_VERSION) into runtime/java/libs with a throwaway POM (39 jars, ~47 MB) and precompiles the Playground proxy helper into runtime/java/classes. The Dockerfile adds openjdk-21-jdk-headless and resolves the jars in a throwaway build stage, so Maven and ~/.m2 never ship in the image (+~333 MB: JDK 21 + jars). Runner: lib/runners/java.ts compiles the snippet as Main.java in a per-run dir and launches it through a generated Launcher that forces JVM exit after main() — ccxt-java's pro close() leaves Netty's shared event loop (non-daemon) alive, so watch* JVMs would otherwise linger until the hard timeout. Proxy: ccxt-java ignores HTTP(S)_PROXY env vars (System.getenv never appears in io/github/ccxt/**), so the runner parses them into -Dhttps.proxyHost/-Dhttps.proxyPort/-Dhttp.* flags, which its java.net.http.HttpClient honors. Netty WebSockets ignore JVM flags, so watch* snippets wrap construction with Playground.proxy(new Binance()), which sets exchange.httpsProxy + exchange.wssProxy from the env (no-op outside the sandbox). Also: docker-compose mem_limit 2g -> 3g (8 concurrent source-launch JVMs measured at ~1.7 GB, sharing the cap with Next.js/dotnet/Go), Java fetchTicker + watchTicker examples, setup-runtimes.sh honors PLAYGROUND_DISABLED for python/php too, README updated (incl. the stale "4 GB cap" prose and the "why Java is install-only" section). Verified: tsc --noEmit and npm run build green; fetchTicker and watchTicker through /api/run on the production build (exit 0); REST and WS through a counting CONNECT proxy (CONNECT api.binance.com:443 and stream.binance.com:9443 seen) with dead-port falsification.

author: kroitor
message: fix(python): guard the ws receive callback against cancelled tasks (#29445) The receive loop registers after_interrupt as a done callback on the receive task and immediately calls exception() on it, but on a cancelled task that call raises CancelledError inside the callback, producing the asyncio "Exception in callback" crash from issue 26756 whenever the receive task gets cancelled mid flight, for example during a shutdown or a reconnect, which is rare in steady state and therefore surfaced only after days of running. The callback now returns quietly when the task was cancelled. Reproduced deterministically against a stub connection with the exact reported signature before the fix and zero loop exception handler captures after it, with the normal message path verified to flow through unchanged. Fixes #26756

author: cardosofede
message: (refactor) server_data_service: drop the dead stale_threshold knob DataTypeDefaults.stale_threshold had exactly one reader in get(), and every one of the 15 _DEFAULTS entries set it strictly below its ttl, so the `if age <= stale_threshold: return entry.value` branch was fully subsumed by the `age <= ttl` return that followed it. The field never changed behavior, yet its docstring advertised a three-tier freshness model and all 15 registrations picked values for it. Remove the field and its 15 kwargs, collapse get() to the single ttl check, and drop the stale "without subscribers" wording on the ttl comment (READ-066 removed that distinction). Pure cleanup, no behavior change. Closes READ-154.

author: cardosofede
message: (refactor) ARCH-146: one historical-candles ladder in the fetcher layer The sequence "get_historical_candles -> unwrap a list-or-{"data": [...]} payload -> fall back to get_candles -> normalize dict-or-tuple rows to float OHLCV" was inlined three times: the REST candles route, the WS candle backfill and the WS REST poll. All three talked to client.market_data directly, against the fetcher layer's contract, and the unwrap ternary appeared four times. It now lives in condor.fetchers.market_data.fetch_historical_candles, with the edges the call sites actually differed on expressed as arguments instead of silently unified: limit (None disables the get_candles fallback, which the poll never had), fallback_on_error (only the REST route degrades to the plain window when the range call fails) and strict (only the REST route surfaces a malformed row instead of dropping it). ws_manager._normalize_candle stays as a thin alias over the one normalizer, for the two WS stream uses unrelated to this ladder.

author: cardosofede
message: (fix) SEC-176: stop offering credential add/delete to non-owner traders SEC-153 raised exchange credential add/delete from TRADER to OWNER, but ApiKeysSettings had no permission awareness: a shared trader still saw the Add API Key and Delete buttons and only learned they were refused after clicking, when a 403 came back. The backend already serializes the answer. `ServerInfo.permission` comes straight from `get_server_permission()` — the same function `_require_owner` and `has_server_access` consult — so the client reads the level rather than re-deriving the rule, and no new API surface was needed. `useServerPermission()` joins the selected server against the `["servers"]` query the server selector already keeps warm, so it costs a cache read. It resolves unknown to *allowed*: a slow or failed server list degrades to the previous behaviour instead of inventing a refusal the API never made. This is UX, not enforcement. The backend gate remains the only thing that secures the route; a disabled button merely stops the dashboard promising what the API will refuse. Accordingly the failure path got louder rather than quieter: a delete that is refused anyway (stale permission, a share revoked mid-session) now renders the API's own detail instead of silently doing nothing. Gateway wallet controls are deliberately left open — those routes are not owner-gated today, and the client should mirror the backend, not lead it.

author: cardosofede
message: (perf) PERF-174: poll each portfolio-history range at its own TTL ARCH-145 moved the history poll into ServerDataService and preserved the old dashboard cadence exactly: all four ranges every 120s, because the hand-rolled loop re-fetched them together on one timer. But the per-range TTLs it also carried across are 1D=120s, 1W=600s, 1M=3600s, 3M=7200s — so the 3M window was refetched ~60 times per TTL, and 1M ~30 times, for data that had not moved. The cadence is now derived from the TTL that already exists rather than declared a second time: DataTypeDefaults.interval_for(params) scales the declared interval by ttl_for(params)/ttl, so a variant that stays valid 60x longer is polled 60x less often. PORTFOLIO_HISTORY declares interval == ttl == 120, so each range polls exactly at its own TTL: 1D unchanged at 120s, 3M at 7200s. Data types with no ttl_by_param are untouched — interval_for returns the flat interval. subscribe() builds the CacheKey before resolving the interval so it can consult the key's own params; ws_manager stops passing an explicit interval and PORTFOLIO_HISTORY_INTERVAL is gone, since a second table of cadences is the same defect this item fixes. Slowing the poll does not make the chart stale: the range switch goes through the REST route's get_or_fetch, which refetches the moment the entry is past its TTL instead of waiting for the next tick.

author: cardosofede
message: (refactor) move the portfolio-history poll into ServerDataService The REST route module held module-level polling state (_history_cache, _refresh_tasks, _last_request_time) and hand-rolled the whole lifecycle: warm + prime, a 120s refresh loop with a 10-min idle timeout, per-range TTLs, and an unsubscribe entry point. ws_manager drove it by importing warm_portfolio_history and stop_history_refresh out of the route file, coupling the WS layer to a REST module. All of that already exists in ServerDataService — subscription-scoped polling, per-server rate limiting, health/backoff — plus the single-flight coalescing the hand-rolled TTL cache lacked, where two concurrent reads of an expired (server, range) pair both hit the backend. PORTFOLIO_HISTORY becomes a data type keyed by range_key, fed by fetch_portfolio_history in condor.fetchers.portfolio. ws_manager subscribes the four ranges alongside the PORTFOLIO subscription and drops them on the last-subscriber-leaves path, so it no longer imports the route module. The endpoint reads through get_or_fetch and returns the same shape. DataTypeDefaults grows an optional ttl_by_param so the four per-range TTLs survive the move — SDS TTLs were per-data-type, and a 1D window going stale in minutes cannot share a TTL with a 3M one. The idle timeout is gone by design: the poll is now scoped to its subscribers, which is what the WS lifecycle already meant to express.

author: cardosofede
message: (feat) candles: pin a chart to one DEX pool The candle channel gains an optional sixth segment, the pool address: `candles:{server}:{connector}:{pair}:{interval}[:{pool}]`. A gateway pair like SOL-USDC exists in dozens of pools, and until now every DEX chart in the dashboard silently drew whichever pool `_resolve_pool` judged deepest. All three sites that read the channel (backfill, WS stream, REST poll fallback) went through `parse_candle_channel` — each used to unpack exactly five names, so a six-part channel raised ValueError in a place nobody watches: a chart that backfills but never ticks, or ticks but never backfills. `useCandleStore` and `TradeChart` carry the address through to the REST backfill, which already accepted it. Omitting the pool reproduces today's five-segment channel byte for byte, so no CLOB chart changes.

author: cardosofede
message: Answer the five questions from tables that outlive the raw events (FEAT-024) Retention and DAU computed over raw events mean a full scan per dashboard panel, and raw events expire at 90 days anyway. So every question is answered from daily_metrics, which the rollup writes and which is never deleted. This is the one piece of "premature" structure worth paying for from day one: backfilling a rollup after dropping the raw data it came from is impossible. The aggregation is split deliberately. SQL does the grouping — cheap, indexed, and identical in both dialects. Python does the date arithmetic and the cohort matching, which is exactly where Postgres and SQLite diverge most. The result is one rollup that runs unchanged against either, so the numbers the tests check are the numbers production computes rather than a parallel implementation. Cohorts come from MIN(day) in install_days rather than installs.first_seen, so retention keeps working for an install whose row was upserted long after its first event. dropped_total and dropped_rate are charted next to volume on purpose. The client's emitter clips a crash loop to 60 events/min and confesses the count in the envelope; without surfacing it, client-side rate limiting would masquerade as "things got quieter" during precisely the incident we most want to see. queries/ is the real deliverable — five plain-ANSI files, each runnable standalone against Postgres or the SQLite the tests seed, each readable without Grafana. Building a UI for five questions is a product; five panels over SQL is an afternoon. No query groups by user_hash. It is salted per install, so it counts distinct users inside one install but is meaningless across them, and grouping by it globally would invent the cross-install identity the client deliberately refused to provide. Partition maintenance runs a month ahead and drops what has aged out, which is an instant DROP TABLE rather than a mass DELETE. It is the one Postgres-only part; SQLite falls back to a DELETE, which is the right answer at the volume SQLite is used for. The table names it builds come from dates it computed itself — nothing from a payload reaches a formatted statement.

author: cardosofede
message: (fix) fail closed when the executor pair validation itself breaks (CORR-132) CORR-124 made validate_trading_pair fail closed, but the grid and position wizards wrapped the whole validation block in a bare except Exception whose fall-through still assigned and persisted the pair. Anything raised around the validator -- the executors client lookup, the get_correct_pair_format fallback read -- therefore landed an unvalidated pair in the executor config with only a log warning, reopening the hole one refactor away. Both panels now resolve a verdict inside the try and gate the write outside it: a raised exception sets is_valid=False with a cause-naming message, so it reaches the same suggestions screen an explicitly invalid pair does and never touches the config. The stale "Allow through if validation fails" comment is gone. The block stays identical in both files. Users can now be blocked where they previously slipped through -- that is the point of the item; no existing test depended on the fail-open path.

author: cardosofede
message: (fix) a failed read is cached as an error, not as an empty result (CORR-108) The four fetchers the SDS registers for positions, active orders, trading rules and credentialed connectors caught bare Exception and returned an empty container. _do_fetch_and_cache branches on whether the fetcher raised, so a transient 502 was recorded as a success: the last known positions were evicted, the server stayed green, no backoff engaged and the empty list was pushed to WS subscribers. Each fetcher now takes strict (default False, so every direct caller is unchanged) and the SDS binds strict=True at registration, the same disambiguation fetch_rates already uses. A failure now keeps the previous value as stale and records the error, which also lets the connector-unavailable unsubscribe in _subscribe_trading_rules_for_server fire for the first time. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: cardosofede
message: (fix) a live zero performance reading no longer pulls stale DB numbers (CORR-109) build_bots_page merged live and DB performance with `or`, so a legitimate live 0 (freshly redeployed controller, nothing closed yet) fell through to the last persisted snapshot for the same controller_id — possibly written by a previous deploy. Select by key presence instead, via a local _pick helper, for realized/unrealized/global_pnl_pct/volume. Absent keys still fall back to the DB snapshot. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: cardosofede
message: (fix) the SDS dashboard broadcast is a tracked task, and a failing one says so (CORR-107) `_on_data_update` fans every successful SDS poll out to the portfolio, prices and bots channels via a bare `asyncio.ensure_future`. Nothing held the returned task, so the event loop's weak reference was the only thing keeping it alive and the GC could collect it mid-await — a dashboard tick that silently never lands. CORR-021 swept the `create_task` sites in this module but missed this one because it spells the dispatch `ensure_future`. Route it through the `_track_oneshot` helper that exists for exactly this, and extend that helper's done-callback to log a non-cancelled failure on this module's logger. Previously a crash in `_broadcast_update` or the downstream `broadcast` surfaced only as asyncio's "Task exception was never retrieved" at GC time, so a channel could stop updating with nothing in the logs to explain it. The one-shots now carry names (`broadcast:<channel>`, `backfill:<channel>`, `warm_portfolio_history:<server>`) so that log line identifies the caller. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: cardosofede
message: (chore) delete the dead handlers/agents/session.py shim (READ-100) The shim re-exported destroy/get_info from condor.runtime.client and was kept "only until the last caller migrates". That condition is met: no production module imports it. Its docstring was also wrong on both counts — it claimed to be listed in reload_handlers(), which deliberately excludes it. Removes the three stale pointers that survived it: - main.py: keep the condor.runtime.* exclusion rationale, drop the session half of the NOTE. - condor/acp/pydantic_ai_client.py: custom@endpoint base_url/api_key are resolved by condor.preferences.resolve_custom_endpoint, not by the shim. - tests/runtime/test_session_facade.py: the hot-reload regression test now reloads handlers.agents.menu, a module that exists and is actually in reload_handlers(). It still asserts live sessions survive the reload. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: cardosofede
message: (feat) give a loop session a canvas it can revise (FEAT-036) The journal answers what happened; nothing answers what the agent currently believes. The canvas is that: four named sections it overwrites in place, plus an append-only revision log so a past belief stays reconstructable. The section set is closed and the per-section cap is hard because the whole canvas is inlined into every tick prompt and prompt caching cannot help — the volatile risk/core-data blocks sit ahead of it. The cap IS the cost control. entry_type="canvas" rides on trading_agent_journal_write rather than getting a tool of its own, so it inherits the engine resolution, the session-dir lookup and — the load-bearing part — the experiment-mode skip already written and tested there. A dry-run or run-once tick keeps no journal, so it keeps no canvas either, and it never sees the prompt block. NudgeTracker decides when the canvas has gone stale (position flip, PnL drift, a tick that errored, plain age) from state the engine already holds, so deciding to nudge costs zero tokens and only the emitted line is paid for. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: cardosofede
message: feat(chat): a reload lands on the conversation you were last in (FEAT-026) The roster picked `sessions[0]` when it did not recognise the previously active slot — server order, not recency — so a reload usually dropped the workspace into an old Condor chat, whatever the rail selection said. It now lands on the session with the most recent turn. `last_prompt_at` was already tracked per session but never reached the client, so the `sessions_list` payload carries it now; a roster without the field falls back to the previous behaviour. The roster order itself is deliberately left alone: slot order is tab order, and reshuffling tabs on every reconnect would be its own annoyance. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: cardosofede
message: fix(chat): the chat socket dies when the app does (CORR-100) `close()` is asynchronous, so clearing the reconnect timer and then closing the socket left `onclose` to fire afterwards and schedule a fresh retry. An unmounted hook rebuilt its socket every 3s forever, authenticated with the JWT captured before logout — log out and back in and two live `/ws/chat` connections served the same user. Adopt the guard `CondorWebSocket` already uses: a `shouldConnect` ref, cleared in `disconnect()` and in the unmount cleanup before the close, and checked in `onclose` before re-arming. `onclose` also ignores any socket that is no longer the hook's, so a replaced connection cannot speak for the current one. `connect()` now rebinds when the token changed instead of riding on a socket authenticated as the previous session, and the retry backs off 1s → 30s rather than hammering a down server every 3s. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: cardosofede
message: fix(runtime): a turn remembers which brain answered it (CORR-075) Attribution lived only on ConversationMeta, which is last-write-wins: a chat that talked to the assistant, switched to a bound Agent and switched back ended up with its whole history implicitly credited to whatever answered last. Unrecoverable after the fact, so any per-model eval slice built on this store was mis-attributed at the row level with no way to detect it. Stamp agent_key/agent_slug/mode on the assistant TurnEntry, from the live session, at the one funnel every surface already goes through. Old turns are not backfilled: an invented attribution is worse than an empty one. The line format has to age in both directions now that more fields are queued behind this one, so every field past `role` carries a default and unknown keys are ignored on read. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: cardosofede
message: (fix) invalidate the query key the chat model picker actually reads (CORR-103) CustomProvidersSettings invalidated ["chat-options"], a key nothing in frontend/src subscribes to, so adding or forgetting a custom LLM endpoint never reached the BrainPicker. The picker's single source is useSessionOptions, registered under ["session-options"] with staleTime: Infinity — a dead invalidation made the stale list permanent rather than merely slow, fixable only by a full page reload. Point the second invalidation at ["session-options"]. Both the add path (AddProviderForm onDone) and the delete path already funnel through the same invalidate(), so one key fix covers appearance and removal, in both the overlay panel and the /agents workspace. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: cardosofede
message: (feat) make Stop actually stop the agent, not just our listening (FEAT-029) `abort_prompt` cancelled the local future and drained the queue; the ACP subprocess never heard about it and ran the turn to completion. Its session history then held a full assistant turn the user never saw, while the transcript held the truncated one — and the next prompt landed in that divergent context, answering as though it had said things nobody read. ACP has `session/cancel`. We send it and leave the pending future alive, so the agent's `stopReason: "cancelled"` flows through the `_on_response` mapping that already existed. The old local cancel+drain becomes the fallback for an agent that ignores the notification, bounded by `TIMEOUTS.prompt_cancel` (2s) and logged at warning so a non-conforming agent is visible rather than silent. The fallback also enqueues a terminal PromptDone, so a consumer parked on an empty queue ends the turn now instead of at the next 30s heartbeat. `PydanticAIClient` had no `abort_prompt` at all, so `Session.abort`'s isinstance guard silently skipped it on local and OpenRouter models. It gets one — a flag the node loop reads between graph steps — and, importantly, it commits the partial turn to `_message_history` on the way out. That is the local-model equivalent of the `session/cancel` guarantee; skipping it reintroduces exactly the divergence this removes. The guard is gone: both clients now answer the same seam. `Session.abort` becomes async, the honest signature now that Stop waits on the agent. The dashboard resets optimistically, so the wait costs nothing visible. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: cardosofede
message: (feat) make Condor an agent and delete the mode axis (FEAT-033) assistants/condor moves to agents/condor and is loaded by AgentStore like every other agent, carrying its skills library and per-user stores intact. One registry, one AGENT.md loader, one frontmatter schema: binding.resolve always resolves an Agent, defaulting to `condor` when no specialist is named, so the chat gets its instructions, model and store scope through the same path a specialist does. `is_agent` now means "a SPECIALIST is bound", which is what its callers always branched on: the chat asserts no separate identity at system level, opens with the coordinator's context, and keeps an ambient (unpinned) server. The slug that gets recorded and shown stays empty for Condor, so session reuse, the conversation records and the dashboard's bound-agent indicator are unchanged. `condor` becomes a reserved slug (create and delete refuse it) and is excluded from the peer indexes: it is in the registry now, and a specialist offered the coordinator could consult back into the chat. The mode axis goes with it — a persona selector that had a single value since FEAT-004 and no reader — from SessionSpec, SessionInfo, Session, the conversation records, both chat payloads, the Telegram menus and the dashboard picker. Stale `mode` keys in persisted sessions, conversation metas and pickled user_data are ignored rather than migrated. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: cardosofede
message: feat(routines): a routine run from chat is a real run (FEAT-028) Ask a bound agent to run one of its routines, watch a full report come back in the chat, and the dock beside it still said "This agent has no routine runs." It was not stale — the MCP tool ran `routine.run_fn` itself, inside a stdio subprocess, so nothing was ever recorded: no instance, no post-run hooks, no result to reopen. Continuous routines were worse, registered in a store that dies with the subprocess and therefore unstoppable from the UI. The subprocess boundary is the whole bug, and the codebase already decided how to cross it. `run`/`start`/`stop`/`list_instances` now go through `call_main_api`, exactly as `consult` and `delegate` do; `run` polls the instance until it leaves `running` and maps it onto the same return shape the model got before, plus the `instance_id` so the answer can point at the run. Resolution and config validation stay in the subprocess — that is the code that knows about `strategy_id` and agent-local dirs, and a bad field must still fail fast with a useful message instead of arriving as a 404. What crosses the wire is the name the store knows (`{slug}/{routine}`, the same prefix the dock filters on) and the agent the run belongs to, which the tool knows better than the routine file does. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: cardosofede
message: (fix) serve report HTML only to authenticated callers (SEC-112) Report bodies were served by an unauthenticated `/reports/{filename:path}` mount while the metadata that points at them sat behind `get_current_user`. The index was protected; the content was not. With the server bound to 0.0.0.0, the only thing between the internet and portfolio value, PnL and positions was a guessable filename (second-resolution timestamp + known title slug + 24 bits of uuid4). Bodies now go through `GET /api/v1/reports/{report_id}/html` behind `get_current_user`, and the public mount is gone. `/reports/*` is an explicit 404 rather than falling through to the SPA shell, so a stale link fails loudly instead of looking like it still works. An iframe `src` cannot carry an Authorization header, so the client fetches the HTML with `authFetch` and hands it to the frame as `srcDoc`. The token stays in a header — never in a URL, where it would land in history, Referer and proxy logs. The sandbox keeps `allow-scripts allow-popups allow-downloads` without `allow-same-origin`, so report scripts stay in an opaque origin and cannot read the JWT out of `localStorage`. The download button saves the same authenticated response as a blob. ReportBrowser's hand-rolled duplicate of the iframe now reuses ReportFrame (with a theme override for its light/dark toggle), so the sandbox flags are defined in exactly one place — the two copies drifting apart is what SEC-016 and SEC-046 had to fix before. `get_report_raw_html` keeps the traversal and `.html`-only guards the deleted route had: the filename comes from the index rather than the caller, but the resolved path must still stay inside the reports directory, so a poisoned index cannot turn the route into an arbitrary file reader. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: cardosofede
message: feat(runtime): the transcript remembers what the tools were asked (ARCH-076) A tool-use training or eval example needs the tool's name, its arguments and its result. The transcript kept only name and status, so every agentic trajectory -- the interesting part of this system -- was unrecoverable. The signal was already in the process: both clients populate `input` on TOOL_CALL and `output` on TOOL_UPDATE, and both reach `Recorder.observe()` through the one `RuntimeEvent.from_acp` mapping. It was discarded ten lines before it would have hit disk. Now it is kept, along with `kind`. Two things make that safe to write down. Size. A tool result is routinely a market-data dump, a whole portfolio payload or a base64 image, and the transcript has no retention sweep -- kept verbatim, one turn could outweigh the conversation it belongs to. Both payloads are capped (1000 chars of arguments, 2000 of result), beside `REPLAY_MAX_CHARS` and for the same reason it lives there rather than in `timeouts.py`. An argument set too big to keep whole collapses to a single `_clipped` rendering rather than to a different type, so a consumer still sees one shape. Secrets. Tool arguments are written by the model, and at least one tool in the agents' own toolset takes a credential directly -- mcp-hummingbot's `configure_server(password=...)` -- so a verbatim transcript would persist a plaintext password. Credential-looking arguments are redacted by key name, never by value: guessing which string is a secret is how a redactor either misses one or mangles a trading pair. `_render_turn` is untouched. Replay still says "used X" rather than the result, because an agent that reads a stale result treats it as current. The new keys are additive on a `list[dict]`, so a line written before this still parses and reads back without them. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: cardosofede
message: feat(runtime): unified event model, REST + SSE session API (FEAT-009) The two frontends each had their own idea of what a session and an event were: chat_ws.py serialized ACP dataclasses to JSON inline while handlers/agents/stream.py pattern-matched the same dataclasses to build Telegram messages, and the web side kept private slot bookkeeping the bot knew nothing about. Two renderers behind an implicit contract drift the moment either side changes. Make the contract explicit and demote both surfaces to consumers of it: - events.py RuntimeEvent, the canonical wire event, plus from_acp() and a recursive serializer (bytes -> base64) so the same value renders in-process today and over SSE later. An unknown upstream event degrades to ERROR instead of killing the stream. - client.py prompt() streams RuntimeEvents and converts a mid-stream failure into error+done, so a consumer waiting on DONE can never hang. prompt_once() covers the blocking turns (context injection, /compact). get_live() is gone: nothing outside condor/runtime/ holds a live session object any more. - sse.py Framing, the no-buffering headers, and a parser the FEAT-014 HTTP client will reuse. event_stream() guarantees a terminal done. - routes/sessions.py REST lifecycle + SSE prompt + a multiplexed action endpoint. Authorization compares the session's recorded user_id, not the key's owner segment, since a Telegram key's owner is a chat id. - adapters/sse_to_queue.py Bridges the stream into a queue for consumers that already loop over one. Unused in local mode, by design. chat_ws.py is now an adapter: its outbound JSON shapes are unchanged (frozen by test_ws_contract_unchanged, since frontend/src/lib/api.ts reads them), but _user_slots is gone and the session list is derived from the runtime, so a session survives a WS reconnect and one killed from Telegram disappears here. MAX_SESSIONS_PER_USER moved into the runtime, so both surfaces share a budget. Deviations from the design doc: routers are registered in condor/web/app.py (the actual convention, not routes/__init__.py), and /chat/options is kept alongside the new /sessions/options because the shipped frontend still calls it. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: rapcmia
message: fix(agents): set grid leverage explicitly and fix stale detection - set leverage in the executor payload; omitted, it falls back to a default well above the envelope cap - leverage comes from the envelope, not agent discretion; ask the user once at session start - stale detection no longer requires a grid older than its time_limit, which the executor never allows to exist Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: rapcmia
message: feat(agents): react to grid results, and commit to a direction sooner The baseline sat on NEUTRAL through obvious moves because it only looked at EMA separation, and a running grid had no feedback path at all — it was kept or flipped purely on chart agreement. baseline_7d: - EMA separation threshold 0.3 -> 0.15 ATR - add a price-action override: price on one side of both EMAs with a 48h slope past +/-1% reads directional even while EMAs are still crossing - add a soft nudge at +/-0.25% for the remaining NEUTRAL cases - retune strength bands to 0.15 / 0.8, and report price-vs-EMAs and slope Layer 2, checked before keep/flip in priority order: - stale grids that stopped filling are torn down and rebuilt on a fresh range - grids at >=2% unrealized profit of trade budget are banked - sustained worsening PnL counts as a confirming vote, substituting for one missing timeframe; it never overrides a clear opposite baseline Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: rapcmia
message: fix(agents): daily timeframe always read NEUTRAL, blocking every flip _trend_direction bails out below slow + 2 = 23 candles, but the routine fetched only 20 daily candles. The daily timeframe therefore returned NEUTRAL unconditionally — proven with a synthetic 2%-per-candle uptrend, which reads NEUTRAL at 20 candles and BULLISH at 23. Because a direction change requires both 4h and 1d to agree, flips were unreachable: cases E and F never fired, case B always fell through to the baseline, and confidence could never exceed LOW. - fetch 60 candles for both 4h and 1d, with the 23-candle floor documented - drop stale "proxy for 6h / 12h" comments left from the previous design - add triple_barrier stop_loss (0.10) so a losing grid closes on PnL instead of waiting for limit_price or the time limit; note that it measures filled-position PnL, not budget Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: dizpers
message: fix: Pacifica connector crash on spot instruments and lost order fills Three live-found issues in the pacifica_perpetual connector: - Pacifica added spot instruments (e.g. SOL-USDC, instrument_type "spot") to /info and the price feeds in April; the perp-only pair parsing built "SOL-USDC-USDC" and crashed trading-rule updates, leaving the connector permanently not-ready for every user. Keep only instrument_type == "perpetual" entries in trading rules and the symbol map (the venue confirmed this is the supported discriminator), and skip unmapped symbols in both price feeds. - A perpetual listed by the venue mid-session permanently broke trading-rule updates. _update_trading_rules() formats the rules before it refreshes the symbol map, so a perp listed since the last poll is present in the fresh /info response but not yet in the map; the unguarded lookup in _format_trading_rules raised, which in turn skipped the map refresh, so the map never learned the new symbol and the failure could not self-heal. The polling loop's error path sleeps 0.5s instead of 30 minutes, so the bot then hot-spun on /info for the rest of the session with the trading rules frozen at their startup values. Found by QA after ~14h of uptime, when Pacifica listed VVV, KAITO and kSHIB at 2026-07-29 07:03 UTC. Skip the offending entry instead of discarding the whole batch, matching the Binance connector, so the map refresh still runs and the new listing is picked up on the following poll. - Market-order fills could be lost: the account_trades WS event may not arrive within the order tracker's 5s grace period, completing the order with zero amounts and never firing OrderFilled. On a filled or partially-filled WS order update, recover missing fills via REST (no extra requests when the WS stream delivered; deduped by trade id). Also fix the private WS keepalive payload ({"method": "ping"} — the venue rejects {"op": "ping"}) and use wall-clock time for the trade-history query window (the tick timestamp is floored to the second and could exclude just-executed fills). Plus one venue-independent dependency fix, noticed while diagnosing a QA report and unrelated to the three above: - Pin a working Brotli. aiohttp advertises "br" in Accept-Encoding whenever Brotli is importable, and aiohttp>=3.13.3 calls Decompressor.process(data, max_length) — a second argument Brotli only accepted from 1.2.0 (2025-11-05). urllib3 pulls brotli-python in transitively with a floor of >=1.0.9, which never forces the upgrade, so any environment solved before that date turns every br-encoded response into ContentEncodingError, reported as "Can not decode content-encoding: br". Reproduced against api.pacifica.fi with aiohttp 3.13.5 on Brotli 1.0.9 and 1.1.0, and confirmed fixed on 1.2.0. Declares Brotli>=1.2.0 and brotli-python>=1.2.0 — the conda package named "brotli" is the C library and CLI, not the Python bindings, so it never satisfied the import. Affects any venue that serves brotli, not just Pacifica. Also refreshes the stale account-info docstrings (data is an object, unified-margin fields) and removes a duplicated balance assignment. Related to #8201

docs(smart-money-flow): Derive-only consult trigger + USDC pair labels in onchain_flow - AGENT.md when_to_consult tightened to Derive perps (drop 'any venue'). - onchain_flow.py: report pair labels SOL/ETH/BTC now show -USDC to match Derive's USDC-quoted perps (signal is venue-independent; the displayed label was stale USDT). Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

The web GET /agents/{slug}/strategies/{sslug} resolves by folder name, so the frontend (open button) passed the slug 'derive_flow_trader' and got 404 'Strategy not found'. author: david-hummingbot
message: feat(agents): scaffold XRPL CLOB market maker agent Adds xrpl_market_maker, an on-ledger market making agent for the XRP Ledger CLOB, with the rlusd_xrp_maker strategy. The edge is structural rather than predictive: XRPL AMM pools charge an LP-voted fee of 0-1% and the ledger's pathfinding routes takers to the cheapest of AMM curve or CLOB offers, so any CLOB offer tighter than the pool fee wins that flow. No forecasting required. Key design points: - Fair value comes from a CEX reference (bitget_perpetual XRP-USDT), not from on-ledger data. RLUSD/XRP is a proxy for XRP/USD and updates on liquid venues first, so an on-ledger fair value is stale by construction and guarantees adverse selection. - Spread has a computable floor and ceiling. Floor is the expected adverse move between requotes (k * sigma * sqrt(tick_interval)); ceiling is the AMM fee. When floor >= ceiling the routine emits viable: false and the strategy holds. This couples tick frequency to viability explicitly. - shutdown.md uses keep_all because XRPL is LIMIT-only and cannot guarantee a flatten; claiming otherwise would be a policy that cannot be honoured. Closing any Bitget hedge leg is its top priority, since an orphaned hedge is a naked directional position. - Controller support for the xrpl connector is unverified, so both execution paths are scaffolded and xrpl_mm_feasibility gates which one is used. Ships as dry_run with $100 default capital and conservative risk limits. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

message: Merge origin/main into feat/custom-openai-compatible-endpoints Resolves three conflicts, all in favour of main's newer work with this branch's custom-endpoint support folded in rather than either side winning. agent_builder/SKILL.md — main added get_available_models and a real model recommendation heuristic, which is strictly better than this branch's "omit agent_key and inherit". Also corrected main's stale custom-endpoint bullet: "openai:<model> + model_base_url" is superseded by "custom@<endpoint>:<model-id>", which resolves URL and key from the user's saved endpoints at run time. api.ts / ChatPanel.tsx — both sides added a two-level model picker (main for OpenRouter and local servers, this branch for custom endpoints). Took main's AgentDropdown, which is the richer implementation and shared by both call sites, and generalized its single `showModels` boolean into a `submenu` discriminated union so OpenRouter and each saved endpoint are peer drill-downs. Also reworks how sentinels reach the web client. This branch had stripped them from /chat/options, which would have broken main's OpenRouter submenu (it needs the "openrouter:" entry present to render the drill-down). Instead every entry now carries an explicit `picker` flag. That fixes the underlying problem both versions had: the client was inferring "is a picker" from `key.endsWith(":")`, which also matches "ollama:" and "lmstudio:" — real, startable keys — so those were being silently hidden from the dashboard. get_available_models now reports custom_endpoints, re-validating each one so a dead endpoint surfaces as reachable:false instead of being recommended and failing on the first consult. author: david-hummingbot
message: feat: custom OpenAI-compatible LLM endpoints across Telegram, web and agents Reworks the custom-endpoint support so an endpoint configured once is usable everywhere, and so the surfaces that build a model can actually resolve it. Storage - Endpoints move out of raw user_data into condor/preferences.py as a named list synced to config.yml, giving Telegram and the web dashboard one shared view. Legacy user_data["custom_llm"] migrates on first read. - Agent keys become "custom@<endpoint>:<model-id>". The "@" segment keeps the model id recoverable with a single partition even when it contains colons and slashes (e.g. meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B:free). Fixes - /cancel matched no handler at all: the unified text handler is registered with ~filters.COMMAND and no CommandHandler existed, so the documented escape hatch silently did nothing while an invalid URL re-armed the prompt, trapping the user. Adds the command plus inline Cancel buttons. - Armed text-input flags survived navigation, so a stale flow ate the user's next message. They are now cleared in clear_all_input_states. - consult/delegate/engine constructed PydanticAIClient with no base_url or api_key, so a custom agent_key died with "No base URL configured" — session.py was the only caller that resolved endpoints. Adds a shared resolve_custom_endpoint() used by all of them. - New Agents inherited nothing, so the coordinator invented an agent_key from the agent_builder skill's examples and pinned agents to backends the user never configured. agent_key now defaults to the creator's active model, and get_user_context() reports it so the coordinator stops guessing. - healthcheck_local_backend skipped custom endpoints (it gated on the raw prefix, which is "custom@venice"), so they failed deep in a run instead of falling back. It now preflights them with the Bearer key. - _infer_tool_filter_mode forced "full" for every custom: model; "custom:" says nothing about capability, so it falls through to the size heuristics. - The web model picker dropped any key ending in ":", which is not the same as "is a sentinel" — it was silently hiding Ollama and LM Studio. Sentinels are now marked server-side and filtered from /chat/options. UX - Telegram: saved-endpoint list, add/manage/forget, error keyboards with Retry and a context-appropriate secondary action, a "No API key needed" button, model search, current model floated to page 1, and content-hashed pick tokens instead of list indices. - Web: Settings -> LLM Endpoints for add/validate/forget, and a two-level chat model picker that lazy-fetches each endpoint's models. API keys are never serialized to the browser, only a has_key flag. Hardening - Base-url candidates are probed concurrently at 8s instead of sequentially at 15s each. - /models entries that are embeddings, rerankers, TTS or image models are filtered out; picking one used to succeed here and fail opaquely at prompt time. Note object="model" is uninformative (OpenAI stamps it on everything) and falls through to id heuristics. - Hostnames are shape-checked, since urlparse accepts "not a url at all". - Link-local/metadata addresses are always refused; loopback and RFC1918 stay allowed by default (local model servers are the common case) and can be refused via CUSTOM_LLM_BLOCK_PRIVATE_URLS on shared deployments. - Model labels truncate through the middle, so the distinguishing tail of ids like ...-Instruct-Turbo-Free survives. Tests: 14 -> 34 cases in tests/test_custom_provider.py; 231 pass overall. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: fengtality
message: fix(portfolio): stop Gateway connectors from overwriting wallet balances A Gateway network such as 'solana-mainnet-beta' can exist twice in the account-state pipeline: as a unified Gateway trading connector and as a Gateway wallet fetched by _update_gateway_balances. Both wrote the same accounts_state[account]['solana-mainnet-beta'] key, and since connector results are applied after the gather, the connector view always won. That view is much narrower: gateway_base.update_balances() only queries Gateway for the tokens of the connector's trading pairs plus the native currency, so wallet tokens the connector doesn't trade disappear from portfolio state, and mint-address trading pairs report mint addresses instead of symbols. Skip Gateway connectors in the per-connector balance pass so the full wallet snapshot is the single source of truth for those keys, and mirror it onto non-master accounts holding the same connector (they trade the same Gateway default wallet) so their state doesn't go stale. Verified against a live Gateway: portfolio state now returns all seven wallet tokens with symbols, matching POST /chains/solana/balances; on the previous code the same setup returned four. Fixes #195 Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
